MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models are highly effective for generalist robot manipulation, yet their reliance on computationally expensive VLM encoding and multi-step iterative action generation imposes a significant latency bottleneck. The resulting inference latency makes it difficult for robots to respond quickly, especially in dynamic environments. We address this limitation with RAVEL (Rolling Asynchronous VLA Enabling Low-Latency Control), an asynchronous inference framework that addresses the computational bottlenecks of both the VLM backbone and the action expert. To reduce the delay from multi-step action denoising, RAVEL allows near-term actions to be executed after a single additional denoising step by carrying partially denoised future actions forward in a rolling buffer. To avoid blocking on slow VLM encoding, RAVEL decouples VLM encoding from rolling action generation, allowing the action expert to operate continuously using the latest available VLM context, while a lightweight Fast Observation Pathway (FOP) directly conditions the action expert on current observations. Across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, RAVEL consistently achieves substantially lower response latency while maintaining the task capability of the underlying VLA, enabling high-frequency and responsive closed-loop control.

MReaLLab.title: SynthDCB: World Distillation for Scalable Device Control Benchmarking
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zichen Zhu, Dingye Liu, Nan Jiang, Danyang Zhang, Hang Zheng
MReaLLab.summary: SynthDCB is a scalable benchmark for device control and environment awareness, utilizing world distillation to evaluate agent performance across diverse tasks and devices.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Scaling device-control evaluation requires scaling both interactive worlds and the tasks agents must solve. We introduce SynthDCB, a benchmark for environment awareness and device control built through world distillation (WD). World distillation transforms knowledge of device behaviors, constraints, and environmental effects into modular executable components. A unified capability representation connects tool discovery, world execution, and task synthesis. SynthDCB instantiates Home, Car, and Phone with 114 device classes, 1,166 functions, and 95 events, supporting five task families with 32 subtypes. Explicit states and tool-call traces support task validation and agent evaluation. We evaluate 22 models on 2,560 test tasks; the best achieves 88.8% mean Pass@1. Construction experiments demonstrate token efficiency and expansion of task coverage. At the richest knowledge level, WD fully covers 22/23 properties, 19/29 functionalities, and 30/39 event requirements specified in a real RobotVacuum protocol. Furthermore, the 1,000 sampled tasks semantically cover 81.6% of the 854 reference instructions in the real-world corpus. SynthDCB connects an expanding space of real-to-sim executable capabilities to verifiable agent evaluation.

MReaLLab.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
MReaLLab.authors_text: Kaiwen Zhang, Yiming Gao, Zeqi Xiao, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan
MReaLLab.summary: ViDecide introduces a decision-centric framework for training video diffusion models, enhancing multi-step reasoning and planning capabilities, achieving significant performance improvements over existing methods.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. We present ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule. We further propose Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), which corrects failed decisions by mapping their noise to the model's own successful continuations, achieving stable improvement without policy-gradient optimization. Across abstract games, planning tasks, and a new benchmark of multi-step robot planning, ViDecide achieves an average strict success rate of 83.8%, far above 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Our framework therefore unlocks greater potential for video generation models as reliable reasoners and planners in the visual world. Project page: https://kevin-thu.github.io/ViDecide.

MReaLLab.title: Composable Driving Style for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
MReaLLab.authors_text: Guantian Zheng, Lidong Yu, Tianyu Gao, Jiashu Li, Jiaxing Chen
MReaLLab.summary: YOUDrive enables composable control of driving styles in end-to-end autonomous driving through a vision-language-action planner that adjusts behavior via learned task vectors.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: End-to-end driving policies can achieve strong task performance while offering limited control over their driving style. Driving style describes how a vehicle accelerates, brakes, and maintains distance. Policies trained without explicit preference conditioning lack a direct mechanism for adjusting these behaviors at inference. We propose YOUDrive, a vision--language--action planner for continuous and composable driving-style control. Each teacher's behavior is distilled into a task vector, a learned parameter update that induces a style direction in the planner's representation. These directions can be scaled and combined at inference without retraining the backbone. Conditioned on these directions, a flow-matching decoder models a multimodal trajectory distribution and generates kinematically feasible motion alternatives. We introduce the Style Alignment Score (SAS) to describe human-referenced kinematic behavior after safety and task gating. On NAVSIM navtest, a single coefficient monotonically controls assertiveness across six teacher-derived personas, while PDMS remains above 0.90 across the tested individual and blended configurations, reaching 0.954. Further analyses reveal systematic policy-specific kinematics after controlling for scene context, whereas the evaluated discrete style labels provide limited additional explanatory power. Code, checkpoints, and the metric will be released.

MReaLLab.title: Plan4D: Generative Plannable 4D Worlds
MReaLLab.authors_text: Hangwei Zhang, Rujing Dang, Ruimin Lin, Jiahong Wu, Xiangxiang Chu
MReaLLab.summary: Plan4D introduces a generative model for 4D world prediction, enhancing visual fidelity and geometric accuracy by integrating video generation and 3D reconstruction techniques.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Most world models for future prediction prioritize aestetic quality of generated videos, but offer only weak physical grounding and limited geometric consistency over time, due to the lack of explicit 4D modeling. In this paper, we introduce plan4d, a possible next milestone towards building a generative plannable 4D world model that predicts future RGB videos together with dense 4D geometry, including depth, cameras, point clouds, and scene flow from an observed scene context and text-specified actions. Since training data with paired actions and dense 4D annotations is inherently scarce, plan4d leverages the complementary priors of foundational video generators and 3D reconstructors. Specifically, we propose a model-stitching architecture that couples Depth Anything 3 with LongCat-Video and augments it with an auxiliary DPT head for scene-flow prediction. The resulting model allows us to plan and generate complex, long-horizon, and fine-grained actions in a dynamic 3D scenes, while substantially improving both visual fidelity and geometric accuracy of the generated future videos. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that plan4d achieves state-of-the-art performance in generative 4D modeling of environmental reactions. Project Page: https://fogradio.github.io/plan4d-project

MReaLLab.title: MyoChallenge 2025: A New Benchmark for Human Athletic Intelligence
MReaLLab.authors_text: Cheryl Wang, Chun Kwang Tan, Balint K. Hodossy, Eric Lyu, Jun Guo
MReaLLab.summary: MyoChallenge 2025 establishes a benchmark for athletic motor intelligence, combining musculoskeletal models and machine learning to enhance robotic performance in sports tasks.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Athletic performance represents the pinnacle of human motor intelligence, demanding rapid choices, precise control, agility, and coordinated physical execution. Replicating this seamless combination of capabilities remains elusive in current artificial intelligence and robotic systems. Concurrently, understanding the biological mastery of these movements is hindered because complex muscle coordination is rarely measured in vivo due to the limitations of physical equipment. To bridge this fundamental gap in understanding, MyoChallenge at NeurIPS 2025 established a pioneering benchmark for motor control intelligence in sports, leveraging high-fidelity musculoskeletal models within physics simulation combined with machine learning-driven algorithms. The competition introduces two distinct tracks emphasizing either upper or lower limbs control: a table tennis rally task utilizing a biomechanic upper limb composed of an arm with a hand and a trunk; and a soccer penalty kick using a biomechanic model of legs and a trunk. Marking the fourth iteration of the MyoChallenge series, this event attracted almost 70 teams and over 560 submissions globally, uniting a diverse community ranging from physicians and neuroscientists to machine learning experts. The competition facilitated the development of several state-of-the-art control algorithms for a musculoskeletal system capable of sports agility, leveraging techniques such as physics-based motion planners, on-policy behaviour cloning, hierarchical planning, and muscle synergies. By integrating standardized tasks and physiologically realistic models into the open-source framework of MyoSuite, MyoChallenge'25 serves as a reproducible and reusable testbed to accelerate interdisciplinary research across machine learning, biomechanics, sports science, and neuroscience. Project page: https://www.myosuite.org//myochallenge/myochallenge-2025.

MReaLLab.title: Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models
MReaLLab.authors_text: Ziyue Wang, Shiqi Huang, Weiwen Xu, Bihan Wen, Xudong Jiang
MReaLLab.summary: Video-OPSD enhances on-policy self-distillation in Video Large Language Models by leveraging privileged visual evidence from videos for improved reasoning and performance.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) has recently emerged as an effective post-training paradigm that provides dense token-level supervision from a privileged self-teacher, yet it remains underexplored for Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs). Existing methods typically construct privileged teachers by augmenting their context with additional information while keeping the primary input unchanged for both teacher and student. In video reasoning, however, privileged information can also be found within the primary input itself: videos contain substantial temporal redundancy, and only a few frames carry the evidence needed to answer a question. Building on this observation, we present $\textbf{Video-OPSD}$, an OPSD framework that exploits privileged visual evidence for both self-teacher construction and knowledge transfer. First, our Evidence-Grounded Self-Teacher conditions the teacher exclusively on annotated evidence frames, while the student reasons over a broader set of frames that contains them. This focused visual context enables more targeted supervision without introducing visual content unavailable to the student. Second, our Evidence-Guided Token Optimization adaptively weights token-level distillation according to an estimate of each reasoning token's reliance on privileged visual evidence, thereby emphasizing perceptually grounded reasoning. Across five video benchmarks and three Qwen-VL backbones, $\textbf{Video-OPSD}$ consistently outperforms Standard OPSD by 1.8-2.3 percentage points on average, establishing an effective and efficient post-training approach for Video-LLMs.

MReaLLab.title: Improving While Deployed: Learning Proactive End-to-End Driving from Imperfect Human Takeover Data
MReaLLab.authors_text: Yangang Ren, Di Zeng, Jun Li, Zirui Li, Chengjiang Zhang
MReaLLab.summary: The paper presents a framework that enhances end-to-end driving models by transforming imperfect human takeover data into proactive supervision, improving performance in real-world scenarios.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Once deployed on vehicles, end-to-end driving models continuously encounter challenging scenarios, generating valuable human takeover data that capture both model outputs and human behaviors. However, human interventions are often imperfect, as drivers may intervene too late or unnecessarily. Consequently, direct imitation can reinforce late responses or discourage otherwise appropriate maneuvers. To address this challenge, we propose an offline post-training framework that transforms imperfect takeover data into proactive supervision. We first construct diverse trajectory candidates by augmenting the plans of the deployed model and shifting recorded human corrective maneuvers earlier in time. We then train a scene-conditioned trajectory scorer to rank these candidates using expert demonstrations and unpaired preference signals from takeover logs. Using this scorer, we selectively replace pre-takeover training targets with higher-scoring candidates while retaining the original targets in normal driving scenarios. Finally, we distill the resulting targets into the driving model without changing its inference architecture. In closed-loop evaluations using real-world scenarios reconstructed with 4D Gaussian splatting, our method achieves the highest overall success rate, outperforming the deployed model, direct imitation learning and trajectory post-optimization. These results highlight a practical path toward efficient updates of deployed driving models using existing fleet logs.

MReaLLab.title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
MReaLLab.authors_text: Rui Li, Liyang He, Zheng Zhang, Zhenya Huang, Qi Liu
MReaLLab.summary: AnyS1 is a framework that optimizes decision-making in autonomous agents by leveraging a lightweight System-1 model, significantly reducing costs and latency while maintaining reliability.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Autonomous LLM agents incur substantial cost and latency by invoking a large model (System-2) at every step, even when many intermediate actions choose among a small set of known candidates. Existing dual-system agents offload such decisions to a lightweight System-1 model, but rely on workflow-specific hooks authored per environment. We present AnyS1, a framework that turns human-authored procedural skills, whose instructions naturally specify where choices arise and which options apply, into a shared, domain-general source of decision points. Offline, AnyS1 mines grounded enumerable decisions across over 1,000 public skills, gathers execution-grounded trajectory states inside isolated containers to construct Any-DP, and trains a single calibrated 4B pointer System-1 with label smoothing. At run time, compiled workflows resolve routine decisions in one forward pass and fall back to System-2 when confidence falls below a calibrated threshold. Across three unseen benchmarks and distinct System-2 model families, AnyS1 preserves task reliability while cutting episode cost by 75-91% and model-call time by 63-92% relative to an uncompiled System-2 agent, and maintains performance under zero-shot threshold transfer.

MReaLLab.title: Facet-SLAM: Real-Time Triangle Splatting SLAM
MReaLLab.authors_text: Edward Beng Wai Tan, Siew-Kei Lam
MReaLLab.summary: Facet-SLAM introduces a real-time triangle splatting SLAM system that enhances tracking speed and surface accuracy for RGB-D cameras, outperforming photometric methods significantly.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Dense SLAM systems based on 3D Gaussian splatting build maps that render photorealistically, but their surface geometry is poor, and obtaining a mesh requires extraction or fusion stages. Triangle splatting avoids this with surface primitives whose vertices can be triangulated directly into a connected mesh, yet SLAM with this representation has so far relied on photometric tracking, which is too slow for localization at sensor rate. We present Facet-SLAM, the first real-time triangle splatting SLAM system for RGB-D cameras. Fast geometric registration is the natural alternative, but it is not sufficient alone, since the mapper's optimization displaces triangles from the observed surface and makes them unreliable registration targets. We therefore separate the two roles: the tracker sets each triangle's centroid from fused depth and registers frames to these centroids by GICP, while the mapper is restricted to non-translating updates via a change of variables. Our system achieves competitive tracking accuracy at around 100 FPS on a desktop GPU and runs at sensor rate on a Jetson AGX Orin. Compared with the photometric approach, it is over 20 times faster, matches rendering quality, and improves surface accuracy, reducing the chamfer distance of the Delaunay mesh on Replica from 1.55 to 0.86 cm. We will release the implementation at https://github.com/edward62740/Facet-SLAM.

MReaLLab.title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification
MReaLLab.authors_text: Jiarui Guo, Saining Zhang, Jiaying Wan, Jiawei Weng, Junhao Chen
MReaLLab.summary: RFW-S is a comprehensive dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified deformable objects, enhancing robotic simulation with reliable physical properties and interaction behaviors across diverse categories.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging. We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags. We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. To ensure physical reliability, we introduce an independent simulation verification framework that evaluates object behaviors under interactions distinct from those used for parameter calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of independent verification and characterize deformable responses under different physical configurations. We further evaluate robotic grasping in terms of both task success and object integrity, and demonstrate the physical realism of our simulated objects through sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation. RFW-S provides a scalable foundation for physically grounded simulation and embodied robotic learning.

MReaLLab.title: Resolution as Attention for Efficient Agent Memory Perception
MReaLLab.authors_text: Siqi Xiang, Zhipeng Xu, Shengrui Liu, Zulong Chen, Chunyan Miao
MReaLLab.summary: The paper introduces Resolution as Attention (RAA), a mechanism that optimizes agent memory by dynamically adjusting the visual resolution of past interactions based on their relevance, significantly reducing token consumption while maintaining performance.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: LLM-based agents accumulate extensive interaction histories when solving complex, long-horizon tasks, making efficient memory management critical to their performance and scalability. While existing memory management methods primarily focus on what to retain or retrieve, they often overlook how much perceptual detail should be allocated to individual past interactions. We posit that effective agent memory depends not only on the information preserved, but also on the granularity at which each past interaction is perceived. Motivated by this insight, we propose Resolution as Attention (RAA), a memory perception mechanism that uses visual resolution as a means of attention allocation across interaction histories. RAA renders past interactions as images and dynamically adjusts their resolution at every step according to their relevance to the agent's upcoming decision, preserving fine-grained information for critical interactions while reducing visual-token consumption for less relevant ones. To adaptively determine the perceptual fidelity of each interaction, we train a lightweight relevance estimator with teacher-model guidance and further optimize it to preserve the agent's decision consistency at a reduced visual-token cost. Experiments across multiple tasks and backbones show that RAA reduces token consumption by over 50% without compromising task performance. Moreover, RAA can be integrated as a plug-in perception layer with existing memory management methods, yielding further token savings and revealing adaptive perception as a complementary dimension of agent memory.

MReaLLab.title: MANGO-Grasp: Mahalanobis Fields over Geometry-Oriented 3D Gaussians for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasping
MReaLLab.authors_text: Heng Zhang, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Mike Zheng Shou, Weisi Lin, Yan Wu
MReaLLab.summary: MANGO-Grasp introduces an anisotropic framework using geometry-oriented 3D Gaussians and Mahalanobis fields for effective cross-embodiment dexterous grasping, outperforming existing methods.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Cross-embodiment dexterous grasping aims to synthesize stable grasps across heterogeneous multi-fingered hands with little or no embodiment-specific tuning. Existing interaction-centric methods achieve promising results, but their object representations often underrepresent local surface geometry, hand descriptors do not explicitly capture both morphology and kinematics, and hand-object interaction modeling is typically isotropic. We propose MANGO-Grasp, an anisotropic interaction framework that represents objects as geometry-oriented 3D Gaussian primitives to better preserve local surface geometry, and encodes hands into pretrained descriptors that capture both morphology and kinematics. Hand-object interaction is modeled using anisotropic Mahalanobis fields that reflect the directional nature of contact and guide a shared optimization for grasp realization across embodiments. On the CMAP and MultiGripperGrasp benchmarks, MANGO-Grasp outperforms the strongest seen-hand baseline by up to 8.24 percentage points in simulation. It also transfers zero-shot to the unseen SharpaWave hand, improving over the strongest zero-shot baseline by up to 16.57 percentage points, and achieves 86% success in real-world experiments. The code and additional materials are available at https://connor-zh.github.io/MANGO-Grasp/.

MReaLLab.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
MReaLLab.authors_text: Yiyang Zhu, Guangyuan Liu, Jingdi Lei, Li Wei, Chau Yuen
MReaLLab.summary: The paper introduces CounterPoint, a module that enhances multimodal alignment in Physical AI by preserving temporal dynamics, enabling better differentiation of physical events compared to traditional pooling methods.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation converges to the stationary recording condition. Consequently, as windows grow, no choice of loss function or embedding geometry can disambiguate twin events from pooled features alone. Instead, we show that physical events are uniquely identified by the event gap, namely the instantaneous, synchronous co-fluctuations across modalities that are erased by pooling and accumulate only along unpooled trajectories. To recover this signal, we introduce CounterPoint, a lightweight plug-in module that strips out each modality's temporal mean to score frame-level cross-modal agreement. Integrated across four state-of-the-art (SOTA) multimodal aligners, CounterPoint shifts representations from coarse condition matching to fine-grained physical event alignment, consistently outperforming existing temporal alignment methods.

MReaLLab.title: Video-HopChain: Multi-Hop Questions and Confidence-Gated Exploration for Video Reasoning Models
MReaLLab.authors_text: Trung Nguyen Quang, Yuhao Dong, Shuo Sun, Shuai Liu, Shulin Tian
MReaLLab.summary: Video-HopChain introduces a dataset for multi-hop video reasoning, enhancing model performance through confidence-gated exploration and addressing limitations in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: HopChain has shown on still images that multi-hop data synthesis improves vision-language reasoning, because long chain-of-thought reasoning exposes errors that compound across steps, while most data used for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) rarely demands a chain of visual evidence, so these weaknesses are likely to stay unexposed. We observe the same problem in video, where this framework has not yet been explored. We therefore build Video-HopChain, a dataset of 22,550 multi-hop video questions over 13,378 videos, together with a held-out benchmark of 1,000 questions. Each question chains three to six yes/no questions about moments in one video, and each yields one of two integers depending on its answer. The final answer is the sum of these integers, so an exact match on that sum gives the verifiable reward that RLVR needs. We first train Qwen3-VL-8B with GRPO on a standard video dataset, and a second stage on Video-HopChain then raises the mean over eight video understanding and reasoning benchmarks from 55.4 to 57.9 and improves every one of them. Training on such a dataset, however, exposes a known limitation of GRPO: its learning signal comes from the reward variance within a group, so hard questions whose rollouts are all incorrect and easy questions whose rollouts are all correct both leave the group with no gradient. To recover these groups at the same compute budget, we introduce Confidence-Gated Exploration (CGE). With 8 rollouts per question, CGE samples the first 4 as usual. If these 4 are either all correct or all incorrect, it samples the last 4 with the policy's most confident token masked inside the reasoning span, and removes the masked positions from the loss while all 8 rollouts enter the advantage. With CGE, the mean rises further to 59.3. We release the dataset, the checkpoint, and the data generation and training code.

MReaLLab.title: ThinkWAM: Rethinking Latent Futures for Action Refinement
MReaLLab.authors_text: Haoyun Tang, Baqiao Deng, Enjin Zhou, Songwen Tian, Keyao Xu
MReaLLab.summary: ThinkWAM enhances action refinement in robotics by utilizing a bidirectional feedback loop for multi-horizon future predictions, achieving high success rates across various environments.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: World-action models (WAMs) couple action generation with predictions of future states. An initial action chunk may be flawed. A future prediction that is not conditioned on the chunk is identical for every proposal and thus carries no proposal-specific signal, limiting its usefulness for refinement before execution. We introduce ThinkWAM, a latent WAM that establishes bidirectional feedback before execution through a proposal-rethink-refine loop: the policy first proposes a complete action chunk, the proposal corrects multi-horizon future latents through a learned residual, and the corrected latents are injected into a second pass of the same action head, which generates the executable chunk. An affordance-guided observation-action memory and a near-fine, far-coarse multi-horizon prediction scheme, both motivated by predictive coding, support this loop, and all prediction stays in latent space. ThinkWAM achieves 98.70% success on LIBERO, 84.76% on LIBERO-Plus without OOD fine-tuning, 85.75%/65.85% on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean/Random, and 65.17% on RoboCasa24. ThinkWAM achieves 64.4% mean success across three real-world OOD conditions. The mean two-pass inference latency per action chunk is 153.48 ms on LIBERO, 164.61 ms on RoboTwin, and 101.2 ms on the Galaxea A1Z. Ablations show complementary gains from rethinking and affordance guidance. Diagnostics indicate that proposal-conditioned corrections change both predicted futures and action trajectories, showing that the corrected future representations improve the final action.

MReaLLab.title: CascadeJEPA: Enhancing 3D Geometric Representations via Spatially Coupled Cascaded Prediction
MReaLLab.authors_text: Kailai Zhou, Ziqi Chen, Xiaoning Xu, Yuefeng Wu, Zixuan Fu
MReaLLab.summary: CascadeJEPA enhances 3D geometric representations in predictive visual learning by integrating spatially coupled cascaded predictions, improving geometric tasks while preserving semantic recognition.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for predictive visual representation learning. However, our analysis of I-JEPA reveals a growing discrepancy between semantic and geometric learning: improved semantic recognition during pretraining is accompanied by degraded 3D geometric representations. We hypothesize that this partly stems from predicting highly abstract latent representations with incomplete spatial context, favoring semantic regularities over fine-grained geometric information. To address this issue, we introduce CascadeJEPA, a spatially coupled cascaded prediction framework that promotes richer patch-level interactions through full-grid context encoding and cross-attention between prediction stages, while largely preserving the original I-JEPA architecture. Extensive experiments demonstrate substantial improvements over I-JEPA across multiple 3D geometric tasks while maintaining strong semantic recognition performance. Furthermore, its advantages extend to future feature forecasting and world model planning, highlighting the potential of enhanced geometric representations to support predictive world modeling.

MReaLLab.title: FAR-Drive: Frame-AutoRegressive Video Generation for Autonomous Driving
MReaLLab.authors_text: Yaoru Li, Federico Landi, Marco Godi, Ruiju Fu, Yufei Ma
MReaLLab.summary: FAR-Drive introduces a novel autoregressive video generation framework for autonomous driving, enhancing long-horizon consistency and stability while achieving sub-second latency and state-of-the-art performance.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Despite rapid progress in autonomous driving, interactive simulation remains a fundamental bottleneck. Existing closed-loop simulators generate video in multi-frame chunks to maintain short-term stability, yet this coarse granularity weakens the fine-grained interaction between agent actions and visual dynamics. Directly adopting frame-level autoregressive generation restores this interaction but sharply intensifies two challenges: long-horizon consistency and autoregressive stability under iterative self-conditioning. In this paradigm, each step is a single action-conditioned update, which also imposes strict low-latency demands since every step requires a full inference pass. In this work, we propose FAR-Drive, a Frame-level AutoRegressive video generation framework for autonomous driving, which integrates a multi-view diffusion transformer with fine-grained structured control to produce geometrically consistent multi-camera videos. At the core of our framework, we design a two-stage training strategy: (i) adaptive reference-horizon conditioning, which expands the temporal conditioning window for long-horizon consistency, and (ii) blend-forcing training, which gradually shifts from ground-truth to self-conditioned inputs to improve autoregressive stability. We further integrate system-level inference optimizations to satisfy the low-latency constraint. Experiments on nuScenes show that our method achieves state-of-the-art results among autoregressive driving video generation methods while keeping sub-second latency on a single GPU.

MReaLLab.title: Stereo-Planner: Learning Stereo-to-Trajectory Planning for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Quadrotor Navigation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Hongming Shen, Junjie Lu, Xun Chen, Wei Wang, Xinhang Xu
MReaLLab.summary: Stereo-Planner is a novel framework enabling zero-shot sim-to-real quadrotor navigation using stereo RGB images for trajectory planning without fine-tuning, achieving high success rates.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Existing navigation systems commonly rely on dedicated depth sensors or explicit depth reconstruction, while learning to generate trajectories directly from RGB images remains challenging due to the sim-to-real domain gap. In this work, we propose Stereo-Planner, an end-to-end vision-to-trajectory framework that enables zero-shot sim-to-real planning from stereo RGB observations. The key idea is to formulate trajectory generation as state- and scale-conditioned querying of latent stereo geometry. A Scene Representor incorporates a pretrained vision grounding foundation model to extract geometric cues shared across simulated and real-world environments, supporting generalization across visual domains. A lightweight Trajectory Decoder then translates these representations into trajectories through interleaved attention, separating trajectory-state interaction from scene-feature retrieval and incorporating the stereo baseline as a metric-scale cue. With these designs, Stereo-Planner is trained entirely on simulated data by minimizing differentiable trajectory costs and deployed directly in real-world environments without fine-tuning. Benchmark results demonstrate strong cross-scene generalization, with a 95% success rate in simulation environments at a commanded speed of 8 m/s, and competitive performance against depth-based planners using only stereo RGB observations for scene perception. Furthermore, deployment on a compact quadrotor equipped with an NVIDIA Orin NX enables autonomous flight at speeds of approaching 8 m/s, with a mean onboard vision-to-action inference time of 14.44 ms. The software, simulation environments, and hardware designs will be open-sourced at https://github.com/Stereo-Planner/Stereo-Planner.

MReaLLab.title: Cassette-Editor: Shared Timeline Semantics for Human and Agent Editing
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zhixin Zeng, Jiahao Zhong
MReaLLab.summary: Cassette-Editor integrates human and automated editing in a shared environment, enhancing video editing efficiency and accuracy through dynamic consequence management and structural validation.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Video editing involves tedious manual manipulation across interconnected timeline tracks, motivating automated agents that offload routine work while keeping the project directly revisable by humans. Fixed operation catalogs limit expressiveness, while even a basic trim requires coordinated updates across later clips, attached titles, and transitions. We present Cassette-Editor, an agent harness that unifies manual user gestures and automated agent patches within a shared editing environment. The shared action language expresses the editor's manual content changes, and a common history records committed edits for undo and manual refinement. When the model selects an edit, a state executor automatically derives its downstream consequences, such as shifting later clips and attached titles after a trim, while a validation rulebook enforces structural invariants and returns localized diagnostics for automated repair. To keep the agent grounded as the project evolves, dynamic read operations map transcripts and shot descriptions onto the current timeline. Evaluated with GPT-6 Luna, the full harness passed the scored request checks in 92/93 trials across 31 authored requests on two interview documentaries, compared with 48/93 for an internal basic-tools baseline. In ablations, disabling the consequences derived by the executor reduced passed trials from 230/232 to 199/232 on edits with dependent timeline elements, while ablating rulebook validation and repair lowered passed trials from 46/48 to 10/48 on requests operating near structural validity boundaries. Evaluating the complete system on 50 TVSum videos further demonstrated greater agreement with human annotations than a general agent using the same model (F1 23.8 vs. 20.1).

MReaLLab.title: DualTopo: Spatio-Temporal Lane Graph Generation with Dual Latent World Models and Parallel Query Supervision
MReaLLab.authors_text: Yiming Yang, Hongbin Lin, Yueru Luo, Suzhong Fu, Chao Zheng
MReaLLab.summary: DualTopo introduces a dual latent world model framework for enhanced spatiotemporal lane graph generation, addressing query supervision and boundary information loss in autonomous driving.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Lane topology reasoning constructs a spatiotemporal road graph G = (V, E) in bird's-eye view (BEV), providing structured road representations for planning-oriented autonomous driving. Stream-based methods propagate temporal cues at both the query and BEV levels, yet suffer from two critical limitations: (1) initialized queries receive insufficient supervision, as temporal queries dominate Hungarian matching and leave them undertrained; and (2) temporal propagation is weakened by BEV boundary information loss during feature warping. Since initialized queries serve as propagation anchors, particularly at the first frame, these deficiencies compound across frames and degrade graph generation quality. We propose DualTopo, a spatio-temporal lane graph generation framework with dual latent world models and dual parallel decoder pathways. The dual-pathway decoder supervises temporal and initialized queries concurrently, ensuring initialized queries are well-trained and serve as reliable anchors. Dual latent world models conditioned on ego-motion propagate latent state representations from past observations to the present, substantially improving spatiotemporal graph generation. Extensive experiments on OpenLane-V2 demonstrate leading lane detection accuracy and competitive topology graph prediction. Code is available at https://github.com/YimingYang23/DualTopo.

MReaLLab.title: VIVID: Beyond Static Multi-Image Reasoning with Localized Visual Differences and Textual Entity Dynamics in Video MLLMs
MReaLLab.authors_text: Chengqian Ma, Yuanze Zeng, Hongyu Wang, Mingfeng Lin, YiCheng Xiao
MReaLLab.summary: VIVID enhances video question answering by integrating localized motion and event order through Dynamic Tokens and inter-frame differences, outperforming existing models in accuracy.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Video question answering under tight frame budgets requires preserving localized motion and event order, yet current video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) reduce comprehension to static multi-image reasoning by discarding unselected frames and encoding keyframes independently: (1) Spatially, whole-frame pooling dilutes small moving targets into static backgrounds; (2) Temporally, dropping intermediate frames or averaging tokens erases inter-frame motion, confusing direction, speed, and order. We propose VIVID (Visual Inter-frame Variations and Individual Dynamics), which moves beyond static snapshots like human vision: keyframes capture core states while inter-frame Patch Diffs preserve neighboring changes within $K_f$ keyframes. Autonomous Delta-Driven Keyframe Planning (ADKP) selects anchors from a $3\text{ fps}$ pool and feeds surrounding patch differences into Dual-Road Change Memory (DRCM), forming Dynamic Tokens at zero extra anchor tokens alongside a camera-stabilized Active Motion Region of Interest (ROI) and chronological Entity State Chains. Adding $0.22\%$ trainable parameters to a frozen $27\text{B}$ backbone, VIVID-Small ($50$ examples, $\sim 1.5$ GPU hours) beats all eleven baselines in overall accuracy across $8,083$ questions and trails only VIVID-Large ($3,600$ examples), which leads on MotionBench, Video-MME, and TempCompass.

MReaLLab.title: SimpleVLN: Towards Simple and Frontier Vision-Language Navigation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Lingyi Hong, Weiren Cai, Jiayu Chen, Xinyu Zhou, Bailin He
MReaLLab.summary: SimpleVLN is a novel framework that enhances Vision-and-Language Navigation using native MLLMs, achieving superior performance without task-specific architectures through efficient memory and data optimization techniques.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires embodied agents to ground language in visual observations and make long-horizon decisions. Existing methods often address these demands through task-specific architectures. As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly capable, an important question remains: Have we truly unlocked the potential of native MLLMs for VLN before introducing task-specific architecture? We present SimpleVLN, an architecture-preserving framework developed through studies of navigation formulation, data construction, and optimization. At the formulation level, SimpleVLN combines single-turn decision inputs with fixed-budget global-local memory to efficiently use navigation history without unbounded context growth, while action chunks enable efficient output of multiple primitive actions per model invocation. For data construction, we combine expert demonstrations with policy-dependent DAgger experience and develop a scalable synthesis pipeline that generates large-scale tasks for reinforcement learning. At the optimization level, a progressive IL-DAgger-RL pipeline advances from action imitation to task-level outcome optimization. Comprehensive experiments validate the effectiveness of these three aspects. We instantiate SimpleVLN across multiple MLLM backbones and model sizes, demonstrating its generality. SimpleVLN achieves 76.7% and 80.1% success rates on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE splits, respectively, substantially outperforming existing methods. These results show that the navigation capabilities of native MLLMs can be effectively unlocked without task-specific architectural designs.

MReaLLab.title: Reliable Conditioned Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability via Subsolution Learning on Exact Local Windows
MReaLLab.authors_text: Seunghwan Jang, Wei Xiao
MReaLLab.summary: This paper presents a conditioned reachability model that conservatively approximates Hamilton-Jacobi reachability, enhancing safety in robotic navigation by minimizing false-safe states across varying obstacle configurations.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability computes the maximal safe set and a safety filter for a given obstacle configuration, but it must be re-solved whenever the obstacles change, which a deployed robot cannot afford. Learning a single value function conditioned on the obstacle set removes the re-solve, yet it sharpens the central weakness of learned reachability: one network must now cover a whole family of safety problems, and its approximation error carries no preferred sign, so rare obstacle configurations silently produce false-safe states. To address these challenges, we present a conditioned reachability model designed so that the remaining error falls on the conservative side. Specifically, our method caps the obstacle margin, which makes the value function provably local, in the sense that obstacles farther than a known threshold cannot affect it, so the model reads only a body-frame window, trains on small scenes, and transfers to scenes of any size with millisecond per-scene preparation. Moreover, the output structure builds the value bound into the model. By training with counterexample mining over the finite-dimensional window configuration space, we maximize the claimed safe volume subject to the HJ inequality, so the learned set grows toward the true safe set from the conservative side. Across all tested obstacle settings, ours is the only method that combines recovery comparable to per-scene DeepReach training with near-zero rollout collisions. We also extend the method to a 10D quadrotor, again with markedly lower collision rates than the baselines.

MReaLLab.title: VLN-Flash: Parallel Action Decoding with Adaptive Execution for Vision-and-Language Navigation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Ruizhe Xie, Honghua Chen, Binglin Wang, Tong Guo, Xu Tang
MReaLLab.summary: VLN-Flash enhances vision-and-language navigation by enabling parallel action decoding, achieving nearly 3x faster execution and improved success rates compared to autoregressive methods.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: When a vision-and-language navigation policy generates an action sequence autoregressively, the robot waits for a chain of dependent predictions. A small discrete action vocabulary makes it possible to score all short-horizon plans in parallel. We introduce VLN-Flash, a training-free decoder that evaluates the complete action-prefix tree in a single forward pass. Branch-specific attention and matched token positions preserve the original policy's conditional action distribution for each prefix in exact arithmetic. We use the score margin between the stepwise-greedy prefix and its strongest alternative at each depth to decide how many actions to execute. The robot then executes the plan with the highest joint score at the chosen depth before observing again. On matched inputs, VLN-Flash achieves a nearly $3\times$ speedup in action decoding over native autoregression on Uni-NaVid and StreamVLN. Compared with the native autoregressive decoders, it improves success rate and success weighted by path length (SPL) on R2R-CE and RxR-CE, with success gains up to 2.7 percentage points. On a Unitree GO2, VLN-Flash improves navigation success and cuts the mean wait between actions by about 160 ms after subtracting network transmission time.

MReaLLab.title: GEM-MM: Reducing VLM Hallucination with Entropy-Guided Preference Alignment
MReaLLab.authors_text: Yuanshan Chua, Xuejiao Zhao
MReaLLab.summary: GEM-MM enhances vision-language models by employing entropy-guided preference alignment, significantly reducing hallucination rates while improving accuracy and preference scores under limited data conditions.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are routinely aligned with offline pairwise RLHF objectives, but multimodal preference data is scarce and treats every response token as equally informative. Under a small preference budget, pair construction becomes nearly irrelevant: standard DPO-style, image-conditional, and self-improvement objectives all perform within 1.1 points on MM-RLHF metrics and 0.5 points on hallucination rates, matching the SFT baseline. We call this entropy-blind preference optimization: the learning signal ignores policy uncertainty, which in chain-of-thought VLMs concentrates on specific fork tokens where visual claims are made. We introduce GEM-MM, extending entropy-guided preference modeling to VLMs. It samples on-policy candidates, rewards high-entropy reasoning forks, penalizes uncertain final answers, and updates the model via group-normalized policy gradients. On a 3000-prompt MM-RLHF budget with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, GEM-MM achieves the best entropy-depth preference score (61.7% vs. 57.3-58.4% baselines) and implicit-reward accuracy (41.4%). Crucially, it reduces AMBER hallucination from 23.4-24.0 to 20.6 and CHAIR from 5.0-5.1 to 4.6 at matched caption coverage. It also ranks best on all three HallusionBench granularities, with a conservative operating point raising the near-chosen rate to 62.4%. An off-the-shelf multimodal reward model ranks GEM-MM first, and two such models independently confirm our main ablations (p < 0.001). We report confidence intervals, paired significance tests, metric-reward functional overlaps, and document a collapse mode when exceeding the fair budget. Code and evaluation harness: https://github.com/SNOWTEAM2023/GEM-MM

MReaLLab.title: Skeleton-to-Image Encoding: Enabling Skeleton Representation Learning via Vision-Pretrained Models
MReaLLab.authors_text: Siyuan Yang, Jun Liu, Hao Cheng, Chong Wang, Shijian Lu
MReaLLab.summary: The paper introduces Skeleton-to-Image Encoding (S2I), transforming skeleton sequences into image-like data to leverage vision-pretrained models for self-supervised skeleton representation learning.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Recent advances in large-scale pretrained vision models have demonstrated impressive capabilities across a wide range of downstream tasks, including cross-modal and multi-modal scenarios. However, their direct application to 3D human skeleton data remains challenging due to fundamental differences in data format. Moreover, the scarcity of large-scale skeleton datasets and the need to incorporate skeleton data into multi-modal action recognition without introducing additional model branches present significant research opportunities. To address these challenges, we introduce Skeleton-to-Image Encoding (S2I), a novel representation that transforms skeleton sequences into image-like data by partitioning and arranging joints based on body-part semantics and resizing to standardized image dimensions. This encoding enables, for the first time, the use of powerful vision-pretrained models for self-supervised skeleton representation learning, effectively transferring rich visual-domain knowledge to skeleton analysis. While existing skeleton methods often design models tailored to specific, homogeneous skeleton formats, they overlook the structural heterogeneity that naturally arises from diverse data sources. In contrast, our S2I representation offers a unified image-like format that naturally accommodates heterogeneous skeleton data. Extensive experiments on NTU-60, NTU-120, and PKU-MMD demonstrate the effectiveness and generalizability of our method for self-supervised skeleton representation learning, including under challenging cross-format evaluation settings.

MReaLLab.title: OA-WAM: Object-Addressable World Action Model for Robust Robot Manipulation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Yushan Liu, Peibo Sun, Shoujie Li, Yifan Xie, Lingfeng Zhang
MReaLLab.summary: OA-WAM introduces an object-addressable world action model that enhances robot manipulation robustness across varying conditions, achieving superior performance in multiple benchmarks and real-robot tasks.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) learn manipulation by predicting actions and future observations, yet their success drops sharply when the camera viewpoint, object layout or robot initial state changes. Such changes keep the instructed object the same but alter the appearance and pose features the policy observes, which in standard attention also form the keys that locate the object. We introduce OA-WAM, an object-addressable WAM that finds each object by an identity address fixed for the episode and reads its changing state. In every layer of a pretrained multimodal trunk, object-slot keys depend only on the address and frame position, and values carry the current state; the same addresses key the action pointer and index per-object forecasts, which can trigger re-grounding. Fine-tuned on standard LIBERO demonstrations, OA-WAM transfers zero-shot to LIBERO-Plus with 90.5% success, outperforming all ten published baselines. It also leads on LIBERO (99.0%) and, fine-tuned on BridgeData V2, on SimplerEnv WidowX (88.9%). On five real-robot tasks, it succeeds in 89 of 100 nominal trials, versus 73 for the strongest baseline. Ablations trace its robustness to addressing rather than to object slots: with standard attention, slots do no better than a slot-free policy, and addressing them by identity raises geometric success by 10.7 points. Forecasting the addressed objects is likewise a stronger training signal than forecasting image codes.

MReaLLab.title: What the Averages Hide: Monocular Metric Depth Models Still Fail in Everyday Scenes, Mostly on Scale
MReaLLab.authors_text: Hualie Jiang, Yujie Luo, Ziyang Song, Ximeng Li, Zhiqiang Lou
MReaLLab.summary: Monocular metric depth models struggle with scale in everyday scenes, revealing significant failure rates and shared errors across architectures despite improvements from ground-truth intrinsics and larger models.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Zero-shot monocular metric depth models are evaluated by averaging metric and scale-aligned scores across datasets. Averages cannot show how many images still have severely wrong metric depth, whether depth is under- or overestimated, or whether different models fail on the same images. We propose an evaluation built on per-image results: the failure rate (metric $δ_1$ < 0.5); scale-aligned metrics for structure, and the bias, dispersion and absolute error of the alignment scale for scale; and a cross-model comparison that separates shared from model-specific failures. We apply it to 11 recent architectures with and without ground-truth intrinsics (18 model evaluations) on the 7 everyday-scene benchmarks (4,406 images) used by MoGe-2. Metric depth estimation is not solved in everyday scenes, and the remaining difficulty is mainly scale: the best of the 18 evaluations still has a failure rate of 7.7% (datasets weighted equally); pooled over all failures, 78.8% have intact structure, and after scale correction 98.3% no longer fail. Images failed by at least 6 architectures make up 7.3% of the data, concentrated on HAMMER and DIODE; even when selected only by architectures of other families, they hold 34% to 40% of the error of the top 6 models, against 14% to 18% for as many random images from the same datasets. Adding objects reduces the scale error of most models; ground-truth intrinsics and, in most families, larger models reduce the failures but do not remove them. We recommend reporting failure rates, structure and scale separately, and results stratified by how many models fail. We will release the code, the per-image results with shared-failure labels, and two diagnostic sets built from TUM RGB-D.

MReaLLab.title: Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation for Multiple Tunnel Defects Under Complex Environments
MReaLLab.authors_text: Mohan Ren, Hang Li, Yifei Liu, Shaowei Wang, James O'Kane
MReaLLab.summary: The paper presents Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation (MDS) for automated tunnel defect inspection, enhancing segmentation by organizing features based on defect morphology, achieving improved accuracy and efficiency.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Automated tunnel-lining inspection must segment different defect geometries: cracks are thin, elongated, and connectivity-sensitive, whereas leakage, lining falling off, and segment damage are spatially extensive and context-dependent. Existing approaches generally apply a common decoder across defect classes or introduce boundary, topology, and directional mechanisms as isolated enhancements. This paper introduces Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation (MDS), in which defect morphology becomes the organising principle for feature routing, decoding, and interaction. A supervised routing module partitions multiscale encoder features into complementary linear and areal streams. The linear stream employs Deformable Strip Attention with image-conditioned direction hypotheses to preserve crack continuity without assuming fixed horizontal or vertical orientations, while the areal stream combines Pyramid Pooling with feature-pyramid fusion to capture diffuse boundaries and regional context. The representations are coupled through gated cross-morphology attention, allowing complementary information exchange while retaining morphology-specific features. A resolution-adaptive tiling and probability-blending pipeline preserves fine defects across variable-resolution imagery. MDS achieves 81.17% mIoU on the internal validation set and improves foreground image-level recognition over a backbone-matched SegDINO model, primarily for areal defects. Controlled ablations demonstrate the complementary contributions of routing supervision and cross-stream interaction while revealing a trade-off between areal-class performance and crack specialisation. The submitted model achieved 67.55% mIoU on an organiser-controlled hidden test, and the team placed second. Selective dynamic INT8 quantisation reduced model storage by 2.83 times with negligible accuracy loss.

MReaLLab.title: UNITE: Consolidating Embodied VLM Specialists via Shared-Anchor One-Bit Factorization
MReaLLab.authors_text: Tao Tao, Anke Tang, Enneng Yang, Zhi Hou, Xiaogang Wang
MReaLLab.summary: UNITE consolidates multiple embodied vision-language specialists into a compact model using shared-anchor one-bit factorization, maintaining performance while significantly reducing storage requirements.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Embodied capabilities such as visual grounding, spatial reasoning, navigation, and driving understanding are often developed in separate vision-language specialists fine-tuned from a common pretrained model.Deploying the specialists separately multiplies storage, whereas merging them into one dense model forces conflicting task updates to share parameters and loses part of each specialist's expertise.We introduce UNITE, a framework that consolidates such specialists into a compact shared-backbone mixture of experts. UNITE keeps the feed-forward block of each specialist as a routable expert and represents the expert bank through a shared-anchor one-bit factorization: a shared floating-point anchor plus expert-specific, row-scaled binary deviations.The anchor is optimized jointly with the scales and signs through closed-form alternating updates, using only source weights and no calibration data.Router adaptation then adjusts token-level expert selection with the backbone and experts frozen, updating fewer than $0.6$M parameters ($<0.01\%$ of the $8.8$B active parameters). Built from four Qwen3-VL-8B specialists, the complete UNITE model occupies $20.3$ GB, $1.16\times$ the storage of one dense specialist and $59.6\%$ below the uncompressed MoE. Across $22$ benchmarks and R2R Val-Unseen, UNITE matches six static merging methods in mean retention of best-specialist performance, leads all of them on Scan2Cap, ScanQA, and all four navigation metrics, and surpasses every source specialist on all five 3D scene understanding benchmarks (up to $+19.1$ on Scan2Cap) and on R2R navigation. Relative to the uncompressed MoE, factorization is nearly lossless on $21$ of $22$ benchmarks; the exception is VSI-Bench, where frame-count experiments suggest impaired use of cross-frame evidence.UNITE thus consolidates complementary embodied capabilities near single-model storage.

MReaLLab.title: VGGT-VLA-World: Intent-Conditioned 3D World Evolution for Autonomous Driving
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zhaoyang Liu, Zhigui Lin, Kun Jiang, Tianhui Li, Changye Liu
MReaLLab.summary: VGGTWorld-VLA enhances 3D world evolution in autonomous driving by integrating intention-based action conditioning, improving future geometry predictions significantly compared to existing models.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: VGGT provides a strong foundation for geometry-centric world models by recovering unified 3D scene geometry from visual observations. Although recent extensions enable temporal 3D prediction, their future evolution remains weakly conditioned on driving intentions and actions, limiting their ability to model alternative action-dependent futures. We propose \textbf{VGGTWorld-VLA}, an intention-conditioned extension of VGGT-World for controllable 3D world evolution in autonomous driving. First, we introduce an action--semantic conditioning mechanism that injects complementary driving semantics and ego-motion representations into the future-token stream, enabling different future geometry predictions for the same observed scene under alternative ego actions. Second, we develop a geometry--language--action bridge that adapts historical geometry, VLA semantic features, and maneuver and trajectory representations for joint conditioning of future geometry prediction. We evaluate future geometry prediction on NAVSIM, with ablation studies examining the contributions of semantic and action conditioning. Compared with baseline, our method reduces future-depth RMSE by 13.7\% and improves $δ_1$ by 4.11 percentage points on NAVSIM motion subset. Controlled action-input interventions further show that the model uses the supplied action information. These results support semantic and action conditioning for controllable VGGT-based world prediction in autonomous driving.

MReaLLab.title: DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
MReaLLab.authors_text: Hanlin Tian, Sihan Zhu, Zhao Yang, Yuxiang Wang, Zhiquan Hu
MReaLLab.summary: DetourBench introduces a trajectory-level evaluation framework for interactive agents, emphasizing minimum-action bounds to distinguish between efficient and inefficient decision-making processes.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Settling this needs a reference cost, and authored solutions establish only that a task is solvable, not that no shorter route exists. We present DetourBench, which constrains the environment until that minimum is computable. Each task is a finite, partially observable transition system with unit-cost accesses whose resources become globally addressable after discovery. Exhaustive search yields the full-information minimum action count $L_0$ with a replayable witness; from graph-recoverable terminal states it also yields exact residual work $R_T$, which separates an episode that stopped one access short from one that wandered, while an irreversible wrong commitment is recorded as having no finite residual distance rather than assigned one. Success, attainment, residual progress, and normalized detour are reported separately. Across 375 scored episodes --- five model endpoints, 25 integrated tasks, three repeats --- success ranges from 58.7% to 96.0% while conditional attainment ranges from 0.803 to 0.890 and orders the models differently. Among recoverable failures, residual work separates near-complete trajectories from costly incompletion and from irreversible commitment. We open-source the instances, oracle witnesses, and evaluation harness at https://github.com/DatagridsAI/DetourBench.

MReaLLab.title: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot
MReaLLab.authors_text: Jiaxin Huang, Chengxing Lin, Xiaoyu Luo, Sirui Chen, Jingyu Guo
MReaLLab.summary: X-Nav is the first system enabling a humanoid robot to autonomously navigate from indoors to outdoors using language instructions, integrating data collection, navigation modeling, and obstacle avoidance.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Long-horizon navigation from indoors to outdoors remains an open problem for humanoid robots: one instruction covers rooms, doors and roads, and the camera moves with the gait. Worken, AGIBOT's measure of productive robot work, depends on robots that reach their workplaces autonomously. We present X-Nav, to our knowledge the first system to take a bipedal humanoid through a language-instructed long-horizon mission from indoors to outdoors. X-Nav covers a pipeline from data to deployment. Its data engine collects navigation data in open-source scenes, in digital twins of deployment sites and on real robots. Its navigation model, MELIOR, takes only RGB images from the robot's built-in camera and comes in two versions: MELIOR-A predicts actions, and MELIOR-N predicts a navigation goal. Its agentic workflow, X-Navarch, turns a brief human instruction into sub-tasks and deploys MELIOR on the robot with explicit target navigation and obstacle avoidance. On the Lingxi X2, X-Nav completes a mission of about a hundred metres from an office lobby to a store in a neighbouring building; LiDAR and odometry are used for target approach and low-level control. The mission is completed with both versions of MELIOR: the robot follows a change of destination and walks through a door from the lobby to the road, and with X-Navarch it also passes static and dynamic obstacles on the route. During deployment, MELIOR is adapted with data collected in a digital twin of the site; the adaptation raises its closed-loop success rate in the twin, and the adapted model is then deployed on the robot at the real site. In addition, MELIOR achieves competitive results on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks.

MReaLLab.title: Per-Agent-Safe Navigation of Globally Driven Robot Collectives via Affine Field Design
MReaLLab.authors_text: Seunghwan Jang, Steven Ceron, Wei Xiao
MReaLLab.summary: The paper presents a broadcast control strategy using a single affine field to ensure safe navigation and adaptive size regulation for robot collectives in constrained environments.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Safe navigation of robot collectives requires coordinating motion and deformation so that the collective can traverse constrained environments while ensuring each robot's safety. Existing controllers for swarmalator collectives largely rely on local control, where each robot receives an individual command, which causes the control and communication requirements to grow with the number of agents. We introduce a broadcast control formulation in which a single spatially affine field governs both the motion and deformation of the collective. The scalar component of the field regulates collective size, and its spatial gradient generates collective translation through non-reciprocal interactions. Both components enter the collective dynamics directly, which allows per-robot wall, actuation, and cohesion constraints to be enforced using control barrier functions within a single quadratic program for the whole collective. The resulting controller continuously adapts the collective size to the local environment, and enables safe passage through corridors narrower than the unconstrained collective without pre-planned resizing. We further derive how the available actuation budget determines the reachable speed and minimum passable corridor width, and we demonstrate that two independently driven collectives can simultaneously traverse a shared junction using distinct fixed phase labels without inter-collective coordination.

MReaLLab.title: RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$: On-Device Reinforcement Learning Runtime
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zexin Li, Xinwei Gao, Arvind Easwaran
MReaLLab.summary: RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$ is an on-device reinforcement learning runtime that optimizes actor-learner coupling to minimize deadline misses on embedded GPUs.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: On-device reinforcement learning runs a periodic actor and a learner on one embedded GPU shared with other workloads. Because the learner produces the actor's weights, existing designs stall the actor or let its policy drift. We present RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$, an on-device runtime that makes this coupling a tunable parameter: a refresh bound limits actor releases between refreshes, and a GPU permit with slack-aware admission prioritises the actor and fills spare time with training atop any base scheduler. Under the real refresh cost on two Jetson boards, RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$ keeps a 16.8 M-parameter policy's deadline misses below 1%, against 85 to 100% without it.

MReaLLab.title: Foundation Model Driven Robotics: A Comprehensive Review
MReaLLab.authors_text: Muhammad Tayyab Khan, Ammar Waheed, Seung Ki Moon
MReaLLab.summary: This review explores the transformative impact of foundation models on robotics, highlighting advances, applications, challenges, and future research directions for integrating semantic reasoning with physical intelligence.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: The rapid emergence of foundation models, particularly large language models and vision-language models, has introduced a transformative paradigm in robotics. The models offer powerful capabilities in semantic understanding, high-level reasoning, and cross-modal generalization, enabling significant advances in perception, planning, control, and human-robot interaction. This critical review provides a structured synthesis of recent developments and organizes applications into four directions: simulation-driven robotics, open-world operation, sim-to-real transfer, and adaptable robotic systems. Unlike existing surveys that emphasize isolated capabilities, this work highlights integrated, system-level strategies and evaluates their practical feasibility in real-world environments. Key enabling trends such as procedural scene generation, policy generalization, and multimodal reasoning are discussed alongside core bottlenecks, including limited embodiment, lack of multimodal data, safety risks, and computational constraints. Through this lens, this paper identifies both the architectural strengths and critical limitations of foundation model-based robotics, highlighting open challenges in real-time operation, grounding, resilience, and trust. The review concludes with a roadmap of proposed future research directions for bridging semantic reasoning and physical intelligence through more robust, interpretable, and embodied models.

MReaLLab.title: LLM-to-Phy3D: Physically Conform Online 3D Object Generation with LLMs
MReaLLab.authors_text: Melvin Wong, Yueming Lyu, Thiago Rios, Stefan Menzel, Yew-Soon Ong
MReaLLab.summary: LLM-to-Phy3D enhances LLM-to-3D models by integrating physical constraints for real-time generation of viable 3D objects, improving design performance significantly.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized the landscape of digital content creation in different modalities. However, its potential use in Physical AI for engineering design, where the production of physically viable artifacts is paramount, remains vastly underexplored. The absence of physical knowledge in existing LLM-to-3D models often results in outputs detached from real-world physical constraints. To address this gap, we introduce LLM-to-Phy3D, a physically conform online 3D object generation that enables existing LLM-to-3D models to produce physically conforming 3D objects on the fly. LLM-to-Phy3D introduces a novel online black-box refinement loop that empowers large language models (LLMs) through synergistic visual and physics-based evaluations. By delivering directional feedback in an iterative refinement process, LLM-to-Phy3D actively drives the discovery of prompts that yield 3D artifacts with enhanced physical performance and greater geometric novelty relative to reference objects, marking a substantial contribution to AI-driven generative design. Systematic evaluations of LLM-to-Phy3D, supported by ablation studies in vehicle design optimization, reveal various LLM improvements gained by 4.5% to 106.7% in producing physically conform target domain 3D designs over conventional LLM-to-3D models. The encouraging results suggest the potential general use of LLM-to-Phy3D in Physical AI for scientific and engineering applications.

MReaLLab.title: NS-VLA: Towards Neuro-Symbolic Vision-Language-Action Models
MReaLLab.authors_text: Ziyue Zhu, Shangyang Wu, Shuai Zhao, Zhiqiu Zhao, Jian Zhang
MReaLLab.summary: The NS-VLA framework enhances Vision-Language-Action models by integrating neuro-symbolic methods for improved performance in long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models ground natural-language instructions in visual observations to generate actions for robotic manipulation. On long-horizon tasks, existing VLA models face structure-blind backbones, backbone-bound generalization, and flat single-objective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Neuro-Symbolic Vision-Language-Action (NS-VLA) framework. It introduces a Neuro-Symbolic Encoder that parses the instruction into a primitive plan tracked by a gated monotone stage pointer, a Neuro-Symbolic Solver that conditions a chunked VLA policy on the active sub-instruction, and Hierarchical Joint Policy Optimization, which fits the pointer on demonstration segments and refines the action policy with success-filtered online learning. Even when trained on few demonstrations, NS-VLA clearly leads on LIBERO and the held-out LIBERO-Plus (76.5% and 51.8% against 71.2% and 45.4% for its backbone), exceeds the strongest baseline by 12.7 points on long-horizon tasks, and raises real-robot success from 40.0% to 60.0%. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Zuzuzzy/NS-VLA.

MReaLLab.title: Emergent Vision-Shaped Thinking in Text-Only Reasoning through Multimodal Training
MReaLLab.authors_text: Qi Zhang, Bohan Wang, Qianru Sun, Hanwang Zhang
MReaLLab.summary: The study demonstrates that multimodal training influences text-only reasoning by integrating vision-based representations, revealing emergent vision-shaped thinking that affects spatial and symbolic tasks differently.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Does multimodal training shape how a language model thinks, even when the input is text only? We test this with targeted causal ablations across 10 multimodal configurations from 6 model families, with matched text-only backbones and cross-family transfer controls. We contrast spatial-imagery tasks that invite mental scene construction with symbol-manipulation tasks solvable by symbolic rules alone. We identify a vision-language axis in hidden-state space and ablate its projection at inference. In Chameleon-7B, this ablation drops accuracy on BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) navigate by 27.6 pp while leaving boolean expressions intact (+5.6 pp), a 33.2 pp double dissociation. The effect is direction-specific and layer-localized, extends to mental-simulation tasks such as mental rotation, paper folding, and perspective taking, and is not explained by task difficulty, reasoning depth, or sequential update load. Together, these results reveal emergent vision-shaped thinking (EVT): text-only reasoning that causally recruits representations introduced or strengthened by vision-language training, without assuming an image-like internal format. The measured effect is spatially concentrated at 7-8B and broadens to non-spatial visual attribute binding in the tested 32B configuration. In dual-path unified models (BAGEL, Janus-Pro), the causal handle localizes to the generation pathway as a compact one-dimensional carrier. The understanding pathway also encodes spatial information in a higher-rank, probe-decodable form, but is not the causal handle. To separate decodability from causal use, we analyze concentration, alignment, and semantic location. These diagnostics explain why behavior, probing, and intervention can diverge. Multimodal training thus reshapes the geometry of text-only reasoning, not just how visual input is processed.

MReaLLab.title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution
MReaLLab.authors_text: Haoran Luo, Shangkai Lin, Jinyang Wu, Xinliang Zhou, Luu Anh Tuan
MReaLLab.summary: HyperSkill introduces a training-free framework utilizing a hypergraph-indexed skill library to enhance reinforcement learning performance across multiple modalities without updating model parameters.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning sharpens LLM reasoning, but parameter updates are expensive, forgetful, and opaque; training-free libraries swap gradients for a textual store but still use trajectory-level, correlation-based admission and flat structure. To address both, we propose HyperSkill, a Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO framework that keeps the backbone frozen and replaces gradient updates with auditable edits to a Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library, where skills are advantage-bearing nodes and compositions are hyperedges. It has three components: training-time distillation admits counterfactually checked skills and learns a protocol skill from failures; gated hypergraph retrieval injects advantage-ranked skills where a per-dataset gate admits them; and an execution protocol makes the frozen backbone commit to an answer. On 11 text, vision-language, and omnimodal benchmarks, HyperSkill is best or tied on every dataset and beats the best baseline by 13.0 average F1 points while keeping the backbone frozen. Our software and data are publicly available at https://github.com/LHRLAB/HyperSkill.

MReaLLab.title: Track4D: Representing Dense 3D Tracking for Video Diffusion Models
MReaLLab.authors_text: Yushi Lan, Zeren Jiang, Kelvin Li, Xingang Pan, Chuanxia Zheng
MReaLLab.summary: Track4D repurposes video diffusion models for dense 3D tracking using two representations, achieving competitive zero-shot performance on multiple benchmarks.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: We study how to repurpose video diffusion models (VDMs), pretrained on millions of videos, for dense 3D point tracking, where training data is scarce. Doing so is non-trivial, as it requires representing 3D tracks as video-like signals that may lie outside the natural-video distribution on which the VDM was trained. We thus systematically assess the effectiveness of two such video representations. The first, Residual 3D Tracking Video (RTV), encodes per-pixel 3D offsets relative to a query frame and allows recovery of 3D trajectories directly from the generated video. The second, Normalized Coordinate Map Video (NCMV), labels each pixel with a canonical coordinate invariant through time. This is closer to a natural video and easier for the VDM to learn, but requires additional post-processing with an off-the-shelf 2D tracker to recover 3D tracks. RTV tracks more accurately, while NCMV shows that a VDM can generate dense correspondence as a video. We instantiate both representations with LoRA adaptation of a frozen Wan backbone, conditioned on point maps from an off-the-shelf 3D reconstructor as a geometric scaffold. Trained with a single dynamic 3D tracking dataset, Track4D achieves competitive zero-shot tracking on four real and synthetic benchmarks. A regression readout that bypasses the video VAE and uses additional training data brings further improvement, demonstrating the potential of this direction for dense 3D tracking.
