Extensive evaluations across diverse embodied agents reveal their consistent weaknesses in spatial understanding. Our findings highlight that these agents struggle to track identities after spatial changes and convert relational or geometric constraints into executable actions. We release the GeoMind benchmark at https://github.com/Notfound-JH/GEOMIND-benchmark.git.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: AutoVLA-D: Learn a Trajectory-Geometric Condition from Reasoning for Autonomous Driving VLA
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yuguang Yang, Zhewen Tan, Canyu Chen, Linlin Yang, Cheng Chi
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: AutoVLA-D enhances autonomous driving trajectory prediction by introducing a discrete trajectory-geometric condition, improving performance through a two-stage learning framework.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Autoregressive VLA planning usually predicts continuous trajectories as the final output, but driving instructions often describe actions rather than ego states, which weakens direct conditioning on the final continuous trajectory. We address this gap with TrajCond, which introduces a discrete trajectory-geometric condition for VLA planning. Specifically, we represent TrajCond as a 1D-Brohan differential action trajectory and learn it with a two-stage training framework before final continuous trajectory prediction. With the simultaneous autoregressive generation of discrete and numeric trajectories, we name our method AutoVLA-D (Double). Experiments on NAVSIM navtest, nuScenes, and NeuroNCAP show that discrete trajectories are weaker as direct outputs but more effective as TrajCond, consistently improving final continuous trajectory prediction across closed-loop and open-loop driving benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/ShivaTeam/AutoVLA-D.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: PFM-HR: Pose Flow Matching for Humanoid Robots
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yukang Gao, Yi Gu, Yangchen Zhou, Xingyu Chen, Zhaorui Wang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: PFM-HR enhances humanoid robot tracking by utilizing a Pose Geometry Score to align joint movements with unordered pose data, improving motion tracking performance.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Motion priors improve reinforcement learning for physics-based humanoid tracking, but temporal priors require ordered motion clips, while pose priors provide limited guidance for policy-induced pose transitions. We present Pose Flow Matching for Humanoid Robots (PFM-HR), a reusable flow matching prior trained directly on large scale unordered pose data. PFM-HR introduces the Pose Geometry Score (PGS), which quantifies how joint coordinate changes during rollouts align with the local geometry of pose variation captured by the prior. Using PGS to modulate the tracking reward guides policy exploration toward structured pose changes while keeping the prior frozen across tracking tasks. Experiments demonstrate that PFM-HR improves both single motion and general motion tracking, especially for highly dynamic motions.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Kinematic Hypothesis Context: Embodiment-Conditioned Learned Video Coding for Bandwidth-Limited Robot Policy Uplinks
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yuze Lu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper presents a kinematic hypothesis context that enhances video coding efficiency for bandwidth-limited robot uplinks, achieving significant bitrate savings and improved policy success rates.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Robots increasingly run large vision-language-action policies on remote servers, making the camera uplink the bottleneck. Existing video codecs spend bits on content the receiver could predict: the robot's own motion. We introduce the kinematic hypothesis context, a zero-rate conditioning signal that both ends build from joint states, the robot model and the camera calibration. Ego-motion homographies, per-link robot reprojections, an end-effector plane and a background memory warp the previous reconstruction into hypotheses that condition a learned video codec. We prove that history-only and global-pose conditioning with a limited receptive field cannot access this information under large motion, and that coding gains become task gains at the policy's success cliff. On LIBERO, the context saves 23.9% bit rate over a capacity-matched history-conditioned codec and 40-56% over x264, x265 and SVT-AV1, and needs 23.2% fewer bits than DCVC-RT at equal policy action deviation; trained to lower rates, it matches DCVC-RT in PSNR. In closed loop at equal rate, OpenVLA-OFT success nearly doubles from 22.8% to 43.1% at 6 kbps (72.6% with lower-rate training, 23.6 points above DCVC-RT), pi_0.5 success rises from 55.5% to 77.4%, and the gain grows under packet loss. The context transfers across three codec hosts and to real robot data.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: IMUDINO: Self-distilled Foundation Model for Inertial Sensing
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zhoutong Ye, Chengwen Zhang, Zixuan Wang, Xufeng Jian, Zhe He
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: IMUDINO is a versatile foundation model for inertial sensing that excels in various tasks by leveraging self-supervised learning and adaptable architecture.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: We present IMUDINO, the first foundation model (FM) for inertial sensing to achieve competitive performance across diverse sensing tasks including human activity recognition (HAR), health, motion capture, and odometry. Prior inertial FMs often focus on one subfield of inertial sensing and sometimes underperform state-of-the-art supervised methods (e.g., in HAR), making their scope considerably narrower than FMs for vision and natural language. Moreover, they often require fixed input length and sampling rate, and generalize poorly to unseen sensor locations. To build a general-purpose foundation model for inertial sensing, we adapt the DINO self-supervised learning (SSL) paradigm to inertial data through a set of semantics-preserving motion transformations that simulate variations in motion pattern and sensor setup. For model architecture, we use a plain transformer encoder with frequency-aware positional encoding that natively supports varying input length and sampling rate. This simple setup proved remarkably effective for learning global and dense features generalizable across users, sensor setups, tasks, and, in the case of robot odometry, embodiments. We hope IMUDINO can serve as a backbone for inertial sensing and kickstart the development of general-purpose inertial FMs.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Teach the Way It Thinks: Guiding LLM Post-training Data Engineering with Sparse Autoencoders
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yi Jing, Zao Dai, Jinwu Hu, Zijun Yao, Lei Hou
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper introduces SAERL, a method using Sparse Autoencoders to enhance LLM reinforcement learning data engineering by leveraging model internals for improved training efficiency and accuracy.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Data engineering for large language model (LLM) reinforcement learning (RL) decides which samples to train on, when to present them, and which to batch together. Existing methods mostly rely on external feedback, such as pass rates or difficulty labels, which observes only the outcome on each sample. We argue that model internals offer richer and more model-intrinsic feedback that can guide all three decisions. We propose SAERL which organizes RL training data in the feature space of Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), a mechanistic interpretability tool that decomposes model internals into sparse, interpretable features. SAE features let us view the model as a set of functional regions, each formed by features that related samples activate together. For each sample, its SAE activations indicate which regions it engages, and its gradients projected onto SAE features indicate how training on it would change these regions. Guided by this view, SAERL keeps samples with strong and non-redundant gradient signals, trains each functional region from easy to hard, and trains one functional region at a time, drawing each batch from a single activation cluster with moderate cross-cluster mixing. The resulting curriculum is constructed once with small models and transfers to larger ones. Experiments on mathematical reasoning show consistent gains across model scales and RL algorithms. For instance, on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, SAERL improves the average accuracy of GRPO by 3.1% and reaches the target accuracy with 42% fewer training steps. Further analyses reveal that ordering and batching are complementary. These results demonstrate that model internals are a powerful and practical foundation for post-training data engineering.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Fuhao Li, Wenxuan Song, Qizhou Huang, Ziyang Zhou, Jingbo Wang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The SLA model enhances robotic manipulation by integrating continual pre-training for spatial understanding, optimizing action prediction, and utilizing diverse datasets for improved 3D spatial alignment.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes. To accommodate this diversity, we introduce feature-dependent gates that adaptively aggregate visual embeddings from multiple VLA layers for spatial supervision. The teacher further exploits partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB observations, enabling effective use of heterogeneous geometric annotations. Probabilistic state dropout encourages reliance on visual cues and mitigates overfitting to demonstration trajectories. All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Resource-Efficient Reinforcement Learning Post-Training through Elastic Expert Parallelism
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Jia Wei, Ziyi Qiu, Yi Xu, Xuehai Qian
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: FlexFloor enhances resource efficiency in reinforcement learning post-training by optimizing worker scheduling and response batching, significantly increasing throughput and response generation without sacrificing performance.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning post-training improves the capabilities of large language models, but generating training responses is a major computational bottleneck. In mixture-of-experts models, workers that finish their assigned responses may remain occupied because their experts are still needed by workers processing longer responses. Consequently, approximately one-third of occupied worker time in the baseline occurs after local response generation finishes. Here we present FlexFloor, a system that enables earlier resource release during synchronous response generation while preserving the expert computation required by ongoing responses. FlexFloor jointly adapts response scheduling and the active group of workers. It uses historical response lengths and memory constraints to guide batching and prompt placement, then progressively releases workers while maintaining expert availability and correct communication. Compared with the verl baseline, FlexFloor generates approximately 65.40% more response tokens per unit of occupied computing time and increases response generation throughput by 52.74%, with little observed variation in rollout reward. By making reinforcement learning post-training more efficient, FlexFloor supports faster development and iterative improvement of large language models and AI agents.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: WoVR: World Models as Reliable Simulators for Post-Training VLA Policies with RL
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zhennan Jiang, Shangqing Zhou, Yutong Jiang, Zefang Huang, Mingjie Wei
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: WoVR introduces a robust framework for using world models in reinforcement learning, enhancing policy optimization and stability in Vision-Language-Action models despite imperfect dynamics.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) promises to unlock capabilities beyond imitation learning for Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models, but its requirement for massive real-world interaction prevents direct deployment on physical robots. Recent work attempts to use learned world models as simulators for policy optimization, yet closed-loop imagined rollouts inevitably suffer from hallucination and long-horizon error accumulation. Such errors not only degrade visual fidelity, but also mislead policy optimization by providing unreliable learning signals. We propose WoVR, a reliable world-model-based RL framework for post-training VLA policies. Instead of assuming a faithful world model, WoVR explicitly regulates how RL interacts with imperfect imagined dynamics. It improves rollout stability through a controllable action-conditioned video world model, reshapes imagined interaction to reduce effective error depth via Keyframe-Initialized Rollouts, and maintains policy--simulator alignment through World Model-Policy co-evolution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that WoVR enables stable long-horizon imagined rollouts and effective policy optimization, achieving superior LIBERO performance and consistent real-world gains across multiple robotic platforms. These results show that world models can serve as practical simulators for RL when hallucination is explicitly controlled. Additional visualization results are available at https://wovr-rlinf.github.io.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: OmniOPSD: Rationale-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation for Affective Computing
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zebang Cheng, Shuimu Chen, Boxue Yang, Yuanshen Guan, Jingyi Chen
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: OmniOPSD introduces a novel on-policy self-distillation framework for multimodal affective reasoning, enhancing generalization through evidence-rich supervision without requiring additional human annotations.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced affective computing by enabling nuanced reasoning over visual, acoustic, and linguistic evidence. A key approach to improving their generalization is outcome-based reinforcement learning, which converts existing label-level annotations into rewards for final-answer correctness. However, its sparse sequence-level supervision provides limited fine-grained guidance for interpreting multimodal affective cues and may reward correct labels even when those cues are misinterpreted. To address this challenge, we introduce OmniOPSD, the first on-policy self-distillation framework for omni-modal affective reasoning. At its core, OmniOPSD transforms label-level supervision into evidence-rich, teacher-only rationales by leveraging reference affective judgments as semantic priors for offline multimodal evidence elicitation from frontier MLLMs. Through rationale-privileged self-distillation, it couples on-policy student rollouts with dense, evidence-informed token-level supervision from a local self-teacher, allowing the student to learn along its own trajectories rather than imitate fixed reasoning traces. This decoupling of offline evidence acquisition from local policy learning enables training without additional human annotation, frontier-model logits, or online frontier-model calls, while preserving student-only inference from the original task input. At both 3B and 7B scales, OmniOPSD outperforms supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and group relative policy optimization (GRPO) in mean macro-F1 on both in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations. Among the compared models, it ranks first by MER-UniBench mean across all three input-modality settings, reaching 84.13 with audio--video--text input, and achieves the highest MME-Emotion recognition score (Rec-S) of 42.4.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: TailorRig: Controllable and Structured Auxiliary Skeleton Generation for Garment-Aware Rigging
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yajing Chen, Xin Chen, Saidan Lu, Yeqi Yuan, Weikai Chen
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: TailorRig introduces a controllable framework for garment-aware humanoid rigging, enhancing artist-driven design and improving skeleton accuracy and deformation stability over existing methods.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Humanoid rigging for modern characters with complex garments remains challenging due to the need for dense auxiliary skeletons and precise skinning control. Existing automatic methods primarily recover rigs from geometry, providing limited artist control over auxiliary articulation and often lacking explicit semantic or kinematic-chain structure for dense garment bones, leading to instability and weight bleeding. We present TailorRig, a framework that reformulates garment-aware humanoid rigging as a structured, controllable full-rig generation problem. This formulation shifts the goal from automatic rig recovery to artist-driven rig authoring, where both body-template compatibility and auxiliary articulation are explicit design choices. TailorRig exposes two explicit axes of artist control within a unified framework: a user-specified body skeleton template that preserves body-rig compatibility, and artist-provided semantic labels that drive an autoregressive generator to synthesize requested category-specific auxiliary bone chains. To robustly assign skinning weights under dense skeletal configurations, we further introduce a hierarchical chain-to-bone formulation: vertices are first associated to a kinematic chain, and bone weights are then refined within that chain, reducing weight bleeding between spatially adjacent but semantically unrelated structures. We evaluate TailorRig on a diverse set of characters and introduce Human-Mix, a large-scale dataset of over 38,000 humanoid models curated for garment-aware rigging. Experiments show that TailorRig improves skeleton accuracy, deformation stability, controllability, and practical usability over existing methods. Project page: https://xxxx0601.github.io/trig/ ; code: https://github.com/Tencent/TailorRig ; dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/tencent/TailorRig

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: HITCH: Teaching a Vision-Language Model to Operate a Humanoid through a Whole-Body Harness
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Qingzhou Lu, Chenxin Liu, Xinming Wang, Liu Cao, Yanjiang Guo
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: HITCH enables vision-language models to effectively control humanoid robots through a whole-body harness, enhancing task success via accurate perception and execution of commands.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Enabling vision-language models (VLMs) to control humanoid robots requires both reliable whole-body interfaces and knowledge of how to use the body that carries over across tasks. We present HITCH (Harness Interfaces To Command Humanoids), a harness in which perception returns the 3D position of any point the VLM selects in its image, and execution turns commands for the pelvis, torso, hands, walking, and gaze into whole-body motion with a learned tracker. We find that both measuring the scene and executing commands accurately raise task success. We then fine-tune a VLM on trajectories in which teacher policies solve five base tasks through HITCH, so that it learns how to operate the humanoid. Without task-specific trajectories, the fine-tuned model completes 51% of SIMPLE episodes and 42.5% of HumanoidArena episodes, and adding five trajectories per SIMPLE task raises its SIMPLE success to 95%. On a real G1, it carries a box and walks to a goal without real training data.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zuo Gou, Chenhao Lu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper proposes a wire protocol for detecting silent faults at the environment-trainer boundary in reinforcement learning, demonstrating effective fault identification through step ledgers and episode records.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Robot reinforcement learning increasingly runs environments outside the trainer: in another process, on another machine, in another language. Many faults at this boundary raise no error. We make the boundary a wire protocol and ask what notices a fault in it. On Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and a 7-joint arm (Pusher), we injected up to 23 faults into what crosses the wire and 2 into the trainer's log, from one value to every value. Unless every value was wrong, a learning-curve threshold caught at most one run in ten, and a comparison with ten fault-free seeds at most 21%. A clean evaluation of all 1,060 final policies agreed with the curves: of the 728 boundary-fault runs both curve checks passed, 723 scored no more than three standard deviations below fault-free seeds, though nearly all ended on other weights and, for reward faults, logged other returns. Checks of the run itself, not of its outcome, saw every fault. A step ledger kept on both sides and compared step by step caught and located every fault that crossed, on Pendulum, Hopper and Pusher on one machine and on Pendulum across two, with no fault-free run and, on Pendulum, a median 3% more training time. An episode record kept at the environment caught the faults in the trainer's log. We list such faults found in practice, in Gymnasium 1.3 and our own code and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries, and recommend a step ledger and episode counts kept at the environment.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: MASBench: Benchmarking LLM-based Multi-Agent Collaboration under Partial Observability
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Qizhi Chu, Zekai Yu, Sijie Wen, Yang Liu, Chen Qian
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: MASBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM-based multi-agent collaboration under partial observability, featuring structured tasks and metrics to assess collaboration mechanisms.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have progressively evolved into the core of autonomous agents. Building on this progress, LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) coordinate multiple agents into a synergistic team to accomplish complex tasks that exceed the capabilities of individual agents. The effectiveness of such systems depends not only on the agents themselves, but also on how collaboration mechanisms are designed and organized. Note that real-world collaboration is typically partially observable, where each agent can only access partial information about the environment due to physical or privacy-related constraints. However, many existing multi-agent benchmarks assume global observability, and leave limited support for systematically evaluating collaboration mechanisms. To bridge this gap, we introduce MASBench, a multi-agent collaboration benchmark designed under partially observable constraints. It is organized into three progressive task categories: Reasoning, Scheduling, and Game. Through this structure, we progressively evaluate three representative collaboration mechanisms: Protocol, Memory, and Routing. MASBench further provides deterministic evaluation metrics, including performance score, communication cost, and cost effectiveness, to characterize both collaboration outcomes and communication overhead. Experiments across diverse LLM backbones and mechanism configurations offer empirical guidance for effective MAS design. Code is available at: https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/MASBench

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding?
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Peiran Wu, Fangfei Gou, Zhaoxi Mu, Changhao Zhang, Jian Liu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: SleuthVLM demonstrates superior video understanding by utilizing transcribed audio instead of direct audio input, achieving higher accuracy than existing models and emphasizing the importance of agentic ability.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Omni models answer questions about videos by jointly processing sampled frames and audio in one turn, with progress driven largely by scaling model size and omni training data. We ask whether a model needs to hear the audio directly at all, and present SleuthVLM, an agent harness built on a VLM that never hears the audio directly: speech will be transcribed into text, and the VLM will sleuth the video on its own without any predefined workflow. On four omni benchmarks with videos up to 90 minutes, SleuthVLM achieves the best average accuracy: \textbf{75.0%}, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash, and it also tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard with \textbf{77.8%}; with an open-source 27B VLM, it beats all open-source omni models. We draw three findings: SleuthVLM beats a model that glances; hearing is not the bottleneck, agentic ability is; omni understanding needs better agentic ability, not just more omni data for modality alignment. So we provide a simple but effective starting point for doing omni video understanding. Omni understanding needs better agents, not just bigger models that hear.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ModalSearcher: Weaving Visual Evidence into Autonomous Cross-Modal Deep Search
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zhihan Yin, Ruyi Li, Chengyu Fang, Yifeng Yao, Nonghai Zhang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: ModalSearcher enhances multimodal large language models by enabling autonomous cross-modal search, integrating visual evidence dynamically, and achieving significant accuracy improvements in knowledge-intensive tasks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Static and incomplete parametric knowledge limits the performance of multimodal large language models on novel-knowledge and knowledge-intensive tasks, especially those requiring multi-hop evidence acquisition. Existing multimodal agentic search methods often fix visual evidence at the input or a predefined trajectory position, making it difficult for agents to select search modalities as their information needs evolve and to handle complex real-world queries. We define this capability as autonomous cross-modal search: an agent chooses among direct reasoning, text-to-text search, text-to-image search, and reverse-image search, actively introduces visual evidence when appropriate, and switches between and integrates modalities across multiple hops. We propose ModalSearch-Pipeline, a scalable procedure for constructing an interleaved multimodal knowledge graph. It samples paths with diverse depths and modality compositions and uses backward question construction to obscure entity names and image targets that would expose reasoning shortcuts while retaining necessary disambiguating clues, yielding text-only, image-initialized, and arbitrarily interleaved multi-hop problems. We train the ModalSearcher Agent with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning in a live Web environment, and construct ModalSearch-Bench. Experiments show that ModalSearcher-8B improves average accuracy by 16.2 points over Qwen3-VL-8B under the same agentic workflow across five multimodal knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks, with consistent gains on independently constructed active visual-search benchmarks.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yuetong Liu, Zhehao Zhou, Yitong Zhang, Haorui Chen, Jia Li
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: Coca-Cola introduces a continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents, significantly reducing token consumption and runtime while enhancing task performance through action-preserving training.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent's attention to task-relevant information. Existing token pruning and summarization methods remain constrained by discrete text representations, limiting the achievable compression ratios. In this work, we challenge the prevailing assumption that agents must consume tool observations as explicit text tokens. To this end, we propose Coca-Cola, a continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents. Coca-Cola compresses tool observations into latent tokens and embeds them into the input embedding space of the agent. We further introduce Action-Preserving Training, which aligns the agent's next-action distributions under full and compressed observations. This trains the compression model to learn action-sufficient latent tokens that retain decision-critical information. Experiments with web-search agents on four QA benchmarks and two model families show that Coca-Cola reduces the agent's token consumption by 70.01%-89.24% and end-to-end runtime by 24.45%-55.97%, while consistently improving task performance. These results suggest that Coca-Cola offers a promising approach for context compression in agents. Our code is available at https://github.com/THU-Agent/Coca-cola.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Compression Forcing: Hierarchical History Tokenization Enables Flexible World Models
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Siqiao Huang, Partha Kaushik, Michael Chen, Hengkai Pan, Kaiwen Geng
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper introduces Compression Forcing, a framework that enhances world modeling by aligning history compression with predictive objectives through Dynamics-Aware Tokenization and Hierarchical History Guidance.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Effective world modeling requires compressing salient history information that facilitates future prediction. However, most existing approaches inherit tokenization and conditioning mechanisms from video generation, where objectives are centered around perceptual realism rather than predictive utility. This discrepancy limits the world model's effectiveness, especially in environments dominated by visual nuisances or task-irrelevant background details. To this end, we introduce Compression Forcing (CF), a general framework that aligns history compression with the predictive objective of world modeling. Compression Forcing features Dynamics-Aware Tokenization (DAT), a novel tokenization method that compresses history observations into a sequence ordered by decreasing dynamics saliency. Built on a diffusion backbone, this structure enables Hierarchical History Guidance (HG-H), allowing selective amplification of dynamics-salient information during inference. Extensive experiments across various environments demonstrate improved prediction fidelity, physical realism, and downstream decision-making performance, establishing Compression Forcing as a highly flexible and effective approach for world modeling.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ReflexArc: Bottom-Up Integration of Instantaneous Tactile Reflexes into Whole-Body Humanoid Control
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Mingyu Wang, Si Li, Ziqing Chen, He Wang, Li Yi
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The ReflexArc framework integrates instantaneous tactile reflexes into humanoid robot control, significantly enhancing responsiveness and safety in hazardous contact situations.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Humanoid robots operating in cluttered environments must react to unexpected contacts before the first impact peak, which arrives within tens of milliseconds. Learned whole-body policies running at 50 Hz introduce a policy-cycle delay and may suppress a protective withdrawal as a tracking error. To address these challenges, we propose ARC (Ascending Reflex Control), a bottom-up framework that integrates instantaneous tactile reflexes with learned whole-body control. ARC consists of two components: an instantaneous reflex pathway and bottom-up reflex integration. The reflex pathway detects hazardous contacts from full-body tactile sensing, solves a whole-body withdrawal pose, and delivers it directly to the motors within 10 ms. Bottom-up reflex integration combines reflex-in-the-loop policy learning, reflex-transparent policy alignment, and reflex-informed policy adaptation to sustain the withdrawal, maintain balance, and complete longer-horizon recovery. We deploy ARC on a Unitree G1 and evaluate three categories of hazardous contact. Compared with an otherwise identical reflex delayed by 20 ms, ARC reduces the first force peak by 34.1% and reduces the contact impulse from 0.2632 N s to 0.1225 N s (a 2.15x ratio). We further demonstrate protected motion tracking, teleoperation, and vision-free obstacle traversal guided by foot tactile sensing. Project page: https://minusmodulo.github.io/reflexarc-website/

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy for Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Mingcong Li, Yihan Zhou, Jiayu Qu, Xueyang Guo, Yilin Mo
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy (SR-DP) enhances multi-task robotic manipulation by improving visual encoding and reducing interference, achieving superior success rates compared to existing methods.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Diffusion-based policies have achieved strong performance on single-task robotic manipulation. However, a single model trained jointly on multiple tasks consistently underperforms the per-task specialists trained on the same demonstrations. We focus on two challenges. First, the convolutional encoders commonly used in diffusion-based policies produce visual conditions that are not discriminative enough. Second, gradients from incompatible action modes update the shared denoiser's dense parameters along the same directions, causing destructive interference during joint training. To address both, we propose SR-DP (Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy). A frozen VGGT encoder with a spatial-compression adapter produces compact multi-scale semantic-geometric tokens, a task-discriminative visual condition for tasks that share a workspace. We first train the denoiser as a standard diffusion policy, then decompose selected linear layers by SVD into a frozen basis of orthogonal rank-one experts, adapted through spectral routing and Householder input rotations. On six RoboTwin tasks, SR-DP averages a 68.4% success rate, surpassing multi-task VO-DP by 21.8 points and the strongest per-task baseline by 3.8 points. On four real-world bimanual tasks, Stage 2 reaches a 43.0% average success rate and improves over Stage 1 by 19.0 points.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Beyond Local Refinement: Wide-Area Precise Cross-View Localization
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Qingguo Hu, Xinyu Ma, Yujie Lin, Yaoxiang Wang, Qi Shi
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper presents RingMatch, a framework for precise cross-view localization over large areas, addressing challenges of spatial disparity and visual ambiguity using predictive uncertainty and a novel depth ring representation.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Fine-grained cross-view localization aims to precisely localize a ground camera against geo-referenced aerial imagery, but current methods typically assume a narrow geographic prior, substantially limiting their applicability when upstream localization remains coarse. To bridge this gap, we study this task over much larger aerial regions. However, this seemingly simple extension fundamentally changes the localization problem: the growing disparity in spatial extent between ground and aerial views makes reliable cross-view matching difficult to establish directly, while the increasing number of look-alike locations in larger regions introduces substantial visual ambiguity. To address these challenges, we propose RingMatch, a search-and-verification framework for wide-area cross-view localization. RingMatch first leverages predictive uncertainty to uncover plausible locations and progressively zooms into their surroundings to obtain increasingly fine-grained evidence, yielding a compact set of promising candidates. We then introduce the depth ring, a novel geometric representation that reveals subtle variations in the spatial layout around a location and serves as a view-shared spatial signature for an LVLM verifier to resolve residual ambiguity. To benchmark this setting, we construct VIGOR-Pro by composing VIGOR aerial tiles into contiguous regions with spatial extents of up to 400 m. Experiments show that RingMatch maintains strong localization performance as the aerial region expands, consistently outperforming representative end-to-end and retrieval-based methods.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ReSI-Math: Exploring Recoverable Capability Frontiers for Efficient Reasoning Improvement
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yao Cui, Zhen Yang, Yuandong Wang, Yangfu Zhu, Tianyu Wo
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: ReSI-Math enhances mathematical reasoning in language models by exploring recoverable capability frontiers through trajectory-level search and adaptive reinforcement learning, improving problem-solving efficiency.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an effective approach for improving mathematical reasoning in large language models. However, a fundamental question remains: when a model fails to solve a problem, does it truly lack the underlying capability? In this work, we reveal that direct failure does not necessarily imply inability. Some reasoning failures can be recovered by exploring the model's own trajectories, exposing a recoverable capability frontier: a policy-dependent region where solutions are not reliably generated through direct decoding but can be elicited through trajectory-level search. Based on this observation, we introduce ReSI-Math, a framework that explores recoverable capability frontiers and converts recovered capabilities into data-efficient RLVR supervision. ReSI-Math uses Self-Judge-guided evolutionary search to identify recoverable failures under a fixed policy and adaptively selects frontier problems for sequential RLVR as the policy evolves. On Qwen3-VL-8B, correct-incorrect trajectory crossover produces 272 verifier-confirmed correct offspring from 621 attempts (43.8%). After three sequential one-shot RLVR stages, the MATH500 and WE-MATH average improves from 78.71 to 80.16. Under matched single-problem RLVR, random selection reaches only 53.31 versus 54.16 for frontier-guided Q1.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: ZhengXian Wu, Qianhao Nie, Zhuohong Chen, Junjie Gao, Yuyao Zhang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: VisSearch-Bench evaluates multimodal agents' long-horizon visual search capabilities across diverse tasks, revealing significant challenges in linking visual evidence to search outcomes.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Multimodal agents use web and image tools to answer questions beyond their internal knowledge. Some search tasks use images mainly to identify an initial entity, then rely on text retrieval. These tasks offer limited insight into how agents connect information across images, objects, and search steps. We therefore focus on visual context management. This involves organizing and using visual information and linking it to other findings during search. Visually intensive tasks require agents to combine object appearance, local details, or spatial relations with external information. We introduce VisSearch-Bench, with 204 human-written tasks across 7 main domains and 25 subdomains. It covers Set-wise Visual Search, Sequential Visual Search, Hybrid Wide-Deep Search, Competitive Visual Disambiguation, and Visual-Structure-Guided Search. Each task provides a reference answer, traceable evidence, and scoring rules. Accuracy measures complete task success, while Process Score measures the correctness and completeness of individual results and subquestion answers. Across 16 multimodal models, the best system fully solves only 26.47% of tasks, even with search tools. These results highlight the challenge of linking visual evidence with search results to produce complete answers.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: HiLo-WAM: Decoupling Long-Horizon Task Evolution and Local Dynamics in World Action Models
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xingyu Wang, Yanjiang Guo, Zhijing Ding, Jiaxin Fang, Zeyu Lai
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: HiLo-WAM enhances robotic manipulation by decoupling long-horizon task evolution from local dynamics, achieving high success rates and efficiency through a dual-DiT architecture.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) improve robotic manipulation by jointly modeling visual dynamics and robot actions. However, most existing WAMs model dense short-horizon visual dynamics, capturing local interactions but providing limited long-range task context. Extending prediction horizons increases uncertainty and computation while entangling task-level evolution with fine-grained local dynamics, obscuring their dependencies and distinct roles in action generation. We propose HiLo-WAM, which decouples long-horizon task evolution from local visual dynamics while jointly modeling their interaction with robot actions. A sparse long-horizon visual stream captures historical task context and future evolution, while a dense local dynamics visual stream models short-horizon robot-object interactions. The two streams operate at different temporal scales within a unified dual-DiT architecture and guide actions through structured cross-stream attention. Progressive inference further reduces unnecessary computation through stream-wise partial denoising, joint denoising, and dynamic skipping. Experiments demonstrate strong long-horizon manipulation performance: HiLo-WAM achieves a 93.70% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 and a 17.43 progress score on RoboDojo long-horizon tasks, with robust in-domain and OOD performance on the Fourier GR-3 robot. Ablations confirm the complementary contributions of long-horizon task evolution and local interaction dynamics, while temporal-scale analyses highlight the importance of balancing temporal coverage and resolution. Progressive inference further achieves a 2.93x speedup while improving performance.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Jiarui Yuan, Yuxin Zuo, Xiaoyu Huang, Wenbo Zhang, Kwanyoung Park
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper presents uni-robot-agent, a unified framework for open-weight Robot-use Agents that enhances zero-shot manipulation and supports further training, outperforming existing models.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Robot-use Agents (RUAs) have shown promising zero-shot manipulation capabilities, but reliance on frontier, proprietary models limits research into further training. To democratize RUA research, we introduce uni-robot-agent, a unified harness for competitive open-weight robot use that supports further training. Without privileged inputs, an out-of-the-box Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves a RoboDojo Score of 31.39, surpassing the published GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe result of 28.97 and many VLA/WAM baselines, and performs competitively on 19 real-world tasks. Our analysis across model generations, families, and sizes links effective robot use to four general capabilities, suggesting that future RUA training should develop them jointly.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: DexArena: A Unified Benchmark for Long-Horizon Dexterous Manipulation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Haonan Ping, Jianshu Hu, Yimin Wang, Yi Zhu, Pai Liang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: DexArena is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating long-horizon bimanual dexterous manipulation in robots, featuring diverse tasks and standardized testing protocols to enhance learning and generalization.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Long-horizon dexterous manipulation remains a fundamental challenge for robot learning, requiring the composition of multiple skills, precise bimanual coordination, generalizable visual understanding, and robust skill transitions. Yet existing manipulation benchmarks largely emphasize isolated skills or support only a limited range of end-effectors, making these capabilities difficult to evaluate systematically. We introduce DexArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate learning and generalization in long-horizon bimanual dexterous manipulation. DexArena features 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level tasks spanning diverse household and industrial scenarios. Each long-horizon task is composed of explicitly defined stages with physically grounded success conditions, enabling reliable evaluation of both intermediate progress and end-to-end task completion. A unified benchmark interface and verified human-teleoperated demonstrations enable testing different policy learning algorithms, with standardized simulation configurations, scene randomization, trajectory replay, and task-level evaluation. Through extensive baseline experiments, we identify substantial challenges in precise manipulation, generalization to scene variation, and skill composition. DexArena establishes a challenging and reproducible benchmark for developing robot learning methods that move toward generalizable long-horizon dexterous behavior.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ReconDreamer#: Self-Evolving Closed-Loop Synergy of Reconstruction and Generation for Dynamic Driving Scenes
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Songling Liu, Guosheng Zhao, Xiaofeng Wang, Chaojun Ni, Guan Huang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: ReconDreamer# is a self-evolving framework that enhances dynamic driving scene reconstruction by iteratively refining generative and reconstruction models, improving fidelity against real-world data.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Dynamic driving scene reconstruction has made remarkable strides in recent years by leveraging generative priors, particularly in the quality of novel trajectory rendering. Nevertheless, a significant gap remains between the generated data and real-world sensor observations, severely hindering further improvements in reconstruction fidelity. In this paper, we present ReconDreamer#, a self-evolving framework that synergizes reconstruction and generation for dynamic driving scenes, which substantially bridges the gap between synthesized novel trajectory data and recorded real-world observations. Within this self-evolving closed-loop framework, the generative and reconstruction models mutually reinforce each other through iterative refinement, ultimately yielding a significant enhancement in the 3D representation capability of the reconstruction model. Additionally, we introduce a geometry-prior-based adaptive ground model to further enhance the rendering quality of the reconstruction model. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conduct comprehensive evaluations on Waymo, nuScenes, PandaSet, and EUVS benchmarks. Specifically on Waymo, at a 6-m lateral shift, ReconDreamer# improves NTA-IoU and NTL-IoU by 8.8% and 3.0%, respectively, and reduces FID by 15.1% relative to ReconDreamer++.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: LLM4Robot-Bench: How Far Can GPT-6 Astra Go in Robotic Manipulation? A Hierarchical, Paired Sim-Real Benchmark
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Haibao Yu, Jiaqi Meng, Zijian Zhang, Bowen Jing, Lei Yang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The LLM4Robot-Bench evaluates GPT-6 Astra's robotic manipulation across 16 tasks, revealing significant performance declines with increasing interaction complexity in both simulated and real environments.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: We introduce LLM4Robot-Bench, a hierarchical, paired Sim-Real benchmark for evaluating physical interaction capabilities in contact-rich manipulation. Its 16 household tasks span three cumulative levels: contact selection and geometric alignment (L1), force regulation within sustained contact (L2), and coordinated contact reconfiguration and force regulation (L3). Each task is instantiated in physically and visually matched simulated and real-world environments, with shared task definitions and success criteria. We evaluate GPT-6 Astra zero-shot with three trials per task in each environment. Real-world success rates decline from 80.0% at L1 to 47.6% at L2 and 0.0% at L3, with corresponding simulation rates of 66.7%, 47.6%, and 0.0%. Ten of the 16 tasks have identical success counts across environments; the remaining six differ by one success out of three trials. Across both environments, recurring difficulties in spatial reasoning, contact selection, force regulation, and coordination often prevent local physical progress from accumulating into task completion. These findings characterize Astra's observed capability boundary across increasing interaction demands and, for this model, support matched simulation as a repeatable, scalable testbed for studying the sustained, coordinated physical interactions that limit reliable manipulation.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: HTCE: Homeomorphism-inspired Topological Cross-Scene Experience Canonicalization and Reuse for Object Navigation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xiaoran Xu, Yupeng Wu, Tianyu Xue, Xuanran Dong, Yifan Xu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: HTCE introduces a topological framework for canonicalizing and reusing object navigation experiences in residential environments, enhancing retrieval efficiency and performance across varying scene representations.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: As embodied agents perform object-goal navigation across residential environments, they accumulate successful experiences whose semantic structure recurs across scenes even when geometric trajectories do not. Reusing such experience is challenging because differences in region naming and observation granularity produce distinct graph representations of similar approaches, while meaningful differences in anchors, branches, and endpoints must stay distinguishable. We introduce HTCE, a homeomorphism-inspired topological framework that canonicalizes and reuses navigation experience. Feature and topology subdivisions characterize representational variations, and their semantically constrained reductions produce comparable semantic sequences and structural signatures while preserving semantic anchors, branching relations, and navigation endpoints. HTCE then retrieves historical successful approaches through subdivision-aware matching as guidance for a frozen vision-language policy. Canonicalization compresses the experience index losslessly, merging 17.7--23.6\% of distinct stored route descriptions while retaining full task performance. Under a single frozen vision-language backbone shared by all compared systems, HTCE attains the best SR and SPL in every setting---59.9\%/31.8\% on HM3D v0.1, 71.0\%/31.5\% on HM3D v0.2, and 46.6\%/16.6\% on MP3D---with SR gains of up to 4.9 points and structured retrieval contributing up to 2.8 SPL points. The code is available in https://github.com/startracker0/htce.git

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Spotter: Let the Embodied Model Lead, and the VLM Reflect for It
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Long Li, Qichao Zhao, Yue Yang, Fan Xu, Zhe Wang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The Spotter framework enhances embodied models by allowing them to lead while a vision-language model monitors and corrects errors, significantly improving performance and efficiency.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Current embodied models do not respond to their own failures, although what just went wrong could inform a small adjustment on the next attempt, the kind of reflection behind the gains of thinking in language models. We test whether they can repair a known error, which requires producing a correction and judging whether it is right. Stopped at a failure and allowed to retry, they seldom repair it through their own randomness or from a language description of the error, and best-of-N selection cannot pick the successful candidate after a failure. We attribute this to training only on successful demonstrations and to inputs too narrow to show what went wrong, and conclude that reflection must come from a vision-language model (VLM), which takes in far more information, such as the episode history and text, and is more general. Prior VLM-led work has the VLM plan every step and invoke the embodied model as a tool, placing the VLM on the critical path. We propose Spotter, which reverses the roles: the embodied model leads and executes continuously, while the VLM runs in parallel, monitors through a lightweight local screener, intervenes only when an error is detected, reflects on and corrects it, and returns control. We run Spotter with Qwen and with GPT as the VLM, and both improve the embodied models; with GPT, Spotter improves Cosmos Policy and $π_{0.5}$ by 5.6 and 7.5 percentage points on RoboCasa, and raises $π_{0.5}$ from 47.2% to 57.0% on the Hard setting of RoboTwin 2.0 and from 53% to 83% on a real robot. Because the VLM steps in only when an error is confirmed, a successful episode with Qwen takes only 13 to 16 s longer than with the embodied model alone and about 70% less time than with a VLM-led baseline using the same model. Our code is available at https://github.com/zqc3117/Spotter.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: A New Formulation of the Elastica Model with Application to Image Inpainting
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zuoqiang Shi, Xue-Cheng Tai
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: This paper introduces a new elastica model formulation using binary curves for efficient image inpainting, leveraging FFT and split Bregman iteration for optimization.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Curves and interfaces play a central role in computer vision and image processing, and Euler's elastica energy is one of the most successful tools to model and manipulate them. The elastica energy is usually computed through a level-set or a phase field representation of the curve, in which the curvature term makes the energy nonlinear, non-convex and, in the level-set case, non-differentiable, so that its minimization is notoriously difficult. In this paper, we propose a new formulation of the elastica model based on a binary representation of curves. The key ingredient is a very simple formula for the curvature: if $ϕ$ is the $\pm1$ binary function associated with a curve $Γ$, then along $Γ$ the curvature is given by $-\frac{1}{C_0ε}\left(R_ε*ϕ\right)+O(ε)$, where $R_ε$ is a radial kernel supported in a ball of radius $ε$ and $C_0$ is an explicit constant. No derivative of $ϕ$ is involved and the convolution is evaluated by FFT. The resulting energy is a weighted total variation, so that formally the new formulation is a generalization of the well-known ROF model; a phase field type model is obtained from the same curvature formula. Combining FFT with the split Bregman iteration, which for the present problem coincides with an augmented Lagrangian method (ALM), we obtain efficient algorithms whose subproblems are either linear systems solved by conjugate gradient or explicit pointwise formulas. Numerical experiments on the inpainting of binary images are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: RoboSnap: One-Shot Real-to-Sim Scene Generation for Generalizable Robot Learning and Evaluation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Shujie Zhang, Jingkun Yi, Weipeng Zhong, Zirui Zhou, Yangkun Zhu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: RoboSnap enables efficient one-shot generation of simulation-ready scenes from real images, enhancing robot learning and evaluation through a layered design for stability and visual fidelity.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Recovering real-world scenes as interactive simulation environments can enable generalizable robot learning and reproducible policy evaluation. However, constructing scenes that are both physically stable and visually faithful remains slow and expensive. In this work, we present RoboSnap, a real-to-sim framework that turns a single RGB image into a simulation-ready scene. The key idea is a layered design that separates the physics-critical interaction area from the surrounding visual context: collision-aware foreground assets are refined for stable robot interaction, while a 3D Gaussian splatting visual layer preserves faithful background appearance under novel views. Experiments on DROID scenes and real-robot tasks show that RoboSnap achieves reliable trajectory replay in the recovered scenes, supports task-specific synthetic data generation for policy training, and yields meaningful sim-real correlation for policy evaluation. To further support real-to-sim research, we introduce DROID-Sim, a real-to-sim companion dataset constructed from 564 real-world scenes in DROID. Extensive experiments suggest that the value of real-to-sim methods lies not only in high-fidelity visual reconstruction, but in turning real environments into reusable infrastructure for robot learning and evaluation.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Why Koopman Structure Does Not Help Differentiable World Models for Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Haizhou Ge, Mengshuo Wang, Yufei Jia, Lei Han, Lu Shi
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: Koopman structure does not enhance differentiable world models for humanoid tracking, yielding similar performance but slower training compared to MLP models.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: We test whether Koopman structure, linear dynamics in a lifted state space, helps when a humanoid whole-body tracking policy is trained by backpropagating through a differentiable world model, replacing the MLP world model of an otherwise unchanged pipeline for simulated Unitree G1 tracking. It does not: return is at best equal (0.823 versus 0.830), one-step error on identical data is 1.3 to 1.6 times the MLP's, and training is about 15% slower. Lifted rollouts diverge or fail to train a policy; of the schemes tested, re-lifting at every imagined step trains best. Re-lifting never uses the lifted linear dynamics and leaves a model affine in the action, with state-dependent offset and slope; an action-affine MLP also predicts worse, so the cost belongs to this class. At a fixed state, the curvature of the true dynamics in the action explains only part of it. Across states, the policy's actions span a curved region, so an affine model fits policy data only as the tangent at the policy's action, the operating point: on G1, the MLP's tangent there is as accurate as the MLP; at the mean action, 31 times worse. The offset must encode, from the state alone, where the policy acts, whereas an MLP reads the action. Supplying the policy's action removes most of the remaining gap on G1, Ant and Humanoid. The only online repair approaching the MLP feeds the action into the nonlinear lift, giving up the structure. The MLP world model thus remains the better choice here.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: OpenHLM: An Empirical Recipe for Whole-Body Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yingdong Hu, Haodong Zhu, Boyuan Zheng, Yihang Hu, Tong Zhang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper presents OpenHLM, an open-source framework for whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation, demonstrating superior performance through a novel vision-language-action model and systematic empirical study.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinating the robot's entire kinematic chain. However, most existing systems typically decouple the upper and lower bodies into separate controllers, limiting such coordination and yielding behaviors similar to those of a wheeled dual-arm platform. In this paper, we ask what it takes to build a whole-body native vision-language-action (VLA) model that maps language and pixels directly to all of the humanoid's degrees of freedom. We conduct a systematic empirical study organized as a roadmap of one-variable-at-a-time experiments across three phases: whole-body teleoperation, VLA model design, and heterogeneous co-training. Our study yields several intriguing findings: a joint-based whole-body teleoperation interface outperforms alternatives that only partially expose the humanoid's degrees of freedom; a VLA pretrained on static and wheeled dual-arm platforms transfers surprisingly well to a humanoid's full action space; and co-training with HuMI, the humanoid analog of UMI, extends the policy to new objects and instructions without additional whole-body teleoperation on those targets. Following this roadmap yields OpenHLM, an open-source recipe for whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation. In a challenging long-horizon task that spans a wide vertical range of the humanoid, OpenHLM outperforms two state-of-the-art humanoid VLA baselines (GR00T N1.6 and $Ψ_0$) using less than half the total demonstration time. Our code, training data, and model checkpoints are available at [https://openhlm-project.github.io/].

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Gnomon4D: Learning Where and When to Focus for Geometric Motion-Grounded World-Action Modeling
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Lingwei Dang, Yan Zhou, Juntong Li, Zhenhao Zhang, Yiteng Chen
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: Gnomon4D introduces a novel world-action model that integrates geometric motion fields for improved robot action prediction and future video generation, outperforming existing methods significantly.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: World-action models (WAMs) use video-generation priors to jointly predict future observations and robot actions. Yet RGB futures entangle physical state changes with appearance, while frame-wise depth and point maps lack temporal correspondence. Existing 4D approaches either keep motion implicit in visual features or translate predicted traces into actions through a separate interface. We present Gnomon4D, a WAM that jointly generates future video, robot actions, and GeoDelta, a video-aligned 4D geometric motion field encoding the cross-frame image-plane displacement and depth change of embodiment and object points. By placing embodiment motion and object responses in a shared space, GeoDelta exposes their motion relations to the action expert at inference. Interaction-Salient Attention (InSAttn) uses these relations to focus spatial readout on task-relevant interaction regions, while Transition-Anchored Aggregation (TransAgg) aggregates evidence around changes in their relative motion, such as grasp and release. GeoDelta describes surface motion independently of embodiment-specific controls, providing a shared human--robot quasi-action for action-free pretraining on EgoManip-5000H followed by robot mid-training on Robot-30H. Gnomon4D leads on RoboTwin~2.0, VLABench, and RoboDojo, and outperforms the strongest real-robot baseline by 7.0 and 16.0 percentage points under in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings, respectively.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ReWorld: Multi-Dimensional Reward Modeling for Embodied Video Generation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Baorui Peng, Wenyao Zhang, Liang Xu, Bohan Li, Hu Zhu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: ReWorld introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enhances embodied video generation by aligning it with physical realism, task logic, and visual quality through a multi-dimensional reward model.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Current embodied video generation models primarily emphasize visual generative quality while overlooking physical fidelity, dynamic consistency, and task logic, especially for contact-rich manipulation tasks, which limits their applicability to downstream tasks. In this paper, we introduce ReWorld, a framework aimed to employ reinforcement learning to align the video generation with physical realism, task completion capability, embodiment plausibility and visual quality. Specifically, we first construct a large-scale (~235K) video preference dataset and employ it to train a hierarchical reward model designed to capture multi-dimensional reward consistent with human preferences. We further propose a practical alignment algorithm that post-trains flow-based video generators using this reward through a computationally efficient PPO-style algorithm. Comprehensive experiments and theoretical analysis demonstrate that ReWorld significantly improves the physical fidelity, logical coherence, embodiment and visual quality of generated rollouts, outperforming previous methods.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Beyond Policy Patches: Distilling RL Specialists into Vision-Language-Action Policies
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zhennan Jiang, Tingying Xie, Shilong Ji, Shu'ang Yu, Tianxing Zhou
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The REPAIR framework effectively distills reinforcement learning specialists into vision-language-action policies, achieving 100% success in precision-critical tasks while minimizing action jitter.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can handle noncritical stages of long-horizon manipulation yet fail during short precision-critical phases. Lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) specialists can address these failures without directly applying RL to the full VLA, but retain auxiliary controllers and switching mechanisms at deployment. We study how to transfer their capabilities into a single flow-matching VLA. Direct imitation of specialist rollouts can reproduce action jitter and leave the VLA unprepared for states encountered during its own execution. We introduce REPAIR, a value-guided distillation framework that combines offline initialization with on-policy refinement. At each critical-phase observation, REPAIR queries the corresponding specialist for multiple action candidates and weights them using its critic to construct a supervision distribution. A shared weighted flow-matching objective trains the VLA first on observations from specialist-assisted rollouts, then on observations collected through its own execution. Specialists provide supervision without taking control during on-policy collection and are removed at deployment. Across six real-robot tasks with 30 evaluation trials per task, REPAIR achieves 100% success on all six tasks, with lower mean end-effector jerk than specialist-assisted execution on every task.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: 3D Gaussian Splatting within Self-Learned Neural View-Dependent Color Fields
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yixiao Yang, Yu-Shen Liu, Zhizhong Han
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper presents a novel approach to 3D Gaussian Splatting using self-learned neural networks for improved radiance field modeling and geometry recovery in novel view synthesis.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a vital tool in novel view synthesis. 3D Gaussian functions with attributes like color, opacity, and scale are stacked together to explicitly model a radiance field. However, discrete 3D Gaussians usually produce poor depth with few geometry details but lots of floaters, which hinders the effective modeling of smooth radiance fields. To address this issue, we propose to learn a radiance field within a continuous view-dependent color field parameterized by neural networks. With continuous constraints in color, the bias on low-frequency signals of neural networks can highly encourage the geometry modeling to contribute to high-frequency color variations on images, getting rid of solely relying on the color attribute itself. Moreover, we impose a constraint to improve the Lipschitz continuity of the neural color field, making large changes of each Gaussian's color also match with large changes of its position in terms of a ratio. To this end, we additionally introduce novel self-learning strategies to improve the learning of the neural view-dependent color field without any external knowledge or priors, aiming for better generalization on unseen scenes. Our numerical and visual comparisons on widely used benchmarks justify our idea and show better ability of high fidelity geometry recovery in 3DGS. Project page: https://github.com/yangyixi21/Neural-Color-Fields-3DGS.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Transfer the Style, Not the Semantics: Mitigating Semantic Leakage in Image-Guided Stylization
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Haojun Tang, Qiwei Lin, Tongda Xu, Wenda Zhao, Yian Zhao
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper introduces SuRe, a framework that mitigates semantic leakage in image-guided stylization by disrupting key-value correspondence in self-attention mechanisms of diffusion models.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Image-guided zero-shot style transfer enables training-free stylization of arbitrary content images using a reference style. Despite recent progress, existing methods commonly rely on self-attention manipulation to inject style information, which may transfer semantic content from the style image, leading to semantic leakage. In this work, we revisit this phenomenon from the perspective of key--value coupling in the self-attention of diffusion models. Our analysis shows that the native correspondence between style keys and values plays an important role in transferring semantic information from the style image. Motivated by this observation, we propose SuRe, a timestep-aware key--value regulation framework that mitigates semantic leakage by disrupting the native key--value correspondence while progressively restoring it for faithful style transfer. Specifically, we present value shuffle to decouple style keys and values while preserving the empirical distribution of the values, together with a progressive recoupling mechanism that gradually recouples them throughout the stylization process. Experiments against 18 representative methods demonstrate that SuRe maintains competitive style similarity while consistently improving content similarity across SD1.5, SDXL, SD3, and FLUX.1-dev, with natural generalization to multi-style transfer. The code will be publicly available at https://github.com/XinR-Tang/SuRe.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ArthroCut: Autonomous Policy Learning for Robotic Bone Resection in Knee Arthroplasty
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xu Lu, Yiling Zhang, Wenquan Cheng, Longfei Ma, Fang Chen
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: ArthroCut enhances robotic knee arthroplasty by integrating multimodal data for autonomous, context-aware decision-making, achieving an 86% success rate in bone resection tasks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Despite rapid commercialization of surgical robots, their autonomy and real-time decision-making remain limited in practice. To address this gap, we propose ArthroCut, an autonomous policy learning framework that upgrades knee arthroplasty robots from assistive execution to context-aware action generation. ArthroCut fine-tunes a Qwen--VL backbone on a self-built, time-synchronized multimodal dataset from 21 complete cases (23,205 RGB--D pairs), integrating preoperative CT/MR, intraoperative NDI tracking of bones and end effector, RGB--D surgical video, robot state, and textual intent. The method operates on two complementary token families -- Preoperative Imaging Tokens (PIT) to encode patient-specific anatomy and planned resection planes, and Time-Aligned Surgical Tokens (TAST) to fuse real-time visual, geometric, and kinematic evidence -- and emits an interpretable action grammar under grammar/safety-constrained decoding. In bench-top experiments on a knee prosthesis across seven trials, ArthroCut achieves an average success rate of 86% over the six standard resections, significantly outperforming strong baselines trained under the same protocol. Ablations show that TAST is the principal driver of reliability while PIT provides essential anatomical grounding, and their combination yields the most stable multi-plane execution. These results indicate that aligning preoperative geometry with time-aligned intraoperative perception and translating that alignment into tokenized, constrained actions is an effective path toward robust, interpretable autonomy in orthopedic robotic surgery.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Lang Mo, Xingxuan Zhang, Qi Wang, Mingchao Hao, Hao Yuan
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM) enhances agent decision-making accuracy by leveraging a shared pretrained learner for conditional predictions, improving performance across various tasks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Agent decisions depend on empirical relationships that deployment observations reveal and task descriptions alone may leave unresolved. We introduce Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM), an architecture that formulates heterogeneous agent decisions as conditional prediction with a shared pretrained learner. Language models provide semantic representations of current and historical records, while a general-purpose conditional predictor predicts task-defined targets from the represented evidence. Pretraining supplies reusable inference capability; deployment evidence instantiates problem-specific predictions without updating either model's neural parameters. Tool judgments, candidate preferences, and reasoning assessments share an evidence-and-query interface, with predictions mapped to choices by a decision rule. This architecture establishes complementary sources of agent capability: semantic knowledge acquired through language pretraining and empirical inference acquired through structured-data pretraining. A single frozen LimiX-2 predictor serves all five task categories. With Qwen3.5-27B as the semantic encoder, DPDM raises mean accuracy across 50 benchmarks from 78.80% with few-shot prompting to 84.92% under their respective evaluated history budgets, and reaches 82.33% with identical histories and queries. On ToolPRMBench's BFCL and ToolSandbox tasks, absolute accuracy gains are 34.26% and 28.87%, respectively, at the methods' respective evaluated history budgets. Accuracy improves as history grows. With identical imbalanced histories, mean balanced accuracy improves by an absolute 14.51% across five reasoning-step assessment tasks and four encoders. DPDM makes learning from experience an independently improvable foundation-model capability, creating a shared route for advances in conditional prediction to improve decisions across agent tasks.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Qianggang Ding, Xingyao Wang, Rui Feng, Chi Qin, Weijian Lin
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The OpenZilo smart-ring platform enables effective human-robot interaction through speech and gesture control, achieving high task success rates and efficient response times.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Wearable robot interfaces must connect user input to timely physical action. We present the proposed platform, an open smart-ring platform for studying this connection across task stages. The ring integrates a microphone, an inertial measurement unit, photoplethysmography, and skin-temperature sensing. Its software architecture separates acquisition, event interpretation, interaction policy, and robot execution. We characterize seven operating modes and evaluate speech and gesture control with 10 participants. Across five commands and 250 trials per modality, speech and gestures achieved task success rates of 90.4% and 88.8%, respectively. Recognition accuracy exceeded task success for both modalities. Gaussian hidden Markov models achieved higher accuracy than a support vector machine across three vocabulary sizes, with longer scoring times. Following a shared spoken task start, gesture-based adjustments had shorter median response times than speech. Whole-task success was 70.0% with gestures and 64.0% with speech. We further examine physiological-event-triggered robot interaction using simulated event notifications. Mean notification-receipt-to-arrival times were 11.71 s for the robot and 9.20 s for an on-site person. These descriptive findings support evaluating wearable robot interfaces through both recognition and physical outcomes, with timing measures appropriate to each task stage.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: $π$-StepNFT: Wider Space Needs Finer Steps in Online RL for Flow-based VLAs
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Siting Wang, Xiaofeng Wang, Zheng Zhu, Minnan Pei, Xinyu Cui
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The $π$-StepNFT framework enhances online reinforcement learning for flow-based VLAs by integrating wider stochastic exploration with fine-tuned supervision, significantly improving success rates in various tasks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for embodied control, but multi-step denoising makes policy-gradient online reinforcement learning (RL) difficult because the final-action likelihood induced by the sampler is not directly tractable. We identify an exploration--supervision mismatch within the denoising trajectory, where stochastic differential equation (SDE) sampling explores a wider local stochastic transition space while supervision derived from the final denoised output does not directly use the adjacent transitions observed during sampling. We propose $π$-StepNFT (Step-wise Negative-aware Fine-Tuning), a flow-native online RL framework that couples wider stochastic exploration with finer step-wise supervision without computing the final-action likelihood. $π$-StepNFT treats observed SDE transitions as supervision units, using variance-normalized transition errors to rank mirrored positive and negative velocity branches and map rollout feedback to local velocity updates. On LIBERO, starting from shared few-shot SFT initializations, $π$-StepNFT raises average success from 57.6\% to 92.0\% for $π_0$ and from 77.1\% to 94.0\% for $π_{0.5}$. On ManiSkill, it achieves the highest reported mean success among the evaluated RL baselines on five test-only visual perturbations. Our project homepage is available at https://wangst0181.github.io/pi-StepNFT/.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: EgoHSI3R: Online 4D Hand-Scene Interaction Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Mingzhi Pei, Zhangchen Ye, Ruoqu Chen, Liu Cao, Mengdi Xu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: EgoHSI3R is a unified framework for online 4D hand-scene interaction reconstruction from egocentric video, achieving superior accuracy and speed in joint estimation of hands, camera, and scene geometry.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Egocentric videos offer an abundant source of hand-scene interactions for embodied learning, which requires recovering hands, camera, and scene consistently in a shared 3D world. Existing methods focus on either camera-frame hands or world-space hand trajectories, without jointly recovering the scene pointmaps or interaction information. Building a complete reconstruction from such specialized predictions therefore typically requires per-sequence optimization. We propose EgoHSI3R, a unified feed-forward framework for online 4D hand-scene interaction reconstruction from egocentric monocular video.
