In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: SARGO: Agreement-Gated Reinforcement and Suppression via On-Policy Self-Guidance for Visual Hallucination Mitigation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jinyu Li, Zhiming Zhang, Hao Fang, Hongyao Yu, Bin Chen
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: SARGO introduces a post-training framework that selectively reinforces accurate visual information while mitigating hallucinations in vision-language models through on-policy self-guidance.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-language models remain susceptible to visual hallucinations, often mixing grounded information with unsupported claims in the same response. Response-level reinforcement learning assigns a shared advantage to all tokens in a response, causing negative updates to suppress correct information alongside unsupported claims. To reduce hallucination while preserving useful visual information, we introduce SARGO (Self-guided Advantage-Routed Grounding Optimization), a post-training framework for selective reinforcement and suppression through on-policy self-guidance. Direct and reciprocal weighting gives better-supported tokens stronger reinforcement on positive updates and weaker penalties on negative updates. Agreement between overall and hallucination-specific advantages selects when to apply this guidance. At the response level, a reference-calibrated reward couples factuality with the retention and expansion of grounded information, discouraging lower hallucination scores obtained through omission. Experiments on Qwen3-VL-4B, Qwen3-VL-8B, and Gemma3-4B demonstrate that SARGO outperforms the evaluated mitigation baselines across Obj-Hal, AMBER, THRONE, and SHR evaluations. SARGO achieves these gains while preserving useful visual information and general multimodal capabilities.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ReST-RL: Reinforcing LLM Reasoning through Unified Self-Training and Value-Guided Search
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Sining Zhoubian, Dan Zhang, Jie Tang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ReST-RL enhances LLM reasoning accuracy through a unified self-training and value-guided search framework, outperforming existing reinforcement learning and decoding methods across various benchmarks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: With respect to improving the reasoning accuracy of LLMs, the representative reinforcement learning (RL) method - Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) - has achieved critical success, yet it still suffers from the issue of insignificant reward signals. This paper introduces ReST-RL, a unified Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) policy-value framework that reconnects policy optimization and value-guided search to improve LLM reasoning ability. Firstly, ReST-GRPO adopts an optimized ReST-style algorithm to reshape the policy-induced trajectory distribution by increasing the reward variance of GRPO sampling and exposing the policy to more informative partial states, thereby improving training efficiency and effectiveness. Then, we further introduce a decoding optimization method, VM-MCTS, which trains a Value Model (VM) from self-collected Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) targets and deploys it through an adapted MCTS algorithm to provide precise process signals and verification scores, further enhancing reasoning accuracy. These two stages are internally dependent - ReST-GRPO yields higher quality trajectories for value learning with VM-MCTS, which in turn enables more effective inference-time search. We validate our framework on multiple coding benchmarks (e.g., APPS, BigCodeBench, and HumanEval), where it significantly outperforms other reinforcement training baselines (naive GRPO, DAPO, and ReST-DPO), as well as decoding and verification baselines (e.g., PRM-BoN and ORM-MCTS), indicating its power to strengthen LLM reasoning capability. Moreover, we further evaluate ReST-RL on out-of-domain math and science reasoning tasks, where it achieves improved performance without target-domain tuning and favorable end-to-end efficiency trade-offs, providing preliminary transfer evidence beyond our primary coding domain.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: USER: A Unified and Extensible System for Online Real-World Policy Learning in Embodied AI
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Hongzhi Zang, Shu'ang Yu, Hao Lin, Tianxing Zhou, Zefang Huang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: USER is a unified system that enhances online real-world policy learning in embodied AI through hardware abstraction, adaptive communication, and asynchronous training frameworks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Online policy learning directly in the physical world is a promising yet challenging direction for embodied intelligence. Unlike simulation, real-world systems cannot be arbitrarily accelerated, cheaply reset, or massively replicated, suggesting that real-world policy learning is not merely an algorithmic problem, but inherently a systems problem. We present \user, a \underline{U}nified and extensible \underline{S}yst\underline{E}m for online real-world policy lea\underline{R}ning. On the systems side, \user introduces a hardware abstraction layer for unified robot management and an adaptive communication plane that enables efficient cloud-edge training. On the learning side, \user adopts a fully asynchronous training framework, designs a persistent and cache-aware replay buffer, and provides extensible abstractions for rewards, algorithms, and policies. Experiments in both simulation and the real world demonstrate that \user supports multi-robot coordination, heterogeneous manipulators, cloud-edge training with large models, and long-running asynchronous training. Together, these capabilities establish \user as a unified and extensible systems foundation for online real-world policy learning.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: LatentUM: Unleashing the Potential of Interleaved Cross-Modal Reasoning via a Latent-Space Unified Model
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jiachun Jin, Zetong Zhou, Xiao Yang, Hao Zhang, Pengfei Liu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: LatentUM introduces a unified model that enhances interleaved cross-modal reasoning by utilizing a shared semantic latent space, achieving state-of-the-art performance in visual tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Unified models (UMs) hold promise for their ability to understand and generate content across heterogeneous modalities. Compared to merely generating visual content, the use of UMs for interleaved cross-modal reasoning is more promising and valuable, e.g., for solving understanding problems that require dense visual thinking, improving visual generation through self-reflection, or modeling visual dynamics of the physical world guided by stepwise action interventions. However, existing UMs typically rely on pixel decoding as a bridge when their visual representations for understanding and generation are disjoint, which is both ineffective and computationally cumbersome. In this paper, we introduce LatentUM, a novel unified model that represents all modalities within a shared semantic latent space, eliminating pixel-space mediation for model-internal reasoning over generated visual states. By making generated visual tokens directly interpretable to the model itself, LatentUM enables flexible interleaved cross-modal reasoning and generation. Empirically, LatentUM achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Visual Spatial Planning benchmark, pushes the limits of visual generation through self-reflection and demonstrates world modeling capability by predicting future visual states in the shared semantic latent space. Code and models are available at https://github.com/SJTU-DENG-Lab/LatentUM.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: RISE-RL: Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jinkun Hou, Zhuo Liu, Huimin Ren, Kuan Zhang, Zirong Chen
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: RISE-RL enhances open-ended reinforcement learning by selectively exploring trajectories based on missed rubric criteria, significantly improving performance across various benchmarks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) for open-ended tasks is challenging because responses must satisfy multidimensional criteria without following a single correct generation trajectory. Existing rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) methods compress fine-grained criterion-level feedback into scalar rewards, making persistent capability gaps difficult to target under limited on-policy exploration. We propose $\textbf{RISE-RL}$ (Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration), which uses repeatedly missed rubric criteria to elicit privileged trajectories that are difficult to discover through unguided exploration alone. RISE-RL retains only trajectories whose complete-rubric reward exceeds the mean reward of natural rollouts, and then re-evaluates them under the original prompt to emphasize behaviors that remain weakly supported by the natural policy. The resulting guidance signal is optimized through a separate auxiliary objective and removed once its additional benefit diminishes. Experiments with 4B and 14B models across writing, chat, health, and science show that RISE-RL achieves the highest mean score on every evaluated benchmark under guidance-free evaluation. Compared with standard Rubric-RL, it improves the average score by 1.3 points at the 4B scale and $\textbf{3.3 points at the 14B scale}$, including a $\textbf{6.0-point}$ gain on CreativeWriting-V3. It also improves creative-writing diversity and yields gains on objectively scored medical and scientific benchmarks. These results indicate that selective internalization through reward filtering and policy support shaping is effective for open-ended reinforcement learning.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: M-CROSS: A Multisensor Simulation Dataset for SLAM across Water--Land Transitions
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yan Dong, Tianyi Wu, Junyu Yang, Shaoqiang Qiu, Zefeng Yan
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: M-CROSS is a novel multisensor simulation dataset for SLAM, addressing localization challenges in water-land transitions with new metrics and demonstrating existing methods' inadequacies.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Water--land cross-domain robots require continuous localization across land, transition and underwater phases, where sensor characteristics and availability change abruptly. Existing datasets and conventional metrics are not designed to capture transition-induced degradation and failures. We present \textbf{M-CROSS}, to the best of our knowledge, the first multisensor simulation dataset and benchmark for SLAM across continuous water--land transitions. It provides synchronized LiDAR, sonar, stereo camera, IMU, DVL, and depth measurements; 6DoF pose ground truth; sensor-wise medium-state annotations; and medium-dependent sensor degradation models. We establish a transition-aware protocol comprising the Trajectory Completion Rate (TCR), Piecewise Absolute Pose Error (PW-APE), Transition End Error (TEE), and Transition Survival Period (TSP), which measure trajectory completion, single-domain accuracy, transition-induced error, and localization survival under prolonged partial immersion, respectively. Experiments with 6 representative SLAM systems show that existing methods fail to maintain both localization accuracy and trajectory continuity across the full set of water--land transitions, exhibiting transition-induced drift, trajectory discontinuities, and tracking failures. M-CROSS is publicly available https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MCross-Dataset

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Beyond Vehicle-Centric Data: Scaling Autonomous Driving through Roadside-to-Vehicle Generation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yichen Zhang, Zihan Wang, Hao Chen, Runyi Huang, Ruixue Zong
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The AnyR2V framework transforms roadside traffic data into diverse vehicle-centric training videos, enhancing autonomous driving model performance by generating multi-perspective datasets.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Training autonomous driving models requires large and diverse datasets, collected primarily by vehicles. Scaling them entails investment in fleet operation, data processing and annotation. Road infrastructure records traffic and multi-vehicle interactions, yet the viewpoint gap between roadside and onboard sensors limits its direct use for training. Here we introduce AnyR2V, a framework that transforms multimodal roadside observations into seven-camera surround-view videos for different vehicle perspectives. It aggregates sequential observations into a shared scene representation of geometry and road-user motion, then renders appearance, depth and layout conditions along target-vehicle trajectories. Supervised by spatiotemporally aligned roadside-vehicle pairs, AnyR2V generates surround-view videos guided by scene structure and road-user motion. Existing roadside 3D bounding boxes are transformed into target-vehicle coordinates and paired with generated images, allowing one traffic recording and its annotations to yield training data from multiple vehicle perspectives. We construct R2V360, a dataset of 89 real traffic sequences at an urban intersection, with aligned multimodal roadside data and onboard surround-view videos. AnyR2V outperforms six scene reconstruction methods in image fidelity and in depth and semantic agreement between generated and real onboard images. We further evaluate generated videos along other vehicles' trajectories by adding them to real training data. Adding generated frames equal to 50% of the original real training frame count improves mean average precision (mAP) by 3.3-3.4 AP-points across three 3D object detectors on the real onboard test set, relative to real-data-only baselines. These results demonstrate that roadside traffic records can provide training data from multiple vehicle perspectives, offering a new data source for autonomous driving.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: PlanDiv: Test-Time Scaling with Latent Plans for Vision-Language-Action Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Hanbo Zhang, Lianlei Shan, Liuhaichen Yang, Zezhi Tang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: PlanDiv enhances vision-language-action models by generating diverse action candidates through latent plans, significantly improving task success rates compared to traditional resampling methods.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Test-time scaling improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies by drawing several action candidates and executing the best one. We find that its returns diminish quickly when the candidates are resampled from one decoder: they differ by noise rather than by plan, and for each of three resampling sources, going from four to eight candidates adds only 0.06-0.07 to the average number of completed tasks on CALVIN. We introduce PlanDiv, an action head that makes the candidates differ by plan: a lightweight planner proposes K latent plan hypotheses, a shared masked-diffusion executor decodes one action chunk per plan from a single backbone pass, and the policy executes the chunk that its own likelihood ranks highest. The plans are learned from demonstrations alone, without plan labels or rewards. With the backbone, data and training recipe held fixed, eight plan-conditioned candidates raise five-task chain success on CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D from 56.9% to 69.9%, while eight candidates from autoregressive, plan-free or same-plan resampling reach at most 64.9%. The same-plan baseline is PlanDiv's own checkpoint with the plan held fixed, so this gap comes from the plans, not from drawing more samples. On LIBERO-Long, four plans remove 40% of single-candidate failures, against at most 21% for matched resampling. On a real Franka arm the gain appears where a task admits more than one solution: PlanDiv is on par with a single-output OpenVLA-OFT+ baseline on a one-solution task and succeeds in 51 of 54 trials against 40 of 54 on two tasks with two solutions.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Beyond Visual Cues: Semantic-Driven Token Filtering and Expert Routing for Anytime Person ReID
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jiaxuan Li, Xin Wen, Zhihang Li
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper presents STFER, a framework utilizing Large Vision-Language Models for robust person re-identification across varying conditions by integrating semantic-driven filtering and expert routing.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Any-Time Person Re-identification (AT-ReID) necessitates the robust retrieval of target individuals under arbitrary conditions, encompassing both modality shifts (daytime and nighttime) and extensive clothing-change scenarios, ranging from short-term to long-term intervals. However, existing methods are highly relying on pure visual features, which are prone to change due to environmental and time factors, resulting in significantly performance deterioration under scenarios involving illumination caused modality shifts or cloth-change. In this paper, we propose Semantic-driven Token Filtering and Expert Routing (STFER), a novel framework that leverages the ability of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to generate identity consistency text, which provides identity-discriminative features that are robust to both clothing variations and cross-modality shifts between RGB and IR. Specifically, we employ instructions to guide the LVLM in generating identity-intrinsic semantic text that captures biometric constants for the semantic model driven. The text token is further used for Semantic-driven Visual Token Filtering (SVTF), which enhances informative visual regions and suppresses redundant background noise. Meanwhile, the text token is also used for Semantic-driven Expert Routing (SER), which integrates the semantic text into expert routing, resulting in more robust multi-scenario gating. Extensive experiments on the Any-Time ReID dataset (AT-USTC) demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art results. Moreover, the model trained on AT-USTC was evaluated across 5 widely-used ReID benchmarks demonstrating superior generalization capabilities with highly competitive results. Our code will be available soon.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: EgoEMG: A Multimodal Egocentric Dataset with Bilateral EMG and Vision for Hand Pose Estimation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Ziheng Xi, Jiayi Yu, Yanbo Duan, Yitao Wang, Jinyang Yu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: EgoEMG introduces a multimodal dataset combining bilateral sEMG and egocentric video for improved hand pose estimation, achieving notable accuracy enhancements through feature fusion.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Hand pose estimation from egocentric video is challenging under adverse visual conditions, such as occlusion. Wrist-worn surface electromyography (sEMG) measures muscle activity without requiring visual access to the hand, offering a wearable complement to egocentric cameras. Evaluating their combined use requires synchronized physiological and visual recordings with continuous pose annotations, which existing EMG-based hand pose datasets do not jointly provide. We introduce EgoEMG, a multimodal dataset pairing bilateral wrist sEMG with egocentric video and motion-capture-derived hand poses, supplemented by external multi-view RGB-D recordings. EgoEMG contains 25.9 hours of recordings from 68 participants, covering 60 bare-hand gesture classes and interactions with 10 everyday objects. We establish EMG-only, vision-only, and fusion benchmarks with shared 22-dimensional pose targets and evaluations on unseen users, gestures, and objects. For EMG-only estimation, EMGFormer achieves the lowest overall MAE among the compared methods on EgoEMG and competitive results on EMG2Pose. Our residual fusion model combines ViT and EMGFormer features. Adding EMG reduces error for both single-frame and temporal vision models, with MAE decreasing from $7.39^\circ$ to $7.06^\circ$ for ViT-L. The largest absolute reduction occurs when evaluating interactions with an unseen object. Generalization to unseen users remains challenging. Project page: https://zhenqis123.github.io/egoemg-site/.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: OA-WAM: Object-Addressable World Action Model for Robust Robot Manipulation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yushan Liu, Peibo Sun, Shoujie Li, Yifan Xie, Lingfeng Zhang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: OA-WAM introduces an object-addressable world action model that enhances robot manipulation robustness across varying conditions, achieving superior performance in multiple benchmarks and real-robot tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) learn manipulation by predicting actions and future observations, yet their success drops sharply when the camera viewpoint, object layout or robot initial state changes. Such changes keep the instructed object the same but alter the appearance and pose features the policy observes, which in standard attention also form the keys that locate the object. We introduce OA-WAM, an object-addressable WAM that finds each object by an identity address fixed for the episode and reads its changing state. In every layer of a pretrained multimodal trunk, object-slot keys depend only on the address and frame position, and values carry the current state; the same addresses key the action pointer and index per-object forecasts, which can trigger re-grounding. Fine-tuned on standard LIBERO demonstrations, OA-WAM transfers zero-shot to LIBERO-Plus with 90.5% success, outperforming all ten published baselines. It also leads on LIBERO (99.0%) and, fine-tuned on BridgeData V2, on SimplerEnv WidowX (88.9%). On five real-robot tasks, it succeeds in 89 of 100 nominal trials, versus 73 for the strongest baseline. Ablations trace its robustness to addressing rather than to object slots: with standard attention, slots do no better than a slot-free policy, and addressing them by identity raises geometric success by 10.7 points. Forecasting the addressed objects is likewise a stronger training signal than forecasting image codes.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ODEWorld: A Continuous Predictive Architecture via Physical-Time Flow
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Dongxiu Liu, Haoyi Niu, Peng Cheng, Yuan Gao, Xirui Kang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ODEWorld introduces a continuous predictive architecture using Physical-Time Flow and ODEs to enhance efficiency in modeling dynamics, enabling high-quality predictions and planning in robotics.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: In the physical world we inhabit, space and time are fundamentally continuous. However, existing machine learning paradigms for world modeling are largely confined to discrete-time prediction, thereby exhibiting significant inefficiency in capturing the dynamics of physical world. We introduce Physical-Time Flow (PT-Flow), a novel approach that learns a continuous latent velocity field operating in physical time. Crucially, the underlying dynamics of sequential data are parameterized by an ordinary differential equation (ODE) embedded in a well-structured representation space. Under this paradigm, the prediction of future can be recast as temporal integration via an ODE solver in the compressed latent space. Building upon PT-Flow, we construct ODEWorld, a continuous-time latent world model that is both efficient and versatile. By extracting time-variant features and enforcing ODE properties on both the dynamical representation space and the latent velocity field, ODEWorld effectively addresses the long-standing representation collapse issue in latent world model literature. This also enables high-quality image reconstruction even after long-horizon prediction. Moreover, its continuous nature allows for arbitrary temporal resolution and even backward prediction, which is impossible for most discrete-time models. Lastly, ODEWorld can provide rich planning-oriented information to facilitate downstream policy learning. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that ODEWorld successfully reconciles planning-conducive dynamics abstraction with visual realism, excelling in both video generation and robotic control. Project page: https://dstate.github.io/odeworld_website/.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ReRead: Wrong Predictions, Useful Representations - Correcting Frozen Robot Policies by Re-reading Their Own Representations
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Xu Su, Shunlong Xiao, Qintao Yi, Mingkuan Zhao, Xinmiao Yu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The ReRead method enhances frozen robot policies by correcting action predictions using past representations, improving success rates significantly across various tasks without additional visual encoders.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: When a pretrained robot policy fails on challenging tasks, common remedies include retraining the backbone, adding an external visual encoder, or introducing a memory module. We argue that wrong predictions do not imply wrong representations: a policy can retain the required information yet fail to read it out as the correct action. To test this view, we propose ReRead: with the backbone frozen, a corrector re-reads the current and two previous caches to predict an action residual. The corrector sees no images, is trained solely on offline demonstrations from all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and adds only 4.17% latency. Ablations and interventions show that the correction relies on the backbone's own representations: none of four external visual encoders adds further gain, and swapping in past caches from other trajectories sharply increases action error. On the 11 hardest RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, ReRead improves the success rates of LingBot-VLA, $π_{0.5}$, and Fast-WAM by 23.45, 13.09, and 8.00 percentage points, respectively. In paired evaluation on all 50 tasks, it raises Fast-WAM's average success rate from 90.73% to 92.66%. On a Flexiv dual-arm robot, it raises success on a phase-ambiguous task from 0% to 36%.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: AsymEEF: Bimanual Manipulation with Asymmetric End Effectors
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Xiaokang Sun, Ningyue Wang, Kunqi Xu, Guangqi Jiang, Jianglong Ye
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: AsymEEF enables efficient bimanual manipulation by transferring demonstrations across diverse end-effectors, enhancing policy learning and execution success without additional teleoperation.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Teleoperated demonstrations are costly to collect and rarely reusable across end-effectors with different kinematics and action spaces. This burden grows in bimanual manipulation, where each end-effector pair may require new data. We present AsymEEF, a framework for executable cross-end-effector demonstration generation and unified bimanual policy learning. Given a small source dataset, AsymEEF transfers demonstrations to heterogeneous combinations of two-, three-, and five-fingered end-effectors without additional teleoperation. Kinematic teacher anchors provide geometric supervision, while sparse real-world X-Calib anchors correct discrepancies in grasp execution. A shared encoder maps wrist poses and actuator states to a morphology-agnostic latent space, and a morphology-conditioned decoder reconstructs target commands. Generated trajectories undergo replay filtering for task-level executability. The representation also supports a unified bimanual visuomotor policy trained across multiple pairs. Across four simulated and six real-world tasks, AsymEEF improves replay success over adapted transfer baselines, achieves a mean replay-valid expansion gain of 16.6 times in simulation, and is evaluated through downstream policy training on real robots. Project website: https://asymeef.vercel.app/.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ExtremeDrive: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Critical Driving
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Xinhan Li, Yuhong Jiang, Shiyue Zhao, Junzhi Zhang, Chengkun He
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ExtremeDrive is a comprehensive dataset and benchmark for autonomous driving, focusing on safety-critical scenarios and extreme conditions, enhancing trajectory prediction and driving performance.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Existing autonomous driving datasets and benchmarks provide extensive resources for routine driving, yet real-world data covering safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions remain limited. To address this gap, we present ExtremeDrive, a real-world dataset and benchmark covering emergency maneuvers, complex traffic interactions, and adverse conditions such as slippery or snow-covered roads, alongside routine driving. The dataset comprises 589 driving scenes curated from a larger pool of real-world driving recordings, with calibrated and aligned multisensor data and reviewed annotations of road structure and traffic participants. We further establish a benchmark to evaluate planned trajectories through simulated vehicle execution, measuring safety-related metrics and driving performance. Experiments at equal training set sizes show that incorporating critical driving data reduces trajectory prediction errors and improves mean critical-success rates in critical scenarios. ExtremeDrive provides a unified resource for learning and evaluating autonomous driving in safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Non-Imaging Optical Tactile Sensors for Robotics: Transduction Principles, System Integration, and Robotic Applications
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Hao Wu, Yu Feng, Haotian Guo, Huichan Zhao, Changsheng Wu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: This review explores non-imaging optical tactile sensors in robotics, emphasizing their design, integration, and performance in accurately detecting contact variables amidst mechanical influences.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Non-imaging optical tactile sensors encode contact through changes in optical intensity, wavelength, spectra, or photon counts, offering diverse architectures for robotic touch. Their usefulness depends on whether contact variables can be reliably distinguished from coupled mechanical and environmental effects, and whether the resulting information can be delivered in time to guide action. This review develops a unified framework linking mechanical load transmission, optical encoding, readout, and tactile inference to robotic task requirements. It examines reflective and waveguide-based devices, micro/nanofibers, fiber gratings, interferometric and resonant structures, and mechanoluminescent composites. Three considerations emerge across these approaches. First, high optical sensitivity supports accurate tactile estimation only when target variables remain identifiable under the relevant contact and calibration conditions. Second, spatial coverage and feedback timing must be assessed at the system level, accounting for multiplexing, acquisition, demodulation, and inference. Third, device characterization, offline recognition, and closed-loop robotic performance provide distinct levels of evidence and require different evaluation criteria. Representative studies illustrate how these considerations shape force estimation, contact localization, slip correction and distributed interaction. This review concludes with priorities for calibration transfer, reliable interfaces, scalable readout, and task-based validation, providing a basis for selecting and developing non-imaging optical tactile architectures for robotics.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: VGGT-VLA-World: Intent-Conditioned 3D World Evolution for Autonomous Driving
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zhaoyang Liu, Zhigui Lin, Kun Jiang, Tianhui Li, Changye Liu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: VGGTWorld-VLA enhances 3D world evolution in autonomous driving by integrating intention-based action conditioning, improving future geometry predictions significantly compared to existing models.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: VGGT provides a strong foundation for geometry-centric world models by recovering unified 3D scene geometry from visual observations. Although recent extensions enable temporal 3D prediction, their future evolution remains weakly conditioned on driving intentions and actions, limiting their ability to model alternative action-dependent futures. We propose \textbf{VGGTWorld-VLA}, an intention-conditioned extension of VGGT-World for controllable 3D world evolution in autonomous driving. First, we introduce an action--semantic conditioning mechanism that injects complementary driving semantics and ego-motion representations into the future-token stream, enabling different future geometry predictions for the same observed scene under alternative ego actions. Second, we develop a geometry--language--action bridge that adapts historical geometry, VLA semantic features, and maneuver and trajectory representations for joint conditioning of future geometry prediction. We evaluate future geometry prediction on NAVSIM, with ablation studies examining the contributions of semantic and action conditioning. Compared with baseline, our method reduces future-depth RMSE by 13.7\% and improves $δ_1$ by 4.11 percentage points on NAVSIM motion subset. Controlled action-input interventions further show that the model uses the supplied action information. These results support semantic and action conditioning for controllable VGGT-based world prediction in autonomous driving.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Ruixi Yu, Dairu Liu, Xuchuan Chen, Zekun Qi, Zekai Li
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ScaleVLA, utilizing a 552B parameter backbone, enhances robot learning efficiency, generalization, and manipulation success compared to smaller Vision-Language-Action models.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: D-VLA: A High-Concurrency Distributed Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yucheng Guo, Yongjian Guo, Zhong Guan, Wen Huang, Haodong Yue
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: D-VLA is a distributed RL framework that enhances throughput and efficiency for Vision-Language-Action models by decoupling training data and optimizing resource management.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: The rapid evolution of Embodied AI has enabled Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to excel in multimodal perception and task execution. However, applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to these massive models in large-scale distributed environments faces severe systemic bottlenecks, primarily due to the resource conflict between high-fidelity physical simulation and the intensive VRAM/bandwidth demands of deep learning. This conflict often leaves overall throughput constrained by execution-phase inefficiencies. To address these challenges, we propose D-VLA, a high-concurrency, low-latency distributed RL framework for large-scale embodied foundation models. D-VLA introduces "Plane Decoupling," physically isolating high-frequency training data from low-frequency weight control to eliminate interference between simulation and optimization. We further design a four-thread asynchronous "Swimlane" pipeline, enabling full parallel overlap of sampling, inference, gradient computation, and parameter distribution. Additionally, a dual-pool VRAM management model and topology-aware replication resolve memory fragmentation and optimize communication efficiency. Experiments on benchmarks like LIBERO show that D-VLA significantly outperforms mainstream RL frameworks in throughput and sampling efficiency for billion-parameter VLA models. In trillion-parameter scalability tests, our framework maintains exceptional stability and linear speedup, providing a robust system for high-performance general-purpose embodied agents.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: MeanFlowAdvantage: Stable Reward Fine-Tuning for Few-Step Average-Velocity Generators
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Haocheng Tang, Tianchi Xie, Xingqiao Lin
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: MeanFlowAdvantage introduces a novel signed advantage-weighted objective for fine-tuning average-velocity generators, enhancing performance across metrics in robotics and DNA design applications.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: MeanFlow enables efficient few-step generation by predicting interval-average velocities, but this representation creates a mismatch for reward fine-tuning: existing advantage-based objectives are typically defined on instantaneous velocities or equivalent $x_0$-space predictions, whereas inference directly uses the learned average-velocity map. We introduce MeanFlowAdvantage, a signed advantage-weighted least-squares objective for average-velocity generators. Our key construction uses a shared, detached MeanFlow derivative correction to express the reward objective in prediction space while making rollout and reference regularization exact penalties on the average-velocity network deployed at inference. The resulting formulation preserves MeanFlow's native few-step sampler and provides a direct mechanism for transferring reward improvements to the deployed flow map. On SD3.5-Medium, MeanFlowAdvantage improves all eight reported metrics over the matched four-step MeanFlowNFT baseline and, with only four NFEs, matches or exceeds the 40-step DiffusionNFT baseline on six of eight metrics. The same objective also transfers to DNA promoter design, where it supports both teacher-free on-policy RL for a generator defined on a manifold and teacher-guided reward-graded distillation, with the latter yielding the lowest one-step Sei profile MSE among the compared configurations.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Agentic-Teacher: An Agentic Data Engine for Failure-Driven VLA Post-Training
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Gongyue Teng, Yuqing Xie, Yixian Zhang, Feng Gao, Shu'ang Yu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: Agentic-Teacher enhances vision-language-action models by autonomously generating and curating failure-driven demonstrations, significantly improving post-training success rates across various tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Improving a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) model requires demonstrations that address its weaknesses and provide effective supervision for learning. Coding agents can autonomously generate demonstrations through environment interaction, yet successful execution alone does not ensure effective supervision for VLA learning. We introduce Agentic-Teacher, an autonomous data engine for failure-driven VLA post-training. Given a VLA checkpoint, a task specification, and configured environment tools, the engine analyzes failed rollouts, selects intervention states, and iteratively develops closed-loop code policies through execution feedback. Validated policies become reusable demonstration generators that collect successful continuations from states where the VLA struggles. To make these demonstrations suitable for learning, Agentic-Teacher introduces temporally correlated action noise to broaden state-action coverage, removes idle frames while preserving gripper transitions, and filters trajectories using the frozen base model's flow-matching loss. The resulting demonstrations are combined with successful VLA rollouts for post-training, yielding an updated policy that operates without coding-agent assistance. Agentic-Teacher thus connects the weaknesses of a target VLA to both the generation and curation of its training data. In simulation, it improves $π_0$ success rates from 79.4% to 87.8% on LIBERO-10, from 80.4% to 90.6% on MetaWorld-10, and from 0% to 30.0% across three RoboCasa tasks.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ERA: Error-Resistant Autonomous Object Navigation with Predicted Depth
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Shunyang Huang, Shuo Wang, Wenyuan Xie, Mingyu Lin, Yue Ding
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ERA is a training-free object navigation system that utilizes predicted depth from RGB images to correct mapping errors and enhance exploration, achieving state-of-the-art performance without depth sensors.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Depth and 3D foundation models can predict geometry from RGB images, allowing zero-shot object navigation without a depth sensor. However, when predicted depth is mapped as if it came from a sensor, view-dependent errors accumulate in the map, remove exploration goals, and end the search before the agent can observe and correct them. We propose ERA, a training-free object navigation system that replaces the depth sensor with depth predicted from RGB images and poses. ERA follows a paradigm we call Move with Error: movement provides new views that correct map errors, and the corrected map enables further movement. It realizes this paradigm with revisable occupancy and with exploration from reachable viewpoints, which continues the search when no frontier remains, and verifies the target across views before stopping. On three benchmarks, ERA achieves state-of-the-art performance among training-free methods without depth sensors. Its map and exploration components also raise VLFM's success from 10.8% to 61.7% under the same predicted depth. We further deploy ERA on a real robot.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Beyond Prediction Gain: LASR as a Metric for Action-Grounded Latents in World Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yu Zhou, Changsong Lei, Yixiang Wei, Kairui Wen, Huankun Sheng
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper introduces the Latent Action Support Ratio (LASR) as a metric for evaluating action-grounded latents in world models, distinguishing genuine action encoding from predictive shortcuts.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: World models that support planning, control, and interpretable reasoning require latent representations that genuinely encode action. Yet the large-scale video data from which such models are learned overwhelmingly lack action annotations. Latent-action models infer action-like variables from observation sequences, enabling action-aware learning from unlabeled videos or trajectories. A fundamental concern, however, remains: a latent that improves future prediction may simply encode the current state, episode progress, task identity, or other predictive shortcuts. Existing evaluation practices---reconstruction loss, rollout fidelity, action recovery, or downstream performance---cannot isolate this distinction. We introduce the Latent Action Support Ratio (LASR), a dimensionless metric that measures, under offline evaluation on held-out data, whether a learned latent provides predictive support for action-related targets beyond the current state and non-action alternatives. LASR provides two complementary summaries: GeoLASR captures typical support, while WorstLASR identifies the weakest case. We instantiate the LASR benchmark with recorded actions and corresponding physical state changes as targets, episode-held-out splits, one predictor type for all comparisons, and positive and negative controls. Experiments on recorded robot manipulation data and a matched multi-task panel demonstrate that LASR detects known action information, rejects representative non-action shortcuts, and enables graded comparisons among imperfect latent representations. We further use LASR to train and audit a lightweight residual adapter, obtaining descriptively better point estimates whose uncertainty is assessed with paired comparisons. LASR thus provides a principled offline protocol for measuring action-related predictive support in world-model latents.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: PROOF: Perceptive Robustness via Out-of-Distribution Fallback for Legged Locomotion
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Siyuan Wang, Dongjie Zhu, Jinxuan Lu, Wenjun Xu, Jiankun Wang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The PROOF framework enhances legged robot locomotion robustness by integrating perception reliability modeling and fallback behaviors, ensuring stability under severe visual disturbances.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-based perceptive locomotion has enabled legged robots to achieve agile and terrain-aware locomotion across complex environments. However, the reliability of such systems heavily depends on visual observations, which are inherently susceptible to occlusion, reflective surfaces, and illumination variations, often resulting in catastrophic locomotion failures under degraded perception conditions. In this paper, we present PROOF (Perceptive Robustness via Out-of-Distribution Fallback for Legged Locomotion), a perceptive locomotion framework that enables robust locomotion under severe visual disturbances. Our method adopts a two-stage teacher-student learning paradigm that explicitly models perception reliability: the teacher learns both perception-driven and proprioceptive fallback behaviors, while the student predicts exteroceptive features with uncertainty and suppresses them under out-of-distribution inputs. We evaluate our method on a Unitree Go2 quadruped equipped with a RealSense D435 depth camera in real-world settings. Under normal visual conditions, our method enables the robot to successfully perform high-dynamic parkour maneuvers, including traversing large gaps, elevated platforms, and narrow beam terrains. Under severe visual degradation, such as heavy occlusion and strong illumination changes, the robot continues to maintain stable and robust locomotion performance.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: LLM-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning with Human-in-the-Loop Calibration for Real-Time Optimal Power Flow
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jiayang Tu, Bozhen Jiang, Bojun Du, Yunxiao Ling, Ershun Du
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: This paper presents an LLM-enhanced DRL framework with human-in-the-loop calibration to improve real-time optimal power flow decision-making by integrating semantic feedback and reliability checks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Real-time optimal power flow (RT-OPF) requires fast and reliable decision-making under time-varying operating conditions. However, many practical operating preferences and safety related requirements are difficult to encode using conventional numerical rewards alone, which limits the effectiveness and controllability of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for RT-OPF. To address this issue, this paper proposes an LLM-enhanced DRL framework with human-in-the-loop (HITL) for RT-OPF. The proposed method augments the physics-based reward with sparse language evaluative feedback during offline training, so that semantic operational requirements can be incorporated into policy learning. To improve reliability in RT-OPF, a selective HITL calibration mechanism is further introduced to inspect and correct questionable LLM judgments before they continuously shape the learning process. Case studies on the IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems show that LLM feedback improves policy safety over vanilla TD3, while further HITL calibration achieves the best overall performance and more stable training behavior. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining language guidance and expert calibration for RT-OPF.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Fast Inference-Time Policy Refinement via Action-Affine World Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Run Wang, Yilin Mo, Liang Wu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper presents an action-affine world model (A²WM) that efficiently refines imitation policies by predicting action sensitivities, enabling fast correction of execution errors during manipulation tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Imitation policies can perform complex manipulation, yet small execution errors can accumulate and cause failure. Refinement can correct these errors, but existing approaches often require additional on-policy learning or costly online planning. Our key insight is that a pretrained policy already supplies a useful nominal behavior: refinement can focus on predicting how small action corrections change its outcome. We therefore learn this local response in a form that is cheap to optimize. Our \textit{action-affine world model} (A\textsuperscript{2}WM) learns local action sensitivities offline from action-perturbed policy rollouts. Given interaction history and a policy proposal, it predicts task-relevant geometry as a nominal trajectory plus a linear response to corrections. It predicts the full planning horizon directly, avoiding the propagation of intermediate errors through recursive model evaluations. Quadratic penalties on predicted task errors and linear correction constraints then yield a cheap convex quadratic program (QP). Online refinement requires one model evaluation and one QP solve, while both policy and model weights remain frozen. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, our framework achieves the highest success rate among evaluated baselines, adding only 3.8 ms of mean refinement overhead per control step, excluding base-policy sampling.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: CFGComposer: Compositional Audio-Text-to-Motion Generation via Copula Score Correction
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Pengyang Shi, Jinlu Zhang, Chunze Lin, Yizhou Wang, Li Yi
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: CFGComposer addresses the Audio-Text-to-Motion challenge by refining joint inference through copula score correction, achieving superior semantic fidelity and beat alignment in embodied AI applications.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Generating whole-body gestures that are simultaneously rhythmically synchronized with speech audio and semantically aligned with text descriptions is a fundamental challenge in embodied AI and social robotics. We tackle this Audio-Text-to-Motion (AT2M) problem by composing two independently-trained diffusion models at inference time and refine bias in joint inference by modeling the copula score $s_I$. A rigorous theoretical analysis reveals that naive epsilon blending corresponds to a Product-of-Experts formulation that omits the copula score $s_I$: the cross-modal interaction between audio and text that neither marginal model can capture. We propose CFGComposer: a jointly-trained AT2M diffusion model that estimates $s_I$ via a CFG analogy and injects it as an $ε$-space correction. Experiments on BEAT demonstrate best-in-class semantic fidelity (SRGR $0.9916$, FID $27.18$) with GT-level beat alignment (BA $0.1826$ vs. GT $0.1743$), and 76-83% win rate in blind pairwise human evaluation against all prior methods. Physical deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid confirms direct sim-to-real transfer.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Haoran Luo, Shangkai Lin, Jinyang Wu, Xinliang Zhou, Luu Anh Tuan
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: HyperSkill introduces a training-free framework utilizing a hypergraph-indexed skill library to enhance reinforcement learning performance across multiple modalities without updating model parameters.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning sharpens LLM reasoning, but parameter updates are expensive, forgetful, and opaque; training-free libraries swap gradients for a textual store but still use trajectory-level, correlation-based admission and flat structure. To address both, we propose HyperSkill, a Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO framework that keeps the backbone frozen and replaces gradient updates with auditable edits to a Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library, where skills are advantage-bearing nodes and compositions are hyperedges. It has three components: training-time distillation admits counterfactually checked skills and learns a protocol skill from failures; gated hypergraph retrieval injects advantage-ranked skills where a per-dataset gate admits them; and an execution protocol makes the frozen backbone commit to an answer. On 11 text, vision-language, and omnimodal benchmarks, HyperSkill is best or tied on every dataset and beats the best baseline by 13.0 average F1 points while keeping the backbone frozen. Our software and data are publicly available at https://github.com/LHRLAB/HyperSkill.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Haojun Tang, Wenda Zhao, Xiang Zhou, Qiwei Lin, Lida Huang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: SkillEarth introduces a self-evolving skill extraction method for remote sensing agents, enabling adaptable, reusable skills without expert intervention or retraining, enhancing performance across multiple models.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Recently developed remote sensing (RS) agents execute real-world tasks with complex workflows through multi-step tool invocation. These agents, however, typically rely on predefined expertise or parameter updates. They thus require updating expert knowledge or retraining models whenever new tools, tasks, or execution patterns emerge, limiting their continual adaptability in dynamic Earth environments. In this work, we seek to equip general-purpose agents with RS tool-call knowledge that can be automatically extracted from demonstrated trajectories without expert intervention or parameter updates. Specifically, we propose SkillEarth, a self-evolving skill extraction method that externalizes RS tool-call knowledge as reusable, retrievable, and evolvable skill files and refines them through observation-grounded evolution. Unlike existing automatic skill extraction methods that rely on outcome-based reflection to refine skills holistically, SkillEarth grounds skill evolution in real tool-chain execution and combines dual-judge feedback with a grounded observation routing graph for precise component-level refinement. The resulting skills are generalizable, reliable, and transferable: they improve overall RS tool-call performance across three frontier LLMs and four open-source LLMs, are refined through real tool execution feedback, and support cross-model reuse without retraining. Experiments on OpenEarth-Bench and Earth-Bench demonstrate that SkillEarth achieves better tool selection, argument correctness, execution-order consistency, and task completion than existing RS agents and skill extraction methods.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ActionCodec2: A Streaming Action Tokenizer
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zibin Dong, Yicheng Liu, Shiduo Zhang, Tianyuan Yuan, Baijun Ye
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ActionCodec2 is a streaming action tokenizer that incrementally releases motion primitives, improving trajectory accuracy and performance in vision-language action models over traditional tokenizers.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Most action tokenizers for autoregressive vision language action (VLA) models compress motion into chunks that must be decoded in full before their actions become executable. We introduce ActionCodec2, a non-neural streaming tokenizer that releases actions incrementally while keeping trajectory reconstruction error within a prescribed tolerance. Its encoder quantizes each step relative to the decoder's reconstructed state, so the selected motion primitive corrects residual error rather than allowing errors from independently quantized increments to accumulate. Finding the smallest such primitive set is a geometric covering problem; we derive the exact minimum for translation and constant-factor-tight bounds for rotation. Set-BPE then losslessly merges co-occurring primitive symbols across coordinates and neighboring steps, without a fixed coordinate ordering. A universal version fitted on 20k hours of data from 24 embodiments averages 8.8 tokens per second for 15 Hz end-effector motion on this corpus. With the same VLA backbone, ActionCodec2 outperforms the compared tokenizers on three simulation benchmarks and in zero-shot real-robot evaluation. Its streaming representation allows policies to incorporate state feedback within an action chunk, substantially improving performance over open-loop execution under randomized dynamics, external disturbances, and moving objects. The same tokens also can serve as a direct control interface for VLM agents, which compose successful action sequences into reusable macros. These agent-built macros reduce control decisions and thinking-token usage across attempts and transfer to a held-out task. More results are available at https://zibindong.github.io/actioncodec2-page/

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Does Seeing More Mean Knowing More? Mono-Anchored Advantage Normalization for Multi-Source Visual Reasoning
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Fanhu Zeng, Zhicong Luo, Zefan Wang, You Li, Chi Chen
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper introduces MARS, a mono-anchored multi-source reasoning framework that improves visual reasoning by effectively integrating diverse information sources while minimizing interference, achieving notable performance gains.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Visual reasoning through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has achieved remarkable progress. However, when dealing with multi-source inputs, existing approaches tend to treat them as a mere accumulation of information, lacking explicit mechanisms to distinguish whether integrating additional sources yields information gain or introduces interference. Therefore, they struggle to effectively model dynamic interaction when integrating multiple sources, particularly when they differ significantly in physical properties and semantics, e.g., infrared and depth, leading to inferior performance to mono-source reasoning when a certain source holds the dominant signal. To address this issue, we propose MARS, a novel mono-anchored multi-source reasoning framework that models each visual modality as an independent information source. Specifically, by treating mono-source rewards as dynamic anchors, our method explicitly incorporates the information gain introduced by multi-source fusion into advantage normalization and adaptively emphasizes mutual promotion between sources while suppressing potential noise or conflicts during RLVR. From theoretical analysis, our method effectively quantifies information gain introduced by multi-source integration in gradient estimation, enabling consistent modality regulation. Empirical results also show impressive 3.2% and 4.9% performance gains on GRPO and DAPO across diverse datasets, confirming the effectiveness of our method. Code is available at https://github.com/AI9Stars/MARS.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: WISE: World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Chenhao Zhang, Hanyu Zhao, Zihan Que, Hang Cheng, Tengfei Pan
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: WISE introduces a framework for efficiently scheduling world-model imagination in post-training vision-language-action models, enhancing policy refinement and reducing computational costs while improving robustness.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Post-training VLA policies typically rely on supervised fine-tuning with costly expert demonstrations or reinforcement learning with expensive and potentially unstable real-world exploration. World models offer a promising alternative by evaluating candidate behaviors through imagined futures, yet effective post-training requires more than accurate prediction: imagination must be scheduled where it is useful, bounded within reliable horizons, and translated into trustworthy policy supervision. In robotic manipulation, the value of imagination varies substantially across execution stages, while extended rollouts can accumulate prediction errors and introduce unreliable learning signals. We introduce WISE (World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models), a unified framework that coordinates when and how world-model imagination is used during policy refinement. WISE selectively invokes imagination at interaction-relevant states, performs bounded multi-view rollouts, evaluates candidate futures using progress and completion signals, and uses their relative outcomes to refine actions generated from real interaction contexts. Extensive experiments with both $π_0$ and $π_{0.5}$ demonstrate consistent improvements across diverse manipulation tasks while reducing GPU computation time by approximately 80% compared with full imagination. Real-world evaluations further show substantial gains in robustness and generalization under diverse real-world distribution shifts.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zefan Wang, Yufan Dang, Xuanwei Shi, Mingqi Gao, Cheng Yin
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: JustRUA demonstrates that a simplified harness for GPT-6 Astra significantly enhances robot arm performance on RoboDojo, achieving a score increase from 29.7 to 50.3.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model. A lean harness that keeps the full episode history and stops each motion early goes a long way. Reusing experience changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch, and scene geometry helps most, even when depth is predicted from RGB alone. JustRUA starts from the official L3 harness and keeps only what matters most. Even with no learned policy, self-improvement loop or task-specific tuning, this simple harness raises the score on the RoboDojo simulation benchmark substantially, from 29.7 to 50.3.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jinze Tao, Yuxiao Han, Kangkang Dong, Yancong Wei, Xiaojun Zhu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The H2E method distills navigation experiences from agents into a VLA model, improving its success rate from 35.0% to 44.9% in unseen episodes.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Navigation agents use a large language model (LLM) planner to call a vision-language-action (VLA) model. Each episode needs the LLM, adding cost and delay. We distill successful agent experience into the VLA instead of distilling the planner. The VLA then navigates alone at test time. Agent sessions are not VLA demonstrations. They include motions driven by planner tools and sub-instructions, along with detours. We present H2E, a task-level experience distillation method that converts these sessions into VLA training data. Every motion becomes a VLA action under the original task instruction, with the resulting poses as targets. H2E masks the loss on steps that move away from the goal. It labels every visited state within 1 m of the goal as a stop. We then update the VLA with low-rank adaptation. The VLA learns to stop at the goal and find goals the base model never reaches. On all 3,189 REVERIE-CE val-unseen episodes, H2E raises the success rate of an 8B VLA from 35.0% to 44.9%.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Haofeng Wang, Pengcheng Wen, Ruiqi Li, Yuhao Zhang, Tiange Zhang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: PhysCapBench is a novel benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, evaluating annotation quality across diverse domains to enhance language supervision in physical AI applications.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning strategies, and guide training-data refinement. Motivated by our data construction for world-model pretraining, we introduce PhysCapBench, to our knowledge the first unified physical-caption benchmark spanning all three domains: third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It provides human-verified annotations for 1,500 video sequences and evaluates accuracy and coverage through seven physical dimensions. We examine downstream utility through video reconstruction and manipulation-policy fine-tuning. Physical captions reduce reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos relative to metadata captions. Training-instruction enrichment improves both PhysCapBench scores and policy success, including a 7.5-percentage-point gain for pi0.5 on a RoboTwin 2.0 subtask. PhysCapBench makes the physical content of language supervision inspectable and comparable, providing a cross-domain basis for its evaluation and improvement.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jiachun Jin, Zetong Zhou, Haonan Wang, Xiao Yang, Jun Zhu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: SALA enhances latent action models by aligning human and robot actions semantically using unpaired video descriptions, improving training efficiency and real-world robot task performance.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for latent actions. Without requiring paired data, we use the language descriptions of unpaired human and robot clips to estimate semantic similarities and supervise cross-embodiment correspondence. Specifically, we translate these similarities into soft neighborhood structures that guide human latent actions toward semantically related robot latents, while robot action reconstruction grounds the latent space in control. The resulting shared latent action space provides a unified supervision signal for training an embodied foundation model on both human and robot videos. Notably, latent action supervision enables scaling along two axes: (1) pre-training on increasing amounts of general human video consistently reduces robot action prediction error on downstream tasks, and (2) post-training on increasing amounts of task-specific human video substantially improves real-world robot task success rates.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: FORGE: Force-Aware Multi-Granularity Control for Efficient Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Liangjun Xing, Ke Fan, Kailin Li, Bin Wang, Xiaojie Niu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: FORGE is a novel force-aware control system for humanoid robots that enables efficient loco-manipulation through multi-granularity command processing and minimal input requirements.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated locomotion, balance regulation, and manipulation under frequent contacts, making teleoperated demonstration collection difficult: a practical controller must simultaneously provide precision, stability, and contact awareness. We propose FORGE, a force-aware multi-granularity control system with a coarse-to-fine command space spanning velocity navigation, planar foot placement, wrist-pose tracking, and optional force-conditioning inputs. Policy training requires no full-body human motion trajectories or joint-angle references; deployment consumes only sparse bilateral wrist poses relative to the pelvis, coarse motion commands, and optional desired wrist-load inputs. For sustained contact, FORGE combines a momentum observer with a learned correction trained using simulator contact-force supervision. At deployment, it estimates low-frequency, wrist-equivalent interaction forces from proprioception and reconstructed low-level arm PD torques, without wrist force/torque sensors. A quasi-static virtual-target loop uses this estimate and an optional desired applied-force input to adapt the wrist target. A frozen locomotion prior and asymmetric residual actions stabilize manipulation-induced whole-body corrections. Experiments evaluate unified-control stability, task-space tracking, quasi-static wrist-equivalent force estimation, squeezing forces during sustained contact with a rigid box, and downstream diffusion-policy execution of a squat-and-lift task across payload conditions. Website: https://bb0928.github.io/forge/.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: EMS-Nav: Embodied Multi-Scale Navigation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zenghui Yang, Xinan Wang, Danyang Li, Zhe Xu, Zheng Yang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: EMS-Nav is a biologically inspired framework that enhances multi-scale navigation efficiency for industrial inspection robots by organizing perception and navigation around local regions, improving success rates and reducing computational costs.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Industrial inspection robots must reach work areas and specific equipment. These destinations span spatial scales from regions to objects, so robots must relate each target to its surroundings to interpret the task and determine where to go. Existing methods support multi-scale navigation through rich environment representations, but at substantial computational and storage cost. These costs limit deployment where wireless coverage is incomplete and robots must rely on onboard computation to keep navigating. We introduce EMS-Nav, a biologically inspired multi-scale navigation framework for online, on-device operation. Its core innovation is to organize perception, spatial understanding, and navigation around regions, making local spaces the basic units of both environmental understanding and computation. EMS-Nav groups objects and their relationships into functionally meaningful spaces and builds a hierarchy from local areas to the broader environment. This organization supports efficient map construction alongside the interpretation and execution of language goals at different scales. In multi-scale navigation experiments, EMS-Nav achieves the highest success rates across all four target categories: objects, rooms, regions, and specific instances. It outperforms state-of-the-art open-vocabulary mapping and navigation methods, improving overall first-attempt success by 9.39 percentage points over the strongest baseline while reducing mapping overhead and language-model input size. Local deployment in real indoor environments further demonstrates its applicability to on-device embodied navigation. By establishing regions as the organizing basis for perception, spatial understanding, and language-guided action, EMS-Nav provides a system that combines multi-scale understanding with computational efficiency to support diverse language goals on resource-constrained robots.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: A Tactile-Informed Bi-Level Framework with Complementary Motion-Contact Planning and Tracking for Robust Model-Based In-Hand Manipulation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yongpeng Jiang, Mingrui Yu, Yi Ren, Xiang Li
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: This paper presents a bi-level framework integrating tactile feedback with model-based control for robust in-hand manipulation, enhancing accuracy and adaptability in real-world tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: In dexterous in-hand manipulation, learning-based methods achieve strong task performance with increasing generalization to unseen objects. A complementary advantage of model-based methods, central to this work, is online adaptation to new task specifications without policy retraining, given suitable system models. However, due to the complexity of physical contacts and limited sensing modalities, existing model-based methods still struggle with modeling errors, even when using advanced contact models or optimization schemes, which limit their real-world applications. To advance the effectiveness and robustness of model-based contact-rich in-hand manipulation, this paper proposes a novel bi-level framework with tactile incorporation to mitigate these limitations. Specifically, at the high level, reference finger motions and contacts are jointly generated via contact-implicit model predictive control. The high-level module enables online reactive planning and disturbance recovery. At the low level, these references are concurrently tracked through a hand force-motion model and tactile feedback. The low-level module compensates for modeling errors and enhances manipulation robustness. The complementarity between the two levels is manifested in two dimensions: 1) subsystem decomposition, with a slow optimization-based planning layer and a fast tactile-reactive control layer; and 2) functional decomposition, combining task-level optimality with contact-level stability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing model-based methods in accuracy and robustness, while supporting online replanning during execution. Our method successfully completes a diverse set of challenging tasks in real-world environments, even under appreciable external disturbances and modeling uncertainties.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Semantic-Coupled Perception Framework for Autonomous Laparoscope Control
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Enduo Zhao, Fangzhou Li, Yujie Zhu, Sicheng Lu, Fang Chen
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper presents a closed-loop framework for autonomous laparoscope control that integrates surgical phase recognition with visual perception to enhance target visibility and task execution in minimally invasive surgery.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: In minimally invasive surgery (MIS), maintaining an appropriate field of view (FoV) is essential for surgical safety and efficiency. However, conventional autonomous laparoscope control methods often treat visual tracking and surgical phase recognition independently, limiting robustness under occlusion, entity overlap, and camera motion. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous laparoscope control framework that couples real-time surgical phase recognition with camera-motion-compensated visual perception. By exploiting phase-dependent relationships among surgical entities, the framework improves target state estimation under challenging visual conditions, supporting task-aware autonomous FoV control. Benchmark and phantom experiments evaluate the framework in surgical phase recognition, target tracking under occlusion and entity overlap, and autonomous FoV control, showing improved target visibility and task execution compared with fixed-FoV control. These results highlight the potential of incorporating task-level semantics into visual state estimation for autonomous laparoscope guidance.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ActWorld-JEPA: Action-Conditioned JEPA World Models Meet Latent Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Ziying Song, Shengkai Zhang, Caiyan Jia, Lei Yang, Lin Liu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ActWorld-JEPA integrates action-conditioned latent prediction with relational reranking for improved autonomous driving decision-making, achieving high performance on benchmark evaluations.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) enable future prediction in latent space without pixel reconstruction. However, latent predictive consistency alone does not establish the relative driving quality of candidate plans. We present ActWorld-JEPA, a joint-embedding formulation for candidate-based driving. Where Plan-Conditioned JEPA (PC-JEPA) uses global and step-wise trajectory intentions to guide recurrent latent prediction, then combines the predicted future with the current scene through gated cross-attention; Relational Residual Reranking ($R^3$) models agreement and discrepancy between plan and future representations under planning supervision, yielding bounded, gated residual corrections to the base planning scores. This formulation connects latent prediction to candidate selection using only observed context and proposed trajectories at inference. Benchmark-specific implementations report 94.1 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, with the final selector calibrated using aggregate NAVTEST feedback, and 91.6 and 42.7 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest and navhard, respectively. The nuScenes evaluation reports a mean $L_2$ error of 1.20 m and a predicted collision rate of 0.76% over 1--6 s.
