智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: ResMerge introduces a two-stage framework for efficient continual adaptation of pre-trained robot policies, utilizing residual reinforcement learning and parameter-space merging to minimize parameter growth and reliance on demonstrations.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Continual adaptation to new tasks is essential for robots deployed in the real world, but adapting pre-trained policies remains challenging due to parameter growth and the need for continual demonstration collection. Parameter-Efficient Continual Fine-Tuning (PECFT) isolates task-specific updates, but adapter-per-task designs require demonstrations and grow with the task set. We propose ResMerge, a two-stage framework that learns mergeable residual policies atop a frozen pre-trained policy: residual reinforcement learning (RL) acquires task-specific corrections without additional expert demonstrations during adaptation, and parameter-space merging consolidates compatible residuals to reduce stored parameters. We introduce Residual-Field Consistency (RFC), a simple, bounded, and interpretable metric that assesses compatibility in residual action-field space by comparing correction direction and magnitude. Experiments on LIBERO across two backbones and on a real-world Franka robot show improved continual learning performance over strong PECFT baselines, while selective merging reduces the residual-parameter footprint. Project website: https://resmerge.github.io/.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Wendong Bu, Tinghong Ye, Qizhou Wang, Jiacheng Li, Zhiqi Ge
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: Movens-Zero enhances humanoid motion foundation models by leveraging 15 million human-motion sequences for real-time, multimodal learning and execution across diverse inputs.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Scaling humanoid motion foundation models is constrained by the scarcity of diverse, robot-executable data and by the difficulty of jointly learning from heterogeneous multimodal inputs while supporting real-time closed-loop control. We present Movens-5M, constructed from raw Internet videos through clip generation, quality filtering, semantic annotation, motion recovery, and physical refinement with humanoid retargeting and execution verification. It contains 15 million human-motion sequences and 5 million physically executable humanoid-motion sequences spanning over 10,000 hours, aligned with text, RGB video, speech, and music. Building on this data, we introduce Movens-Zero, a scalable understanding-generation-execution architecture that supports joint learning across modalities and real-time closed-loop execution. Task-mixed flow-matching training jointly optimizes a single action expert across seven generation tasks, enabling direct motion generation from text, speech, music, and video. Multimodal Real-Time Chunking connects overlapping chunks under continuously updated instructions and robot states for continuous closed-loop execution. We further introduce Movens-Intent, a four-track benchmark with 8,192 expert-verified condition-motion pairs across text, speech, music, and video. Experiments show consistent gains across all four modalities when scaling execution-verified data from 1% to 100% and action-expert capacity from 64M to 911M parameters, while demonstrating that data quality and cross-modal supervision improve generation and execution.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Feng Chen, Jianguo Huang, Yushan Xiao, Yue Li, Bijun Tang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: FrontierMat introduces a benchmark of 330 validated research problems to evaluate language models' effectiveness in advanced materials discovery, highlighting significant performance gaps and improvement strategies.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. The strongest general-purpose model scores only 53.7%, and on matched problems, cross-scale problems score 8.7 points below single-scale ones. Half of the problems are solved by at most one model, and models fail chiefly by endorsing what is plausible rather than what was observed. A domain-adaptation study with meta-weighted continued pretraining and scale-modular self-distillation raises an open-weight model from 36.7% to 55.4%, matching the strongest proprietary model, with improvements on public materials benchmarks and no decline in aggregate performance on general benchmarks. FrontierMat provides a testbed for measuring progress toward language models that support frontier materials R&D.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Semantic-Enriched Latent Visual Reasoning
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Tianrun Xu, Yue Sun, Qixun Wang, Jingyi Lu, Yuan Wang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: SLVR enhances latent visual reasoning by integrating attribute-level semantics and aligning representations across queries, supported by a comprehensive dataset and benchmark for evaluation.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Multimodal latent-space reasoning aims to replace explicit thinking with images by performing visual reasoning directly in a compact latent space. However, existing approaches largely rely on visual supervision and produce latent representations that lack sufficient semantic richness, limiting their ability to support diverse region-level reasoning tasks. In this work, we introduce Semantic-Enriched Latent Visual Reasoning (SLVR), a two-stage learning framework that enriches latent representations with attribute-level visual semantics and aligns them with diverse reasoning objectives. In the first stage, SLVR learns semantically enriched region-centric latents under fine-grained attribute supervision. In the second stage, we design Multi-query Group Relative Policy Optimization (M-GRPO) to align latent representations across multiple queries grounded in the same region. To support this framework, we construct SLV-Set, comprising approximately 400K region-level attribute annotations and 800K multi-query question answering samples, and introduce SV-QA, a benchmark that evaluates latent reasoning under semantic variation. Experiments demonstrate that SLVR improves the robustness and semantic consistency of latent visual reasoning compared to existing baselines.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: From Reasoning to Action: Consequence-Grounded Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yixue Zhang, Wenke Xia, Kun Wu, Wenbo Yu, Pei Ren
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: CoRAct introduces a framework that explicitly aligns reasoning and action in vision-language-action models through reward-guided optimization, enhancing task success and generalization.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Reasoning informs decision-making by connecting intended actions with their expected consequences. Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models incorporate embodied chains of thought (ECoTs) to guide action generation. However, such guidance remains implicit, as actions are conditioned on ECoTs rather than explicitly optimized to align with them. We introduce CoRAct, a consequence-grounded reasoning-to-action alignment framework that explicitly aligns reasoning and action through reward-guided optimization in action noise space. CoRAct formulates two physically grounded ECoT components as verifiable signals: movement specifies intended motion, while waypoints encode expected spatial consequences. A unified Mixture-of-Transformers jointly models ECoT reasoning, action generation, and action-conditioned future prediction. For candidate actions generated from sampled noise, CoRAct computes alignment rewards based on movement consistency and agreement between predicted outcomes and specified waypoints. These rewards guide group-relative optimization of the initial noise distribution, steering action generation toward consistency with intended actions and expected consequences. Experiments across RoboCasa, VLABench, and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate improvements in task success, generalization, and reasoning-execution alignment over strong ECoT-based VLA baselines. CoRAct also grounds externally provided ECoTs in executable behavior, enabling zero-shot adaptation to novel scenarios by leveraging knowledge from powerful vision-language models. Project page and dataset: https://onlyxingxingzyx.github.io/CoRAct/

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: TactoHand: Learning Geometry-Based Dense Hand-Surface Interaction Fields from Video
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Ziheng Xi, Weibo Li, Jiayi Yu, Sipeng Zheng, Wanpeng Zhang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: TactoHand predicts dense hand-surface interaction fields from monocular video using geometry-based labels and a temporal transformer, improving estimation and motion accuracy without tactile data collection.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Understanding how humans interact with the world requires a representation of physical interactions at the hand surface. Tactile sensing captures these interactions, but collecting tactile data at scale requires specialized hardware. We introduce TactoHand, a model that predicts three dense hand-surface interaction fields---contact, proximity, and 3D force---from monocular video. We derive geometry-based contact and proximity labels and motion-derived force labels from eligible training data within a curated collection spanning approximately 50 million source frames. TactoHand uses a temporal transformer to aggregate visual evidence across frames, while three learned queries decode the corresponding hand-surface fields. A differentiable physics layer further constrains force predictions using observed object motion. Across in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, TactoHand improves contact and proximity estimation over prior methods. In addition, physics supervision reduces position and rotation errors in motion rollouts, and the predicted contact and proximity fields improve downstream hand-object reconstruction. Together, these results show a scalable, low-cost path to learning hand-surface interaction fields without collecting tactile measurements. Code will be released at https://github.com/zhenqis123/Tactohand.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: PhysAg3D: Bridging 3D Generative and Agentic Models for High-Fidelity and Physically-Interactive Assets
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Bi'an Du, Fanpeng Meng, Jiemin Fang, Chen Yang, Pufan Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: PhysAg3D integrates 3D generative models with agentic reasoning to create interactive, physically realistic 3D assets from single images, enhancing fidelity and plausible behavior.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Generating interactive 3D assets from a single image requires realistic appearance, fidelity to the depicted object, and plausible physical behavior. Yet detailed geometry alone does not determine how an object should move or deform. We introduce PhysAg3D, which couples 3D generative models with agentic reasoning and tool use. A vision-language agent first infers semantic parts, candidate interactions, and physical priors from the image; a 3D generator then produces a textured whole-object mesh from the same image. A hierarchical interaction representation links these revisable priors to mechanisms and the generated surfaces they control, organizing interaction construction and refinement. Guided by this representation and observations of the mesh, the agent uses geometric and physical tools to construct parts, joints, deformable regions, and surface bindings while retaining useful generated geometry and materials. Rendered interactions and execution measurements guide targeted revisions within a fixed budget. The framework accommodates both rigid articulation and compliant deformation. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations on real photographs and external benchmarks demonstrate detailed, image-aligned assets with plausible interactions. Ablations support bounded refinement and source-surface preservation. Project Page: supra-3d.github.io/PhysAg3D.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Reward-Adaptive Co-Evolution of Policy and Rubric
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yizhu Chen, Jianguang Jiang, Jiameng Huang, Chuyu Fang, Bojun Zhang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: RACE is a novel framework that adaptively co-evolves policies and rubrics in reinforcement learning, enhancing performance and rubric discrimination through dynamic training signal routing and phase optimization.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Rubric-based rewards provide fine-grained, interpretable supervision for open-ended reinforcement learning, where holistic scalar rewards struggle to capture multidimensional response quality. Static rubrics can lose discriminative power as the policy distribution evolves, while existing policy--rubric co-evolution methods rely on globally prescribed update schedules that ignore heterogeneous reward informativeness. We introduce RACE, a Reward-Adaptive Co-Evolution framework. At the group level, per-rollout-group training-signal routing classifies groups as informative, diversity-collapsed, or rubric-failed, updating the policy only with informative groups while caching rubric failures. At the phase level, event-triggered phase switching enters rubric optimization upon persistent reward saturation and returns when rubric-reward improvement plateaus. Rubric phases train the generator on cached pairs using a frozen judge and a scale-normalized pairwise-margin reward. Across both levels, online threshold adaptation adjusts routing and switching thresholds through proportional control. Under a unified evaluation protocol, RACE achieves the highest average performance and outperforms the strongest fixed-alternation baseline on all eight tasks, while improving rubric discrimination.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: TaskFrame: Connecting Task-Level Planning with Frame-Level Control for Game Agents
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Guangzhi Wang, Junfu Pu, Yiran Wang, Xingyilang Yin, Honghao Chen
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: TaskFrame integrates task-level planning and frame-level control in game agents, enhancing performance in dynamic environments through a hierarchical planner-controller framework.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Building general game agents requires both high-level task reasoning and low-latency action control in rapidly changing visual environments. These capabilities favor models with substantially different computational profiles, making them difficult to realize within a single model. In this work, we present TaskFrame, a hierarchical planner-controller framework that connects task-level planning with frame-level keyboard-and-mouse control. A vision-language task planner decomposes a high-level goal into an ordered sequence of atomic instructions and is optimized through supervised learning and dependency-aware GRPO. The hidden states of special goal tokens that terminate each atomic instruction provide continuous goal embeddings that are cached and reused across control steps. A causal Transformer controller combines the embedding of the active goal with recent observations to predict discrete keyboard and mouse-button actions and continuous camera motion at every game step. We train the system in three stages: planner training, controller pretraining, and joint alignment. Experiments in Minecraft show that TaskFrame is competitive with general-purpose vision-language models on instruction decomposition, and that in closed-loop evaluation the agent achieves a higher combat success rate than the evaluated baselines.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: RFW-A: Agentic Procedural Generation of 400K Articulated Assets over 500 Categories
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yuanbo Lyu, Changjian Pan, Saining Zhang, Yi Yang, Peishuo Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: RFW-A introduces a novel paradigm for generating over 400K articulated assets efficiently by combining agentic synthesis with procedural generation, significantly reducing costs and improving asset validity.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: High-quality articulated assets are essential for embodied perception, simulation, and manipulation, yet constructing them at scale remains difficult. Manual annotation and procedural modeling require substantial human effort. Recent agentic systems automate asset construction through program synthesis, but repeat costly reasoning and refinement for every new asset. Our key observation is that assets within a category can share construction logic despite variations in structure and appearance. Agentic synthesis and procedural generation are therefore complementary: agents can construct reusable programs, while procedural execution reuses the resulting logic across many samples. We therefore present RFW-A, which combines the two in a new articulated-asset generation paradigm. Starting from existing articulated programs, RFW-A organizes reusable components and their dependencies into category-level generators. Agents test and refine these generators across sampled configurations and motion states. Once constructed and validated, the generators produce diverse assets through procedural execution with no further model calls or token charges. The estimated API cost of generator authoring averages $10.62, amortizing to $0.05 per asset over 200 assets, versus $1.24 for the sampled per-asset agentic synthesis baseline. Using RFW-A, we built RFW-A-400K, containing over 400K sim-ready articulated assets across more than 500 categories. Experiments show high structural and kinematic validity and stable execution across physics simulators. Beyond asset validity, training with RFW-A-400K improves part-level articulation estimation on seen and unseen categories, while policies trained in simulation with retrieved and program-edited assets transfer zero-shot to real articulated objects.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: TouchBridge: Tactile-Conditioned Human-to-Robot Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Haozhe Zhang, Gu Zhang, Zirui Zou, Yuzheng Chen, Jinlong Wu
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: TouchBridge enables efficient human-to-robot transfer of dexterous manipulation through tactile-conditioned retargeting, achieving high success rates with faster demonstration collection compared to traditional methods.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Human demonstrations offer an efficient and scalable source of data for dexterous robot manipulation, but differences in sensing and hand morphology complicate the transfer of contact-rich interactions. We present TouchBridge, a hardware--software co-designed framework for human-to-robot data transformation. A wearable human demonstration interface and a corresponding robot interface establish cross-embodiment correspondence in visual and fingertip tactile sensing. We introduce Tac-Retarget, a tactile-conditioned retargeting method that uses measured contact to align fingertip contact patches and preserve their spatial relations within and across hands. Unlike object-aware or simulation-based transfer pipelines, Tac-Retarget requires no object mesh, object-pose estimate, or physics simulation for retargeting, enabling direct and scalable conversion of human demonstrations into robot-domain training data. Combined with visual synthesis and camera-anchored action conversion, TouchBridge produces robot-domain demonstrations for fine-tuning a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) model. Across four real-world contact-rich tasks, policies fine-tuned solely on TouchBridge-converted human demonstrations achieve a 72.5% average success rate, compared with 77.5% using an equal number of teleoperated robot demonstrations, while human demonstration collection is 7.0x faster. Under the same policy and training setup, Tac-Retarget outperforms DexPilot and UniDex by 25.0 and 42.5 percentage points, respectively.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Event2Reward: Learning Robotic Rewards from Progress Relations
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Junnan Nie, Zitian Fan, Jiachen Zhang, Junyi Lao, Likui Zhang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: Event2Reward enhances robotic reinforcement learning by leveraging local progress relations from demonstrations to improve reward shaping, achieving significant success rate increases across various tasks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Learning task progress from robot demonstrations provides a practical way to construct dense shaping rewards for robotic reinforcement learning. A common approach uses normalized demonstration time as progress labels, implicitly assuming monotonically increasing task progress. During policy exploration, however, actual task progress can stall or even regress. Such models may mistake regressions for progress, assigning positive shaping rewards to actions that cause progress loss. Real suboptimal and failed executions offer corrective experience, but assigning absolute progress values to their states is difficult. Our key observation is that stalls, regressions, and recoveries establish local relative progress relations even when absolute progress is unknown. We introduce Event2Reward, which uses normalized temporal labels to anchor the progress scale and these within-trajectory relations to constrain local changes, combining absolute and relative progress supervision. Its progress predictions serve as potentials for reward shaping. We curate an event-annotated dataset from approximately 100K raw real-robot execution records, covering successful, suboptimal, and failed executions, without requiring framewise absolute progress labels. Under the same training budgets, Event2Reward improves average policy success by 18.16 percentage points over a baseline using only sparse task rewards across 40 tasks in four LIBERO suites. On real robots, average success after 30 minutes of wall-clock training reaches 60.0% on three precise insertion tasks and 90.0% on three object manipulation tasks, exceeding the sparse-reward baseline under the same budget by 36.7 and 23.3 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies further show that absolute progress supervision and relative progress relations are complementary, with joint supervision yielding better downstream policy learning.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Aligned Delta-Triplane Transformers as Occupancy World Models
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Haoran Xu, Peixi Peng, Shijun Guo, Guang Tan, Yiqian Chang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The Aligned Delta-Triplane Transformer (ADTT) efficiently predicts future 3D occupancy changes in autonomous driving by aligning historical data and compensating for ego motion.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Occupancy World Models (OWMs) aim to predict future 3D occupancy scenes from historical observations and future ego motions, providing a useful world simulation tool for autonomous driving. Existing methods usually rely on large networks to implicitly align multi-frame historical states and predict future occupancy in a full-state manner, which is costly and redundant because most scene regions remain unchanged over short time intervals. In this paper, we propose Aligned Delta-Triplane Transformer (ADTT), a compact 4D OWM that explicitly aligns historical triplanes with ego-motion compensation and predicts only future scene changes. Based on the aligned triplane prior, a query-conditioned Transformer predicts residual changes, where ego-motion queries guide controllable future motion and learnable external queries capture scene changes beyond ego motion. The predicted changes are added to the aligned prior and decoded into future occupancy scenes. Experiments on Occ3D-nus show that ADTT achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance with fewer parameters and higher FPS. Our code is publicly available online: https://github.com/kyoran/ADTT.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: LaWAM: Latent World Action Models for Efficient Dynamics-Aware Robot Policies
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Jialei Chen, Kai Wang, Kang Chen, Shuaihang Chen, Feng Gao
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: LaWAM introduces a Latent World Action Model that enhances robot control by predicting future dynamics through compact latent visual subgoals, achieving state-of-the-art performance with low latency.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) leverage large-scale vision-language pretraining for semantic robot control, but often lack explicit foresight into how robot actions change the scene. World-Action Models (WAMs) address this limitation by conditioning policies on predicted futures, yet existing approaches typically rely on computationally expensive video generation with substantial pixel-level redundancy. We present LaWAM, a Latent World Action Model that exposes predictive dynamics to robot policies through compact latent visual subgoals instead of reconstructed future video. At the core of LaWAM is a latent-action-conditioned Latent World Model (LaWM). We obtain LaWM by training a latent action model in the latent space of a pretrained vision foundation model and repurposing its forward decoder to predict future observation features for scene evolution. LaWAM then conditions action generation on these predicted latent visual subgoals to enable dynamics-aware robot control. LaWAM achieves state-of-the-art or competitive success rates (SRs) across LIBERO (98.6% SR), RoboTwin (91.22% SR), and real-world manipulation tasks while retaining low-latency inference. LaWAM runs in 187 ms per action-chunk prediction and achieves up to 24x lower wall-clock latency than pixel-space WAMs.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: AI for Science in Space: Orbital Laboratories, Planetary Fieldwork, and Embodied Autonomy
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zizhe Wang, Jia Deng, Xin Lu, Zehao Jia, Yi Huang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper reviews the role of AI in enhancing scientific experimentation in space through autonomous robotics, addressing challenges in data interpretation, execution, and evidence validity.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Artificial intelligence for science (AI4S) is extending from interpretation of existing data to the design and execution of experiments. Space offers distinctive scientific opportunities while restricting physical support. Microgravity and extraterrestrial environments expose phenomena that terrestrial experiments cannot fully reproduce; finite samples, constrained resources, and limited opportunities for intervention complicate sustained investigation. This critical review examines orbital laboratories and planetary in situ science across biology, materials, fluid and thermal physics, and adaptive exploration. We distinguish learning from space-derived data, selecting scientific actions, executing them, and preserving experimental validity. Terrestrial self-driving laboratories provide complementary evidence on optimization, dedicated automation, robotic manipulation, and the support needed for unattended operation. The synthesis connects scientific gains already demonstrated by bounded AI systems to gaps in observation, executable actions, and continuity of valid evidence. Space robots can expand the attainable scope of autonomous science when necessary interventions exceed validated instrument capabilities and timely human support is unavailable. Their value must be established against dedicated mechanisms, redundancy, and human-supported operation. We develop a framework connecting sample history, scientific decisions, physical execution, and claim-specific validity. A worked orbital design, a planetary extension, and matched evaluation schemes separate the contributions of sensing, decision policies, and physical actions. The resulting agenda measures autonomy through valid scientific return, task coverage, intervention costs, and evidence integrity across complete campaigns.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: WorldProbe: When Video World Models Fall Apart under Long-Horizon Spatial Exploration
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Minqi Wang, Jie Peng, Hejun Dong, Ruchang Yao, Puyi Wang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: WorldProbe introduces a benchmark revealing that video world models struggle with long-horizon exploration, highlighting inconsistencies in long-range memory despite improved local generation quality.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Video world models generate future visual observations from camera or action inputs, with the goal of synthesizing persistent 3D worlds that can be explored across time and space. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate short interactions or rely on camera trajectories fixed before generation. The performance of video world models under long-horizon exploration with extensive camera motion remains under-explored. We introduce WorldProbe, a diagnostic benchmark that uses a goal-conditioned multimodal agent to adapt camera actions online during generation. WorldProbe comprises 164 test cases across four probing families. Across 10 state-of-the-art models, we generate more than 1,600 rollouts totaling approximately 800 minutes, with horizons up to 180 seconds. Our evaluation across four dimensions reveals both the degradation of local measures and the emergence of long-range inconsistencies. We find that recent models sustain visual and content quality for longer, while long-range memory and evolution remain weak. These results expose a gap between locally stable generation and persistent world consistency that is largely missed by existing benchmarks. Code and benchmark resources are available at https://github.com/Untitled-W/WorldProbe.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: MemPrism: Task-Conditioned Relational Memory Views for Long-Horizon Agents
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Bingfan Zeng, Zhisheng Chen, Zhengwei Xie, Bangde Cao, Yuxuan Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: MemPrism introduces a task-conditioned relational memory framework that enhances long-horizon agent performance by dynamically constructing relevant memory views for decision-making.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Long-horizon agents performing multi-step Web tasks must reuse earlier page observations and interactions to support subsequent actions. However, preserving relevant history does not ensure that it exposes the relations needed for the current decision. We call this gap representation mismatch. To this end, we propose MemPrism, a task-conditioned relational memory framework that separates persistent experience storage from decision-time working memory. MemPrism records interactions as the event stream and dynamically constructs relational views according to the current task context. A lightweight view policy selects the relation structure, evidence range, outcome condition, and granularity, while a deterministic composer and renderer transform historical facts into a temporary optical working-memory view for a frozen task policy. Experiments on long-horizon embodied and web-agent benchmarks show that MemPrism consistently improves the task performance, especially as trajectories become longer, while reducing memory token consumption. Furthermore, the learned view policy transfers across different VLMs without additional adaptation, demonstrating the effectiveness of task-conditioned relational views as a general memory interface for agents.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Ziyang Zeng, Tingyang Chen, Jia Deng, Qiyao Wang, Shuo Tang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: WorkFactory is a scalable framework that transforms professional intents into executable tasks, enhancing agent training through structured planning and repair, demonstrated across 112,686 tasks and improved model performance.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Scaling supervised training for working agents requires diverse professional tasks that yield reliable expert demonstrations. However, missing or inconsistent task information can obstruct teacher execution and weaken the resulting supervision. We propose WorkFactory, a scalable framework for constructing coherent and executable professional tasks. Starting from professional intents, information-level planning builds an information support graph to guide task instantiation, explicitly representing the dependencies and locations of information required for the intended outputs. Probe executions then identify support failures and guide repairs while preserving the intended work. We construct 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and use the collected teacher trajectories to fine-tune Qwen models at 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B scales, yielding the WorkPilot family. All three models improve over their respective base models across four professional-work benchmarks, with WorkPilot-35B-A3B improving from 879 to 1565 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1. Scaling analyses reveal model-dependent diminishing returns, with execution length first increasing and then decreasing. Controlled component analyses show that planning and repair reduce probe-diagnosed task environment defects and improve downstream performance. The data and models are available at https://github.com/IQuestLab/WorkFactory.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: FAWAM: Force-Aware World Action Models for Closed-Loop Contact-Rich Manipulation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Haotian He, Zeyu Yan, Qipeng Liu, Ning Guo, Wenzhao Lian
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: FAWAM enhances contact-rich robotic manipulation by integrating force signals into perception, prediction, and execution, improving success rates significantly over existing methods.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Force signals provide critical interaction cues for contact-rich robotic manipulation. However, existing methods mostly use force as an additional observation modality, without fully exploiting its role in modeling future interaction dynamics or guiding execution-time feedback correction. In this paper, we propose FAWAM, a force-aware world action model that incorporates force information at three levels: perception, prediction, and closed-loop execution. FAWAM first encodes historical 6-axis force/torque signals to modulate action generation, then jointly predicts future actions and end-effector wrenches to explicitly model contact evolution. It further introduces a residual correction module that uses the predicted wrench trajectory as an execution-time reference to refine actions online based on real-time force feedback. Real-world experiments across multiple contact-rich tasks show that FAWAM improves the average success rate by 36.25% over vision-only baselines and 21.25% over existing force-aware baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of our force-aware framework for robust contact-rich manipulation.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: MemVLN: Streaming Episodic Memory for Vision-Language Navigation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yan Wang, Jiangyong Huang, Siyuan Huang, Baoxiong Jia
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: MEMVLN introduces a streaming episodic memory framework for vision-language navigation, enhancing long-horizon task performance and achieving state-of-the-art results on VLN benchmarks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Vision-language navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to follow language instructions through 3D environments. Maintaining persistent episodic memory remains a challenge for VLM-based streaming agents in long-horizon navigation. We present MEMVLN, a streaming episodic memory framework that maintains a bounded bank of compressed perceptual features annotated with timesteps and action-derived relative poses, and produces compact memory tokens via cross-attention. We pair the proposed memory with a frozen pretrained geometry encoder. To learn the memory module, we design a masking-based trajectory summarization task with multi-granularity sub-trajectory decomposition, encouraging route reconstruction exclusively from episodic memory. Under navigation training restricted to the official R2R/RxR trajectories, MEMVLN achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics on standard VLN-CE benchmarks. Long-horizon analyses further characterize when episodic memory is useful. For physical evaluation, we collect 30 instruction-conditioned episodes in one physical scene, use 24 as demonstrations for post-training, and hold out six for testing. On the held-out episodes, MEMVLN improves success over the VLM baseline from 17% to 40%, and post-training further raises it to 47%.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: UnityBench-Mini3D: Evaluating LLM Agents for 3D Game Development in Unity
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yijun Zhou, Minghao Shao, Ke Zhang, Renkai Yuan, Hongbo Yuan
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: UnityBench-Mini3D is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in Unity game development, featuring 77 project-level tasks across varying difficulties and providing objective performance assessments.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Game development stresses coding agents in ways general software engineering does not: correctness depends on how engine APIs, serialized scene state, and runtime behavior interact, not on source code alone. Existing benchmarks mainly target platforms such as Godot and heavily rely on LLM judges or coarse task-level outcomes. We present UnityBench-Mini3D, a benchmark of 77 project-level Unity tasks organized around seven expert-defined skill categories rather than tutorials or genres, with three difficulty tiers. Each task pairs a complete Unity project with natural-language requirements and is evaluated using 1,178 held-out, human-authored milestone tests covering scene structure, component configuration, and runtime behavior. This in-engine evaluation provides deterministic partial credit, localizes failures, and distinguishes partial implementations from complete solutions without relying on subjective judges. Across 21 models and 9 coding harnesses, the average pass rate reaches 80.9% on easy tasks but falls to 35.2% on hard tasks, with just 57.7% overall. UnityBench-Mini3D provides a reproducible, diagnostic testbed distinguishing systems across difficulty levels.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Learning to Code the World: Harness Evolution for Compositional 3D Reconstruction
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Haoyu Yao, Chenguo Lin, Ruize Du, Yadong Mu
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: SceneEvolve introduces a framework for compositional 3D reconstruction by evolving a harness around a small agent, improving efficiency and quality without parameter updates.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Reconstructing editable and compositional 3D scenes from a real image requires jointly reasoning about geometry, object structure, and spatial relationships. We introduce SceneEvolve, a framework that represents 3D scenes as executable code and improves reconstruction by evolving the harness around a small open-source agent. SceneEvolve combines SceneAct, a compositional semantic action interface built on parameterized primitives, hierarchical composition, and semantic spatial relations, with SceneHarness-RSI, which leverages a stronger teacher agent to iteratively evolve the harness using feedback from development-set reconstructions. Throughout harness evolution, the model parameters, action semantics, and execution backend remain fixed. The resulting harness provides a reusable reconstruction procedure that enables the small open-source model to reconstruct unseen scenes without parameter updates or teacher assistance. Across two in-domain datasets and one out-of-domain dataset, SceneEvolve with the comparatively compact Qwen3.8-27B model improves all four evaluated reconstruction metrics while reducing mean inference time by 47.0% relative to the base model. More notably, despite relying on a substantially smaller model, SceneEvolve achieves 32.3% higher reconstruction quality than the large proprietary GPT-5.6-Sol model, while reducing mean equivalent deployment cost by 59.8%. Furthermore, the harness evolved using Qwen3.8-27B also generalizes to Kimi-K3, achieving comparable reconstruction performance to GPT-6-Astra. The project page is https://haoyu-agent.github.io/SceneEvolve.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: How Much Can Best-of-N Help a World Action Model? Measuring Selectable Headroom and Realizing It in Closed Loop
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Haojia Gao, Yue Cao, Yumin Liu, Haohua Que, Mingkai Liu
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: This paper presents a novel protocol for measuring and realizing selectable headroom in world action models, enhancing task success rates through improved action selection strategies.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict the visual consequences of the actions they generate, which makes test-time selection a natural way to improve a fixed policy: imagine the futures of candidate actions and execute the best one. The benefit of selection is bounded by the selectable headroom, how much better the best candidate truly is, but the standard estimate, which executes each candidate once and keeps the best outcome, conflates candidate quality with the randomness of everything that follows. We introduce a denoised counterfactual protocol, based on bitwise-reproducible branching, repeated continuations, held-out oracles, and common random numbers, that measures the headroom a selector can realize, and use its measurements to build a fail-gated selector. Across four WAMs, two benchmarks, over 100,000 branched rollouts, and pre-registered tests, we find that (i) the standard estimate overstates the selectable headroom of native samples: bounds from 17 continuations per candidate place its selectable share between 24% and 66% for three WAMs; (ii) structured action perturbations create up to 16 points of selectable headroom; and (iii) in both WAMs with action-conditioned imagination, imagined futures carry candidate-outcome information with no detectable loss relative to real futures, information that the value head of Cosmos Policy leaves unused. Deviating from the policy chunk only when a readout of the WAM predicts failure, the selector raises closed-loop task success from 76.9% to 81.6% on held-out episodes of training tasks, with the largest gain where the policy fails most often, and from 62.6% to 69.8% on unseen tasks.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Hanqing Wang, Zhaotian Cai, Ruichuan An, Bohan Zeng, Tao Zhang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: PDRVLA enhances Vision-Language-Action models by integrating a Physical Dynamics Module for efficient action generation from visual and linguistic inputs without video latency, achieving high success rates in simulations.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Detailed balance in large language model-driven agents
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zhuo-Yang Song, Qing-Hong Cao, Ming-xing Luo, Hua Xing Zhu
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: This paper introduces a theoretical framework for understanding the dynamics of LLM-driven agents, highlighting a tendency toward detailed balance in their generative processes.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM)-driven agents are emerging as a powerful new paradigm for solving complex problems. Despite the empirical success of these practices, a theoretical framework to understand and unify their macroscopic dynamics remains lacking. This paper proposes a method based on the least action principle to estimate the underlying generative directionality of LLMs embedded within agents. By experimentally measuring the transition probabilities between LLM-generated states, we report evidence consistent with a tendency toward detailed balance in LLM-generated transitions, indicating that LLM generation may not be achieved by generally learning rule sets and strategies, but rather by implicitly learning a class of underlying potential functions that may transcend different LLM architectures and prompt templates. To our knowledge, this provides an effective macroscopic description of LLM generative dynamics that does not depend on specific model details. This work is an attempt to establish a macroscopic dynamics theory of complex AI systems, aiming to elevate the study of AI agents from a collection of engineering practices to a science built on effective measurements that are predictable and quantifiable.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: VLA-Stem: A Lightweight Safety Mechanism for Vision-Language-Action Models via Reinforcement Learning
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Bojun Zou, Wenhao Yu, Jiaohao Li, Jiaxuan Lin, Guanting Ye
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: VLA-Stem is a reinforcement-learning-based safety mechanism that enhances Vision-Language-Action models' adaptability to dynamic obstacles without degrading original task performance.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models integrate high-level reasoning with low-level action execution for end-to-end robotic control. However, most VLA models target static manipulation in unconstrained environments, overlooking spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles. Fine-tuning VLAs on obstacle-avoidance data is a straightforward solution, but collecting such data is costly, especially for dynamic scenarios, and may degrade their original task capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose VLA-Stem, a lightweight, reinforcement-learning-based safety mechanism for VLA systems. Without fine-tuning the underlying VLA policy, VLA-Stem converts its action chunks into motion references and uses trajectory-level guidance to preserve their spatial intent while allowing flexible motion and timing adjustments. Conditioned on these references, robot proprioception, and local obstacle information, the Stem policy adaptively modifies execution at inference time, preserving the original task intent while enabling responsive adaptation to spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles. For robust and sample-efficient training, we combine teacher-student distillation with curriculum learning. We evaluate VLA-Stem on reference following, static spatial constraints, and dynamic obstacle avoidance. Across six constrained simulation settings, VLA-Stem achieves 52.8% average collision-free task success versus 23.7% for the strongest safety baseline, while preserving base-policy performance in obstacle-free settings; real-world experiments further show consistent collision reductions under static and dynamic obstacles. These results demonstrate that VLA-Stem couples high-level VLA task intent with rapid, reflex-like responses to immediate physical risks, providing a brainstem-inspired mechanism for robust robot execution.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Search or Scoring? Diagnosing Why Visual World-Model Planners Fail
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Shang Luo, Chenhao Wu, Zixiang Ni
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper diagnoses failures in visual world-model planners as either search or scoring issues, proposing tailored remedies to improve planning outcomes across various environments.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Visual world models such as DINO-WM and JEPA-WM plan with an optimizer that searches for actions whose predicted outcome has the lowest cost, its distance to a goal image. A plan can thus fail in two ways: the optimizer never tries a good action that the cost would prefer (a search failure), or the cost, computed on predictions, ranks a bad action first (a scoring failure). The two need different remedies, more search or a better model, but a planner does not record which one occurred. We tell them apart by executing the optimizer's candidates, scoring a known solution with the planner's own cost, and comparing costs on predicted and real outcomes. An error model explains when each arises and so how to use retrieved demonstration windows (DemoProp): start the search from them (a warm start) when prediction errors are small, and average them without the model when large errors make the optimizer pick overrated actions. Across four simulated environments and three world models, on short tasks whose goals the planner can represent, PushT and Wall fail mostly by search, while Metaworld and RoboCasa fail by scoring because the cost, sound on real outcomes (AUROC 0.94 on Metaworld), is at chance on predictions (0.54). The diagnosis tells which remedy pays off: a four times larger search lowers the real-outcome cost only where failures come from search (clearly for DINO-WM), and where they come from scoring, averaging the windows without the model solves 127 of 168 new Metaworld tasks, against at most 87 when the model chooses among them. Within PushT, degrading only the model flips which use is better, and our rule, frozen in advance, follows the flip and solves 678 of 960 new episodes, against 530 for the best fixed use.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: RoboForge: Cross-space Motion Refinement for Physically Executable Humanoid Whole-body Tracking
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xichen Yuan, Zhe Li, Zhenzhe Zhang, Yangyang Wei, Xinying Guo
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: RoboForge enhances humanoid robot motion tracking by refining motion references through a data-centric framework, improving tracking success rates and enabling complex dynamic movements.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Whole-body motion tracking has rapidly expanded the skill repertoire of humanoid robots, yet nearly all of this progress has come from stronger tracking policies, while the motion references they imitate are treated as fixed supervision. We argue that reference quality is a first-order factor in tracking performance. Human motion data carry capture and estimation artifacts, and retargeting adds physical inconsistencies due to the human-robot embodiment gap; discarding such motions sacrifices valuable skill content, whereas retaining them uncorrected undermines policy learning. We present RoboForge, a data-centric framework that resolves this dilemma by refining references instead of filtering them, repairing each error in the space where it arises. In human motion space, a quality-guided diffusion model localizes corrupted segments and inpaints only those segments, leaving the rest of the motion intact. In robot motion space, kinematic repair corrects foot-contact and self-collision defects, and annealed sampling-based optimization under physics rollouts turns kinematically plausible references into dynamically executable ones. RoboForge requires no change to the tracker: it improves three retargeting methods and four tracking policies, raising the success rate of BeyondMimic from 89.51% to 96.20% while reducing the mean per-joint position error (MPJPE-L) by 31.6%. Refined references also accelerate policy learning, restore tracking performance from heavily corrupted inputs, and enable more than 30 high-dynamic motions, including flips and the Thomas flare, on a real Unitree G1.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Structured Role-Aware Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Bingqing Jiang, Guoxi Zhang, Jasper Wang, Bingning Wang, Difan Zou
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces Structured Role-aware Policy Optimization (SRPO) to enhance multimodal reasoning in vision-language models by assigning role-specific credit to perception and reasoning tokens.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR), especially with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), has shown strong potential for improving the reasoning capabilities of large vision-language models (LVLMs). However, in multimodal reasoning, final-answer rewards are typically assigned at the sequence level and do not distinguish the functional roles of different tokens, making it difficult to determine whether a correct answer is supported by task-relevant visual evidence. In this paper, we revisit multimodal RLVR from the perspective of role-aware token-level credit assignment, where structured responses are decomposed into perception tokens for extracting visual evidence and reasoning tokens for deriving answers from that evidence. Based on this perspective, we propose Structured Role-aware Policy Optimization (SRPO), which refines the sequence-level GRPO advantage into role-aware token-level advantages without changing the reward function. Specifically, SRPO assigns role-specific credit by using self-distilled on-policy contrasts: perception tokens are emphasized according to their visual dependency under original versus corrupted visual inputs, while reasoning tokens are emphasized according to their consistency with the generated perception. These role-specific signals are further unified through a shared trajectory-level baseline, yielding positive token weights that adjust relative update magnitudes while preserving the original GRPO reward and advantage signs, without requiring external reward models or separate teachers. Experiments across diverse multimodal reasoning benchmarks show that SRPO improves evidence-grounded reasoning, highlighting the importance of moving beyond uniform sequence-level credit toward role-aware optimization for reliable multimodal reasoning.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: SpatialScout-V2: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore Real-World 3D Scenes and Localize Objects?
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zhaoxi Zhang, Hao Liang, Linxuan Wu, Yiming Xu, Yifu Yuan
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: SpatialScout-V2 enhances active mapping in real 3D environments, revealing significant challenges in object localization accuracy among various vision-language models.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence requires agents to acquire visual evidence and integrate partial observations into coherent three-dimensional representations. We introduce SpatialScout-V2, which extends SpatialScout's active mapping task from simulation to real residential scenes through three advances: real visual observations, preservation of original scene content, and interactive exploration of recorded views. Built from 100 homes in Realsee3D, the benchmark covers 3,171 target objects across 29 categories. Given a fixed target inventory, agents autonomously select recorded viewpoints and viewing directions, integrate calibrated RGB observations, and iteratively estimate and revise object centers within a fixed interaction budget. We evaluate the localization accuracy and completeness of object-center maps using mean IoU, IoU-threshold hit rates, and target coverage. Evaluating seven frontier vision-language models (VLMs), we find that six achieve an all-target mean IoU below 20\%. Even the best-performing model, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches only 22.52\%, with just 18.36\% of targets exceeding an IoU of 0.5. Further analysis shows that broad submission coverage can coexist with limited localization accuracy, while target omissions further reduce overall scores. These results highlight substantial challenges in constructing accurate and complete object-center maps through active exploration of real scenes.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Weile Li, Yunfan Lou, Muqing Shi, Zihao Zhang, Zhenbiao Huang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: TacInno introduces a novel approach to enhance Vision-Language-Action models by using tactile innovation as a training target, significantly improving manipulation success rates.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: GroundAnything: Reconciling Parallel Decoding with Precise Visual Grounding at Flash Speed
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Qize Yu, Lianrui Fan, Bowen Ping, Xini Ding, Zetian Song
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: GroundAnything is a 4B-parameter model that achieves fast, precise visual grounding through parallel decoding and iterative denoising, outperforming existing models on multiple benchmarks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Autoregressive (AR) grounding models serialize spatial predictions, introducing sequential latency and imposing a causal order on output tokens. We view grounding as visual evidence extraction: objects, locations, and spatial relations are jointly constrained by the image and query, yet their dependencies do not imply an intrinsic left-to-right generation order. This distinction makes bidirectional diffusion a natural fit, allowing spatial hypotheses to emerge in parallel and be jointly refined through iterative denoising. We introduce GroundAnything, a 4B-parameter grounding foundation model that reconciles fast parallel decoding with precise localization through blockwise denoising. Training combines grounding pretraining from public datasets and dedicated data engines, direct AR-to-diffusion conversion with joint AR and diffusion objectives, supervised fine-tuning, and GRPO-based reinforcement post-training. Across 30 grounding benchmarks, our autoregressive variant, GroundAnything-VLM, establishes a new overall state of the art among similarly sized models at 72.42%, remaining competitive with GPT-6 Astra (71.35%). With entropy-guided decoding, GroundAnything also surpasses the prior state of the art at this scale, averaging 61.75% versus 53.32% for the fast MTP-based LocateAnything model. We further explore decoding strategies, showing that an optional self-speculative mode achieves a 4.51$\times$ speedup over the AR counterpart with a 0.74 percentage-point drop in COCO F1mIoU. Infrastructure experiments show that progressive inference optimizations translate parallel decoding into practical speedups. These gains support efficient visual grounding in latency-sensitive real-world systems.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: GroundingPI: A Grounding Foundation Model towards Physical Intelligence with Visual Primitives
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Qize Yu, Lianrui Fan, Boyu Chen, Jiaqi Liang, Xini Ding
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: GroundingPI is a state-of-the-art grounding foundation model that enhances physical intelligence in robotics by improving object localization and manipulation through advanced multimodal training techniques.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Precise grounding matters. It specifies which object is the target and where that object is, even in clutter and for tiny objects, and it has to be fast enough for closed-loop control. Yet vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAMs) take perception from general-purpose vision-language and video-generation backbones, which still fail in these settings. We introduce GroundingPI, a 4B grounding foundation model that generates points and boxes as quantized coordinates in a shared vocabulary. Training combines multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with GRPO, using supervision from public datasets and dedicated data engines. Against 44 baselines across 34 grounding benchmarks spanning 11 perceptual capabilities, GroundingPI establishes a new state of the art, averaging 73.68%, above the larger GPT-6 Astra (71.54%). As a downstream visual backbone, GroundingPI improves performance on robotic manipulation and autonomous driving. Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1, it outperforms all evaluated backbones in all four out-of-distribution settings, with relative gains of up to 24.8% over the strongest baseline. On RoboCasa-GR1, GroundingPI trained with 50% of the demonstrations outperforms those baselines trained with 75%. Its mean open-loop L2 error on nuScenes is 0.296 m. We systematically analyze GroundingPI's pretraining in scale and data composition. Grounding quality and downstream manipulation improve with pretraining scale, with generalization tracking perceptual gains most closely. Analyzing the data recipe across these 11 perceptual capabilities shows dense grounding's substantial benefits for both, and OCR's potential as a catalyst for perceptual learning. These results support grounding as a perceptual foundation, and dedicated perceptual pretraining as a promising direction for foundation models of physical intelligence.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Haoran Ye, Yuxing Lu, Haonan Dong, Zhaochen Su, Guojie Song
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Harness-Zero enables agent harness distillation by using an optimized harness to guide training, enhancing model performance and behavior recovery while eliminating the need for specialized harnesses at deployment.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the harness at deployment. Because the best harness varies across domains, instances, and models, a general-purpose agent must either settle for a suboptimal shared harness or route among an ever-growing set of specialized ones. We therefore study agent harness distillation: using a domain- or instance-optimized harness as training-time guidance and transferring the behaviors it induces into model weights, so that its gains survive under a single fixed target harness. The challenge is that the two harnesses differ in action space and available information, so guidance from the optimized harness cannot serve directly as supervision for the target one. We introduce Harness-Zero, which enables harness distillation through agent-as-harness. Guided by the optimized harness, a harnessing agent corrects student responses before execution in the target harness's action space, turning harness guidance into training demonstrations. Fine-tuning on the resulting trajectories internalizes harness-induced behavior into the model, so the specialized harness can be removed at deployment. Our experiments spanning knowledge work, tool use, and science domains show that: (1) For frontier LLMs using the same evolved harness, agent-as-harness outperforms code-as-harness. (2) With the specialized harness removed at deployment, Harness-Zero improves the base model's macro-average task success from 23.3% to 44.3%, even exceeding the 41.7% it reaches with that harness still attached, while reducing inference token usage by 27%-86%. (3) Harness-Zero recovers harness-induced behaviors absent from the base model, with 82.3% average recovery across 28 patterns in the three domains.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Bo Li, Taoyong Cui, Bob Zhang, Mengran Li, Chengyang Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: WeightCode introduces Weight-Space Programming to enhance neural networks' capabilities by directly modifying weights with executable programs, achieving significant performance improvements without retraining.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Neural networks encode learned capabilities in their weights, yet extending those capabilities with explicit task knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. Here we show that Weight-Space Programming (WSP), in which executable programs read, construct or modify a network's weights directly, can install new capabilities within trained neural networks. WeightCode, a WSP framework, uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks using task knowledge and their existing weights, without gradient-based training. Once installed, the new capabilities run independently of the language model. Given a grammar or eight demonstrations, weight programs enable previously unseen command compositions (0% to 99.8% exact match) and a new pickup action (0% to 98.4% success), while preserving the original command and navigation capabilities. On ImageNet, four weight programs achieve net gains of 8.84-17.62 points while preserving clean accuracy, outperforming the best of eight fine-tuning methods under matched examples, checks, and retention constraints. In a Vision Transformer, causal interventions show that installed noise-correction gates drive robustness gains, while their selective activation preserves clean accuracy. Rerun on five independently trained Vision Transformers without further language model calls, ten weight programs retain 83-110% of their source-network gains on average, whereas copying their fixed weight edits yields negligible gains. Six programs written for an already edited network add 5.23-14.50 points of contrast robustness while retaining the previously installed noise gain. Together, these results establish WSP as a new route to acquiring and accumulating capabilities in trained neural networks through reusable weight programs.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Agent^2 RL-Bench: Can LLM Agents Engineer Agentic RL Post-Training?
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Wanyi Chen, Xiao Yang, Xu Yang, Tianming Sha, Qizheng Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Agent^2 RL-Bench evaluates LLM agents' capabilities in autonomously engineering RL post-training pipelines, revealing both intelligent behaviors and significant limitations across various tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: We introduce Agent^2 RL-Bench, a compact diagnostic benchmark for evaluating agentic RL post-training, which tests whether LLM agents can autonomously design, implement, debug, and execute post-training pipelines that improve foundation models. RL post-training increasingly drives model alignment and specialization, yet existing benchmarks are largely static, rewarding supervised fine-tuning or script generation without assessing an agent's ability to close an interactive RL loop. Agent^2 RL-Bench provides a unified agent-facing interface: each run starts from an isolated workspace containing a base model, task data, instructions, and a grading API, and agents must iterate within a fixed budget by training models and submitting artifacts for evaluation. The benchmark spans six tasks across three levels, from static rule-based training to judge-based optimization and closed-loop online RL with trajectory collection. Two diagnostic skills, namely runtime recording and post-hoc summarization, enable structured analysis of agent behavior, facilitating smooth and effective iteration of the benchmark's evaluation framework. Across five agent systems and six driver LLMs, agents show intelligent behavior but clear limitations: one RL-oriented run improves ALFWorld from 4.85 to 93.28 via SFT warm-up and GRPO with online rollouts, yet DeepSearchQA remains difficult, most successful routes rely on supervised pipelines, and interactive outcomes show large differences across agent stacks. Overall, Agent2 RL-Bench shows that current agents can sometimes engineer online RL, but stable agent-driven RL post-training remains rare under fixed budgets. It also demonstrates that our benchmark provides a strong and effective evaluation framework for future research in this direction. Code is available at https://github.com/microsoft/RD-Agent.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: StreamEgo: Streaming Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Tianyi Xu, Boyang Lyu, Yunkai Tang, Kairan Ding, Jiahang Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: StreamEgo is a real-time framework for unbounded exocentric-to-egocentric video generation, enhancing immersive experiences and overcoming limitations of existing methods with innovative training techniques.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Exocentric-to-egocentric (Exo2Ego) video generation transforms third-person recordings into first-person viewpoints, unlocking immersive AR/VR experiences and scalable demonstration synthesis for embodied robotics. Extending it to a streaming setting is expected to further enable live applications. However, existing methods suffer from degraded manipulation regions, overfitting and confinement to fixed-length clips with prohibitive latency. To address these limitations, we present StreamEgo, a real-time framework for unbounded, generalizable Exo2Ego video generation. To resolve intricate manipulation dynamics while supporting the streaming pipeline, a streaming dual-branch prior provides pixel-aligned guidance for translating appearance and skeletal kinematics. We also introduce a region-aware loss curriculum to improve generalization and stabilize multi-objective diffusion training. Furthermore, we distill the model into a chunk-wise autoregressive model, augmented with a region-aware corruption mechanism and a first-chunk curriculum, enabling high-quality, generalizable real-time streaming Exo2Ego generation at 24.3 FPS on a single H100 GPU.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiaming Li, Lingzhen Li, Xiaze Yang, Chenyu Zhu, Kaiqi Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: SpecWM introduces a training-free inference framework that enhances streaming world models by refining draft chunks through latent velocity verification, achieving improved visual quality and speed.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement reuses it to improve perceptual quality, while three-step refinement strengthens camera following and trajectory consistency. These findings motivate transition-aware refinement. On WBench Navigation, SpecWM improves visual quality at 1.63$\times$ speedup over the target and raises NavScore from the draft's 75.99 to 85.63, achieving the best quality-speed-control trade-off. Additionally, our LongSpecBench shows sustained quality and control over long, multi-turn rollouts, while experiments on Hy-Nomas validate SpecWM across backbones and denoising budgets.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Shihan Wu, You Liu, Chunyu He, Minghui Qin, Longhan Jiao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: HumanCOIN is a comprehensive 12,500-hour dataset capturing human intent in egocentric manipulation through three observational tiers: gaze, muscle exertion, and cognitive decision-making.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: https://flagopen.github.io/HumanCOIN.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: V-Zero: Gating On-Policy Distillation with Contrastive Visual Evidence for Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Haoxiang Sun, Zhihang Yi, Langxuan Deng, Yuhao Zhou, Peiqi Jia
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: V-Zero enhances on-policy distillation for fine-grained visual reasoning by using contrastive visual evidence to improve trajectory evaluation and training efficiency without relying on external supervision.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Fine-grained visual reasoning requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to identify task-relevant visual evidence and ground their reasoning in local image regions. Existing methods typically rely on reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards or supervised fine-tuning on large-scale annotated reasoning traces, resulting in costly exploration, hand-designed verification rules, or heavy dependence on textual supervision. While On-Policy Distillation (OPD) offers a promising alternative via dense teacher supervision, its token-level objective inherently focuses on local token corrections, failing to assess global trajectory quality. In this work, we first reinterpret OPD as a stop-gradient alignment objective, revealing that its potential is limited by the absence of trajectory-level discrimination. Motivated by this observation, we propose V-Zero, which gates on-policy distillation with contrastive visual evidence. Specifically, V-Zero evaluates each trajectory under paired positive and negative visual views; the resulting likelihood contrast forms a trajectory-level gate that selectively amplifies updates from visually well-supported reasoning paths while suppressing ungrounded ones. Experiments on multiple visual reasoning and perception benchmarks show that V-Zero improves the Qwen3.5-4B backbone by 3.9 points on average while preserving strong generalization. Notably, V-Zero achieves more than 3$\times$ and 6$\times$ training speedups over representative supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning baselines, respectively. It requires neither annotated textual reasoning traces nor external reward signals. Code and dataset are released at https://github.com/eVI-group-SCU/V-Zero.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: WorldComposer: Generative High-Fidelity Simulation with Digital Cousins for Generalizable Robot Learning and Evaluation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jasper Lu, Zhenhao Shen, Yuanfei Wang, Shugao Liu, Shengqiang Xu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: WorldComposer is a generative framework that transforms real-world scenes into high-fidelity simulations, enhancing robot learning through diverse data augmentation and realistic environment synthesis.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Learning robust robot policies in real-world environments requires diverse data augmentation, yet scaling real-world data collection is costly due to the need for acquiring physical assets and reconfiguring environments. Therefore, augmenting real-world scenes into simulation has become a practical augmentation for efficient learning and evaluation.
