We present WorldComposer, an automated generative Real2Sim2Real framework that maps real-world panoramas into high-fidelity, task-ready simulation environments and further synthesizes diverse Digital Cousins through scene and object variations. Combined with high-quality physics engines and realistic assets, WorldComposer supports interactive manipulation across rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Additionally, we incorporate multi-room stitching to construct consistent large-scale environments for long-horizon tasks. Experiments demonstrate a strong sim-to-real correlation validating our platform's fidelity, and show that extensively scaling up data generation leads to significantly better generalization to unseen scene and object variations, demonstrating the effectiveness of Digital Cousins for generalizable robot learning and evaluation.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: EmbodiedLab: Beyond Manipulation, Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Hongcheng Gao, Zelin Zheng, Alex Zhou, Jay Zhu, Shijia Ge
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: EmbodiedLab introduces a simulated laboratory for benchmarking embodied agents that must physically act to discover hidden properties, enhancing understanding through 35 quantitative experiments.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Physical action not only changes the state of an environment but is also the way to know its hidden properties: what cannot be seen must be inferred from the feedback to the change. As embodied agents advance from executing procedures to pursuing goals, success depends on properties neither given nor visible, so they must act to know. Existing benchmarks separate changing from knowing: manipulation benchmarks give the target state, so nothing has to be found out, whereas exploration and discovery benchmarks let the agent find out by looking or querying, so nothing physical has to be changed. Quantitative science experiments offer a natural testbed: the properties sought are new in every instance, appear only in instrument readings under conditions the agent sets up, and can be checked exactly. We introduce EmbodiedLab, a simulated laboratory of 35 such experiments. Given only a goal, the agent must decide what to measure, operate the apparatus with a robot arm, read instruments through cameras and judge when its readings suffice. Its 30 determination tasks specify what to find out, whereas its 5 optimization tasks ask only for the best result the apparatus allows. With native control, the strongest of seven frontier agents succeeds on 41.4% of the tasks. Ablations reveal two bottlenecks: contact-rich manipulation, where ground-truth depth and motion planning change the success rate by at most 10 points, whereas executing every operation for the agent on five of the tasks raises it from at most 20% to at least 70%, so what an agent can know is bounded by how reliably it acts; and closed-loop experimental rigor, where with manipulation supplied, agents fail to gather sufficient readings or read instruments accurately, and most optimization runs stop at one design. Beyond evaluation, EmbodiedLab offers a resamplable environment with verifiable rewards for training embodied agents.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Beyond Appearance: Evidence-Guided Programmatic 3D Scene Reconstruction with Agentic Lighting Reasoning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zeting Luo, Yifan Li, Shuai Yang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: LightHarness enhances 3D scene reconstruction by integrating lighting reasoning with geometric and material cues, improving accuracy and supporting complex visual simulations without extra training.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Image-to-code methods for 3D scene reconstruction produce executable code that generates editable digital content and supports visual simulation. However, existing methods primarily rely on appearance similarity, which provides limited guidance for distinguishing errors in geometry, materials, and illumination. Light shapes scene appearance through its interactions with geometry and materials, influencing shading, cast shadows, and reflections. We therefore present LightHarness, a VLM-based agentic framework that incorporates explicit lighting reasoning into iterative scene reconstruction. To be specific, we leverage complementary geometric, intrinsic, and illumination cues to jointly refine scene structure and appearance, and propose Lighting Reasoning Memory to maintain light-source hypotheses, which supports evidence, and revision history throughout iterations. Together, they support reasoning about partially visible and unseen sources, with evidence-guided verification directing subsequent revisions. Our framework reconstructs explicit scenes through coherent reasoning about geometry, materials, and illumination without additional training or differentiable rendering. Extensive experiments demonstrate superior image-to-code reconstruction accuracy under challenging shadows and complex illumination, further supporting downstream scene editing, object insertion, and versatile relighting.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Siyuan Du, Yuxin Liu, Meng Tang, Haoran Li, Yechao Bai
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents a reverse-to-forward curriculum with advantage decomposition to enhance long-horizon task performance in LLM agents, achieving superior success rates in complex environments.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a common approach for training large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon tasks. However, learning from sparse terminal rewards makes credit assignment and exploration difficult. We approach these challenges through a policy-induced capability region, the set of states from which the current policy can reliably complete a task. Near its boundary, an agent may need only a few actions to reach a more solvable state, even when the goal remains distant. This reduces long-horizon learning to two coupled subproblems of reaching that state and completing the task from there. We address them with paired advantages and a progressive reverse-to-forward curriculum. The advantages provide separate signals for reaching more solvable states and completing the task from them, while the curriculum expands the capability region backward along successful reference trajectories and then into off-reference states through on-policy exploration. On ALFWorld and WebShop, our method outperforms competitive agentic RL methods at both model scales, achieving success rates of 90.1%/96.1% and 80.2%/82.6% with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, respectively.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: RoboMorpher: Scaling Robot Morphology Representations for Cross-Embodiment Action Prediction
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Wenwei Lin, Yan Qin, Weiliang Deng, Zixuan Li, Kaixuan Wang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: RoboMorpher enhances cross-embodiment action prediction by integrating morphology-conditioned action tokenization and scalable kinematic supervision, outperforming traditional joint-space control methods.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Learning shared action representations is central to cross-embodiment manipulation. However, identical joint values can produce different spatial configurations across robots, limiting representations learned from joint values alone. We introduce RoboMorpher, a morphology-conditioned action tokenizer that jointly reconstructs joint angles and link poses to associate control coordinates with their kinematic effects. MorphGen supplies scalable kinematic supervision by generating serial-arm descriptions from survey-derived geometric priors. We pretrain RoboMorpher on 40 million morphology-state pairs and integrate the frozen tokenizer into a vision-language-action policy for discrete prediction and continuous refinement. We also introduce EmbodiBench, a ten-task benchmark with 30 generated URDFs per task. With downstream URDFs excluded from tokenizer pretraining, the policy achieves 56.40% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and 23.27% on EmbodiBench, exceeding continuous joint-space control by 9.73 and 15.34 percentage points. Removing link-pose supervision reduces EmbodiBench success by 17.94 percentage points, supporting morphology-aware geometric supervision for joint-action representation learning.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Where Is the Cost of Third-Party API Routers in Agentic Software Development?
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Donghao Fu, Jingxin Li, Xue Jiang, Yihong Dong
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This study investigates the impact of third-party API routers on coding agents, revealing significant vulnerabilities in client-side safeguards against router-side interventions.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Third-party API routers have become a common layer that unifies access across increasingly diverse LLM providers. In coding-agent workflows, high-autonomy operation is widely adopted because it reduces interaction overhead. As a result, a third-party API router, which sits between the agent and the upstream provider, inevitably occupies the trusted path. It can inspect and modify every request and response, yet no mechanism verifies alignment between the provider's output and the repository-level actions ultimately executed by the agent. Consequently, client-side permission mechanisms may become ineffective in practice. Whether this control gap produces real, hard-to-detect effects on software development tasks remains empirically unmeasured. In this paper, we conduct an empirical study of router-side injection in coding agents, examining four intervention levels of increasing subtlety: Response Substitution (L1), Response Append (L2), LLM-Polished Injection (L3), and LLM-Polished with Distribution Alignment Injection (L4). Moreover, we develop SIDEL, a framework for trace recording, replay, injection, and defense evaluation, with a curated dataset of 400 samples. We evaluate four representative coding agents, and further evaluate whitelist-based execution control and LLM review. Router-side intervention substantially alters repository-level actions and remains difficult for existing client-side safeguards to detect. Without additional mitigations, all evaluated agents achieved a defense success rate of 0 percent across all injection levels. Client-side mitigations and reactive reviews improve resistance but do not fully restore end-to-end control, motivating provider-side output-integrity guarantees. Our code is available at https://github.com/Riyasushin/SIDEL.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: mmTherm: Absolute 3D Human Pose Estimation from Low-Resolution Thermal Images and mmWave Radar
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zhaoxin Chang, Badii Jouaber, Daqing Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: mmTherm is a lightweight framework that enhances 3D human pose estimation by integrating low-resolution thermal images with mmWave radar, improving accuracy and efficiency.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Absolute 3D human pose estimation (HPE) aims to recover both a person's body pose and their global position in 3D space. Privacy-preserving millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides distance and direction measurement capabilities, but its sparse point clouds make HPE under-constrained. Low-resolution thermal imaging can provide complementary observations of body direction and structure. However, our evaluation shows that a strong feature-level fusion baseline loses much of its localization and HPE advantage when generalizing to unseen subjects, with radial localization becoming less accurate than a radar-only baseline. Motivated by this finding, we introduce mmTherm, a lightweight framework that explicitly incorporates the complementary geometric properties of thermal imaging and mmWave radar. It combines body structure and joint directions estimated from thermal images with range information from radar to localize the body and reconstruct its 3D pose. Experiments on OctoNet show that mmTherm reduces cross-user absolute joint error by 33% and root localization error by 38% relative to the strongest corresponding baselines, while requiring substantially fewer parameters and less computation at inference.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: AdaS-ViT: Test-Time Adaptive Routing for Spiking Vision Transformers with Ultra-High Energy Efficiency
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zecheng Hao, Zihan Huang, Shenghao Xie, Jiyuan Zhang, Zhaofei Yu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: AdaS-ViT introduces a test-time adaptive routing mechanism for spiking vision transformers, enhancing energy efficiency and performance through selective spike emission and fine-grained firing patterns.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise event-driven and energy-efficient vision, yet existing spiking vision transformers (S-ViTs) largely confine spiking tokens to fixed and uniform firing schemes along the temporal, spatial and channel dimensions, whereas suppressing the computational redundancy thus incurred calls for adaptive firing mechanisms that operate jointly across all three axes at test time. To this end, we propose the Adaptive Efficient Integrate-and-Fire (AdaE-IF) model, which consults the attention score of each spiking token and routes salient regions to fine-grained firing patterns while assigning energy-frugal coarse patterns to the remaining regions. Building on AdaE-IF, we further introduce Spiking Gated Self-Attention (S-GSA) and Spiking Local-Gated Unit (S-LGU), which enforce selective spike emission at token and channel granularity. We integrate the aforementioned mechanisms and modules into AdaS-ViT, a test-time adaptive-routing architecture trained with a progressive spatio-temporal curriculum that stabilizes the co-adaptation of firing precision and routing masks. Extensive experiments across benchmarks spanning diverse data scales and modalities demonstrate that AdaS-ViT consistently achieves highly competitive performance. Notably, on ImageNet-1k it consumes only 1.02 to 2.45 millijoules per image and attains an accuracy-per-energy ratio of 32$\times$ to 72$\times$, operating in an economical inference regime and thereby pushing the energy-efficiency boundary further.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Ruisi Zhao, You Li, Sihan Chen, Aosong Cheng, Chixiang Ma
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: RoughCut-Bench introduces a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating automatic video rough-cut processes using large vision-language models, addressing both visually and speech-driven settings.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Video rough-cut is a core stage in media production workflows, organizing raw media materials into an initial video cut. Despite recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) for video-related tasks, automatic rough-cut remains underexplored, without a comprehensive benchmark for evaluation or mature workflows for producing executable cut plans. To address the evaluation gap, we introduce RoughCut-Bench, which covers two practical settings: (1) a visually driven setting over video cases, covering highlight detection and selection, source-video ordering, and adherence to user requirements when provided; and (2) a speech-driven setting over automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts, covering filler removal, expression deduplication, and low-value content trimming. Across these settings, the benchmark contains 101 visually driven cases, including 831 raw videos with 1,476 highlight annotations. It also includes 84 speech-driven cases, each consisting of an ASR transcript with annotated cleanup spans. The evaluation compares cut plans with these annotations in both settings and additionally uses a human-aligned agentic evaluator to assess rendered-cut quality in the visual setting. To apply LVLMs to automatic rough-cut, we further propose agentic workflows that guide them to produce structured cut plans from input materials. Experiments show that current LVLMs remain limited in producing expert-aligned cut plans. Our benchmark, code, and prompts are released at https://whalesong-zrs.github.io/RoughCut-Bench-Project-Page.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: F$^3$: What Makes Good Experience in World-Action Models?
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zihe Huang, Sirui Zhou, Haozhi Han, Ruge Zhang, Teng Ma
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The F$^3$ framework enhances world-action models by optimizing experience utilization through Form, Fit, and Fusion, achieving significant performance improvements in robotic tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Deployed world-action models (WAMs) can keep improving only if they make good use of their own experience. Existing methods supply retrieved rollouts or demonstrations to the policy as context, yet such experience often turns previously solved tasks into failures. What, then, makes good experience for a WAM? We show that experience is valuable only in use: its value depends not on whether the source rollout succeeded but on what is stored, when it is used, and where it enters the policy. We therefore propose F$^3$, which makes these three decisions with Form, Fit, and Fusion. Form compresses successful and failed rollouts alike into short, verified operation records; Fit teaches the policy to read a record and to predict when it helps; Fusion injects the record's images, text and actions into the policy as a prefix and an action prior. Trained once on only 200 examples and deployed with a growing experience library, the model achieves state-of-the-art results on MolmoSpaces and RoboLab without any training on RoboLab: over native Cosmos 3 Nano, it raises success by 12.0 pp and 10.8 pp, reduces steps to success by 12.2% and 11.3%, and cuts regressions by 57%.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Multispectral-Polarization-Infrared Multi-Aperture Camouflaged Vehicle Detection
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Shu Wang, Xiong Lin, Yuan Song, Junjie Wang, Feng Huang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The proposed tri-modal detection framework utilizes spectral, polarization, and infrared data with decision-level fusion to enhance camouflaged vehicle detection accuracy and speed.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Camouflaged vehicle detection is challenging because camouflage suppresses discriminative cues across sensing modalities. Existing multimodal methods often require precise pixel-level registration and feature-level fusion, creating a trade-off between accuracy and latency. We propose a spectral-polarization-infrared tri-modal detection framework co-designed with a multi-aperture imaging setup to exploit complementary imaging physics. A consensus-guided decision-level fusion strategy combines cross-modal detections within bounded registration tolerances, reducing dependence on precise alignment while maintaining accuracy and real-time performance. We construct a tri-modal camouflaged vehicle dataset containing infrared, polarization, and spectral data. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves 82.7% mean Average Precision (mAP) with an end-to-end latency of 16 ms, outperforming representative feature-level fusion approaches. On the public MID-1K dataset, the framework generalizes to RGB-Depth-Infrared modalities without architectural modification and improves mAP@0.5 by 5.7% over state-of-the-art methods. These results demonstrate the potential of decision-level consensus fusion and multi-aperture sensing for robust and deployable camouflaged vehicle detection.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: SR-VLA: Stall-Reduced VLA Execution via Predicted-Input Lookahead and Selective KV Cache Repair
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Tao Zhang, Yi Zhong, Jinhao Ruan, Yipeng Gao, Linfeng Zhong
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: SR-VLA enhances vision-language-action execution by using predicted-input lookahead and selective KV cache repair, achieving significant speedups while maintaining task success rates.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies incur control stalls when inference blocks the next action chunk. Asynchronous early inference can hide latency, but its results may be inconsistent with the arriving actual inputs. Unconditional reuse risks acting on mismatched inputs, whereas full recomputation discards useful precomputation. We propose SR-VLA, combining predicted-input lookahead with selective KV cache repair. During current chunk execution, a lightweight action-conditioned predictor generates next-boundary visual observations and proprioceptive state. These predictions, together with the task instruction, drive the frozen VLA to precompute a speculative KV cache and action chunk. After real inputs are available to VLA, predicted--real differences and task conditions determine whether to accept the action chunk or trigger selective KV repair. On LIBERO, SR-VLA achieves $2.67\times$ and $1.27\times$ query speedups over the respective synchronous $π_{0.5}$ and OpenVLA-OFT baselines, while maintaining competitive average task success rates. Under target-motion perturbation, success remains baseline-comparable, with $1.52\times$--$1.93\times$ query speedup.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Zero-Shot Compositional Generalization for Embodied Manipulation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Baicheng Li, Wenkang Qin, Youqi Pan, Dongxiao Mao, Yukun Zhou
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents a geometry-supervised framework enabling zero-shot compositional generalization in robotic manipulation by leveraging demonstrated commands across different robot embodiments without requiring joint labels.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Robot demonstrations are collected on different embodiments, leaving many robot-skill combinations unobserved. Pooling these data shares visual knowledge, while joint labels remain tied to the demonstrating kinematic chain. We propose a geometry-supervised training framework for zero-shot composition of familiar robots and skills. The central insight is that a demonstrated command provides a tool-space target for every robot that can realize it. Calibrated forward kinematics supplies this supervision to foreign native action interfaces without their joint labels for that skill. Native reconstruction retains demonstrated configurations, and positive reachability checks select targets for cross-robot supervision. A visual policy learns to predict shared actions and executes through the target robot's native decoder. During policy learning, one prediction receives geometric supervision through both source and foreign native realizations. Matched supervision controls, repeated policy training and evaluations across three backbones and two simulators demonstrate improved transfer to missing robot-task combinations.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: VIVID: Beyond Static Multi-Image Reasoning with Localized Visual Differences and Textual Entity Dynamics in Video MLLMs
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Chengqian Ma, Yuanze Zeng, Hongyu Wang, Mingfeng Lin, YiCheng Xiao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: VIVID enhances video question answering by integrating localized motion and event order through Dynamic Tokens and inter-frame differences, outperforming existing models in accuracy.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Video question answering under tight frame budgets requires preserving localized motion and event order, yet current video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) reduce comprehension to static multi-image reasoning by discarding unselected frames and encoding keyframes independently: (1) Spatially, whole-frame pooling dilutes small moving targets into static backgrounds; (2) Temporally, dropping intermediate frames or averaging tokens erases inter-frame motion, confusing direction, speed, and order. We propose VIVID (Visual Inter-frame Variations and Individual Dynamics), which moves beyond static snapshots like human vision: keyframes capture core states while inter-frame Patch Diffs preserve neighboring changes within $K_f$ keyframes. Autonomous Delta-Driven Keyframe Planning (ADKP) selects anchors from a $3\text{ fps}$ pool and feeds surrounding patch differences into Dual-Road Change Memory (DRCM), forming Dynamic Tokens at zero extra anchor tokens alongside a camera-stabilized Active Motion Region of Interest (ROI) and chronological Entity State Chains. Adding $0.22\%$ trainable parameters to a frozen $27\text{B}$ backbone, VIVID-Small ($50$ examples, $\sim 1.5$ GPU hours) beats all eleven baselines in overall accuracy across $8,083$ questions and trails only VIVID-Large ($3,600$ examples), which leads on MotionBench, Video-MME, and TempCompass.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Passage-Focused Soft Coordination for Hierarchical Multi-Robot Navigation in Bottleneck Environments
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Haoze Dong, Stepan Dergachev, Meng Guo, Konstantin Yakovlev, Zhongkui Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The proposed passage-focused framework enhances multi-robot navigation by integrating soft global coordination with flexible local execution, achieving high success rates and efficient collision avoidance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: In multi-robot navigation, rigid global schedules are sensitive to execution deviations, while local methods lack long-horizon coordination. We propose a passage-focused framework combining soft global coordination with flexible local execution. A passage-induced graph of convex sets supports priority-ordered planning with two levels of soft coordination. Passage-aware route selection accounts for passage usage and traversal directions, while route-restricted continuous space-time planning penalizes temporal conflicts. The resulting references guide a model predictive path integral controller that avoids collisions online. Adaptive temporal and geometric tracking accommodates execution deviations, while selective replanning maintains coordination without rigid trajectory reservations. Across 1,200 instances in 4 different environments with 5-30 robots, the framework achieves a near-perfect success rate and outperforms evaluated baselines in makespan and flowtime. Hardware experiments with 8 robots demonstrate successful completion of all trials without collisions. These results highlight the effectiveness of passage-focused coordination in balancing long-horizon cooperation with flexible execution.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Yuan Wei, Ying Wei
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper explores how on-policy distillation reshapes interaction patterns in language-model agents across various domains, revealing both improvements and negative transfers in performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: TARGO and TARGO-Net: Benchmarking Target-driven Object Grasping under Occlusions
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yan Xia, Ran Ding, Ziyuan Qin, Guanqi Zhan, Kaichen Zhou
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces TARGO, a benchmark dataset for target-driven grasping under occlusions, and TARGO-Net, a robust model that improves grasp prediction accuracy in cluttered environments.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Predicting 6-DoF grasp poses from a single RGB-D frame has recently achieved impressive accuracy, yet performance can degrade significantly when the target object is heavily occluded by clutter. In this paper, we establish TARGO, the first benchmark dataset for TARget-driven Grasping under Occlusions, and introduce TARGO-Net, a grasp prediction model designed for visual occlusion. Our main contributions are fourfold: 1) We identify the visual occlusion challenge in single-view RGB-D 6-DoF grasping and show that current state-of-the-art models still suffer under severe occlusion. 2) We propose the TARGO dataset, which supports training and testing 6-DoF grasp models across different visual occlusion levels and enables robustness evaluation in real-world scenarios. 3) We devise TARGO-Net, a transformer-based grasping model with a target completion module and target-scene cross-attention, which achieves the most robust performance across all visual occlusion levels. 4) We show that target completion, number of occluders, and target minimum dimension also relate to grasp success in addition to visual occlusion.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: RISE-RL: Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jinkun Hou, Zhuo Liu, Huimin Ren, Kuan Zhang, Zirong Chen
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: RISE-RL enhances open-ended reinforcement learning by selectively exploring trajectories based on missed rubric criteria, significantly improving performance across various benchmarks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) for open-ended tasks is challenging because responses must satisfy multidimensional criteria without following a single correct generation trajectory. Existing rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) methods compress fine-grained criterion-level feedback into scalar rewards, making persistent capability gaps difficult to target under limited on-policy exploration. We propose $\textbf{RISE-RL}$ (Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration), which uses repeatedly missed rubric criteria to elicit privileged trajectories that are difficult to discover through unguided exploration alone. RISE-RL retains only trajectories whose complete-rubric reward exceeds the mean reward of natural rollouts, and then re-evaluates them under the original prompt to emphasize behaviors that remain weakly supported by the natural policy. The resulting guidance signal is optimized through a separate auxiliary objective and removed once its additional benefit diminishes. Experiments with 4B and 14B models across writing, chat, health, and science show that RISE-RL achieves the highest mean score on every evaluated benchmark under guidance-free evaluation. Compared with standard Rubric-RL, it improves the average score by 1.3 points at the 4B scale and $\textbf{3.3 points at the 14B scale}$, including a $\textbf{6.0-point}$ gain on CreativeWriting-V3. It also improves creative-writing diversity and yields gains on objectively scored medical and scientific benchmarks. These results indicate that selective internalization through reward filtering and policy support shaping is effective for open-ended reinforcement learning.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiarui Dong, Zhiheng Liang, Yanjun Li, Zeyu Zhang, Heejeong Nam
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: JEPA4R enhances JEPA world models by enabling 4D point planning from depth-camera point clouds, achieving superior performance in robotic manipulation tasks and zero-shot real-world application.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiajun Sun, Zeyu Zhang, Zeyu Ren, Guangfeng Jiang, Yang Zhao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: PanDWM introduces a panoramic 4D driving world model that enhances video generation efficiency and consistency by integrating multiple camera views into a continuous 360° image.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one $360^\circ$ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched $360^\circ$ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at $8$-$46\times$ their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Glance, then Select: Evidence-Tempered Visual Token Selection for Extremely Compressed Multimodal LLMs
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yuxuan Wang, Guangxiang Zhao, Yuxuan Tian, Yahui Han, Xinyu Tan
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The Glance-ETD framework efficiently reduces visual tokens in multimodal large language models, maintaining high performance while significantly speeding up processing and improving token selection.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) encode a high-resolution image into thousands of visual tokens, which dominate the cost of the prefill stage. Visual token reduction removes most of these tokens, but two problems remain at extreme budgets. The vision encoder still processes every patch of the image, and the few surviving tokens often miss the small regions that hold the answer. In this paper, we propose Glance-ETD, a two-stage token reduction framework guided by a lightweight question-conditioned scorer. In the first stage, a glance encoder views the image at low resolution and re-encodes only the question-relevant regions at native resolution. In the second stage, Evidence-Tempered Diversity (ETD) selects the final tokens by combining diversity with the evidence predicted by the scorer, so that the kept tokens cover the scene and retain the answer. A single-rollout self-distillation recipe trains the MLLM with the glance encoder. With only 5% of the visual tokens, Glance-ETD retains 91.6% of the full-token performance of Qwen3.5-4B across fourteen benchmarks and outperforms the strongest prior method, LT-OPD, by 17.3 points and the same training recipe with DivPrune by 6.0. It also speeds up the time to first token on 4K images by 3.1x and generalizes to three other MLLMs and to high-resolution document benchmarks, with the largest gains on text-rich tasks.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Learning and Verifying Progress: Closed-Loop Agentic Planning with Progress-Enhanced Execution for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Navigation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Kangjie Zhou, Sukai Wang, Yuhan Xiao, Qinghang Liu, Zhejia Wen
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: LeaP-VLN enhances long-horizon vision-language navigation by integrating progress-aware execution and verification, improving agent recovery from errors and achieving state-of-the-art success rates.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Long-horizon vision-language navigation (VLN) requires agents to track instruction progress and recover from local errors before they propagate across subtasks. However, executors trained on expert trajectories encounter policy-induced state shifts during deployment, and their stop signals do not reliably indicate subtask completion. We introduce Learning and Verifying Progress for VLN (LeaP-VLN), an agentic VLN system that couples progress-aware execution with independent progress verification through plan--execute--verify--recover cycles. LeaP-VLN leverages progress both explicitly, through a progress verifier that verifies subtask completion before the agent advances and triggers dual-phase recovery upon route deviation, and implicitly, by co-training the executor on progress reasoning and action prediction to enhance the executor's progress awareness and corrective control. To adapt the executor to this closed-loop interface, we propose a two-stage progress-enhanced curriculum: behavior cloning on expert demonstrations, followed by joint training on demonstrations, expert action corrections, and progress-reasoning supervision. Policy-generated trajectories expose the executor to both intra-subtask drift and inter-subtask state shifts, aligning training with the deviations encountered during closed-loop execution. Extensive experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE demonstrate state-of-the-art success rates among monocular methods trained without additional navigation datasets, while real-world experiments further validate the effectiveness of LeaP-VLN in long-horizon navigation.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: An LLM-assisted theoretical model for aeroengine installation noise scattering
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xun Huang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents a theoretical model for aeroengine noise scattering using LLM-assisted algebraic manipulation, demonstrating AI's potential in theoretical fluid mechanics research.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: A theoretical model is developed for the canonical problem of aeroengine fan noise impinging on, and scattering from, a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate. The model chains two Wiener--Hopf problems in different coordinate systems. The first stage solves the duct-radiation problem analytically in axisymmetric cylindrical coordinates. The second stage expands the field incident on the plate into a double angular spectrum of plane waves: the axial spectrum is inherited from the first stage, while the spanwise spectrum is generated by a Weyl--Sommerfeld expansion of the cylindrical harmonics. Each spectral component is then scattered by the plate. The mathematical crux is the coordinate transformation between the axisymmetric duct frame and the Cartesian plate frame. The core physical insight--that the Weyl--Sommerfeld identity provides an exact spectral bridge between these systems--originates entirely with the authors. The heavy algebra of translating between the two spectral representations, together with the associated numerical verification, was carried out with the assistance of a large language model (LLM), under strict human oversight and independent numerical cross-checking. This division of labour enables the LLM to handle tedious symbolic manipulation without compromising rigour. Results are presented for spinning modes radiating from a cylindrical duct with a subsonic jet into a quiescent ambient. The case study demonstrates that, under systematic verification, LLMs can accelerate tedious algebra in theoretical fluid mechanics, contributing a concrete empirical example to the broader discussion on AI's role in theoretical research.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: UbiHearo: Bringing Scenario-Aware Sound Guidance to DHH Users with Mobile Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Fengmin Wu, Sicong Liu, Zimu Zhou, Chenren Xu, Wanbing Zhao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: UbiHearo is a mobile assistant for Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing users that provides scenario-aware sound guidance through a neuro-symbolic approach, enhancing situational awareness and personalized responses.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: For Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) users, effective sound awareness goes beyond detecting \emph{what} sound occurs; it requires understanding \emph{what it means}, \emph{how urgent it is}, and \emph{what to do}. However, existing mobile assistants largely reduce acoustic scenes to isolated labels or generic alerts, failing to provide contextual guidance when the same sound implies different risks across scenarios. We present \sysname, a mobile hearing assistant agent that closes the sensing--reasoning--action loop for \textit{scenario-aware} and \textit{personalized} DHH assistance. \sysname adopts a \textit{neuro-symbolic} design that transforms continuous acoustic and physical context streams into structured intermediate representations (IRs) for controllable reasoning and guidance. It introduces three key mechanisms. \textit{First}, a perception-thresholded sensing mechanism enables energy-efficient always-on awareness by activating processing only for perceptually meaningful events while preserving safety-critical cues through deterministic overrides. \textit{Second}, a staged neuro-symbolic reasoning framework performs promptless scenario understanding by conditioning an on-device audio-language model on structured IRs instead of user-authored context descriptions. \textit{Third}, a bounded human-in-the-loop personalization mechanism adapts user-specific guidance through lightweight on-device decision-boundary updates while preserving population-aligned reasoning. We evaluate \sysname on smartphones and in-vehicle systems across diverse scenarios. It achieves favorable accuracy--latency--energy tradeoffs and personalized guidance.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Hanlin Tian, Sihan Zhu, Zhao Yang, Yuxiang Wang, Zhiquan Hu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: DetourBench introduces a trajectory-level evaluation framework for interactive agents, emphasizing minimum-action bounds to distinguish between efficient and inefficient decision-making processes.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Settling this needs a reference cost, and authored solutions establish only that a task is solvable, not that no shorter route exists. We present DetourBench, which constrains the environment until that minimum is computable. Each task is a finite, partially observable transition system with unit-cost accesses whose resources become globally addressable after discovery. Exhaustive search yields the full-information minimum action count $L_0$ with a replayable witness; from graph-recoverable terminal states it also yields exact residual work $R_T$, which separates an episode that stopped one access short from one that wandered, while an irreversible wrong commitment is recorded as having no finite residual distance rather than assigned one. Success, attainment, residual progress, and normalized detour are reported separately. Across 375 scored episodes --- five model endpoints, 25 integrated tasks, three repeats --- success ranges from 58.7% to 96.0% while conditional attainment ranges from 0.803 to 0.890 and orders the models differently. Among recoverable failures, residual work separates near-complete trajectories from costly incompletion and from irreversible commitment. We open-source the instances, oracle witnesses, and evaluation harness at https://github.com/DatagridsAI/DetourBench.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Ruixi Yu, Dairu Liu, Xuchuan Chen, Zekun Qi, Zekai Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: ScaleVLA, utilizing a 552B parameter backbone, enhances robot learning efficiency, generalization, and manipulation success compared to smaller Vision-Language-Action models.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yuke Li, Xuehan Hou, Jie Chen
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents a regression-free framework for GUI grounding that improves accuracy by decoupling instruction parsing from layout-aware localization, eliminating hallucinations in multimodal models.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: GUI agents are shifting from metadata-dependent large language models to purely visual multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that operate directly on screenshots. The core task, GUI grounding, requires translating abstract user instructions into precise element coordinates. This task faces a persistent dual obstacle: conventional grounding models lack the semantic richness to interpret abstract instructions, while end-to-end MLLMs suffer from coordinate hallucinations caused by deficient fine-grained perception. We propose a regression-free framework where a frozen MLLM performs instruction parsing and a dedicated grounding model handles precise localization without learning any coordinate regression. A frozen MLLM first elaborates the abstract instruction into a structured visual description rich in layout cues. These descriptions are then fed to a novel Layout-Aware GUI Grounding Model, which performs regression-free localization by matching against layout-prior candidates, inherently suppressing hallucinations and avoiding expensive fine-tuning. The grounding model is trained with only Text/Icon binary labels, requiring no coordinate regression parameters. On ScreenSpot-Pro, our method achieves over 20% improvement in grounding accuracy over end-to-end systems; on Mind2Web, it raises success rate and element selection rate by more than 15%. These results demonstrate that decoupling instruction understanding from layout-aware localization effectively resolves the core challenges of GUI interaction.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: When Does Cross-View Consistency Matter in Multi-View Appearance Augmentation? A Controlled Study for Visuomotor Policies
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zixuan Jiang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This study investigates the impact of cross-view consistency on multi-view visual augmentation for visuomotor policies, revealing selective constraints for appearance and geometry in manipulation tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Multi-view visual augmentation often seeks consistency across cameras, but it is unclear which forms of consistency matter for downstream control. We use simulation-state replay to manipulate cross-view coupling while preserving the per-camera perturbation distributions, physical trajectories, and action labels. Across seven LIBERO manipulation tasks, marginal-matched changes in global appearance, ghost injection, and target color have small average costs for a late-fusion Diffusion Policy: point estimates are near zero or negative, and the largest upper endpoint of the 90% posterior credible intervals is 2.55 percentage points. In contrast, geometrically anti-coupled observations reduce success by 3.30 percentage points relative to coupled observations (90% CrI [0.64, 6.28]), with displacement magnitude, direction marginals, and the number of affected views matched. Camera interventions reveal substantial dependence on wrist-view geometry, while feature analysis shows appearance sensitivity patterns associated with the factors randomized during training. ACT shows a higher target-color cost estimate than DP, with uncertainty that includes zero and sensitivity to task composition. Within the tested tasks and policy configurations, these findings motivate selective consistency constraints: appearance coupling can sometimes be relaxed, whereas task-relevant geometry and cross-view spatial correspondence warrant protection.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Vision-as-a-Tool: Visual Harness for Multimodal Agentic Coding
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Haolin Yang, Wenshan Wu, Jin Jiang, Yu Cheng, Yan Xia
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The Vision-as-a-Tool (VaaT) paradigm enhances multimodal agentic coding by enabling text-only agents to offload visual reasoning, improving performance across various generation tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Multimodal agentic coding requires robust visual reasoning to analyze observations and evaluate generated artifacts. Current frameworks largely rely on a Thinking-with-Images paradigm, where agents depend on their intrinsic vision to execute visually grounded tasks. However, this architectural coupling introduces a fundamental bottleneck. Agent performance remains strictly bounded by internal perceptual limitations. Furthermore, text-only agents lack native perception. Without specialized tools, they cannot perform visual reasoning. To overcome these constraints, we introduce the Vision-as-a-Tool (VaaT) paradigm. Prior visual tool-use merely manipulates images for an agent's intrinsic vision to read. In contrast, VaaT reframes general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as callable external utilities. As a result, text-only agents can completely offload visual reasoning during agentic execution. Meanwhile, vision-capable agents can dynamically augment their native perception on demand. We instantiate this paradigm in VHarness, a unified framework driven by five atomic actions. We comprehensively evaluate VHarness across Image-to-HTML, Image-to-SVG, and Image-to-3D generation tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that VHarness consistently improves visual fidelity and geometric accuracy across both text-only and multimodal coding agents. These findings highlight that modularizing visual reasoning into callable utilities provides a flexible and scalable foundation for future agentic coding systems.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Exposing and Mitigating Temporal Attack in Deepfake Video Detection
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zheyuan Gu, Minghao Shao, Zhen Wang, Keyu Mao, Ailiang Lin
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces SpInShield, a defense framework that enhances deepfake video detection by mitigating vulnerabilities to temporal evasion attacks through robust spectral analysis.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: While spatiotemporal deepfake detectors achieve high AUC, our experiments reveal their susceptibility to evasion attacks. These models tend to overfit on fragile temporal spectrum cues, rather than learning robust semantic causality. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose SpInShield, a temporal spectral-invariant defense framework explicitly designed to decouple semantic motion from manipulatable spectral artifacts. We propose a learnable spectral adversary that dynamically synthesizes severe spectral deformations, simulating extreme attack scenarios. By employing a shortcut suppression optimization strategy, SpInShield compels the encoder to extract reliable forensic cues while purging unstable spectral statistics from the latent space. Experiments show that SpInShield obtains competitive performance on widely used datasets and outperforms the strongest baseline by 21.30 percentage points in AUC under simulated amplitude spectral attacks.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jie Huang, Yuecheng Hong, Yao Chen, Shengding Jiao, Xudong Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: OutfitterBench evaluates LLM agents' performance in long-horizon resource allocation and commitment coordination, revealing limitations in maintaining feasible plans and reassessing resource value.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: In many long-horizon settings, an agent's own choices create future constraints: committing finite capacity establishes future obligations and forecloses later opportunities. Sustaining performance therefore requires both keeping evolving plans feasible and comparing the value of resource allocations with the alternatives they displace. Recent benchmarks increasingly evaluate LLM agents in continuing operations, but give less attention to how agents keep their own commitments feasible while reassessing resource allocations as opportunities change. We introduce OutfitterBench, where agents manage an outdoor-equipment rental business for 200 days, purchasing from a 46-product catalog and handling roughly 1,100 reservation requests. Under a fixed capital ceiling, reservations and uncertain walk-in demand compete for reusable equipment whose availability changes over time. Experiments with seven frontier LLMs show that several agents underperform a simple rule-based baseline, while only the leading agent consistently surpasses it. Trajectory analysis shows that some agents apply known constraints inconsistently and make new decisions that conflict with existing commitments. Agents with more reliable fulfillment can still secure low returns from comparable commitments or delay resource reallocation. The leading agent better connects preparation with economic choices but also misses opportunities for more profitable asset use. These findings highlight limitations in sustaining coherent resource plans and reassessing their value over time. The benchmark code is publicly available at https://github.com/adminblackjack/OutfitterBench.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: CFGComposer: Compositional Audio-Text-to-Motion Generation via Copula Score Correction
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Pengyang Shi, Jinlu Zhang, Chunze Lin, Yizhou Wang, Li Yi
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: CFGComposer addresses the Audio-Text-to-Motion challenge by refining joint inference through copula score correction, achieving superior semantic fidelity and beat alignment in embodied AI applications.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Generating whole-body gestures that are simultaneously rhythmically synchronized with speech audio and semantically aligned with text descriptions is a fundamental challenge in embodied AI and social robotics. We tackle this Audio-Text-to-Motion (AT2M) problem by composing two independently-trained diffusion models at inference time and refine bias in joint inference by modeling the copula score $s_I$. A rigorous theoretical analysis reveals that naive epsilon blending corresponds to a Product-of-Experts formulation that omits the copula score $s_I$: the cross-modal interaction between audio and text that neither marginal model can capture. We propose CFGComposer: a jointly-trained AT2M diffusion model that estimates $s_I$ via a CFG analogy and injects it as an $ε$-space correction. Experiments on BEAT demonstrate best-in-class semantic fidelity (SRGR $0.9916$, FID $27.18$) with GT-level beat alignment (BA $0.1826$ vs. GT $0.1743$), and 76-83% win rate in blind pairwise human evaluation against all prior methods. Physical deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid confirms direct sim-to-real transfer.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: TIDE: Token-Level Credit Assignment via Entropy-Gated Bounded Deviation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Qiaoman Zhang, Shunhua Min, Xiang He, Zhenghan Zhang, Yuting Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: TIDE introduces a critic-free reinforcement learning framework that enhances token-level supervision and exploration in large language models by using entropy-gated bounded deviation, outperforming existing methods.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is central for aligning large language models (LLMs) with complex reasoning, yet the leading critic-free algorithm, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), broadcasts a single sequence-level advantage uniformly across long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generations and constrains exploration with an unbounded Kullback-Leibler (KL) penalty, which dilutes token-level supervision and induces gradient instability and mode-seeking conservatism. We propose TIDE (Token-level Importance via Deviation and Entropy), a critic-free RL framework that reinterprets distribution deviation as a guiding signal rather than a rigid penalty. TIDE replaces the volatile reverse KL divergence with the bounded Hellinger distance, safely quantifying token-level exploration without risk of gradient explosion. To separate genuine reasoning breakthroughs from confident hallucinations, an entropy gating mechanism scales this deviation by the policy's predictive uncertainty, and the gated scores redistribute the sequence-level advantage across tokens. The resulting updates amplify exploratory steps while suppressing low-entropy deviations, without a value network and with negligible overhead. Across in-domain, held-out, and out-of-domain benchmarks, TIDE outperforms strong critic-free baselines: on the Qwen2.5-32B backbone it reaches 60.0% and 46.0% Avg@32 accuracy on AIME 2024 and AIME 2025, respectively, above competitive baselines such as DAPO. Token-level attribution, causal perturbation, and exploration analyses further support the interpretation that the entropy-gated deviation identifies pivotal reasoning steps rather than merely perturbing optimization dynamics.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Planning as Dynamics Relaxation: Hippocampal Recurrent Network Realizes Optimal Goal-Directed Navigation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yuhang He, Junfeng Zuo, Tianhao Chu, Si Wu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The hippocampal network utilizes relaxation dynamics and recurrent connections to transform cognitive maps into optimal, obstacle-avoiding navigation strategies through synaptic plasticity and goal-directed activity fields.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Neural correlates of the cognitive map are well documented, yet how a neural circuit turns a stored map into an obstacle-avoiding route remains unclear. Here we show that a hippocampal network with appropriate recurrent connections achieves optimal goal-directed navigation through its own relaxation dynamics. The recurrent weights represent the transition probabilities between the locations the neurons encode, walls are reflected by vanishing weights, and behavioral-timescale synaptic plasticity (BTSP) writes this connectivity during goal-free exploration. When a goal is recalled, a top-down current clamps the goal neuron and the population relaxes into a goal-locked activity field. We prove that this field is the desirability field of a linearly-solvable Markov decision process: the relaxed state is the exact optimum of a stated control problem, the KL-regularized objective of Todorov, and the optimal next-step distribution is carried by the branch synaptic currents. The identity extends to directed transitions, and a weak-cost limit returns the Green's function of the recurrent Laplacian. A place-tuned readout converts the field's log-gradient into a direction of travel, and the same synapses answer a predictive query when the source is placed at the current location. Simulations on mazes with complex obstacles show near-shortest routes, an identity that survives a thousand-fold range of recall amplitude, the loss of 80% of place cells, and tens of thousands of states, low-rank updates of every plan after a local change, and a transient that is anytime: the local action is ready long before the field converges. We hope this offers a general circuit principle for planning in abstract cognitive maps beyond spatial navigation.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zefan Wang, Yufan Dang, Xuanwei Shi, Mingqi Gao, Cheng Yin
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: JustRUA demonstrates that a simplified harness for GPT-6 Astra significantly enhances robot arm performance on RoboDojo, achieving a score increase from 29.7 to 50.3.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model. A lean harness that keeps the full episode history and stops each motion early goes a long way. Reusing experience changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch, and scene geometry helps most, even when depth is predicted from RGB alone. JustRUA starts from the official L3 harness and keeps only what matters most. Even with no learned policy, self-improvement loop or task-specific tuning, this simple harness raises the score on the RoboDojo simulation benchmark substantially, from 29.7 to 50.3.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Haofeng Wang, Pengcheng Wen, Ruiqi Li, Yuhao Zhang, Tiange Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: PhysCapBench is a novel benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, evaluating annotation quality across diverse domains to enhance language supervision in physical AI applications.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning strategies, and guide training-data refinement. Motivated by our data construction for world-model pretraining, we introduce PhysCapBench, to our knowledge the first unified physical-caption benchmark spanning all three domains: third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It provides human-verified annotations for 1,500 video sequences and evaluates accuracy and coverage through seven physical dimensions. We examine downstream utility through video reconstruction and manipulation-policy fine-tuning. Physical captions reduce reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos relative to metadata captions. Training-instruction enrichment improves both PhysCapBench scores and policy success, including a 7.5-percentage-point gain for pi0.5 on a RoboTwin 2.0 subtask. PhysCapBench makes the physical content of language supervision inspectable and comparable, providing a cross-domain basis for its evaluation and improvement.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: ManiLadder: Benchmarking Robot Manipulation Through a Categorized and Multi-Difficulty Level Task Ladder
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Chongkai Gao, Jieao Shi, Zhaoyu Mu, Yudi Lin, Xuanwei Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: ManiLadder introduces a structured benchmark with 112 robotic manipulation tasks across four difficulty levels, enabling systematic evaluation and comparison of learning progress in robotics.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Recent advances in robotic manipulation have enabled increasingly complex and dexterous behaviors, yet existing benchmarks still focus on simple pick-and-place tasks and lack a systematic framework for measuring progress in robot learning along the axis of task difficulty. We present ManiLadder, a large-scale and organized simulation benchmark for robotic manipulation. ManiLadder contains 112 carefully designed tasks stratified into 4 difficulty levels, with 8 categories in each level, spanning rigid-body and deformable-object manipulation, single-arm and dual-arm settings, and gripper and dexterous-hand end-effectors. To calibrate difficulty, we fix the data amount the same for every task and use a unified flow- matching imitation learning policy under the same training and evaluation protocols, then use its evaluation success rate as an operational empirical difficulty signal. All tasks are iteratively refined until they fall into target difficulty ranges, which are then verified across different random seeds, policies, and agentic learning systems. We further analyze the task properties, compare different policy performances and training settings, analyze task transfer and data scaling behaviors, and conduct real-world experiments showing that the designed tasks preserve their difficulty ordering beyond simulation. ManiLad- der provides a calibrated ladder for measuring, comparing, and advancing robotic manipulation capabilities. More results are available at https://maniladder-benchmark.github.io/.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via On-Policy Distillation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Lirui Luo, Kelong Mao, Xinwei Yang, Rongqing Li, Luyu Chen
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents CAMP-II, a method enhancing long-horizon task performance in language-model agents through on-policy distillation and file-based memory management in diverse environments.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Language-model agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks whose interaction histories exceed the model's active context. They must therefore decide what to write down and what to read back, and when to do either. Recent work has begun to use on-policy distillation (OPD) to make memory control part of the policy, relying on memory tools and compaction protocols that lie outside either model's pre-training. However, this weakens the distillation on both sides: the teacher cannot give useful guidance on an interface it has never used, and the student samples too few meaningful memory actions for that guidance to take effect. To study this problem, we introduce Coding Agent Memory Gym II (CAMG-II), a suite of long-horizon agentic-RL environments spanning Shop, Coding, AutoResearch, General, and Visual. Alongside each environment's native task interface, CAMG-II provides ordinary Bash access and an episode-persistent workspace, enabling the policy to create, revise, search, and reuse files as memory across context replacements. We also introduce Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II (CAMP-II), which trains a single policy jointly across all five environments with fully asynchronous OPD to learn this file-based memory behavior directly from a frozen teacher with a prior for file operations. On CAMG-II, CAMP-II obtains 2.97 times the gain of the strongest OPD baseline. The memory behavior CAMP-II learns generalizes to two external benchmarks, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Pro V2, with improved success rates.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Stylization as Geodesic Navigation on Diffusion Manifolds
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yan Li, Zehao Li, Xinlong Sun, Fuchen Long, Xi Chen
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Stylus is a training-free framework for facial stylization that navigates diffusion manifolds, enabling fine control over style while preserving identity through geodesic energy optimization.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Facial stylization asks for a delicate transformation: the image should look unmistakably artistic, yet the person should remain unmistakably the same. Existing training-free and instruction-driven methods often fail to expose such control, either drifting away from identity or producing only weak stylization. We introduce Stylus, a training-free framework that treats facial style transfer as navigation on the curved latent manifold of a pretrained diffusion model. Rather than interpolating in flat Euclidean space, \method refines the interpolated content--style point by lowering a ratio-weighted discrete geodesic energy under the pullback metric, made tractable by a rank-one power-iteration approximation of the Jacobian. This principle drives two complementary controls: content--style latent interpolation for smooth semantic fusion, and self-attention query optimization for spatially adaptive style injection. The resulting dual-control mechanism provides continuous, fine-grained control over stylization strength while preserving identity-critical facial structure, all without additional training. Experiments show that Stylus achieves the strongest identity and content preservation at competitive stylization strength.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: With Tools or Because of Tools? Tracing Capability Gains in Multimodal Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiawei Guo, Donglei Yu, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The study critiques the assumption that tool-augmented multimodal agents improve capabilities, revealing they often learn tool-calling patterns without significant enhancement in problem-solving abilities.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Tool-augmented multimodal agents show strong benchmark gains, often taken as evidence that agents have learned to use tools. We argue that this interpretation can be premature: a tool-call trace alone does not show whether the tool supplied answer-critical information. We study two representative ``thinking with images'' agents, Thyme and DeepEyesV2, across real-world understanding, OCR, chart understanding, and mathematical reasoning. Each agent is compared with its Tool-Free counterpart and with a Pure-Text Reasoner trained from the same source pool without tool-calling trajectories. Tool access yields little consistent aggregate improvement, does not reliably reduce generated-token cost, and leaves only a small tool-only solved set: 93% of DeepEyesV2's tool-solved problems and 96% of Thyme's are also solved by at least one non-tool setting. Mechanism ablations further show that the full tool-use loop does not consistently outperform either the tool-call format or the returned execution result alone. In the settings we study, the analyzed agents appear to learn tool-calling patterns more reliably than tool-contributed capabilities, suggesting that evaluation should distinguish tool availability from whether tools actually expand what agents can solve.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Sirui Li, Rui Zhao, Siqi Cai, Haizhou Li, Tiejun Huang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: MADSNet is a novel spiking neural network that enhances image reconstruction from spike camera data, achieving superior fidelity and efficiency compared to existing methods.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Spike cameras encode dynamic scenes into high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams for efficient high-speed vision. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) can process such signals with sparse and accumulate-only computation, existing SNN-based reconstruction methods are typically shallow and still lag behind ANN-based models in reconstruction fidelity. This paper proposes MADSNet, a Multi-scale Axial-attentive Dense Spiking Network for spike camera image reconstruction. MADSNet adopts a hierarchical spiking encoder--decoder, where a multi-scale spike stem extracts early features, axial spike attention captures long-range dependencies, a dense spiking bottleneck enhances feature reuse, and a spike-to-continuous decoder reconstructs continuous intensity images from spike-domain representations. Experiments on gray-scale and color spike reconstruction show that MADSNet outperforms SSIR by 4.3 dB PSNR and Spk2ImgNet by 1.94 dB on SREDS. Compared with Spk2ImgNet, it achieves about 15$\times$ lower latency and uses only about 1/40 of the estimated energy, demonstrating that carefully designed SNN architectures can improve reconstruction quality while preserving computational efficiency.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yuhan Tang, Ke Fan, Xinkai Zou, Baichuan Mo, Kangxin Cui
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces Ask2Decide, a benchmark assessing LLM agents' ability to acquire crucial decision-making information from humans, revealing significant shortcomings in their planning efficacy.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Lin Long, Tianren Ma, Zhong Chu, Di Wu, Maosong Cao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper presents SPAR, a method leveraging human egocentric videos to enhance robot policy learning through independent visual state predictions, improving performance on diverse tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: In this paper, we investigate how human egocentric videos can benefit robot policy learning without action supervision. Building on a pretrained VLM, we propose Shared Prediction on Action and Representation (SPAR), an MoT architecture in which future visual state prediction can provide independent and complementary learning signals alongside action prediction. We find that representations learned from egocentric videos improve downstream performance on out-of-distribution robot tasks, with further gains as video data scales. We also study the effects of objective choices and data curation, providing insights into how to leverage action-free videos for scalable robot learning.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: A 10K drone image dataset with component-level annotations for rooftop photovoltaic inspection
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Penglei Zhang, Wan Zhang, Ruizhe Deng, Bo Chen, Wenhao Duan
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The PVIS-10K dataset consists of 10,065 annotated drone images for precise component-level inspection of rooftop photovoltaic systems, enhancing localization and counting capabilities.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Component-level information supports rooftop photovoltaic (PV) inspection, but recognizing individual components across complex scenes remains challenging. We present PVIS-10K, a dataset of 10,065 drone images with component-level annotations covering 63,632 physical PV modules across 22 rooftop installations. The high-resolution red-green-blue (RGB) images were acquired by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs, also known as drones) in Ningbo, Shaoxing and Shenzhen, China. Multi-angle oblique observations capture installation-height and scale variation, dense arrangements, occlusion, shadows and reflections. Three-dimensional delineation, reprojection and image-by-image review produced 3,516,675 image-level polygon annotations, stored in Common Objects in Context (COCO) format. Station-disjoint partitions support evaluation on unseen stations within and across cities. Four supervised models and text-prompted zero-shot Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) provide full-resolution benchmarks of instance matching and foreground coverage. PVIS-10K supports component localization, delineation and image-based counting for drone-based rooftop PV inspection research.
