During training, action consistency regularization reconstructs the first demonstrated command from observed and predicted feature changes, encouraging the predictor to retain action-relevant information. On ten tasks in the humanoid loco-manipulation simulation benchmark SIMPLE, our method achieves 89.7% average success, compared with 73.7% for Psi-Zero and 82.0% for DiT4DiT. On seven real-robot tasks, it achieves 85.7% under standard conditions and 65.7% under unseen object configurations, while GR00T N1.7 achieves 70.0% and 48.6%, respectively. Project page: https://ju6276.github.io/Action-Grounded-Foresight/

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: ExeWorldBench: Benchmarking Code-Based Executable 3D World Modeling
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Xinge Peng, Zhen Fang, Ruibing Wang, Yongxuan Lv, Haodong Li
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: ExeWorldBench is a novel benchmark for evaluating code-based 3D world modeling, integrating world understanding and executable realization across three progressively challenging tasks.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Coding agents are increasingly evolving beyond reproducing what a world looks like toward constructing executable worlds that capture how a world works. This shift calls for executable world modeling, which integrates two core capabilities: world understanding, reasoning about the underlying structural, mechanical, and causal principles of a world, and executable realization, translating that understanding into a code-based system whose behavior emerges from physical interactions. However, existing benchmarks provide only fragmented evaluations centered on physical reasoning, visual fidelity, or behavioral correctness, leaving the integration of these capabilities insufficiently assessed. To bridge this gap, we introduce ExeWorldBench, to our knowledge the first benchmark to comprehensively evaluate world understanding and executable realization through code-based 3D world construction. ExeWorldBench comprises three progressively challenging tasks: Mechanism Executability, which evaluates the realization of individual mechanisms from visual observations; Compositional Executability, which extends to multi-stage systems with spatial, mechanical, and causal dependencies; and Intent-Driven Executable World Synthesis, which requires constructing executable worlds from high-level goals and physical requirements. Extensive experiments on frontier models reveal substantial limitations in executable world modeling, offering insights into the development of more physically grounded and causally coherent world construction systems.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: GSExplorer: Interactive World Generation with a Persistent 3D Gaussian World State
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Sicheng Yu, Liu Liu, Xinjie Wang, Xinjiang Wang, Taojun Ding
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: GSExplorer introduces a persistent 3D Gaussian world state for interactive world generation, enhancing scene consistency and camera control through a novel generation-reconstruction framework.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Interactive world generation requires both accurate local control and stable scene consistency over long rollouts. Existing methods improve local generation through camera or geometry conditioning and extend historical context with memory mechanisms. However, long-horizon exploration remains challenging as target-view guidance becomes incomplete and inconsistencies accumulate across repeated scene updates. We present \textbf{GSExplorer}, a generation--reconstruction framework built around a persistent 3D Gaussian world state. At each step, the current 3DGS scene provides multimodal rendering conditions for a condition-driven video generator, while camera geometry is injected through a separate Relative Ray Encoding branch. Generated videos are then fed back to a SLAM-based reconstruction backend, where inconsistency filtering prevents conflicting content from corrupting the scene and cross-chunk bundle adjustment improves spatial alignment across generation steps. We further design a data-construction pipeline that reproduces realistic 3DGS degradation during scene extrapolation, yielding 293K training pairs of degraded multimodal renderings and real target videos. GSExplorer achieves the best overall performance among the compared methods on both single-step and three-step WorldScore evaluation, with strong camera control and consistency across both settings, including a Camera Control score of 99.07 in single-step extrapolation. On 481-frame leave-and-return rollouts, it also shows strong revisit consistency, demonstrating the value of maintaining a reliable 3D world state for continued exploration.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: UA-Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Depth Restoration for Material-Agnostic Object Manipulation
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Rui Cao, Jia-Hui Pan, Yin Zhang, Qiwei Meng, Jiapeng Li
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: UA-Depth is an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that enhances robotic manipulation by improving depth accuracy for non-Lambertian objects through iterative co-refinement and uncertainty-gated features.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Robotic manipulation requires accurate metric depth, yet commodity RGB-D cameras often fail on non-Lambertian objects such as transparent, reflective, and translucent materials, producing holes, structured noise, and biased depth. Most restoration methods produce only a single depth map, treating noisy and reliable regions uniformly for downstream tasks while ignoring regional uncertainty. We present UA-Depth, an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that iteratively co-refines depth and pixel-wise uncertainty, and uses uncertainty-gated features to suppress unreliable cues for stable updates. To strengthen zero-shot behavior, UA-Depth leverages a frozen depth foundation model as a prior to initialize missing or unreliable depth, and applies two-stage MAD-weighted log-depth scale normalization to reduce outlier bias in relative-to-metric alignment. We introduce an eight-dataset zero-shot benchmark across diverse scenes, materials, and sensors. Across these benchmarks, UA-Depth achieves the best mean rank among representative baselines, with particularly strong gains on datasets dominated by transparent and reflective objects. Beyond depth metrics, we demonstrate downstream improvements in category-level 6D pose estimation and 6D grasp synthesis by exploiting the predicted uncertainty. \emph{Code, models, and data for training and evaluation will be released upon publication.}

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Efficient Agentic Audio-Visual Question Answering through Toolset Pruning and Modality Consolidation
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yi Wang, Tianzi Wang, Peter Bell
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: This paper demonstrates that a compact omni-modal agent for audio-visual question answering can achieve similar or improved accuracy while reducing inference costs by 70% compared to specialized agents.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Fine-grained audio-visual question answering (AVQA) requires models to resolve complex cross-modal correspondences and temporally grounding from sparsely distributed evidence. Omni-modal agents, which autonomously orchestrate perception tools to actively collect evidence, achieve strong performance, but it remains unclear whether active perception from both audio and visual modalities depends on broad specialized toolsets, especially audio or visual modality-specific tools. Such systems may also introduce long execution trajectories and substantial inference cost. We investigate whether comparable performance can be retained with a compact workflow exposing only essential perceptual capabilities. Starting from the specialized-tool OmniAgent, we conduct staged controlled experiments that prune the toolset and progressively consolidate modality-specific tools into omni-modal tools, motivating a two-tool agent comprising only Omni-modal captioning and Omni-modal QA. Across three widely used AVQA benchmarks, our compact agent achieves comparable or better accuracy than the specialized-tool agent while reducing inference cost by around 70%.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Self-Evolving Agentic Workflows via Semantic Decomposition of Complex Tasks
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Zichuan Fu, Junjia Qi, Xian Wu, Wenlin Zhang, Yimin Deng
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper presents a framework for self-evolving agentic workflows that optimizes complex task execution through semantic decomposition and iterative refinement based on execution feedback.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Agentic workflows organize complex tasks into reusable procedures. However, invoking an LLM at every step incurs repeated inference costs and delays. We propose a framework for self-evolving agentic workflows through semantic task decomposition. Each subtask has explicit applicability conditions and a procedure that executes code or invokes a model as needed. An agent uses execution feedback to refine the decomposition and update these procedures. Experiments in the GLEE competition show the framework on bargaining, negotiation and persuasion. Most observed final-decision procedures are implemented in code. Code is available at https://github.com/Applied-Machine-Learning-Lab/NeurIPS2026_SeaFlow.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: PointPilot: Unified Robotic Manipulation via Object-Centric 3D Point Flow Prediction
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yihan Fang, Yuxin Tian, Ruixiang Wang, Zhanqi Zhang, Xing Hu
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: PointPilot is a unified robotic manipulation framework that predicts 3D point flow for task-focused objects, enabling zero-shot generalization across diverse embodiments and manipulation modes.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Generalization remains a central challenge in robotics, calling for policies that address domain variations from multiple dimensions such as diverse embodiments, camera poses, and/or scene layouts. In order to approach this problem, we introduce PointPilot, a task-focused and 3D aligned manipulation framework built on a 3D space point-flow prediction. Rather than modeling the global scene, PointPilot only represents task-focused objects (robot grippers treated as objects), avoiding the prediction of potentially redundant scene parts unrelated to the manipulation tasks. Moreover, PointPilot aligns 3D spatial representation in one unified coordinate and supports closed-loop and fully automatic action execution across different manipulation modes from object point flow without a separately trained action expert, while existing works typically need an extra action head or are (semi-)automatic and single-arm mode specific. Given sensor observations and language instructions, our model jointly learns subtask planning, task-relevant object grounding, and 3D point flow prediction in an end-to-end way. By processing heterogeneous data in a shared 3D point flow space, PointPilot is able to absorb demonstrations from different embodiments. Extensive simulative and real world experiments validate our method. Notably, we demonstrate zero-shot embodiment generalization with PointPilot. A single trained policy can be deployed on previously unseen embodiments and successfully complete manipulation tasks without any additional fine-tuning.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Positive Safety Margins from Artificial Potential Field Reward Augmentation for Size-Robust Obstacle Avoidance under Partial Observability
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Ziyi Hao
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper demonstrates that augmenting reinforcement learning rewards with an artificial potential field can significantly enhance obstacle avoidance safety margins under partial observability, achieving high success rates.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Collision-free reaching is central to manipulation, yet real cells often leave the size and exact position of an obstacle unobserved, which excludes reinforcement learning controllers that take obstacle geometry as input. A reward limited to a collision penalty does not depend on the clearance outside the obstacle, so under a step cost its learned policy skims the obstacle surface and fails once the obstacle radius exceeds its training value. We investigate whether a single analytic reward term can induce a safety margin without exposing the obstacle to the policy. We augment the reward of a simulated Franka Emika Panda reaching task with a horizontal artificial potential field that penalizes proximity within a safety margin around each of two pillars (fixed nominal layout, random drift). Under hidden observation, policies trained with this term maintain a safe success rate above 88% across a radius sweep from 0.03 m to 0.055 m (30 seeds), while policies without it fall below 10% at the maximum tested radius; the term induces a minimum clearance of 47.9 mm against 9.6 mm without it and eliminates training collisions at least eight times earlier (median steps). The advantage is statistically significant at all out-of-distribution radii and holds across three reinforcement learning solvers and under full observation. Its safe success rate is comparable to that of a classical potential-field planner given the pillar positions. The margin is a fixed buffer rather than an adaptation to the radius, and it lengthens the path by about 19%.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Zhicheng He, Xiaohan Xing, Hongqiu Wang, Kun Yuan, Guankun Wang
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: SurgPace introduces a complexity-aware framework for progressive distillation of surgical multimodal large language models, enhancing efficiency and stability in training through tailored supervision strategies.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: ROOF: Learning Humanoid Fall Recovery under Overhead Constraints
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yidan Lu, Jiayuan Yu, Zongrui Cai, Jingwen Sun, Jinrui Han
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper presents a reinforcement learning approach for humanoid fall recovery under overhead constraints, achieving significant success in both simulation and real-world scenarios.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: A fallen humanoid beneath an overhead obstacle faces a coupled recovery problem. It must create clearance while organizing support for a stable rise, since attempting to stand before making room can further increase obstruction. We introduce a reinforcement learning method with contact-supported geometric escape guidance, which rewards incremental reduction of robot-obstacle overlap without prescribing an escape path. To achieve this, a learned motion prior, together with posture-dependent support and joint-stall costs, is proposed to shape a single policy that learns when to clear the obstacle, how to establish support, and when to complete the rise, all using proprioception alone. In simulation, it recovers in 88.5% of trials beneath plates that can only be lifted, compared with 18.9% without geometric guidance, and in 98.6% of trials beneath free plates with randomized size, mass and placement. On a Unitree G1, the deployed policy recovered in 95 of 150 attempts across seven real-world obstacle scenes, including furniture and multi-object arrangements absent from training. Project page: https://lu-yidan.github.io/ROOF/

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: OmniPiano: Diverse Dexterous Piano-Playing Challenges for Standard, Robust, Safe, and Multi-Agent RL
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Fan Xu, Fan Yang, Yifan Xu, Ruiyuan Zhang, Yimou Wu
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: OmniPiano introduces a modular benchmark for multi-agent RL in piano playing, enhancing evaluation with diverse tasks, safety constraints, and extensive algorithm comparisons.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Dexterous robotic manipulation remains a major challenge in robotics, exemplified by piano playing, which requires coordinated control of fingers and provides a demanding testbed for reinforcement learning (RL). Although previous work established a benchmark for robotic piano playing, it is restricted to two hands and does not support unified evaluation. To address this gap, we introduce OmniPiano, a benchmark that provides one to up to five Shadow Hands and supports standard, robust, safe, and multi-agent RL within a shared piano-playing task family. OmniPiano is developed for scalable and diverse piano-playing tasks with configurable perturbations, explicit safety constraints, and decentralized cooperation settings. Particularly, to facilitate usability and extendability, OmniPiano adopts a highly modular design and provides comprehensive tasks to support RL study of task performance, robustness, safety, and cooperation in dexterous control. With at least 912 task settings and 36 baseline algorithms, OmniPiano further incorporates LLM-based agents to broaden the evaluation scope and reveal new insights. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art RL algorithms and frontier LLM-based agents still struggle on challenging piano-playing tasks, even under standard RL settings, highlighting substantial room for improvement in dexterous control. The code, dataset, tutorial, and demo are available at https://sail-research-lab.github.io/omnipiano/.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Reconstruction as Spatial Evaluation: Diagnosing Cross-View Spatial Intelligence in Large Vision-Language Models
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Junfei Wu, Qiuyue Wang, Xuhong Huang, Qihang Peng, Mingsheng Li
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces RECONSPATIAL, a benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models' spatial intelligence through multi-view 3D scene reconstruction, revealing significant gaps in structural and metric accuracy.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: The spatial intelligence of large vision-language models (LVLMs) requires the ability to combine local visual observations into a geometrically consistent representation of the physical world. Many static benchmarks assess isolated spatial judgments, such as relative direction or distance, while interactive embodied evaluations combine perception with exploration, planning, control, and simulator-specific execution. To bridge this gap, we introduce RECONSPATIAL, a benchmark centered on multi-view 3D scene reconstruction across indoor, tabletop, and outdoor environments. Given real multi-view images and target-object queries, LVLMs are required to jointly predict oriented 3D bounding boxes in a shared, camera-anchored metric coordinate frame. Reconstructions are evaluated along two complementary axes: Structure for relative layout and Metric for physical scale and camera-anchored placement. Nine atomic spatial QA tasks, grouped into Geometric Perception and Spatial Relations, probe spatial capabilities involved in joint reconstruction. Offline navigation extends evaluation to path planning. Evaluation of 18 frontier LVLMs reveals a consistent gap between relative scene structure and metric reconstruction; even GPT-6-Astra scores 81.4% on Structure but only 58.7% on Metric. Tracing this gap, diagnostic analyses link atomic spatial capabilities to reconstruction quality and show that relational consistency alone does not ensure metric accuracy. Experiments with 3D map injection further separate scene construction from path planning, revealing how these geometric errors limit navigation success. Finally, spatial fine-tuning yields broad transfer across both spatial and general vision-language benchmarks.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: The Alignment Illusion: How BadReward Corrupts Text-to-Image Generation
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Kaiwen Duan, Hongwei Yao, Yufei Chen, Ziyun Li, Tong Qiao
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: This paper introduces BadReward, a novel attack exploiting Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback vulnerabilities in text-to-image models, demonstrating effective reward signal corruption through clean-label poisoning.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Modern text-to-image generative models increasingly rely on Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to align generated content with human preferences and safety standards. This post-training stage is critical for optimizing models toward high-fidelity and value-aligned behaviors using human preference data. However, while previous works have extensively investigated poisoning attacks against the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) stage of text-to-image training, the security vulnerabilities introduced by the RLHF process remain unexplored. In this paper, we present the first exploration into the feasibility of poisoning the RLHF process as a novel attack surface for compromising text-to-image models. We introduce BadReward, an indirect clean-label poisoning attack that manipulates reward signals to embed malicious behaviors. Our approach leverages a feature collision mechanism to produce poison preference image pairs that are visually benign, but aligned with a malicious target concept in the reward feature space. Our experiments demonstrate that this manipulation effectively corrupts the reward signal. Online RLHF further amplifies this corruption through its reward-model feedback loop, whereas offline preference optimization learns directly from the poisoned preferences. Finally, we demonstrate the real-world effectiveness of BadReward on modern text-to-image architectures, showing high attack success rates and visual stealthiness across different RLHF algorithms. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZJUICSR/BadReward.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: DiffCap-Bench: A Comprehensive, Challenging, Robust Benchmark for Image Difference Captioning
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yuancheng Wei, Haojie Zhang, Linli Yao, Lei Li, Jiali Chen
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: DiffCap-Bench introduces a robust benchmark for Image Difference Captioning, addressing existing evaluation gaps and enhancing multimodal language model assessments through diverse categories and human-validated metrics.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Image Difference Captioning (IDC) generates natural language descriptions that precisely identify differences between two images, serving as a key benchmark for fine-grained change perception, cross-modal reasoning, and image editing data construction. However, existing benchmarks lack diversity and compositional complexity, and standard lexical-overlap metrics (e.g., BLEU, METEOR) fail to capture semantic consistency or penalize hallucinations, which together prevent a comprehensive and robust evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on IDC. To address these gaps, we introduce DiffCap-Bench, a comprehensive IDC benchmark covering ten distinct difference categories to ensure diversity and compositional complexity. Furthermore, we propose an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation protocol grounded in human-validated Difference Lists, enabling a robust assessment of models' ability to both capture and describe visual changes. Through extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art MLLMs, we reveal significant performance gaps between proprietary and open-source models, highlight the critical importance of reasoning capability, and identify clear limitations in model scaling. Our framework also demonstrates strong alignment with human expert judgments and strong correlation with downstream image editing data construction quality. These findings establish DiffCap-Bench as both a reliable IDC evaluation framework and a practical predictor of downstream utility. The benchmark and code will be made publicly available to support further research.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Lookahead Prediction-Guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing for Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Mengzhao Wang, Yanli Ji, Peng Ye
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper presents LPAVR, a framework that enhances multimodal reasoning by dynamically refocusing visual evidence based on anticipated reasoning needs, addressing Temporal Evidence Myopia.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning improves the visual reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models by dynamically incorporating visual evidence during reasoning. However, existing methods primarily select evidence from historical context. When the reasoning focus shifts, history-guided evidence may remain focused on prior regions and fail to cover the visual information required by the next step. We refer to this lag between visual evidence and subsequent reasoning demands as Temporal Evidence Myopia. To address this issue, we propose Lookahead Prediction-guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing (LPAVR), a training-free test-time framework. LPAVR transforms Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) from a decoding acceleration mechanism into a lookahead signal for anticipating upcoming reasoning intent. During MTP decoding, the draft head generates multiple future tokens, while the target model verifies them in parallel and retains the longest prefix consistent with its decoding trajectory. This target-verified prefix contains near-future semantics, which LPAVR uses to construct lookahead-guided visual evidence and assess whether history-guided evidence covers the indicated regions. If the coverage is sufficient, the history-guided evidence is retained; otherwise, LPAVR switches to the lookahead-guided evidence. This better aligns the visual context with upcoming reasoning and improves consistency between draft predictions and target-model decoding. Experiments on multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks show that LPAVR improves both reasoning accuracy and the acceptance rates of MTP speculative tokens, jointly enhancing visual reasoning and speculative decoding efficiency.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: PlanContext: Benchmarking In-Context Driving Decision-Making
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Ruikai Li, Naiyu Gao, Hao Shan, Yizhe Fan, Yanhao Wu
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: PlanContext introduces a benchmark for evaluating context-aware driving decision-making, revealing that high trajectory quality does not guarantee effective in-context decisions across various driving scenarios.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Real-world driving requires context-aware decision-making. Existing end-to-end driving benchmarks primarily assess trajectory quality through safety, compliance, comfort, and driving progress, leaving context-dependent decision-making insufficiently characterized. To fill this gap, we present PlanContext, a benchmark for evaluating in-context driving decision-making. PlanContext constructs paired evaluations by varying high-level driving intentions while keeping the observed scene fixed, enabling a natural and controllable assessment of context-dependent decision-making. We further define six representative driving contexts and jointly evaluate contextual decision correctness, road compliance, and dynamic safety with class-balanced metrics. Experiments on 9,561 scene-condition instances from NAVSIM and 23 public end-to-end driving models show that high conventional driving-quality scores do not consistently correspond to strong route-level in-context driving decision-making. Further analysis shows that model behavior varies with decision timing, road structure, and traffic interaction depending on the decision required by the current context. Our results highlight in-context driving decision-making as an important complementary dimension for evaluating end-to-end driving systems.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yijia Fan, Xilin He, Yilei Jiang, Dongming Wu, Jiaxu Wang
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: CaPtain is an open post-training pipeline that transforms small vision-language models into effective code-as-policy robot agents, achieving significant performance improvements without relying on pre-trained models.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Across coding, web, and tool-use tasks, language-model agents are now routinely trained with the same recipe: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn the interface, then multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) to master it. Code-as-policy (CaP) casts robot manipulation in the same form, as the policy writes code against robot APIs and reads back the results, so the same recipe should apply. Yet existing CaP agents sidestep training: they either prompt closed frontier models or delegate manipulation to pre-trained vision-language-action models (VLAs) and high-level skills, while small open vision-language models (VLMs) fail outright. We present CaPtain, an open post-training pipeline that turns a small open VLM into a capable CaP agent, with no VLA, frontier model, or privileged state at test time. CaPtain trains and deploys the policy inside CaPtain-Harness, which exposes low-level perception, geometry, and guarded-motion primitives across simulation and real hardware. We first align the base model via SFT on synthetic trajectories generated with GPT-6 Astra, then apply multi-turn RL. Multi-turn RL must credit tens of agent requests, whose physical effects often surface turns later, from a single end-of-episode outcome. We therefore introduce a physical critic that reads privileged simulator state, never seen by the policy, and credits each request by how much it changes the predicted chance of success. Starting from Qwen3.5-4B (0% zero-shot), CaPtain-4B reaches 55.4% held-out LIBERO success after SFT and 73.8% after RL. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 78.5%, surpassing several frontier-model agents, and its RL gains persist across three perturbation suites (+17.6 to +21.2 points). Without target-domain training, it attains 83.3% on SimplerEnv WidowX, exceeds frontier models on CaP-Bench, and runs on a real robot after simulation-only adaptation. We release all code, data, and model weights.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: FlowMoDE: Coarse-to-fine Flow Matching for Detail-aware Sim-to-Real Monocular Depth Estimation
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Jinsong Lin, Zhiwei Fang, Hongliang Ren
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: FlowMoDE introduces a coarse-to-fine flow-matching framework for efficient, detail-aware monocular depth estimation, outperforming existing methods in sim-to-real applications.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Monocular depth estimation is a fundamental capability for 3D spatial perception in robotic and intelligent systems. While data-driven discriminative methods have achieved compelling performance for monocular depth estimation, generative approaches can reconstruct fine structural details with stronger generalization. However, most existing generative diffusion models suffer from low inference efficiency caused by multi-step sampling, whereas single-step diffusion models struggle to recover high-fidelity depth maps. To mitigate these drawbacks, this paper presents FlowMoDE, a coarse-to-fine flow-matching-based framework for efficient, structure-aware monocular depth estimation supporting sim-to-real and cross-scene generalization. The core architecture first conducts coarse-level decoding conditioned on diffused features extracted from a pre-trained semantic encoder, and subsequently restores fine-grained structural patterns via expanded decoding layers. Trained exclusively on a single synthetic indoor dataset, our proposed method outperforms prior methods across five real-world indoor and outdoor datasets, yielding an average 14.1% reduction in relative error against state-of-the-art works as well as 9.9\% reduction in chamfer distance for point cloud reconstruction. We further validate the generalization capability of FlowMoDE on realistic robotic scenes, with qualitative comparisons against state-of-the-art methods. The project page is https://flowmode-shao.netlify.app/

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: HandMimicX: Learning Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation via an Object-Centric Policy from Egocentric Videos
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Zihan Gao, Yufei Liu, Yuhong Zhang, Zhen Yu, Xinhao Huang
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: HandMimicX presents an object-centric framework for learning dexterous manipulation from egocentric videos, enabling generalizable robotic skills through reinforcement learning and natural hand-object interactions.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from human videos remains an open challenge, particularly in the context of transferring a single demonstration into a spatially generalizable robotic skill and maintaining physically plausible human-like interactions. Unlike prior works that emphasize hand-motion imitation, we introduce an object-centric framework for acquiring dexterous skills from egocentric human RGB-D videos. Within our framework, we formulate the reinforcement learning (RL) objective in terms of object motion to decouple the underlying skill from the specific hand trajectory and impose constraints on hand-object interaction states to promote more anatomically natural hand configurations. Extensive experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate that our method enables efficient learning from human videos and generalizable skill transfer across novel spatial configurations.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Parse Before You Execute: Efficient Spatial Reasoning with Executable Primitives
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xinling Zhuang, Xuhui Li, Yichen Li
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The PEPS framework enhances spatial reasoning in Vision-Language Models by committing to executable requirements before execution, improving accuracy and efficiency while reducing costs and latency.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) has increasingly benefited from tool-integrated pipelines that ground computation in explicit geometry. However, existing systems often compile queries into relatively open-ended artifacts, such as code, task constraints, tool plans, or gathered evidence, leaving what must be resolved before execution under-specified. This can lead to unnecessary tool acquisition and iterative refinement, while still producing plausible reasoning traces from incomplete spatial commitments. We identify this failure mode as under-committed query compilation. To address it, we propose PEPS, a training-free agentic paradigm Parsing Executable Primitives for Spatial reasoning under a typed FESM schema over Frame, Entity, State, and Metric. PEPS follows a parse-before-execute principle: the Parser commits each query to a compact set of executable requirements; the Executor selectively grounds the required primitives through fixed geometric APIs and deterministic computation; and the Verifier checks execution sufficiency, enabling early termination or targeted repair. Extensive experiments across challenging spatial reasoning benchmarks show that PEPS consistently improves reasoning accuracy while substantially reducing refinement rounds, API cost, and end-to-end latency over strong tool-integrated baselines. These results demonstrate that explicit requirement commitment can make tool-integrated spatial reasoning not only more reliable, but also more execution-efficient.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Verify--Backtrack Loop: Structured Precondition Recovery for Long-Horizon Language Agents
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Mingyang Liu, Qingcan Kang, Shixiong Kai, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The Verify--Backtrack Loop (VBL) enhances long-horizon language agents by structuring precondition recovery and failure diagnosis, significantly improving task success rates over existing methods.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Language agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks in interactive environments, where actions often depend on latent preconditions. The core difficulty is not trajectory length but recovery: when a prerequisite is missing or an earlier decomposition fails, trying another plausible action rarely helps. ReAct and later reflection or adaptive-planning methods support local correction, but express recovery as free-form text, with no explicit control state linking the terminal goal, the active goal, and the failure source. We introduce the Verify--Backtrack Loop (VBL), a training-free extension of ReAct that turns precondition discovery and failure diagnosis into structured planning-state updates. VBL maintains the task decomposition as a bounded goal stack and, on goal activation, execution failure, or material state change, jointly verifies two horizons---whether the active goal contributes to the terminal goal and whether it is feasible in the current state. These dual-horizon judgments, combined with typed failure attribution, trigger explicit operations---Push, Pop, retry, or BacktrackTo the parent. We evaluate VBL with Qwen3.5-9B, GPT-4o, and DeepSeek-V3.2 on AppWorld, ALFWorld, and ScienceWorld. VBL improves over ReAct and reflection-based control on every backbone--benchmark pair. On the challenging AppWorld setting, it improves task success by up to 22.07 percentage points over ReAct. Ablations show that removing either verification or diagnosis degrades performance, in several settings below ReAct, confirming that the two mechanisms are complementary. These results show that reliable long-horizon interaction benefits from revising the planning state, not merely the next action.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: M$^\star$: Every Task Deserves Its Own Memory Harness
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Wenbo Pan, Shujie Liu, Xiangyang Zhou, Xianlong Wang, Shiwei Zhang
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: M$^\star$ introduces a method for automatically creating task-specific memory harnesses, enhancing performance in diverse applications like conversation and planning through reflective code evolution.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Large language model agents rely on a memory harness to write, organize, retrieve, and use past experience. A harness that works for one task often fails on another, because conversations, embodied planning, and expert reasoning require different storage and retrieval behavior. To address this limitation, we introduce Mstar, a method that automatically discovers task-optimized memory programs through reflective code evolution. Specifically, Mstar operationalizes a memory harness as an executable Python memory program that defines the Schema, Logic, and Instruction, and optimizes these components jointly. We evaluate Mstar on four tasks covering conversation, embodied planning, and specialized reasoning. Our results demonstrate that Mstar improves performance over existing baselines across all evaluated tasks. Furthermore, the evolved memory programs exhibit structurally distinct processing mechanisms for each evaluated domain. These findings suggest that every task benefits from its own memory harness, and that memory-program search provides a concrete way to discover it.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: GUI-Lens: Enabling Precise GUI Grounding for Off-the-Shelf VLMs via Coarse-to-Fine Cropping
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Zichuan Fu, Shirong Wang, Wenlin Zhang, Guojing Li, Yimin Deng
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: GUI-Lens enhances GUI grounding accuracy for VLMs by employing a coarse-to-fine cropping approach that iteratively refines target localization through active visual observations.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: GUI grounding maps natural-language instructions to click locations and is essential for reliable GUI agents. The task remains difficult on high-resolution, densely populated interfaces because a vision-language model (VLM) may recognize a requested control without locating it precisely enough for interaction. Most existing methods provide various forms of localization assistance, but still rely on a direct click prediction, allowing visual ambiguity or an inaccurate initial estimate to propagate to the final result. In this paper, we introduce GUI-Lens, a coarse-to-fine grounding framework that allows a general-purpose VLM to determine the target through active visual observations. Specifically, GUI-Lens extracts OCR text and detected UI components from the screenshot and presents their positions as coordinate references. Using the instruction, the current view, and these references, the VLM selects the region and scale of the next view, which is cropped and enlarged to provide finer visual details. This process continues over successively focused views until the target is determined. Proposed crops and clicks are checked against the instruction throughout the process, and the final local position is mapped back to the original screen coordinates. Experiments on five GUI grounding benchmarks and six general-purpose base models show that GUI-Lens consistently improves grounding accuracy, achieving up to 9.3 times the accuracy of direct grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Decompose and Reorganize: Planning with Primitives and Visuomotor Policies Learned from Demonstrations
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yizhou Chen, Hang Xu, Dongjie Yu, Yupu Lu, Tengye Xu
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The DR-LfD framework integrates visuomotor policies into TAMP, enabling efficient skill decomposition and reorganization for dexterous bimanual manipulation with fewer demonstrations.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Successfully automating dexterous, long-horizon bimanual manipulation requires frameworks capable of both high-level reasoning and fine-grained execution. Traditional task and motion planning (TAMP), while excellent at symbolic planning, is often brittle in contact-rich operations. Simultaneously, imitation learning (IL), while effective in manipulation tasks with visual feedback, is limited by its low capability in spatial generalization and multi-stage operation. To reconcile their complementary strengths and limitations, we propose DR-LfD (Decomposed and Reorganized Skills Learned from Demonstrations), a framework that integrates visuomotor policies into a TAMP-gated decision-making system. Based on contact relationships, DR-LfD decomposes human demonstrations into atomic skills, which are reproduced as visuomotor policies or object-centric primitives. The initiation, termination, and constraints of the visuomotor policies are carefully modeled and implemented in a TAMP-compatible form, enabling reorganization of skills learned from different sources. DR-LfD transforms the learning problem from one requiring exponential demonstration data over possible skill sequences to one whose demonstration burden scales with the number of distinct skill types, with limited data for each skill. Real-world and simulation benchmarks demonstrate data-efficient skill composition under unseen setups and physical constraints. On two DexMimicGen tasks, DR-LfD with 100 demonstrations outperforms diffusion-based imitation policies with 1000.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: GPU-accelerated Incremental Euclidean Distance Transform for Online Motion Planning of Mobile Robots
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yizhou Chen, Shupeng Lai, Jinqiang Cui, Biao Wang, Ben M. Chen
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: This paper presents a GPU-accelerated system for incremental Euclidean Distance Transform and Occupancy Grid Maps, enhancing real-time online motion planning for mobile robots.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: In this letter, we present a volumetric mapping system that effectively calculates Occupancy Grid Maps (OGMs) and Euclidean Distance Transforms (EDTs) with parallel computing. Unlike these mappers for high-precision structural reconstruction, our system incrementally constructs global EDT and outputs high-frequency local distance information for online robot motion planning. The proposed system constructs OGM with massive amount of data from multiple types of sensor inputs. Using GPU programming techniques, the system quickly computes EDT in parallel within local volume. The new observation is continuously integrated into the global EDT using the parallel wavefront algorithm while preserving the historical observations. Experiments with datasets have shown that our proposed approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art robot mapping systems and is particularly suitable for mapping unexplored areas. In its actual implementations on aerial and ground vehicles, the proposed system achieves real-time performance with limited onboard computational resources.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Online Learning of Heterogeneous Locomotion Dynamics under Reinforcement Learning Policies for Precise Loco-Manipulation
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Tianlin Zhang, Weipeng Xia, Lingwei Zhang, Yiyang Shao, Zhongyu Li
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper presents an online learning method using a contaminated Gaussian model to improve loco-manipulation accuracy by addressing heterogeneous locomotion dynamics under a fixed policy.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: How to reuse a pretrained locomotion policy for precise loco-manipulation is still an open problem. We propose an online method to learn the closed-loop dynamics under a frozen locomotion policy. The learned model predicts floating-base motion and improves loco-manipulation accuracy. However, unobserved latent conditions of the policy introduce heterogeneous responses, meaning that the same observed state will lead to different motions. Direct learning without accounting for this heterogeneity introduces bias and fluctuations into dynamics estimates, degrading floating-base prediction and end-effector tracking. To address this problem, a contaminated Gaussian model is proposed to approximate the effects of latent conditions. The model uses two Gaussian components to approximate predictable and unpredictable responses under the same observed state. Then, the contaminated Gaussian model is combined with a Gaussian process to construct an online learner using random Fourier features (RFFs). The learner estimates each response's probability of belonging to the predictable component and uses it to weight online updates, capturing predictable responses while reducing bias and fluctuations caused by heterogeneous observations. With consistent and unbiased dynamics estimates, model predictive control (MPC) predicts floating-base motion accurately and enables precise loco-manipulation. A finite-sample error bound is established to ensure uniform convergence in online learning. Simulation and hardware experiments demonstrate consistent end-effector tracking across different manipulator configurations and tasks, with errors of 0.01 m.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Qiushi Sun, Da Yu, Alexander Knop, Amer Sinha, Lingpeng Kong
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: VeriCUA introduces a platform-agnostic framework for verifying computer-using agents through dynamic evidence gathering and assessment, enhancing task completion accuracy across diverse environments.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Building and scaling computer-using agents (CUAs) across desktop, mobile, and web environments requires reliable task-completion verification for data curation, evaluation, and reinforcement learning. Typical automated approaches prompt vision-language models (VLMs) to judge trajectories or generate programs to inspect application state. However, both rely on partial views of complex digital environments. VLM judges are restricted to supplied observations, while generated programs depend on accessible state. These views can omit decisive evidence or leave completion judgments unsupported. Tailoring separate verifiers to different platforms and access settings adds further engineering cost. We present VeriCUA, a platform-agnostic framework for verification through agentic exploration. It treats verification as dynamic evidence gathering and assessment within a shared procedure for online and offline settings across platforms and observation modalities. After inspecting the available context to construct a task rubric, the verifier selects GUI or code checks for unresolved requirements and combines their findings under explicit evidence rules. Experiments show improved agreement with reference labels over the compared baselines across these settings, with the largest offline gains on hard cases and stronger rejection of false completion claims online. Further analyses connect these gains to complementary evidence and test-time exploration.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Joint Latent Reasoning and Observation for Agentic Video Understanding
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Junzhang Liu, Hao Yuan, Yiming Wu, Qi Zhang, Long Chen
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The LARVA framework enhances video understanding by jointly training latent reasoning and visual observations, outperforming traditional methods in multiple benchmarks.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Effective video agents must learn not only how to answer, but also where to look next. Transferring this capability to smaller models is challenging because each observation serves two purposes: supporting an answer and guiding the search for further evidence. Textual descriptions may capture what is currently visible while omitting cues needed for subsequent acquisition. We introduce Latent Agentic Reasoning for Video Analysis (LARVA), a framework that distills multi-round video agents through jointly learned latent reasoning and visual observations. Rather than communicating through captions, an observer passes compact continuous representations to a reasoner that selects the next acquisition action or produces the final answer. Crucially, action and answer supervision propagate through this interface, training the observer to communicate information useful for downstream decisions. Observation reconstruction and reasoning-distribution alignment provide auxiliary supervision from textual teacher trajectories. Across five video-understanding benchmarks, LARVA achieves strong performance with 4B and 7B backbones. On VideoHolmes, Video-MME, and LVBench, the 7B model outperforms a textual CoT student trained on the same teacher trajectories by 5.1, 2.5, and 3.7 percentage points, respectively. These results highlight the value of jointly learning how agents represent evidence and act on it when distilling video-understanding capabilities.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: From Events to Enhancement: A Survey on Event-Based Imaging Technologies
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yunfan Lu, Xiaogang Xu, Pengteng Li, Yusheng Wang, Yi Cui
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: This survey reviews event-based imaging technologies, detailing sensor characteristics, enhancement tasks, advanced applications, and ongoing challenges in the field.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Event cameras offering high dynamic range and low latency have emerged as disruptive technologies in imaging. Despite growing research on leveraging these benefits for different imaging tasks, a comprehensive study of recently advances and challenges are still lacking. This limits the broader understanding of how to utilize events in universal imaging applications. In this survey, we first introduce a physical model and the characteristics of different event sensors as the foundation. Following this, we highlight the advancement and interaction of image/video enhancement tasks with events. Additionally, we explore advanced tasks, which capture richer light information with events, \eg~light field estimation, multi-view generation, and photometric. Finally, we discuss new challenges and open questions offering a perspective for this rapidly evolving field. More continuously updated resources are at this link: https://github.com/yunfanLu/Awesome-Event-Imaging

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Where to Learn and How Far to Roll Out: Efficient Adaptive Training for GUI Agents
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yuxiang Chai, Quyu Kong, Panrong Tong, Steven Hoi, Yue Wang
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper presents a two-stage adaptive training framework for GUI agents that enhances efficiency by optimizing learning locations and rollout lengths, reducing interactions by 56-61%.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Trajectory-level GRPO is a common approach for training multi-step GUI agents, but repeatedly rolling out complete trajectories from the task root can be inefficient: task-level rewards provide coarse supervision over which intermediate decisions require improvement, while already-mastered prefixes are repeatedly re-executed before reaching difficult states. We introduce a two-stage adaptive training framework that jointly addresses where to learn and how far to roll out. We first construct reusable intermediate checkpoints from successful expert trajectories and select informative pivots using action disagreement, which measures uncertainty directly from sampled GUI actions. Stage I performs one-step RL at these pivots to improve uncertain local decisions. Stage II then progressively expands policy responsibility through adaptive Local, Suffix, and Root training according to task progress. Recoverable checkpoints enable repeated training from intermediate states without replaying the preceding trajectory. Across MobileGym and CUA-Gym-Hub, our method reduces environment interaction by 56-61% relative to Vanilla GRPO while improving task performance, demonstrating that jointly allocating training across states and rollout ranges can substantially improve GUI-agent RL efficiency.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: CuBot-STT: Simultaneously Transport and Tighten for Lattice-type Modular Reconfiguration Robot
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Chongxi Meng, Da Zhao, Yanmin Zhou, Runjie Shen, Zhipeng Wang
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: CuBot-STT is a modular reconfiguration robot that simultaneously transports and locks modules, enhancing efficiency and structural integrity while optimizing planning through advanced learning techniques.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Lattice-type modular reconfigurable robots rearrange standardized modules across tasks. Dedicated transport robots reduce module weight and cost by eliminating module level reconfiguration actuators. But existing systems use low capacity connections or internal fastening robots that occupy space for functional components. This paper presents CuBot-STT, which integrates module transport, interface locking, and release in one external robot. Cubic modules provide structural support and $24\,\mathrm{V}$ power distribution. On each face, a gear transmission converts one external input into motion of four helical locking points, preserving internal space. The robot uses alternating foot support, a gripper for module handling, and a tightening head for interface actuation. The controller coordinates two-foot support and module locking through continuous constraint transfers. The planner decomposes relocation costs into an analytical lower bound and a residual learned through expert-guided, goal conditioned Q-learning. Contact face $A^*$ search expands relocation sequences into robot primitives satisfying connectivity, asymmetric manipulation, and foot stance constraints. Experiments demonstrate normal and tangential interface capacities of $300\,\mathrm{N}$ and $490\,\mathrm{N}$, electrical continuity across six modules, and autonomous reconfiguration of an 11-module lattice. Planning benchmarks show superior search efficiency over analytical guidance and bidirectional heuristic search, with generalization beyond training lattice sizes without fine-tuning.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: YOLOF-MLD: A Multi-Level Distillation Framework for Efficient Object Detection
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Xiaolong Wu, Liming Zheng, Zitong Liu, Yue Zheng
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: YOLOF-MLD introduces a multi-level distillation framework that enhances object detection efficiency on edge devices, achieving significant parameter reduction and competitive accuracy.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Efficient object detection on resource-constrained edge devices is essential for safety-critical applications such as fire-smoke monitoring. However, current lightweight frameworks, such as YOLO26, still rely on the parameter-dense multi-branch Feature Pyramid Network (FPN), preventing full exploitation of their lightweight advantage. Replacing FPN with YOLOF's single-input-single-output (SiSo) neck is a promising solution but causes substantial accuracy loss. To alleviate this, we propose YOLOF-MLD, a CPU-efficient multi-level distillation (MLD) framework that combines a YOLO26n backbone, a SiSo neck, and MLD. It aligns features at the backbone via sliced-semantics matching, neck with receptive-field matching, and response levels. On D-Fire and Annotated Fire-Smoke (AFS) datasets, YOLOF-MLD reduces the parameter count of YOLO26n by 35.7\% and achieves a 62.3\% speedup on Raspberry Pi 5, attaining 71.6% and 59.9% mAP@50, respectively, compared with 75.5% and 60.0% for YOLO26n. These results demonstrate a competitive accuracy--latency trade-off for edge deployment. Our code is available at https://github.com/XiaolongWU111/YOLOF---MLD/blob/main/README.md.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: TaskFrame: Connecting Task-Level Planning with Frame-Level Control for Game Agents
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Guangzhi Wang, Junfu Pu, Yiran Wang, Xingyilang Yin, Honghao Chen
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: TaskFrame integrates task-level planning and frame-level control in game agents, enhancing performance in dynamic environments through a hierarchical planner-controller framework.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Building general game agents requires both high-level task reasoning and low-latency action control in rapidly changing visual environments. These capabilities favor models with substantially different computational profiles, making them difficult to realize within a single model. In this work, we present TaskFrame, a hierarchical planner-controller framework that connects task-level planning with frame-level keyboard-and-mouse control. A vision-language task planner decomposes a high-level goal into an ordered sequence of atomic instructions and is optimized through supervised learning and dependency-aware GRPO. The hidden states of special goal tokens that terminate each atomic instruction provide continuous goal embeddings that are cached and reused across control steps. A causal Transformer controller combines the embedding of the active goal with recent observations to predict discrete keyboard and mouse-button actions and continuous camera motion at every game step. We train the system in three stages: planner training, controller pretraining, and joint alignment. Experiments in Minecraft show that TaskFrame is competitive with general-purpose vision-language models on instruction decomposition, and that in closed-loop evaluation the agent achieves a higher combat success rate than the evaluated baselines.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Baiqiao Yin, Zhongang Cai, Ruisi Wang, Qiwei Liang, Lei Yang
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: This study evaluates visual foundation models' spatial representations, revealing varied capabilities in object persistence, predictive updates, and actionability under dynamic viewing conditions.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: An observer sees only part of the surrounding world, yet must keep track of what lies beyond the current view. Spatial perception therefore involves more than recognizing individual images: it calls for a persistent spatial state that is updated under self-motion and used to guide action. Do visual foundation models provide representations that support such a state? We study this question through four levels of spatial capability---spatial structure, object persistence, predictive spatial update, and actionability---using frozen-feature probes on ten representations under streaming egocentric observations of static indoor environments. The resulting capability profiles vary across tasks, network layers, and prefix lengths: strong readout of the visible scene does not ensure accurate object persistence or future-feature retrieval. Matched controls separate readout accuracy from reliance on visual history and motion. Native future prediction retains recoverable spatial structure, but a spatial reader trained on real features does not transfer to predicted features unchanged. Finally, goal-dependent candidate selection does not establish reliable continuous action utility: predicted actions respond to goal changes, yet supplying the correct goal does not reliably improve progress. Across the four levels, object persistence and actionability build on camera-pose readout, whereas feature prediction builds on visible-scene readout. Together, these findings motivate evaluating spatial representations not only by what can be decoded from them, but by whether that information is maintained beyond observation, updated predictively, and used for goal-directed action.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Test-time Correction: An Online 3D Detection System via Visual Prompting
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Hanxue Zhang, Zetong Yang, Yanan Sun, Li Chen, Fatma Güney
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper presents Test-time Correction (TTC), an online 3D detection system that uses visual prompting for real-time error correction in autonomous driving, enhancing safety and adaptability.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: This paper introduces Test-time Correction (TTC), an online 3D detection system designed to rectify test-time errors using various auxiliary feedback, aiming to enhance the safety of deployed autonomous driving systems. Unlike conventional offline 3D detectors that remain fixed during inference, TTC enables immediate online error correction without retraining, allowing autonomous vehicles to adapt to new scenarios and reduce deployment risks. To achieve this, we equip existing 3D detectors with an Online Adapter (OA) module -- a prompt-driven query generator for real-time correction. At the core of OA module are visual prompts: image-based descriptions of objects of interest derived from auxiliary feedback such as mismatches with 2D detections, road descriptions, or user clicks. These visual prompts, collected from risky objects during inference, are maintained in a visual prompt buffer to enable continuous correction in future frames. By leveraging this mechanism, TTC consistently detects risky objects, achieving reliable, adaptive, and versatile driving autonomy. Extensive experiments show that TTC significantly improves instant error rectification over frozen 3D detectors, even under limited labels, zero-shot settings, and adverse conditions. We hope this work inspires future research on post-deployment online rectification systems for autonomous driving.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Safe Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning: Zero Constraint Violation and Primal-Averaging Convergence
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Chenxi Li, Yao Shu, Siyang Gao, Shuang Qiu, Guangxin Jiang
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: This paper presents safe multi-objective reinforcement learning algorithms ensuring zero constraint violation while achieving efficient exploration and suboptimality guarantees under unknown dynamics.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Many applications of multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) require policies that balance conflicting objectives while satisfying safety constraints. We study safe MORL with zero constraint violation throughout learning, covering both cumulative and stepwise constraints. A key challenge is to explore sufficiently under unknown dynamics and constraint costs without violating the constraints. For a given preference over objectives, we develop an algorithm to learn a safe Pareto optimal policy by combining optimistic reward estimates with pessimistic cost bounds. With high probability, every policy executed over $T$ episodes incurs zero constraint violation. The algorithm returns a safe Markov policy induced by the averaged occupancy measure and achieves an $\widetilde{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ suboptimality gap under smooth Tchebycheff scalarization. We further develop a preference-free algorithm that first explores safely without a prespecified preference and then computes a safe policy for any given preference without further interaction. Over $T$ exploration episodes and $K$ planning iterations, it retains the same safety guarantee and achieves an $\widetilde{O}(1/\sqrt{T}+1/\sqrt{K})$ suboptimality gap. Both algorithms require knowledge of a policy that strictly satisfies the constraints and its costs. We then relax these requirements, incurring at most constant cumulative violation. To our knowledge, we provide the first sample-efficient MORL algorithms that guarantee safety for every executed policy.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Kinematic-Tactile Aligned Dexterous Retargeting with Contact Wrench Space Alignment
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Xinyuan He, Ziheng Xu, Yueyuan Chen, Yufan Ye, Yuanshuo Tan
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical framework for aligning kinematics and tactile information in dexterous manipulation, achieving high replay success and fidelity in robot hand trajectories.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Human demonstrations provide a natural and scalable source of data for learning dexterous manipulation policies. However, existing retargeting methods primarily transfer human kinematics, while the tactile information underlying physical interaction is rarely preserved across embodiments. To address this limitation, we present a hierarchical three-stage framework for kinematic-tactile aligned dexterous retargeting. We use object-centric contact wrench space as a physical representation for tactile alignment between human and robot hands. The framework first aligns hand kinematics and contact geometry, and then constructs a human wrench support profile from tactile forces and contact geometry. Robot fingertip force targets are subsequently optimized to cover the human wrench support and converted into joint position corrections, yielding directly replayable robot hand trajectories. We evaluate the framework in simulation and real robot experiments across three pouring conditions. In the real robot experiments, our method achieves a 96.7\% replay success rate and higher wrench transfer fidelity than representative retargeting baselines. The framework enables physically grounded transfer of kinematic and tactile information from human demonstrations to robot hands, providing a path toward scalable learning of contact-rich dexterous manipulation.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: WorldProbe: When Video World Models Fall Apart under Long-Horizon Spatial Exploration
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Minqi Wang, Jie Peng, Hejun Dong, Ruchang Yao, Puyi Wang
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: WorldProbe introduces a benchmark revealing that video world models struggle with long-horizon exploration, highlighting inconsistencies in long-range memory despite improved local generation quality.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Video world models generate future visual observations from camera or action inputs, with the goal of synthesizing persistent 3D worlds that can be explored across time and space. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate short interactions or rely on camera trajectories fixed before generation. The performance of video world models under long-horizon exploration with extensive camera motion remains under-explored. We introduce WorldProbe, a diagnostic benchmark that uses a goal-conditioned multimodal agent to adapt camera actions online during generation. WorldProbe comprises 164 test cases across four probing families. Across 10 state-of-the-art models, we generate more than 1,600 rollouts totaling approximately 800 minutes, with horizons up to 180 seconds. Our evaluation across four dimensions reveals both the degradation of local measures and the emergence of long-range inconsistencies. We find that recent models sustain visual and content quality for longer, while long-range memory and evolution remain weak. These results expose a gap between locally stable generation and persistent world consistency that is largely missed by existing benchmarks. Code and benchmark resources are available at https://github.com/Untitled-W/WorldProbe.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: GROME: GROunding Factorized MEmory into Video World Models
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Fang Yu, Xiaoxue Wu, Haiyu Zhang, Yangfu Li, Botong Zhao
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: GROME is a novel memory framework that enhances video world models by decoupling static and dynamic information for improved long-horizon consistency and scene fidelity.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Long-horizon consistency is essential for video world models, yet it becomes difficult to maintain once observed content falls outside the context window. Existing memory mechanisms either retrieve history as implicit context, which remains constrained by context capacity and entangles static and dynamic information or consolidate history into explicit global representations, which struggle to model evolving dynamics and accumulate geometric errors. To overcome these limitations, we introduce \textbf{GROME}, a novel factorized memory framework that augments video world models for long-horizon coherence across both static scenes and dynamic entities. GROME operates via three synergistic components: 1)~\emph{Static-Dynamic Factorization} decouples historical evidence into static and dynamic components, preserving static scene geometry and dynamic entity states separately; 2)~\emph{Local Memory Retrieval} selects spatially aligned static history to eliminate geometric drift alongside the latest dynamic entity states to ensure temporal continuity; 3)~\emph{Training-Free Memory Injection} seamlessly grounds the factorized memory into video world models via their native conditioning pathways. Experiments on long-horizon revisit scenarios demonstrate that GROME substantially enhances scene persistence and dynamic entity fidelity over existing methods, all while preserving the visual quality and controllability of the frozen backbone without additional training. Beyond self-rollouts, GROME readily accommodates external observations as plug-and-play memory, unlocking flexible and controllable video continuation and scene exploration.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: RoboSeed: Multidimensional Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action and World-Action Models: Capability, Resource Affordability, and Research Evidence
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Xin Ma, Furong Chen, Xinlong Man, Bo Zhang, Yalong Guo
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: RoboSeed introduces a multidimensional evaluation framework for comparing vision-language-action and world-action models based on capability, affordability, and research reliability, aiding informed robot action model selection.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Choosing a robot action model requires evidence about task capability, adaptation cost, deployment requirements, and the reliability of reported conclusions. Success rates alone offer limited guidance to researchers with different computing budgets and goals. We propose RoboSeed, a multidimensional evaluation framework for vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAM), within a continuing program to train, evaluate, and openly release robot models with verifiable evidence for model selection. The framework defines five dimensions: capability, downstream training affordability, deployment affordability, locally verified research value, and reproduction evidence. It maps empirical measurements and audit criteria to 0-100 profiles using fixed normalization anchors, with balanced, training-constrained, and deployment-constrained preference settings. Interface and protocol checks establish when comparisons are appropriate. Missing measurements remain explicit, incomplete aggregate scores are withheld, and weighted input coverage identifies evidence gaps. We apply the framework to representative VLA and WAM models, drawing on local training, released-weight evaluation, task-level audits, and an evaluation-system study. The results reveal budget-dependent backbone choices, sensitivity to adaptation recipes, and differences between language and visual task interfaces. Reproducible scoring code and machine-readable evidence support extension to additional models. The study provides dimension-level assessments and priorities for further measurement, while incomplete serving traces and heterogeneous protocols preclude overall numerical rankings.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Rongxing Ding, Hongyu Qu, Kehong Wu, Xudong Wang, Fan Zhang
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: HiFOR introduces a hierarchical foresight framework that integrates short-term and long-term predictions with action-guided retrieval to enhance robotic manipulation in Vision-Language-Action models.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capabilities in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Recent advances have further incorporated future prediction to enhance the understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression. However, existing methods often model short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives separately, while directly incorporating predicted futures into action policies without sufficiently considering their relevance to current action requirements. To address these limitations, we propose HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework with action-guided world retrieval. Specifically, Hierarchical Foresight Prediction jointly predicts short-term state evolution, semantic milestones, and final goal states through a Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM), establishing dependencies across temporal horizons. Building upon these predictions, Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling organizes future latent representations along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions to facilitate fine-grained retrieval. Furthermore, Action-Guided Factorized World Retrieval adaptively retrieves relevant future information from the structured latent world based on evolving action representations during denoising, providing targeted guidance for action generation. Extensive experiments on two simulation benchmarks and six real-world robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: RESPLE2: Inertial-Informed Recursive Non-Uniform Spline Estimation for Multi-Sensor Odometry with Global Refinement
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Ziyu Cao, William Talbot, Song Li, Pakpong Chirarattananon, Fredrik Gustafsson
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: RESPLE2 is a recursive multi-sensor odometry framework utilizing non-uniform B-splines and inertial data for accurate, real-time 6-DoF motion estimation across various platforms.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: We present RESPLE2, a recursive multi-sensor state estimation framework using non-uniform B-splines for 6-DoF motion representation. By exploiting the knot-clamping boundary property, we propose a theoretically grounded mechanism for exact control-point prediction directly informed by inertial kinematics along the trajectory, with knot placement adapted to motion and measurement availability. Within an iterated extended Kalman filter, we perform this prediction using a subset of inertial measurements. A subsequent reset step preserves trajectory consistency as the knots extend. The update step further incorporates heterogeneous sensor measurements at their native timestamps through continuous-time observation models, supporting flexible combinations of LiDARs, cameras, inertial measurement units, and leg kinematics. We further develop a lightweight global optimization module that directly refines non-uniform B-spline control points by incorporating loop-closure constraints derived from LiDAR-visual cues. We conduct extensive evaluations on public and experimental datasets across handheld, tracked, legged, and hybrid aerial-legged platforms, covering highly dynamic maneuvers with extreme accelerations. Compared with state-of-the-art multi-sensor odometry systems, RESPLE2 achieves competitive or superior estimation accuracy and robustness in the corresponding sensor configurations, particularly under aggressive motion, while maintaining real-time operation. We publicly release our code and experimental datasets at https://github.com/ASIG-X/RESPLE2.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: SELF: A Robust Singular Value and Eigenvalue Approach for LLM Fingerprinting
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Hanxiu Zhang, Qiang Xu, Yue Zheng
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: SELF is a robust fingerprinting method for LLMs that enhances IP protection by using singular and eigenvalue decomposition to resist false claims and modifications.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Safeguarding the Intellectual Property (IP) of Large Language Models (LLMs) against model theft represents a critical challenge in contemporary AI research. Although fingerprinting is essential for establishing forensic evidence for model derivation, existing methods are susceptible to false claim attacks, weight manipulations, or high false positive rates, undermining their utility.
