However, existing tactile manipulation studies are often developed and evaluated within specific task settings, making it difficult to systematically compare how tactile information contributes under different interaction conditions. In this work, we develop a benchmark in simulation comprising 128 tasks organized around three complementary evaluation regimes: Precise, Recognition, and Dynamic. The benchmark further includes controlled static and dynamic task variants and 12 perturbation settings for evaluating robustness under changes in visual and physical conditions. These settings motivate studying tactile information as a temporally evolving interaction representation rather than only as an instantaneous observation. We therefore propose an action-conditioned latent predictive world model that integrates tactile history and learns a tactile state through prediction of future tactile latents. Building on this representation, we design a model that conditions action generation on the learned tactile state and uses predicted future tactile information to refine candidate actions through predictive tactile reflection. Experiments on the proposed benchmark show consistent gains from incorporating tactile information across the evaluated regimes. Project Page: https://tacmind-bench.github.io/

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: W2A: Distilling World Priors into Action Models for Real-Time Robotic Control
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Xiaopeng Zhang, Yongjin Mu, Yueyang Weng, Chengzhi Zhao, Yanjie Li
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: W2A introduces a two-stage distillation framework that enhances real-time robotic control by efficiently transferring video model representations into action models, achieving 21x faster inference.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have recently shown great promise in robotic control, benefiting from the future imagination capability of large-scale pretrained video models. However, most existing WAMs require explicitly imagining future states at test time, incurring substantial computational overhead and latency that make them unsuitable for real-time robotic control. In this paper, we propose W2A, a two-stage distillation framework for real-time robotic manipulation that distills intermediate denoising representations from a video diffusion model into an action model during training, while entirely discarding the video model at test time. We hypothesize that although video latent representations are high-dimensional, a compressed low-dimensional subspace is sufficient to provide effective supervision for action generation. This makes it possible to transfer such information effectively into an action model. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world settings demonstrate competitive success rates while significantly improving inference efficiency. On LIBERO, W2A achieves a 95.9% average success rate. More importantly, W2A achieves about 21x faster inference than the representative WAM baseline.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Predictive Safety Guardrails Do Not Always Make LLM Agents Safer
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Weixiang Zhao, Zhihao Liu, Guancheng Li, Yanyan Zhao, Bing Qin
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The study reveals that predictive safety guardrails in LLM agents do not guarantee improved safety, highlighting issues in prediction reliability and decision integration.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Large language model agents increasingly take consequential actions in digital and physical environments, where safety risks may emerge only after multiple interaction steps. This has motivated world-model-driven predictive safety guardrails, which anticipate future consequences before execution. However, existing evaluations largely focus on end-to-end safety outcomes, leaving unclear whether safety gains arise from reliable prediction and faithful use of predicted risks. In this work, we systematically diagnose the prediction-to-action pipeline along three dimensions: how world-model predictions are integrated into decision making, whether the predictions themselves are reliable, and whether their content is faithfully used. Across seven policy models and two safety environments, we find that stronger prediction involvement does not yield monotonic safety gains and can reduce task completion while substantially increasing inference cost. We further find that world-model predictions remain insufficiently reliable, especially over longer horizons, where safety prediction degrades substantially relative to near-term forecasting. Finally, we find that safety gains can persist even under corrupted predictions, while locally verified predictions still leave subsequent safety violations, showing that predictive content is not faithfully incorporated into the decision process. Together, these findings expose a fundamental prediction-to-action gap in current predictive guardrails: producing more or seemingly accurate foresight is insufficient unless that foresight is both reliable and faithfully translated into safer decisions.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Scaling Action-Free Video Latent Prediction for Transferable Representations in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Xingtai Gui, Xubin Zhou, Yucheng Zhou, Dongqian Guo, Jiahao Gong
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The paper introduces ScaleDrive, a framework that enhances end-to-end autonomous driving by using action-free video latent prediction for scalable, transferable visual representations.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving policies require effective visual representations that capture both spatial scene structure and temporal dynamics. Video latent prediction has emerged as an effective paradigm for learning spatiotemporal visual representations, yet it remains unclear whether scaling this objective with action-free driving videos can yield representations that benefit end-to-end planning. We study action-free video latent prediction as a scalable pretraining objective and introduce ScaleDrive, a driving-oriented framework pretrained exclusively on large-scale internet open-world driving videos, without action annotations or benchmark-specific data. We keep the pretrained video encoder frozen during downstream end-to-end planning training to isolate the transferability of representations learned from internet driving videos. Ego-motion and depth probes show that scaling action-free video pretraining progressively strengthens the temporal and geometric information encoded in the frozen representation. We systematically study the visual representation transfer across different end-to-end driving policies and closed-loop benchmarks, where ScaleDrive consistently improves downstream performance and demonstrates that scaling action-free video latent prediction yields representations that generalize across both planning policy architectures and evaluation scenarios and protocols.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: FineCraft: Enhancing VLA Models for Fine-Grained Manipulation
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Shuaike Zhang, Ziheng Quan, Junhao Ran, Muhe Ding, Shaokun Wang
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: FineCraft is a framework that enhances VLA models for fine-grained manipulation, achieving fourth place in the MetaFine Challenge through task-specific policy adaptations and local visual feature integration.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Fine-grained manipulation couples instruction grounding, local visual precision, and sustained execution. We present FineCraft, a framework that adapts pretrained models for fine-grained manipulation in the MetaFine Challenge. A task-routed mixture of policies selects independently adapted DINOv2-DiT or pretrained $π_{0.5}$ policies through a common observation-action interface. Local visual features help identify the instructed object parts, demonstrations and expert continuations teach the required actions, and new observations guide replanning during execution. FineCraft ranks fourth with an overall score of $0.878$, exceeding the published reference on all five tasks. Official results and local diagnostics characterize performance across visual perturbations, instruction changes, and multi-stage manipulation. Code is available at https://github.com/eqcy/FineCraft

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: CoEnv: Code-Driven Exploration in Real-to-Sim Digital Twins for Multi-Arm Manipulation
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Li Kang, Yutao Fan, Rui Li, Heng Zhou, Yiran Qin
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: CoEnv enables a coding agent to efficiently explore and refine multi-arm manipulation programs in a realistic digital twin, achieving higher success rates than previous methods.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: General-purpose coding agents can now write, debug, and refine entire robot programs, but only if they have somewhere to practice. Physical hardware is a poor practice ground: exploratory rollouts are slow to reset and, when several arms share a workspace, unsafe. Generic simulation benchmarks are safe but do not match the geometry, assets, or viewpoints of the workspace where the robot must actually work. We present CoEx (Code-driven Exploration), which lets the agent practice in an executable digital twin of its own deployment workspace. The twin is built by CoEnv, our real-to-sim framework, which reconstructs the physical scene from multi-view RGBD into a physics simulation. Inside it, a centralized code agent explores at the program level, writing a complete multi-arm program, running it in the twin, and refining it against grounded verification (privileged state checks, checkpoint predicates on risky steps, and adaptive viewpoints against inter-arm occlusion). Verified programs transfer to hardware through collision-checked deployment. On five real-world multi-arm tasks with up to three heterogeneous robots, CoEx reaches 70% average success, against 50% for the same system without the code agent (where a VLM must choose every primitive step by step), outperforms two prior VLM-planning frameworks, and produces verified episodes at 3.8-11.7x the ablated rate. Because every verified rollout is also a demonstration, exploration leaves reusable experience behind: a $π_{0.5}$ policy fine-tuned purely on 200 agent-generated rollouts reaches 100% and 70% real-robot success on two tasks, with no human demonstrations.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: DRT: Dense Reasoning Trace for Efficient and Grounded Multimodal Reasoning
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Wan Xu, Yuanfan Guo, Kevin Han, LaLa Chen, Wangmeng Zuo
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The Dense Reasoning Trace (DRT) improves multimodal reasoning efficiency by using structured traces instead of verbose natural language, enhancing token efficiency and logical grounding.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Despite the remarkable progress in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), prevailing Chain-of-Thought (CoT) paradigms remain confined to the natural-language expression space. Consequently, they inherently incur excessive linguistic overhead, leading to information dilution and weak visual grounding. To address this challenge, we propose Dense Reasoning Trace (DRT), a paradigm that departs from natural-language-centered CoT by expressing reasoning as compact structured traces, which include concise intermediate states with symbolic connectors and disentangle visual observations from logical deductions. First, we introduce the Dense Trace Initialization to internalize the DRT reasoning mode into the model, substantially improving token efficiency while preserving visual evidence. To further enable the model to faithfully capture the logical relations within traces, we propose the Trace-Grounded Reinforcement Learning framework, which builds reference traces through a tri-perspective verification pipeline and employs Trace-Grounded GRPO with structured rewards, encouraging the model to generate concise DRT-style traces with reduced hallucination and stronger logical grounding. Extensive experiments on challenging reasoning benchmarks show that DRT achieves 5.5$\times$ token efficiency improvement while improving 1.3 accuracy points over the Qwen3-VL baseline. These findings suggest that complex multimodal reasoning may not require verbose natural-language traces, opening a more efficient path for next-generation MLLMs. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/HIT-leaderone/DRT

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Feng Chen, Jianguo Huang, Yushan Xiao, Yue Li, Bijun Tang
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: FrontierMat introduces a benchmark of 330 validated research problems to evaluate language models' effectiveness in advanced materials discovery, highlighting significant performance gaps and improvement strategies.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. The strongest general-purpose model scores only 53.7%, and on matched problems, cross-scale problems score 8.7 points below single-scale ones. Half of the problems are solved by at most one model, and models fail chiefly by endorsing what is plausible rather than what was observed. A domain-adaptation study with meta-weighted continued pretraining and scale-modular self-distillation raises an open-weight model from 36.7% to 55.4%, matching the strongest proprietary model, with improvements on public materials benchmarks and no decline in aggregate performance on general benchmarks. FrontierMat provides a testbed for measuring progress toward language models that support frontier materials R&D.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: CSO: Refining Robotic Policies via Skill Distribution Alignment and Skill-Grained Optimization
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Zhiyuan Xiang, Xiang Deng, Wanjie Tao, Xu Chen, Zhao Jielun
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The CSO framework enhances robotic manipulation performance by refining skill distributions through a two-stage optimization process, significantly increasing task success rates.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Discretizing continuous actions into discrete skills using methods like VQ-VAE has emerged as a powerful paradigm for robotic manipulation. However, quantization errors yield a suboptimal distribution for the skill prior, degrading its performance. While reinforcement learning offers a path for refinement, its direct application faces unstable encoder updates and a granularity dilemma in importance sampling. To address these challenges, we introduce Cascaded Skills Optimization (CSO), a two-stage post-training framework. First, Rejection-Sampling Supervised Fine-tuning aligns the model's observation-to-skill mapping with the distribution of successful online trajectories via supervised fine-tuning. Second, with the observation encoder frozen, Skills Policy Optimization computes an independent, clipped importance ratio for each complete skill, enabling stable and efficient updates. With a lightweight QueST-style policy, CSO raises overall LIBERO success from 80.1% to 97.5%, improves performance on RoboTwin2.0, and achieves 61.0% success across five physical single-arm tasks. Additional comparisons with FAST, discrete BEAST, and fixed-buffer IQL further validate the effectiveness of our two-stage post-training strategy.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Cheap Retrieval and Observation Credit Assignment from One Quantity: The Value of Information
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Daniel Strauss, Nikolaos Sotirakis, Zhenshan Bing, Alois Knoll
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The paper proposes a method for efficient memory retrieval in reinforcement learning by using the value of information to optimize credit assignment and decision-making.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Memory in reinforcement learning raises two problems. Attention finds the relevant item by scoring the whole store, which is costly for robots under latency and energy limits. When a retrieved memory pays off, credit for acquiring it must cross the whole sequence. We argue that both are governed by one quantity, the value of information, and propose to estimate it from archived rollouts with a learned world model. We obtain that, when read at the observation, it yields a provable lower bound on the optimal value of the acquiring action, which floors its TD target and attributes this floor to the observation that earned it. Read at the decision, it defines the optimal retrieval set. A pilot retrieval system, to be trained and improved with this signal, solves a memory task with reduced context.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Aligned Delta-Triplane Transformers as Occupancy World Models
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Haoran Xu, Peixi Peng, Shijun Guo, Guang Tan, Yiqian Chang
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The Aligned Delta-Triplane Transformer (ADTT) efficiently predicts future 3D occupancy changes in autonomous driving by aligning historical data and compensating for ego motion.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Occupancy World Models (OWMs) aim to predict future 3D occupancy scenes from historical observations and future ego motions, providing a useful world simulation tool for autonomous driving. Existing methods usually rely on large networks to implicitly align multi-frame historical states and predict future occupancy in a full-state manner, which is costly and redundant because most scene regions remain unchanged over short time intervals. In this paper, we propose Aligned Delta-Triplane Transformer (ADTT), a compact 4D OWM that explicitly aligns historical triplanes with ego-motion compensation and predicts only future scene changes. Based on the aligned triplane prior, a query-conditioned Transformer predicts residual changes, where ego-motion queries guide controllable future motion and learnable external queries capture scene changes beyond ego motion. The predicted changes are added to the aligned prior and decoded into future occupancy scenes. Experiments on Occ3D-nus show that ADTT achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance with fewer parameters and higher FPS. Our code is publicly available online: https://github.com/kyoran/ADTT.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Train the Agent, Not the Expert: Learning to Harness Heterogeneous Experts for Multi-Turn Visual Reasoning
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Yaowu Fan, Tao Han, Dazhao Du, Andy J. Ma, Jia Wan
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: VisHarness is a trainable visual agent that effectively utilizes heterogeneous experts for multi-turn visual reasoning, outperforming existing models in complex scenarios.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Recent advances in computer vision have produced powerful specialized models for detection, segmentation, counting, and other visual tasks. However, these models are typically optimized for isolated tasks, limiting their ability to support general-purpose visual intelligence, particularly when complex language understanding and dense small-object perception are required. We propose VisHarness, a trainable visual agent that decouples high-level perception, reasoning, and decision-making from low-level task execution. Rather than training a task-specific model, we train VisHarness to harness a set of carefully designed heterogeneous visual experts. This paradigm preserves the agent's general intelligence while leveraging the precision of specialized visual experts for specific tasks. With only lightweight training, VisHarness learns a generalizable policy for harnessing visual experts, enabling it to solve fundamental vision tasks in diverse complex scenarios through multi-turn interactions with these experts. To enable efficient on-policy reinforcement learning in a live environment, we introduce dynamic visual memory archiving to reduce the visual-token overhead that rapidly accumulates during multi-turn interactions with visual experts. Experiments on four representative benchmarks spanning reasoning segmentation, generalized referring expression segmentation, dense small-object detection, and referring expression counting show that VisHarness substantially outperforms existing general-purpose models and is competitive with or superior to task-specific models. Our code, model weights, and training data are publicly available at https://github.com/fyw1999/VisHarness.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: LaWAM: Latent World Action Models for Efficient Dynamics-Aware Robot Policies
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Jialei Chen, Kai Wang, Kang Chen, Shuaihang Chen, Feng Gao
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: LaWAM introduces a Latent World Action Model that enhances robot control by predicting future dynamics through compact latent visual subgoals, achieving state-of-the-art performance with low latency.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) leverage large-scale vision-language pretraining for semantic robot control, but often lack explicit foresight into how robot actions change the scene. World-Action Models (WAMs) address this limitation by conditioning policies on predicted futures, yet existing approaches typically rely on computationally expensive video generation with substantial pixel-level redundancy. We present LaWAM, a Latent World Action Model that exposes predictive dynamics to robot policies through compact latent visual subgoals instead of reconstructed future video. At the core of LaWAM is a latent-action-conditioned Latent World Model (LaWM). We obtain LaWM by training a latent action model in the latent space of a pretrained vision foundation model and repurposing its forward decoder to predict future observation features for scene evolution. LaWAM then conditions action generation on these predicted latent visual subgoals to enable dynamics-aware robot control. LaWAM achieves state-of-the-art or competitive success rates (SRs) across LIBERO (98.6% SR), RoboTwin (91.22% SR), and real-world manipulation tasks while retaining low-latency inference. LaWAM runs in 187 ms per action-chunk prediction and achieves up to 24x lower wall-clock latency than pixel-space WAMs.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Safe Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning: Zero Constraint Violation and Primal-Averaging Convergence
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Chenxi Li, Yao Shu, Siyang Gao, Shuang Qiu, Guangxin Jiang
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: This paper presents safe multi-objective reinforcement learning algorithms ensuring zero constraint violation while achieving efficient exploration and suboptimality guarantees under unknown dynamics.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Many applications of multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) require policies that balance conflicting objectives while satisfying safety constraints. We study safe MORL with zero constraint violation throughout learning, covering both cumulative and stepwise constraints. A key challenge is to explore sufficiently under unknown dynamics and constraint costs without violating the constraints. For a given preference over objectives, we develop an algorithm to learn a safe Pareto optimal policy by combining optimistic reward estimates with pessimistic cost bounds. With high probability, every policy executed over $T$ episodes incurs zero constraint violation. The algorithm returns a safe Markov policy induced by the averaged occupancy measure and achieves an $\widetilde{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ suboptimality gap under smooth Tchebycheff scalarization. We further develop a preference-free algorithm that first explores safely without a prespecified preference and then computes a safe policy for any given preference without further interaction. Over $T$ exploration episodes and $K$ planning iterations, it retains the same safety guarantee and achieves an $\widetilde{O}(1/\sqrt{T}+1/\sqrt{K})$ suboptimality gap. Both algorithms require knowledge of a policy that strictly satisfies the constraints and its costs. We then relax these requirements, incurring at most constant cumulative violation. To our knowledge, we provide the first sample-efficient MORL algorithms that guarantee safety for every executed policy.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: AI for Science in Space: Orbital Laboratories, Planetary Fieldwork, and Embodied Autonomy
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Zizhe Wang, Jia Deng, Xin Lu, Zehao Jia, Yi Huang
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The paper reviews the role of AI in enhancing scientific experimentation in space through autonomous robotics, addressing challenges in data interpretation, execution, and evidence validity.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Artificial intelligence for science (AI4S) is extending from interpretation of existing data to the design and execution of experiments. Space offers distinctive scientific opportunities while restricting physical support. Microgravity and extraterrestrial environments expose phenomena that terrestrial experiments cannot fully reproduce; finite samples, constrained resources, and limited opportunities for intervention complicate sustained investigation. This critical review examines orbital laboratories and planetary in situ science across biology, materials, fluid and thermal physics, and adaptive exploration. We distinguish learning from space-derived data, selecting scientific actions, executing them, and preserving experimental validity. Terrestrial self-driving laboratories provide complementary evidence on optimization, dedicated automation, robotic manipulation, and the support needed for unattended operation. The synthesis connects scientific gains already demonstrated by bounded AI systems to gaps in observation, executable actions, and continuity of valid evidence. Space robots can expand the attainable scope of autonomous science when necessary interventions exceed validated instrument capabilities and timely human support is unavailable. Their value must be established against dedicated mechanisms, redundancy, and human-supported operation. We develop a framework connecting sample history, scientific decisions, physical execution, and claim-specific validity. A worked orbital design, a planetary extension, and matched evaluation schemes separate the contributions of sensing, decision policies, and physical actions. The resulting agenda measures autonomy through valid scientific return, task coverage, intervention costs, and evidence integrity across complete campaigns.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Yubo Cui, Xianchao Guan, Zheng Zhang
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The paper introduces Textual Response-Aware Guidance (TRAG) to enhance zero-shot adversarial robustness in vision-language models by effectively constraining visual representation drift while preserving image-text relationships.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong zero-shot generalization but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Existing adversarial fine-tuning methods often use pre-trained model guidance to preserve image--text alignment while improving robustness. Our analysis of visual representation drift reveals complementary limitations of two representative forms of guidance. Matching visual features provides broad coverage by constraining all directions equally, but lacks semantic emphasis. Matching prediction distributions prioritizes semantically relevant directions, but remains limited by the candidate texts and prediction probabilities. These limitations can hinder preservation of pre-trained image--text relationships and degrade zero-shot performance. To address these issues, we propose Textual Response-Aware Guidance (TRAG), which constrains visual representation drift using the pre-trained text encoder's responses to local variations in input embeddings. Specifically, TRAG constructs anchor-level constraints from the response directions and magnitudes around semantic anchors, then aggregates them using pre-trained image--anchor relevance, yielding an image-adaptive constraint. Extensive experiments across architectures and tasks demonstrate state-of-the-art clean and robust performance. Further analysis shows that TRAG helps preserve pre-trained image--text relationships.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Seeing the Options: Typed Decisions over Visual Candidates with Reusable Option Memory
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Fengxin Li
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: This paper presents Iris, a multimodal decision-making model that efficiently processes visual candidates while maintaining accuracy and desirable properties through independent encoding and reusable option memory.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Agents end many steps in a typed decision over a set of candidates: which screen element to click, which product to pick. System One models answer in one forward pass, and Jeva showed that four properties the setting demands - a "none of the above" probability, invariance to candidate order, scalability in the number of candidates, and reuse of candidate computation - follow from encoding the request and each candidate separately and letting a request state read a candidate memory. Jeva is text-only, and existing multimodal System One models (OneJev, Jev-Omni) put images in the request while candidates stay text in letter slots. This paper asks what happens to the four properties, and to accuracy, when the candidates themselves are images. Iris admits image, text, or mixed candidates and leaves Jeva's decision module untouched. On a visual-candidate benchmark built from Multimodal-Mind2Web (every candidate is the element's screenshot crop, K=16, three splits), independent encoding reaches 78.4/72.1/74.8% with a flip rate of exactly zero, while joint encoding (OneJev-4B fine-tuned on the same data) reaches 90.6/89.5/91.6% but changes its answer on 8-10% of records when the crops are reordered. Most of the gap is the candidate not seeing the request: a third design that encodes each candidate after the state - but never after another candidate - keeps order invariance exactly, shares the state pass through a forked cache, and reaches 92.1/87.0/90.2% at a third of OneJev's latency with a calibrated null probability (AUROC 0.93-0.97). Letting pooled candidates see each other (set attention, token-level reads, multi-vector memory) buys nothing, because the encoder maps visually distinct elements to vectors within cosine 0.999 of each other. Reusing image candidates across requests cuts latency 37x at K=256 and 191x at K=2048. Code: https://github.com/lllfx/Iris

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Evaluation-Guided Demonstration Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Policies: The Winning Entry in the MetaFine Open Competition
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Lifan Zheng, Guotao Chen, Zhenyang Li, Shujie Cui, Qiang Huang
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The paper presents a refined vision-language-action policy that improved task performance in the MetaFine Open Competition by addressing failures through demonstration revisions and expert continuations.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: We fine-tuned a separate $π_{0.5}$ policy for each of the five tasks in the MetaFine Open Competition, with a task-specific training mixture and number of actions executed per prediction. Training started from the official demonstrations and expert procedures. Local evaluation exposed recurring grasping, pushing, and insertion failures. We addressed them by revising the demonstrated motions and by adding expert continuations from states the policy reached, while keeping nominal demonstrations in training. Checkpoints were compared on every instruction, so that a gain on one instruction could not hide a loss on another. Our submission, MAI, ranked first overall with a score of 96.66.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Hao Chen, Yukun Yan, Ziyu Han, Ye He, Chuanzhe Guo
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: RuHarness is a co-evolution framework that enhances autonomous agents' self-improvement by dynamically updating rubrics and harnesses based on evolving behavioral weaknesses during execution.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Autonomous agents increasingly depend on harnesses that govern interaction, memory, tools, and execution around large language models (LLMs). While recent work has begun to evolve these harnesses from execution experience, the supervision used to guide evolution often remains relatively static, making it difficult to track changing behavioral weaknesses across rounds and potentially limiting generalization to unseen tasks. To address this issue, we propose RuHarness, a rubric--harness co-evolution framework for continual agent self-improvement. RuHarness continually discovers and reassesses behavioral criteria from execution trajectories, prioritizes the most relevant unresolved weaknesses, and uses them to guide targeted harness updates while keeping the task objective fixed. Extensive experiments across diverse agent tasks and backbone models show that RuHarness outperforms strong harness-evolution baselines, particularly on unseen held-out tasks. Further analyses show that adaptive rubric prioritization tracks shifting weaknesses and supports more sustained improvement and stable generalization across evolution rounds.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Keru Zhou, Zhirui Fang, Xinrun Xu, Yaopeng Lou, Zeyuan He
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: Ego-CEVR is a framework that leverages egocentric videos to learn hierarchical visual representations for robot manipulation, enhancing task understanding and action alignment.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: As egocentric video becomes increasingly available for embodied learning, an important research question is how to turn this low-cost, scalable source of data into robot manipulation capabilities. Egocentric videos naturally provide rich context for high-level task understanding, while real-robot demonstrations with wrist observations and action annotations provide supervision for fine-grained action alignment. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns object relations, task state, and temporal progress through future prediction on egocentric video. The Interaction module interprets wrist observations in global context and learns local alignment and contact cues through robot action supervision. Separate residual paths expose both representations to the action policy, preserving direct access to task context alongside fine-grained execution information. Ego-CEVR supports independent pretraining of its global video module on large-scale human egocentric videos and videos from diverse robot embodiments, without requiring robot action labels or paired wrist observations.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: RePO-VLA: Recovery-Driven Policy Optimization for Vision-Language-Action Models
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Weijia Liufu, Xiaoyu Guo, Ruiyi Chen, Jingzhi Liu, Kaidong Zhang
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: RePO-VLA enhances Vision-Language-Action models' robustness in manipulation tasks by optimizing recovery-driven policies through a novel framework that utilizes success, recovery, and failure trajectories.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models remain brittle in long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation because success-only imitation provides little supervision for execution drift, while failed rollouts are often discarded. We introduce RePO-VLA, a recovery-driven policy optimization framework that assigns distinct roles to success, recovery, and failure trajectories. RePO-VLA first applies Recovery-Aware Initialization (RAI), slicing each corrective suffix into a new episode so corrective actions depend on the current adverse state rather than the preceding failure. It then learns a Progress-Aware Semantic Value Function (PAS-VF), aligning spatiotemporal trajectory features with instructions and successful references. The resulting labels salvage useful failure prefixes via reliability decay, while low-value labels mark drift and terminal breakdowns, teaching differences among nominal, failed, and corrective actions. The data engine turns adverse states into planner-generated or human-collected corrective rollouts, teaching recovery to the success manifold. Value-Conditioned Refinement (VCR) trains the policy to prefer high-progress actions. At deployment, a fixed high-value token biases actions toward the learned success manifold without online failure detectors or heuristic retries. We introduce the Failure-Recovery Benchmark (FRBench), with standardized error injection and recovery-focused evaluation. Across simulated and real-world bimanual tasks, RePO-VLA improves robustness, raising adversarial success from 20% to 75% on average and up to 80% in scaled real-world trials. Code and video results are available at https://1018weijia.github.io/RePO-VLA-Web/.

BIGAI.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
BIGAI.authors_text: Yuanhao Zeng, Shaocheng Lan, Ao Lu, Kuang Yan, Heng Lin
BIGAI.summary: The paper posits that agent evolution is hindered by unreliable evaluations that fail to distinguish beneficial artifacts from harmful ones, necessitating a shift in improvement detection methods.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: Agent evolution follows a simple loop: a proposer writes candidate artifacts (prompts, skills, memories) and selection accepts those that score higher. This loop has shown promise, yet practitioners face a puzzle: methods trade wins across papers, and evolution often fails to bootstrap on certain tasks. We trace this puzzle to the Resolution Hypothesis: agent evolution stalls not because methods fail to propose better artifacts, but because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify them. Across seven evolution methods and six models (over 10M LLM calls), we find support for the hypothesis at both levels where evaluation scores are used. At the candidate level (choosing artifacts), helpful candidate artifacts exist, but selection is no better than random at telling them from harmful ones, so errors accumulate across rounds. At the method level (ranking methods), typical margins of a few percentage points are smaller than the difference between two independent runs of the same method, so published rankings often rest on luck. Together, these findings indicate that agent evolution is often bottlenecked by reliably identifying improvements. This calls for a shift in how we develop and evaluate self-improving agents, from designing ever more candidate improvement systems to making true improvements detectable and accumulable.

BIGAI.title: LessMimic: Versatile Humanoid-Object Interaction with Unified Distance Field Representations
BIGAI.authors_text: Yutang Lin, Jieming Cui, Yixuan Li, Wei Liang, Baoxiong Jia
BIGAI.summary: LessMimic introduces a unified framework for humanoid-object interaction that enables versatile, command-steered control based on local geometry, enhancing generalization and skill composition.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: Humanoid robots capable of versatile whole-body interaction with everyday objects represent a central goal of embodied intelligence. Existing approaches often rely on motion-reference inputs or task-specific rewards, coupling policies to particular motion scripts, object geometries, and contact timings. This limits geometric generalization and flexible interaction control, where simple commands specify motion intent while object geometry determines how contact should be executed. We introduce LessMimic, a framework for versatile motion-free-at-inference humanoid-object interaction. At inference, a single whole-body policy is steered by root commands and an interaction-type flag instead of motion-reference inputs, and is conditioned on a compact interaction representation built from short histories of distance-field-derived surface distances and local surface directions. This geometry-conditioned interface enables command-steered control while adapting contact behavior to local object geometry. Through visual distillation, LessMimic further enables egocentric-depth-based deployment for MoCap-free sensing. Across object scales from 0.4x to 1.6x, LessMimic maintains robust performance over four interaction tasks, including PickUp, SitStand, Push, and Carry, where motion-conditioned baselines degrade sharply away from the training scale. Beyond single-task evaluation, LessMimic further supports sequential composition of heterogeneous interaction skills, attaining 62.1% success on five-task sequences and retaining 23.5% success at 15 task instances. By grounding interaction control in local geometry rather than motion references, LessMimic provides a path toward geometry-generalizable, command-steerable humanoid-object control with heterogeneous skill composition.

BIGAI.title: Learning Contextual Motion Constraints for Object Rearrangement Exploration
BIGAI.authors_text: Lexing Zhang, Zeyu Zhang, Gang Zeng, Hangxin Liu
BIGAI.summary: MoCo-Net, a two-stream neural network, predicts articulated motion ranges and obstacle heatmaps, enhancing object rearrangement exploration by integrating internal and external constraints.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: The motion of an articulated part in cluttered surroundings is constrained not only by an object's intrinsic joint limits but also by extrinsic obstacles. However, existing approaches primarily consider object articulation properties alone. Here we present Motion Constraint Prediction Network (MoCo-Net), a two-stream neural network that jointly predicts the continuous motion ranges of articulated parts and obstacle heatmaps highlighting potential collision regions from partial-view point cloud observation. By capturing both internal and external motion constraints, MoCo-Net produces more accurate feasible motion range prediction and obstacles recognition, improves generalization for novel objects in new scenes, and enables robots to construct a scene configuration space for efficient exploration of rearrangement actions. Our experiments show that MoCo-Net's two-stream design enhances each other to deliver more accurate predictions, which subsequently form a compact configuration space for a customized planner to efficiently rearrange the scene.

BIGAI.title: AetheRock: An Arm-Worn Robot Teaching System for Force-Guided Vision-Tactile Learning
BIGAI.authors_text: Hong Li, Yue Xu, Yihan Tang, Yankang Dong, Chenyuan Liu
BIGAI.summary: AetheRock is an arm-worn robot system that enhances force-guided vision-tactile learning through improved sensor integration and a novel multimodal representation framework.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: Force and tactile sensing are essential for contact-rich manipulation, but their integration into handheld or wearable devices is constrained by cost, size, and mechanical compatibility. Tactile signals are also sensitive to manufacturing variations and wear during use, posing further challenges to policy learning. To address these hardware and learning challenges, we introduce AetheRock, an arm-worn device for collecting gripper-force, visual, and tactile data. AetheRock incorporates GelSlim-Mini, our improved version of GelSlim 4.0 designed for low-cost, easy manufacturing, at the gripper fingertip, together with a resistive pressure sensor at the human finger contact area. To learn robust representations from the collected data, we propose ForceVT, a framework that aligns multimodal representations and uses force and vision to guide tactile learning, mitigating the effects of manufacturing variations and sensor degradation. Real-world experiments demonstrate efficient data collection with AetheRock. ForceVT improves average performance by 13% over the vision-tactile baseline and maintains an average task progress of 55.0% under reduced tactile fidelity, compared with 58.0% at full fidelity. Project page: https://lihongcs.github.io/aetherock.

BIGAI.title: PCTac: Mechanochromic Photonic-Crystal Tactile Sensor for Dexterous Manipulation
BIGAI.authors_text: Ruilin Zhang, Xuanshuo Liu, Junzhe Dai, Kefei Wu, Xuhao Qin
BIGAI.summary: PCTac introduces a mechanochromic photonic-crystal tactile sensor that directly translates contact load into color changes, enhancing robot manipulation success rates in various tasks.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: Modern visuotactile sensors primarily sense contact by imaging the deformation of a compliant interface. Using techniques such as photometric stereo, they can recover detailed contact geometry, often represented as surface normals or depth. However, force-related information typically still needs to be inferred indirectly through calibration, geometric reconstruction, or learned mappings. Mechanochromic photonic-crystal (PC) materials offer an alternative physical encoding mechanism: contact loading changes their periodic microstructure and spectral response, directly transforming local stress into a spatially resolved structural-color field. Despite this potential, PC materials have rarely been explored as visuotactile sensors for closed-loop robot learning. We present PCTac, an open-source mechanochromic PC fingertip that uses a dense hue field as its tactile observation. Loading characterization demonstrates a repeatable relationship between the applied normal load and the observed hue response. We further integrate this representation directly into a Diffusion Policy and evaluate it on three real-robot manipulation tasks. Across 90 physical rollouts, PCTac Hue achieves 68 successes (75.6\%), compared with 60 (66.7\%) for PCTac RGB, 57 (63.3\%) for Wedge RGB, and 29 (32.2\%) for vision-only. PCTac Hue also achieves the highest observed success rate on each evaluated task, including Perturbed Test-Tube Insertion, where it achieves 16/30 successes versus 13/30 for tactile RGB baselines and 1/30 for vision-only. These results demonstrate the potential of mechanochromic structural color as a compact, load-sensitive tactile representation for robot learning and closed-loop manipulation. Project page: https://bey0ndt1me.github.io/PCTac-page/.

BIGAI.title: Playing Soccer Like Humans Do: Learning Versatile and Agile Humanoid Soccer via Latent Motion Priors
BIGAI.authors_text: Haoyu Shao, Yunshen Wang, Jingze Zhang, Shaohang Zhu, Yong-Lu Li
BIGAI.summary: The paper presents "soccerbot," a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that enables humanoid robots to perform versatile, agile soccer skills with human-like motion using latent motion priors.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: Humanoid soccer requires a robot to seamlessly combine agile locomotion, ball manipulation, and impact-rich contact dynamics across a continuous, dynamic behavioral spectrum. Yet existing approaches either cover only a limited set of skills, or forego motion priors entirely and produce unnatural behaviors, leaving the combination of a unified skill set and human-like motion quality unaddressed. We present soccerbot, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that resolves both limitations through a structured latent motion prior distilled from large-scale human soccer motion capture data. By constraining policy learning within this dynamically plausible motion manifold, a single skill-conditioned policy naturally learns to perform moving, dribbling, trapping, and kicking in a unified formulation, while inherently producing human-like motion and fluid transitions during commanded skill switching. Augmented by robustness-oriented simulation design, soccerbot transfers zero-shot to the Unitree G1 humanoid robot, demonstrating agile, natural, and robust execution of the full soccer skill repertoire under real-world conditions.

BIGAI.title: DexHOT: Learning Hand-Object Configuration Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
BIGAI.authors_text: Zhewei Gui, Anthony Bolton, Jiyao Zhang, Zeyuan Chen, Qiyang Yan
BIGAI.summary: DexHOT introduces a method for dexterous manipulation by learning hand-object configuration transfer, achieving high success rates in both simulated and real environments without human demonstrations.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: Dexterous manipulation involves not only moving objects, but also arranging the hand around them to maintain useful contacts and enable subsequent actions. Yet many learning-based systems specify goals primarily through object poses or trajectories, leaving hand-object configurations to emerge implicitly. We introduce DexHOT, which formulates dexterous manipulation as hand-object configuration transfer: moving between feasible configurations that jointly specify hand articulation and object pose relative to the wrist. DexHOT learns a reusable relation-conditioned transfer primitive from synthetic feasible configuration pairs, without human reference motions, and composes long-horizon behaviors through closed-loop tracking of configuration subgoals. On DexHOTBench with 120 objects, a single policy achieves 80.5% transfer success on seen objects and 69.4% on unseen objects; on a real dexterous hand, it achieves 61.5% success over 200 real-robot transfers and 90% task success across six demonstration-guided tasks. These results show that explicit hand-object goals provide an expressive and composable interface for dexterous manipulation. More details and videos are available at https://dex-hot.github.io/.

BIGAI.title: STAR: Steering Action Representations during Inference
BIGAI.authors_text: Guangyu Zhao, Yongchang Zhang, Haoxuan Ru, Kaichen He, Haoran Wen
BIGAI.summary: STAR enhances vision-language-action models by improving late-layer object awareness during inference, boosting task success rates by 4.0% without requiring model updates.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) map language instructions and visual observations to robot actions, showing strong capabilities across robotic manipulation tasks. However, in our probing experiment, we find that action representations near the action output do not fully preserve task-relevant visual grounding. Motivated by this late-layer grounding gap, we introduce STAR, for STeering Action Representations, a training-free inference method for pre-trained VLAs. STAR applies an exponential moving average over late-layer residual updates, allowing later action representations to inherit object-aware update directions from earlier layers without model updates or architectural changes. It further uses recent proprioceptive states to adapt the mixing strength, using conservative mixing when execution dynamics change rapidly. Experiments on robot manipulation benchmarks show that STAR improves late-layer object awareness and increases average task success rates by 4.0 percentage points. Our code is available at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/STAR.

BIGAI.title: MemVLN: Streaming Episodic Memory for Vision-Language Navigation
BIGAI.authors_text: Yan Wang, Jiangyong Huang, Siyuan Huang, Baoxiong Jia
BIGAI.summary: MEMVLN introduces a streaming episodic memory framework for vision-language navigation, enhancing long-horizon task performance and achieving state-of-the-art results on VLN benchmarks.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: Vision-language navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to follow language instructions through 3D environments. Maintaining persistent episodic memory remains a challenge for VLM-based streaming agents in long-horizon navigation. We present MEMVLN, a streaming episodic memory framework that maintains a bounded bank of compressed perceptual features annotated with timesteps and action-derived relative poses, and produces compact memory tokens via cross-attention. We pair the proposed memory with a frozen pretrained geometry encoder. To learn the memory module, we design a masking-based trajectory summarization task with multi-granularity sub-trajectory decomposition, encouraging route reconstruction exclusively from episodic memory. Under navigation training restricted to the official R2R/RxR trajectories, MEMVLN achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics on standard VLN-CE benchmarks. Long-horizon analyses further characterize when episodic memory is useful. For physical evaluation, we collect 30 instruction-conditioned episodes in one physical scene, use 24 as demonstrations for post-training, and hold out six for testing. On the held-out episodes, MEMVLN improves success over the VLM baseline from 17% to 40%, and post-training further raises it to 47%.

南京大学.title: SimVLA: Attributing Gains in VLA Models Through Controlled Ablation
南京大学.authors_text: Yuankai Luo, Woping Chen, Tong Liang, Zhenguo Li
南京大学.summary: SimVLA is a minimal Vision-Language-Action model that reveals training dynamics as the primary performance driver, achieving high success rates across benchmarks with controlled ablation studies.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models often bundle architectural changes with different pretraining data, backbone scales, and optimization recipes, obscuring what actually drives progress. We introduce SimVLA, a deliberately minimal VLA, a standard vision-language backbone with a lightweight continuous-action head, as a controlled testbed for this attribution problem; our contribution is methodological and empirical (a controlled attribution study and a minimal-baseline calibration), not a new technique. Across LIBERO, CALVIN, WidowX, and Google Robot, one-knob-at-a-time ablations show that training dynamics are the largest measured driver, producing performance swings of $Δ$$\approx$54--94\%, while task configuration and architecture have smaller effects under matched settings. Despite using a small backbone and no additional large-scale robot-data VLA pretraining before benchmark-specific training, SimVLA reaches 98.6\% average success on LIBERO, remains competitive across the other benchmarks, and transfers to held-out real-robot scenes. These results suggest that simple, carefully controlled VLA baselines remain underexplored and provide a calibration point for future architectural claims within the VLM-encoder plus lightweight-head family. Website: https://frontierrobo.github.io/SimVLA

南京大学.title: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking: Memory-Guided Adaptive Reasoning for Embodied Navigation
南京大学.authors_text: Weile Gong, Zijian Lu, Jiahao Zheng, Bo Xu, Yiping Zuo
南京大学.summary: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking (CHAC) optimizes embodied navigation by reducing model calls and inference time while maintaining effective performance through memory-guided adaptive reasoning.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Multimodal foundation models are advancing embodied navigation, but frequent inference incurs substantial computational cost. We present Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking (CHAC), a training-free framework for memory-guided adaptive reasoning with a frozen navigation policy. Retained visual context, completion cues, and controller feedback determine the cognitive horizon, or how many cached waypoints the robot executes before refreshing its prediction. At the policy's stop request, local visitation history guides a bounded correction with at most one extra movement and no additional model calls. CHAC reduces vision-language model calls by 33.4% on HM3D-OVON and 64.7% on R2R-CE, with success-rate decreases of 0.63 and 10.82 percentage points, respectively. Success rate and success weighted by path length improve per model call on both benchmarks. Across four physical navigation tasks with 40 runs per method, CHAC achieves 18 successes versus 14 for native execution, reducing model calls by 54.9% and GPU inference time by 49.7%.

南京大学.title: Don't Lose the Future: Latent-Aware 4-Bit Quantization of World Action Models
南京大学.authors_text: Yichen Guo, Yanlong Chen, Xinyue Zhang, Mohan Liu, Song Zhang
南京大学.summary: The paper presents LAQ, a latent-aware quantization framework for 4-bit world action models that enhances future prediction fidelity while maintaining performance and efficiency on robotic systems.
南京大学.debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict how a scene will evolve and condition their actions on this predicted future. Deploying them on a robot's onboard computer calls for 4-bit weights, activations and key-value caches (W4A4KV4). Existing 4-bit quantizers for WAMs preserve the generated action, and estimate sensitivity one denoising step at a time. However, they fail to preserve the fidelity of the predicted future: once the action pathway is protected, the remaining action error enters mostly through a degraded future that none of them deliberately protects. We propose LAQ, a latent-aware quantization framework that preserves the predicted future where it is written, stored and read. Specifically, we introduce a reader metric, which measures future error by its effect on the action, and a read count, which weights each rounding error by the number of denoising steps that read it. Together they give the allocation of precision over activations and caches a closed-form solution. We further develop gaze-guided refinement, which gives the tokens the action attends to a second 4-bit pass in the denoising loop and in the cache. All weights stay at 4 bits, with no high-precision branch and no per-task recalibration. On the LIBERO-Plus benchmark, LAQ reaches 76.4% and 83.3% average success on Fast-WAM and Cosmos-Policy, within 1.2 percentage points of the 16-bit models and all above the baselines with 16-bit KV caches. It compresses the model by 3.8x, reduces the peak GPU memory of the whole policy by 2.3x, and runs 1.66x faster than the 16-bit model. On a real AgileX PiPER arm, it reaches 47.0% average success over three tasks, against 52.0% for the 16-bit model and 30.0% higher than QuaRot.

南京大学.title: MultiWorldBench: Do Independently Controlled Views Describe One Shared World?
南京大学.authors_text: Zhangbo Xu, Ruoxi Zhang, Rui Hu, Yisong Wang, Xitong Li
南京大学.summary: MultiWorldBench evaluates multiplayer world models in Minecraft, revealing that while Gamma-World outperforms others, all models significantly lag behind Engine GT in shared world coherence.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Multiplayer world models must ensure that independently controlled views remain consistent with a single shared and persistent world. We introduce MultiWorldBench, a diagnostic Minecraft benchmark comprising 495 case configurations across seven task suites and ten capabilities, including independent control, cross-view motion, shared-state synchronization, persistence, structural reasoning, concurrent interaction, and delayed revisit. Using Engine GT as a reference, we evaluate two multiplayer world models, Solaris (MP) and Gamma-World, together with a single-player generation variant, Solaris (SP). Among the generated systems, Gamma-World achieves the highest ten-capability average at 21.39, followed by Solaris (MP) at 20.88 and Solaris (SP) at 10.06, while Engine GT reaches 91.69. Gamma-World performs better on several control, shared-state, and revisit capabilities, whereas Solaris (MP) leads in cross-view motion and race-condition consistency. Nevertheless, all generated systems score at most 8.00 on state persistence and 1.33 on structural consistency, and none succeeds in spatial reasoning or building-identity preservation. Human pairwise evaluation yields the same overall system ranking and shows strong alignment with the automatic evaluation, with a mean dimension-level Spearman correlation of 0.95. These results show that current multiplayer world models still exhibit a substantial gap relative to Engine GT in maintaining a coherent shared world.

南京大学.title: Policy Improvement-Guided Replay for Continual Reinforcement Learning
南京大学.authors_text: Qin-Wen Luo, Haoxuan Gao, Sheng Ren, Xiang Chen, Sheng-Jun Huang
南京大学.summary: The paper presents Contrastive Likelihood Replay (CoLiR), a method for continual reinforcement learning that enhances performance retention and new-task learning in vision-language models.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Continual reinforcement learning (CRL) requires models to acquire new capabilities while retaining performance on previous tasks. A stability-oriented perspective common in conventional continual learning emphasizes knowledge preservation and interference mitigation. Complementing this perspective, we revisit CRL for vision-language models through policy improvement, a fundamental principle of RL, to preserve acquired performance gains. Using the performance difference lemma, we characterize historical performance changes through the current policy's expected advantages on historical task distributions, motivating replay of historical prompts with the current policy. To allocate limited replay memory, we propose Contrastive Likelihood Replay (CoLiR), which contrasts likelihood gains on correct responses from the final task policy with likelihood reductions on incorrect responses from the initial policy. Our analysis links correct-response likelihood gains to reference-policy advantages under an idealized KL-regularized optimal update and provides an endogenous-reward interpretation for general policy updates. CoLiR estimates scores from finite training rollouts and cached log-likelihoods, selects prompts at task boundaries, and replays them uniformly during subsequent training, with KL regularization restricted to replayed prompts. Memory construction only requires a small amount of additional cross-policy scoring but no additional response generation. Across three Qwen3-VL model sizes on MRCL, CoLiR achieves the highest mean final accuracy and mean task accuracy among the compared methods while maintaining competitive new-task performance.

南京大学.title: Alignment Drives Reuse: Learning Generalizable Robot-Use Agents from Heterogeneous Experience
南京大学.authors_text: Ziyue Wang, Yaopeng Yang, Liyi Zhou
南京大学.summary: UniCraft enhances robot manipulation skill learning by aligning heterogeneous experiences across benchmarks, improving task success rates and enabling zero-shot transfer across different robot embodiments.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate broad generalization across tasks and domains. However, comparable generalization in robot manipulation remains challenging. Heterogeneity in robot embodiments, task formulations, geometric conventions, and action interfaces fragments interaction experience across benchmarks and hardware. We rethink robot skill learning through alignment: Can heterogeneous interactions across benchmarks and embodiments jointly improve one shared skillset for robot manipulation? We propose UniCraft, a framework for learning robot manipulation skills by aligning heterogeneous settings. Specifically, UniCraft represents observed scene geometry using consistent coordinate conventions and aligns sensing and control interfaces across robots. It organizes tasks from different benchmarks in a canonical format, allowing interaction feedback to jointly refine shared skills and the orchestration policy that guides their selection and composition, without any demonstrations or model weight updates. We interleave tasks from 3 benchmarks and 6 embodiments, collecting 2,700 learning rollouts per agent model. During training, UniCraft improves pooled task success on unseen scenarios and tasks by 9-28 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO, 10.8-13.3 on RoboTwin 2.0, and 3.1-14.4 on RoboCasa365 (Epochs 1-3). After training, with the learned skills frozen, UniCraft demonstrates zero-shot transfer across 4 new robot embodiments and 5 additional agent models on robosuite and RoboDojo.

南京大学.title: Evo-DexBench: Benchmarking Generalization across Related Tasks for Dexterous Manipulation
南京大学.authors_text: Bing Cheng, Yiran Mao, Zewei Ye, Yifan Jin, Xinyi Chen
南京大学.summary: Evo-DexBench introduces a controlled benchmark for evaluating dexterous manipulation policies' ability to generalize knowledge transfer across related tasks with limited demonstrations.
南京大学.debug_abstract: General-purpose dexterous manipulation requires policies to transfer knowledge from related tasks to new tasks with only a few target demonstrations. Existing benchmarks often provide too many target demonstrations and leave the differences between source and target tasks uncontrolled. As a result, they cannot clearly distinguish knowledge transfer from task memorization. Our key insight is the Core-Gen principle. Core tasks are related tasks that share a functional interaction and provide source knowledge, while a Gen task is a novel target within the same functional family that has only a few demonstrations. This setup tests whether a policy can reuse functional interaction knowledge. Based on this principle, we propose Evo-DexBench, which controls both source-task relatedness and target-task exposure. It comprises 30 tasks in six functional families, three everyday layouts per task, and 1,248 multimodal demonstrations collected via VR teleoperation with simulated Shadow Hands equipped with 123 taxels. We first compare few-shot adaptation strategies and find that joint Core + Gen training makes the most effective use of Core knowledge. Under this setting, we evaluate six representative policies. The best-performing policy, $π_{0.5}$, achieves a mean success rate of only 24.4%, revealing the limitations of existing methods in transferring functional interaction knowledge. Further analysis shows that on the tested Gen targets, functionally matched Core data yields larger success-rate gains than mismatched data, and that with matched Core data, 8 Gen demonstrations reach the performance of training on 16--32 Gen demonstrations alone. These results indicate that Evo-DexBench separates knowledge transfer from task memorization under controlled conditions and effectively evaluates the generalization of dexterous manipulation policies across related tasks.

南京大学.title: Hindsight Self-Distillation: Teaching Robots to Act from the Present
南京大学.authors_text: Haisen He, Yechi Liu, Tianle Shi, Haoyun Liu, Chuanzhang Meng
南京大学.summary: Hindsight Self-Distillation (HSD) trains robots to optimize actions using future visual feedback, achieving high success rates in task performance.
南京大学.debug_abstract: A robot must choose an action before it can see the outcome. In a recorded demonstration, later camera frames show what happened after the robot moved. Hindsight Self-Distillation (HSD) uses these later frames to teach a policy what to extract from current images. During training, a teacher sees both the current and later frames, while a student sees the current frames. They share a visual encoder and an action predictor. Each branch summarizes its images with a small set of feature vectors. These visual summaries supply all visual input to the action predictor. The teacher learns from demonstrated actions. For each noisy action sequence, the student learns from either the demonstration or the teacher's denoising prediction. It also learns to match the teacher's visual summaries. We analyze which aspects of the teacher's predictions the student can recover from its inputs. At deployment, the student encodes the current images once and reuses its summaries at every denoising step. HSD achieves average success rates of 98.50\% on LIBERO and 92.31\% on RoboTwin 2.0.

南京大学.title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
南京大学.authors_text: Yao Zhang, Bin Yu, Shijie Lian, Haishan Liu, Changti Wu
南京大学.summary: Fast-JEPA enhances latent world model planning by enabling efficient action-sequence search with low latency, achieving high success rates across various benchmarks and dynamic conditions.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost. It constructs a goal-directed plan to guide search and directly predicts the outcomes of complete candidates for efficient comparison, avoiding recursive state rollout during refinement. Across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, Fast-JEPA achieves 96.50% average success rate with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT. Search-budget sweeps show that its competitive success and low latency extend across candidate counts and refinement depths. We further introduce DynaGoal, a benchmark for evaluating world-model planning under dynamic out-of-distribution conditions, execution deadlines, and controlled response delays. Fast-JEPA achieves average success rates of 73.83% on DynaGoal-Shift and 87.67% on DynaGoal-Deadline, demonstrating the practical value of low-latency predictive planning under changing control conditions and execution-time constraints. Our code is available at https://github.com/Sofilyzia/Fast-JEPA.

南京大学.title: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain
南京大学.authors_text: Shuang Wu, Jiachen Qian, Youtian Lin, Feihu Zhang, Philip Torr
南京大学.summary: Direct3D-V3 introduces a latent-free diffusion transformer for native 3D generation, directly modeling SDF voxel grids and enhancing geometry fidelity through implicit regularization and camera parameter prediction.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. Despite their architectural differences, these methods all share the same premise: geometry is first compressed into a latent space and only then modeled by the generator. We take a different route and propose Direct3D-V3, a latent-free diffusion transformer (DiT) framework that discards the VAE altogether and operates in the native voxel domain, directly modeling raw SDF voxel grids during both training and sampling. To make this direct voxel formulation geometrically reliable, we introduce an implicit manifold regularization over neighboring voxels to suppress non-watertight surfaces, and convert predicted SDF grids into meshes via Marching Cubes so that rendered normal losses can supervise the model directly from its predicted SDF. To improve alignment between the conditioning image and generated geometry, Direct3D-V3 also predicts the camera parameters of the conditioning image as an auxiliary task, encouraging the DiT to learn the mapping from image observations to 3D shape. This latent-free design removes the reconstruction bottleneck, brings training under an objective in the native voxel domain, and yields meshes with substantially richer local detail. The predicted camera and native SDF voxel output further make Direct3D-V3 extensible to generative reconstruction, where diffusion is interleaved with normal-guided refinement to improve alignment with the observed view while the generative prior completes unseen regions. Project page: https://dreamtechai.github.io/Direct3D-V3.

南京大学.title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification
南京大学.authors_text: Jiarui Guo, Saining Zhang, Jiaying Wan, Jiawei Weng, Junhao Chen
南京大学.summary: RFW-S is a comprehensive dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified deformable objects, enhancing robotic simulation with reliable physical properties and interaction behaviors across diverse categories.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging. We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags. We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. To ensure physical reliability, we introduce an independent simulation verification framework that evaluates object behaviors under interactions distinct from those used for parameter calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of independent verification and characterize deformable responses under different physical configurations. We further evaluate robotic grasping in terms of both task success and object integrity, and demonstrate the physical realism of our simulated objects through sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation. RFW-S provides a scalable foundation for physically grounded simulation and embodied robotic learning.

南京大学.title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent
南京大学.authors_text: Siyuan Du, Yuxin Liu, Meng Tang, Haoran Li, Yechao Bai
南京大学.summary: The paper presents a reverse-to-forward curriculum with advantage decomposition to enhance long-horizon task performance in LLM agents, achieving superior success rates in complex environments.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a common approach for training large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon tasks. However, learning from sparse terminal rewards makes credit assignment and exploration difficult. We approach these challenges through a policy-induced capability region, the set of states from which the current policy can reliably complete a task. Near its boundary, an agent may need only a few actions to reach a more solvable state, even when the goal remains distant. This reduces long-horizon learning to two coupled subproblems of reaching that state and completing the task from there. We address them with paired advantages and a progressive reverse-to-forward curriculum. The advantages provide separate signals for reaching more solvable states and completing the task from them, while the curriculum expands the capability region backward along successful reference trajectories and then into off-reference states through on-policy exploration. On ALFWorld and WebShop, our method outperforms competitive agentic RL methods at both model scales, achieving success rates of 90.1%/96.1% and 80.2%/82.6% with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, respectively.

南京大学.title: Every Camera Grows Up: Camera-Height Regression in Interactive Video World Models
南京大学.authors_text: Sheng Lu, Guangpin Tao, Tong Lu, Ying Tai
南京大学.summary: The paper identifies and analyzes the issue of camera-height regression in interactive video world models, demonstrating that six models inaccurately shift camera height towards human eye level during motion.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Interactive video world models serve as simulators for embodied agents: from a starting image and an action trajectory, they generate the views the agent would see. The starting image fixes how high the camera is, for example 0.15 m for a floor robot or 2.2 m for an overhead camera, and a faithful simulator must keep this height as the camera moves. We show that six recent open-weight models fail to do so: as motion replaces the starting view with generated content, they move the camera toward human eye level, a failure we call camera-height regression. Our benchmark, EyeHeight, pairs six rendered elevations (0.15 m to 2.2 m) and four calibrated real-world rig heights with scale-free multi-view height estimation. All six models lose their initial height during a $180^\circ$ turn-and-walk rollout: initialized at 0.15 m, only 0-20% of clips end within $1.3\times$ of the starting height as inferred viewpoints converge to human heights of 1.1 m to 1.5 m, whereas ground-truth renders remain within a few percent. In Matrix-Game models, homography-tracked floor motion stays consistent with constant elevation during rotation even as newly outpainted room geometry yields a higher reconstructed viewpoint. Regression grows with rotation angle, begins while the start frame remains in context, and largely reverses in SANA-WM when a $360^\circ$ turn restores the initial view. We trace this pull to human-centric video priors in which floor-level views are nearly absent: in SANA-WM, textual height cues and dense floor-disparity maps do not prevent it, whereas classifier-free text guidance during the first half of denoising strengthens it. Combining unguided sampling with height-balanced fine-tuning recovers more retention but costs 5 MUSIQ points, a loss fixed during those same early steps. Viewpoint drift alone shifts the paths predicted by visual navigation policies.

南京大学.title: Sketch, Don't Paint: Allocating Test-Time Compute in Generative Visual Reasoning
南京大学.authors_text: Sheng Lu, Guangpin Tao, Tong Lu, Ying Tai
南京大学.summary: The paper proposes a method for optimizing test-time compute in generative visual reasoning by prioritizing sketching over full rendering, enhancing accuracy and efficiency.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Multimodal models increasingly reason by synthesizing pixels, sketching maze paths within interleaved chains of thought or rolling out video solutions frame by frame. Each visual thought runs the full diffusion schedule inherited from photorealistic synthesis, so iterative denoising dominates inference cost. We study how to allocate test-time compute along two axes: when to render visual thoughts rather than thinking in text or answering directly, and how many denoising steps each thought requires. Controlled interventions that vary only how the thought is rendered uncover three regimes. Causal thoughts carry the plan and become legible early: an 8-step sketch nearly matches a 50-step render in accuracy, commits to the same plan as often as two independent full renders agree, and in video models mostly fails by stalling short of the goal, so the rollout abstains. Decorative thoughts can be omitted without loss, whereas harmful thoughts lower accuracy. Because the regime depends on both model and task, always drawing is suboptimal. Across 14 model-benchmark pairs of three interleaved reasoners, answering directly, without any thinking, wins 9 pairs, and choosing among direct, text-only, and visual tiers from ten labeled examples per pair raises mean accuracy from 60.7% (always drawing) to 65.1%. Where drawing pays, we propose sketch-and-vote, which samples 8-step sketches (a step count chosen without labels) from independent noises until one answer reaches three votes. With this one setting, sketch-and-vote beats full rendering with fewer denoising steps on an image reasoner and two video reasoners, by 8.6 points on VSP spatial planning and by 9.6 and 22.1 points on mazes.

南京大学.title: Text-Guided Modality Correction for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
南京大学.authors_text: Yu Quan, Dong Zhang, Ping Gong, Peng Huang, JinHui Tang
