The best performing models achieve mean current-frame localization errors of 0.14 m for the ego player and 0.54 m for the ball, future forecasting errors of 0.34 m for the ego player and 0.91 m for the ball over 1.1 s, and a mean contact-time prediction error of 0.14 s. Auxiliary depth information substantially improves 3D ball localization, suggesting that inferring metric depth remains a challenge. Longer image histories do not improve ball forecasting, indicating that representations exploit scene context rather than rely solely on inter-frame motion. Finally, we propose a conditional diffusion model to generate whole-body kinematic tennis motion from vision encoder predictions on egocentric video at real-time rates, adapting movements as predictions are refined. These results move towards a deeper understanding of how foundation vision models can support real-time dynamic robots using egocentric video.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Recoverability, Not Invariance: Certified Safety for Robots at the Limits of Performance
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Thomas A. Berrueta, Joshua D. Ibrahim, Gilchrist X. Johnson, John Lathrop, Soon-Jo Chung
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: This paper introduces recoverability as a safety certification method for robots, enabling certified recovery from aggressive maneuvers without relying on forward invariance.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Safety certification in robotics typically rests on forward invariance of the deployed controller, a property that demands high-fidelity models at the edge of the operating envelope, exactly where models are least reliable and robots perform best. As a result, many of the behaviors we most want robots to run, from learned policies to aggressive maneuvers at the limits of traction, cannot be certified at all. We introduce recoverability, a contraction-theoretic safety concept that resolves this tension by certifying a robot's ability to reengage a trusted recovery mode rather than the invariance of a deployed behavior. We prove that switching to the recovery mode from anywhere inside a certified tube guarantees exponential convergence, even under disturbances and model error. To decide when to switch, we derive the contraction insertion gradient, the first-order effect of a recovery insertion on the certificate, and embed it in a switching-time program in which feasibility alone guarantees safety and optimality only shapes performance. To supply the certificates, we develop sequential convex synthesis that monotonically grows the certified tube toward the exact viability kernel. We validate our approach in simulated quadrotor flight through uncertain obstacles, where it outperforms invariance-based safety filters, and in hardware deployments aboard a full-scale IndyNXT autonomous racecar, where it repeatedly recovers the car from an aggressive raceline at the limits of handling in the rain. Recoverability provides a certified exit strategy, extending formal safety guarantees to aggressive, learned, and experimental behaviors without requiring their invariance.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Dual-Actuation Emulation of Scaled Relative Orbital Dynamics on a Free-Flyer
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Elias Krantz, Pedro Roque, Gunnar Tibert, Huina Mao, Christer Fuglesang
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: The paper presents a dual-actuation system that emulates orbital dynamics in a free-flyer testbed, validating its effectiveness through hardware tests and simulations.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Ground-based free-flyer testbeds reproduce the planar motion of a free-floating spacecraft using air bearings, but not the relative dynamics of spacecraft in orbit. We present a dual-actuation architecture that physically emulates Clohessy-Wiltshire dynamics on an open-source free-flyer. Two model predictive controllers run in parallel: one drives the solenoid thrusters with an orbital dynamics model, representing the spacecraft under test; the other drives bidirectional propellers that physically apply the orbital accelerations, continuously updating its reference to account for thruster-induced velocity changes. A dynamic similitude maps the orbital scenario onto the limited floor area and actuation rates of the testbed, letting the spacecraft controller run directly at orbital scale. We validate the architecture on hardware and against a high-fidelity orbital simulation, where the orbital accelerations instead arise naturally, both driven by the identical spacecraft controller. Their agreement indicates that the testbed reproduces the relative orbital motion the controller would encounter in flight.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Adapting Monocular Depth Estimation in Novel Scenes through Disparity Refinement and Robot Ego-Motion
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Dimitrios Chatziparaschis, Georgios Georgakis, Adnan I. Ansar, Shehryar Khattak, Konstantinos Karydis
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: EM-ViT enhances monocular depth estimation in novel scenes by refining disparity and leveraging robot ego-motion for real-time adaptation and improved accuracy.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: The geometric understanding of a scene is a crucial component for safe and efficient robotic operations in novel and unstructured environments. The recent emergence of foundation models for Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) has provided an opportunity to enrich robotic perception capabilities with dense long-range depth predictions, replacing expensive onboard hardware (e.g., LiDARs and stereo cameras). However, these offline models are primarily trained on affine-invariant depth representations, and their generalization to novel scenes remains unclear. In this work we present EM-ViT, a monocular depth estimation model that learns to adapt online relative depth inputs from a foundation model prior to the metric scale with observations collected during robotic operations. Motivated by the stereo camera parameterization, our method decomposes depth prediction via dense disparity refinement to recover the scene's relative structure and an effective baseline scalar prediction to determine the missing metric scale. The learning process leverages sparse LiDAR points and, optionally, the robot's Ego-Motion (EM) to rapidly train a lightweight Vision Transformer (ViT), while an internal gradient matching loss preserves the fine-grained semantic structure of the input disparity in real-time. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on publicly available sequences, such as KITTI, and show that our online learning pipeline can adapt to novel scenes faster and with higher accuracy than existing MDE foundation models. The code and supplementary materials will be publicly available at https://emvit-mde.github.io.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Practical Adversarial Attacks on Stochastic Bandits via Fake Data Injection
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Qirun Zeng, Eric He, Richard Hoffmann, Xuchuang Wang, Jinhang Zuo
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: This paper introduces a practical adversarial attack model for stochastic bandits, employing limited fake data injection to mislead algorithms while minimizing attack costs.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Adversarial attacks on stochastic bandits have traditionally relied on some unrealistic assumptions, such as per-round reward manipulation and unbounded perturbations, limiting their relevance to real-world systems. We propose a more practical threat model, Fake Data Injection, which reflects realistic adversarial constraints: the attacker can inject only a limited number of bounded fake feedback samples into the learner's history, simulating legitimate interactions. We design effective attack strategies under this model, explicitly addressing both magnitude constraints (on reward values) and temporal constraints (on when and how often data can be injected). Our theoretical analysis shows that these attacks can mislead a class of bandit algorithms into selecting a target arm in nearly all rounds while incurring only sublinear attack cost. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets validate the effectiveness of our strategies, revealing vulnerabilities in stochastic bandit algorithms under practical adversarial scenarios.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Beyond Topology: A Morphological Symmetry Graph Representation for Locomotion Policy Learning
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Sizhe Wei, Xulin Chen, Fengze Xie, Garrett Ethan Katz, Zhenyu Gan
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: The paper presents a morphological symmetry graph representation for locomotion policy learning, enhancing performance in articulated robots by integrating topology and symmetry in reinforcement learning.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning has enabled impressive locomotion skills on articulated robots, but common policy representations remain only weakly aligned with robot physics. Generic networks ignore kinematic structure, while graph-based policies encode connectivity without specifying how physical quantities transform across symmetric body parts. We introduce a morphological symmetry graph representation for locomotion policy learning, instantiated as MS-PPO with PPO on Go2 and MS-SAC with FastSAC on G1. Starting from the robot's topological graph, our representation explicitly incorporates the permutations and sign changes induced by morphological symmetry on observations and actions, yielding a graph actor with an equivariant action mean and an invariant critic. We evaluate the representation on Unitree Go2 command tracking and asymmetric joint-failure tasks, and on Unitree G1 29-DoF whole-body locomotion, including zero-shot sim-to-real deployment. Our approach achieves the lowest tracking errors in both simulation and hardware, and the highest mean simulation returns across all three joint-failure types on Go2 among the evaluated baselines. On Go2, MS-PPO uses only 34.6% of the parameters of the PPO baseline. These results support the effectiveness of jointly encoding topology and morphological symmetry across robot embodiments and learning frameworks.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: GeoWind2Plan: Mission-Time 3D Urban Wind Prediction for Energy-Efficient UAV Planning
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Shaoxiang Qin, Yucheng Zhao, Fuyuan Lyu, Di Zhou, Jiachen Yao
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: GeoWind2Plan is a rapid framework for 3D urban wind prediction that enhances energy-efficient UAV planning by utilizing localized geometry and neural operators, outperforming traditional CFD methods.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: In urban low-altitude flight, buildings reshape ambient wind into spatially varying 3D flow, making unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) energy depend on local wind exposure as well as path length. However, building-resolved wind is rarely available when a mission must be planned. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) produces high-fidelity urban flow fields, but each simulation is tied to a fixed inflow boundary condition and can take hours to days, which is incompatible with urban UAV missions that typically last minutes to tens of minutes. We present GeoWind2Plan, a geometry-to-wind-to-planning framework for mission-time 3D urban wind prediction and energy-efficient UAV planning. Given only a background wind vector, 3D building geometry, and a start-goal pair, GeoWind2Plan transforms the building geometry into a reference-wind frame, predicts mission-relevant 3D wind patches with a localized geometry-conditioned neural operator, stitches them into a local wind field, and optimizes a feasible 3D path and speed profile using a physically grounded UAV energy model. Rather than pursuing CFD-perfect reconstruction, GeoWind2Plan targets decision-useful wind prediction: trajectories are planned with predicted wind and evaluated under high-fidelity CFD wind. Across held-out urban domains, wind speeds, and mission wind-angle regimes, GeoWind2Plan performs corridor-localized wind inference in about 3 s, compared with roughly 8 h for CFD. Under CFD evaluation, trajectories planned with GeoWind2Plan reduce energy by 6.9%, 12.7%, and 4.5% in tailwind, headwind, and crosswind missions relative to wind-agnostic planning, recovering 87.9%, 85.7%, and 75.0% of CFD-reference savings. These results show that fast, corridor-localized 3D urban wind prediction can make wind-aware UAV energy planning practical at mission time. Code/dataset: https://github.com/DUAL-Xiao/GeoWind2Plan/ . Demo: https://geowind2plan.com .

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Neural Integral Control Barrier Functions for Agile Collision Avoidance
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Dasari Raj Vamsi, Vrushabh Zinage, Efstathios Bakolas, Rohan Chandra
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: This paper introduces a data-driven approach to learn integral control barrier functions for agile collision avoidance, enhancing safety and performance in dynamic environments.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) are a standard way to keep a planner inside a safe set, but they assume control affine dynamics, a barrier function given in closed form, and a known nominal controller. Integral control barrier functions (ICBFs) remove the first assumption and absorb input constraints, yet they still assume a given nominal controller and a barrier function. In this work, we present an approach to learn all three from data, using neural ordinary differential equations (ODEs) for the dynamics, imitation for the nominal controller, and supervised regression for the barrier function. The learned dynamics, nominal controller, and the barrier function are used to build the ICBF filter constraint analytically. Furthermore, the barrier is trained on viability rather than geometry, meaning that a state counts as safe only if some emergency maneuver can still avoid the constraint under the actuator limits, a correction that geometric labels miss entirely and that grows with speed. Actuator limits then enter the online program as hard bounds while the learned barrier rows may be relaxed, which keeps the program solvable at every state and the actuator limits exact, and we bound how far the input it returns can drift from the one the true models would give. On agile racing with a 6-D dynamic bicycle, the filter removes all 12 unsafe episodes from 200 held out layouts at an unchanged success rate and above 100 Hz on one CPU core, holds the input constraint on every episode of a benchmark where a jointly trained baseline holds it on 53.38%, and keeps that advantage under large errors in the plant friction.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: ImplicitHop: Evaluating knowledge integration across context and memory
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Alexander Detkov, Dashiel Karish, Matthew Oleynikov, Matt Thomson
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: The paper introduces benchmarks to evaluate knowledge integration in large language models, revealing that in-context information significantly enhances reasoning over pretrained knowledge.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: The ability to integrate new information and deduce its consequences is central to learning, understanding, and reasoning in large language models (LLMs). Whether information arrives during training or in-context, models must not only store local facts, but propagate their long-range implications globally. To explore information integration in LLMs, we introduce two complementary natural language benchmarks for large-scale evaluation of deductive reasoning as a function of inference depth. The first is a formal graph benchmark enabling controlled evaluation over a wide range of graph topologies and integration tasks; the second is a knowledge composition benchmark grounded in real-world knowledge graphs. We use these benchmarks to compare knowledge integration from information encoded in context versus information encoded in model weights during pretraining, evaluating a set of open models implicitly, without chain of thought. We find that accuracy decays sharply with increased composition length for both pretrained and in-context knowledge. Information presented in-context, however, substantially outperforms deduction over information encoded in weights. These results quantify a fundamental limitation of current models with direct implications for prompt-based control of agent behavior and for continual learning strategies, and they provide a foundation for developing training, prompting, and integration methods that support deeper reasoning.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: WildOS: Open-Vocabulary Object Search in the Wild
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Hardik Shah, Manthan Patel, Erica Tevere, Deegan Atha, Marcel Kaufmann
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: WildOS integrates safe geometric exploration with semantic visual reasoning for efficient long-range object search in unstructured environments, outperforming traditional navigation methods.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Autonomous navigation in complex, unstructured outdoor environments requires robots to operate over long ranges without prior maps and limited depth sensing. In such settings, relying solely on geometric frontiers for exploration is often insufficient. In such settings, the ability to reason semantically about where to go and what is safe to traverse is crucial for robust, efficient exploration. This work presents WildOS, a unified system for long-range, open-vocabulary object search that combines safe geometric exploration with semantic visual reasoning. WildOS builds a sparse navigation graph to maintain spatial memory, while utilizing a foundation-model-based vision module, ExploRFM, to score frontier nodes of the graph. ExploRFM simultaneously predicts traversability, visual frontiers, and object similarity in image space, enabling real-time, onboard semantic navigation tasks. The resulting vision-scored graph enables the robot to explore semantically meaningful directions while ensuring geometric safety. Furthermore, we introduce a particle-filter-based method for coarse localization of the open-vocabulary target query, that estimates candidate goal positions beyond the robot's immediate depth horizon, enabling effective planning toward distant goals. Extensive closed-loop field experiments across diverse off-road and urban terrains demonstrate that WildOS enables robust navigation, significantly outperforming purely geometric and purely vision-based baselines in both efficiency and autonomy. Our results highlight the potential of vision foundation models to drive open-world robotic behaviors that are both semantically informed and geometrically grounded. Project Page: https://leggedrobotics.github.io/wildos/

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: FORGE: Feasible Online Reduced-Order Reference Generation and Whole-Body Execution for Agile Humanoid Locomotion
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Adrian B. Ghansah, Yujin An, Jeeseop Kim, Soon-Jo Chung
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: The paper introduces FORGE, a two-stage framework for agile humanoid locomotion that combines online reduced-order model reference generation with whole-body tracking control, achieving versatile movement capabilities.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: This paper presents a two-stage learning framework for versatile and agile humanoid locomotion that couples online reduced-order model (ROM) reference generation with whole-body tracking control. In the first stage, we train a command-conditioned whole-body reference generator using single rigid body dynamics combined with full humanoid kinematics. In the second stage, the frozen ROM policy is rolled out online to generate references for training a whole-body tracking policy on the full-order dynamics model. Learning a kino-dynamically consistent reference generator in the simplified ROM space enables us to generate references over a broad command space and over multiple locomotion strategies using a single unified framework. We demonstrate the approach on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, achieving longitudinal velocities from -2.0 m/s to 2.8 m/s, lateral velocities up to +-1.0 m/s, angular velocities up to +-3.0 rad/s, one-legged hopping, and continuous transitions across the commands, all using one unified reference policy and one whole-body tracking policy.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Explore Where It Matters: Targeted Exploration for Efficient Rover Adaptation
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Jacob Levy, Arthur Bouton, Tristan D. Hassler, Hari Nayar, David Fridovich-Keil
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: TERRA is an online adaptation framework that enhances rover mobility on challenging terrains by efficiently targeting exploration to correct model errors during deployment.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Future planetary rovers will traverse steep, deformable terrain where slip, sinkage, and terrain deformation can threaten mobility. Although simulation can capture some wheel-soil effects, unmodeled deformable-terrain phenomena create sim-to-real gaps requiring deployment-time adaptation. Yet, rover operations leave little room for extensive trial-and-error. We introduce TERRA (Targeted Exploration for Reward-Relevant Adaptation), an online adaptation framework that efficiently seeks deployment data exposing task-relevant model errors and corrects them. TERRA adapts a simulation-trained world model with a reward-weighted prediction loss and trains a loss predictor to estimate where future performance-relevant errors are likely to occur, using this signal to guide exploration during MPC. In simulation, TERRA reaches approximately 90% slope-climbing success within five trials under severe out-of-distribution pretraining conditions, outperforming exploration baselines in reward, completion time, and energy to first success. On the ERNEST rover, TERRA recovers coordinated active-suspension locomotion on a deformable Mars-simulant slope within three to five real-world trials. Project website: https://terra-explore.github.io

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Embodied Learning of Reward for Musculoskeletal Control with Vision Language Models
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Saraswati Soedarmadji, Yunyue Wei, Chen Zhang, Yisong Yue, Yanan Sui
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: The MoVLR framework utilizes vision-language models to iteratively explore and refine reward functions for musculoskeletal control, aligning high-level movement goals with effective motor strategies.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Discovering effective reward functions remains a fundamental challenge in motor control of high-dimensional musculoskeletal systems. While humans can describe movement goals explicitly such as "walking forward with an upright posture," the underlying control strategies that realize these goals are largely implicit, making it difficult to directly design rewards from high-level goals and natural language descriptions. We introduce Motion from Vision-Language Representation (MoVLR), a framework that leverages vision-language models (VLMs) to bridge the gap between goal specification and movement control. Rather than relying on handcrafted rewards, MoVLR iteratively explores the reward space through iterative interaction between control optimization and VLM feedback, aligning control policies with physically coordinated behaviors. Our approach transforms language and vision-based assessments into structured guidance for embodied learning, enabling the discovery and refinement of reward functions for high-dimensional musculoskeletal locomotion and manipulation. These results suggest that VLMs can effectively ground abstract motion descriptions in the implicit principles governing physiological motor control.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: StreamEgo: Streaming Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Tianyi Xu, Boyang Lyu, Yunkai Tang, Kairan Ding, Jiahang Li
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: StreamEgo is a real-time framework for unbounded exocentric-to-egocentric video generation, enhancing immersive experiences and overcoming limitations of existing methods with innovative training techniques.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Exocentric-to-egocentric (Exo2Ego) video generation transforms third-person recordings into first-person viewpoints, unlocking immersive AR/VR experiences and scalable demonstration synthesis for embodied robotics. Extending it to a streaming setting is expected to further enable live applications. However, existing methods suffer from degraded manipulation regions, overfitting and confinement to fixed-length clips with prohibitive latency. To address these limitations, we present StreamEgo, a real-time framework for unbounded, generalizable Exo2Ego video generation. To resolve intricate manipulation dynamics while supporting the streaming pipeline, a streaming dual-branch prior provides pixel-aligned guidance for translating appearance and skeletal kinematics. We also introduce a region-aware loss curriculum to improve generalization and stabilize multi-objective diffusion training. Furthermore, we distill the model into a chunk-wise autoregressive model, augmented with a region-aware corruption mechanism and a first-chunk curriculum, enabling high-quality, generalizable real-time streaming Exo2Ego generation at 24.3 FPS on a single H100 GPU.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Shihan Wu, You Liu, Chunyu He, Minghui Qin, Longhan Jiao
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: HumanCOIN is a comprehensive 12,500-hour dataset capturing human intent in egocentric manipulation through three observational tiers: gaze, muscle exertion, and cognitive decision-making.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: https://flagopen.github.io/HumanCOIN.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: AdaS-ViT: Test-Time Adaptive Routing for Spiking Vision Transformers with Ultra-High Energy Efficiency
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Zecheng Hao, Zihan Huang, Shenghao Xie, Jiyuan Zhang, Zhaofei Yu
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: AdaS-ViT introduces a test-time adaptive routing mechanism for spiking vision transformers, enhancing energy efficiency and performance through selective spike emission and fine-grained firing patterns.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise event-driven and energy-efficient vision, yet existing spiking vision transformers (S-ViTs) largely confine spiking tokens to fixed and uniform firing schemes along the temporal, spatial and channel dimensions, whereas suppressing the computational redundancy thus incurred calls for adaptive firing mechanisms that operate jointly across all three axes at test time. To this end, we propose the Adaptive Efficient Integrate-and-Fire (AdaE-IF) model, which consults the attention score of each spiking token and routes salient regions to fine-grained firing patterns while assigning energy-frugal coarse patterns to the remaining regions. Building on AdaE-IF, we further introduce Spiking Gated Self-Attention (S-GSA) and Spiking Local-Gated Unit (S-LGU), which enforce selective spike emission at token and channel granularity. We integrate the aforementioned mechanisms and modules into AdaS-ViT, a test-time adaptive-routing architecture trained with a progressive spatio-temporal curriculum that stabilizes the co-adaptation of firing precision and routing masks. Extensive experiments across benchmarks spanning diverse data scales and modalities demonstrate that AdaS-ViT consistently achieves highly competitive performance. Notably, on ImageNet-1k it consumes only 1.02 to 2.45 millijoules per image and attains an accuracy-per-energy ratio of 32$\times$ to 72$\times$, operating in an economical inference regime and thereby pushing the energy-efficiency boundary further.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: WISE: World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Chenhao Zhang, Hanyu Zhao, Zihan Que, Hang Cheng, Tengfei Pan
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: WISE introduces a framework for efficiently scheduling world-model imagination in post-training vision-language-action models, enhancing policy refinement and reducing computational costs while improving robustness.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Post-training VLA policies typically rely on supervised fine-tuning with costly expert demonstrations or reinforcement learning with expensive and potentially unstable real-world exploration. World models offer a promising alternative by evaluating candidate behaviors through imagined futures, yet effective post-training requires more than accurate prediction: imagination must be scheduled where it is useful, bounded within reliable horizons, and translated into trustworthy policy supervision. In robotic manipulation, the value of imagination varies substantially across execution stages, while extended rollouts can accumulate prediction errors and introduce unreliable learning signals. We introduce WISE (World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models), a unified framework that coordinates when and how world-model imagination is used during policy refinement. WISE selectively invokes imagination at interaction-relevant states, performs bounded multi-view rollouts, evaluates candidate futures using progress and completion signals, and uses their relative outcomes to refine actions generated from real interaction contexts. Extensive experiments with both $π_0$ and $π_{0.5}$ demonstrate consistent improvements across diverse manipulation tasks while reducing GPU computation time by approximately 80% compared with full imagination. Real-world evaluations further show substantial gains in robustness and generalization under diverse real-world distribution shifts.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Haofeng Wang, Pengcheng Wen, Ruiqi Li, Yuhao Zhang, Tiange Zhang
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: PhysCapBench is a novel benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, evaluating annotation quality across diverse domains to enhance language supervision in physical AI applications.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning strategies, and guide training-data refinement. Motivated by our data construction for world-model pretraining, we introduce PhysCapBench, to our knowledge the first unified physical-caption benchmark spanning all three domains: third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It provides human-verified annotations for 1,500 video sequences and evaluates accuracy and coverage through seven physical dimensions. We examine downstream utility through video reconstruction and manipulation-policy fine-tuning. Physical captions reduce reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos relative to metadata captions. Training-instruction enrichment improves both PhysCapBench scores and policy success, including a 7.5-percentage-point gain for pi0.5 on a RoboTwin 2.0 subtask. PhysCapBench makes the physical content of language supervision inspectable and comparable, providing a cross-domain basis for its evaluation and improvement.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Yichi Zhang, Bo Wang, Zhenghan Zhu, Yutong Han, Jiayin Zou
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: HEIR is a resource for studying human-robot interactions by integrating speech, gaze, and video data to enhance intent understanding and task execution in natural settings.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: For robots to assist, serve, and collaborate with humans, they must not only interpret human requests conveyed through language and multimodal intentional cues, but also execute long-horizon tasks that interleave navigation and manipulation. In this paper, we introduce HEIR, a resource for studying how to Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interaction. HEIR pairs human speech, measured gaze, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories, while each session preserves successive episodes, with each request fulfilled through multiple execution subtasks. The captured data, together with human-authored annotations, support the study of intent grounding, execution planning, and task completion within a unified interaction setting. To demonstrate the value of HEIR, we conduct extensive offline experiments to evaluate how models benefit from additional human-centric context across these tasks, together with real-robot experiments that assess execution task completion. HEIR thus provides a valuable resource for studying user-centric robot interaction in naturalistic household environments. Our demo and dataset are available online.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Agent Distillation across Models, Artifacts, and Harnesses
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Ziluowen Luo, Senzhang Wang, Chaozhuo Li, Jun Yin, Hao Yan
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: This paper presents a unified survey on Agent Distillation, emphasizing persistent knowledge transfer across models, artifacts, and harnesses to enhance agent capabilities and adaptability.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Knowledge distillation provides a teacher-student framework for transferring capabilities at reduced cost and has been widely studied for large language models (LLMs). As LLM-based agents move from response generation to sustained, closed-loop task solving, distillation expands beyond model parameters to knowledge retained in reusable resources and execution workflows. This shift from model-level to agent-level knowledge transfer supports efficient deployment, broader capability access, and continual self-evolution. However, existing surveys largely examine model distillation and agent system design separately, limiting comparison of transfer strategies across agent components. To bridge this gap, we formalize Agent Distillation as persistent knowledge transfer between teacher and student agents and present its first unified survey. Distinguishing experience used for transfer from knowledge retained for reuse, we develop a knowledge-substrate taxonomy based on where knowledge persists: models, artifacts, or harnesses. Building on this taxonomy, we analyze cross-substrate transfer paths and hybrid strategies. To assess the resulting capabilities, we review benchmarks and evaluation protocols for retention, causal attribution, and deployed utility without further teacher support. This survey provides a unified basis for studying agent knowledge transfer and developing efficient, adaptable, and self-evolving agents.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Fuhao Li, Wenxuan Song, Qizhou Huang, Ziyang Zhou, Jingbo Wang
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: The SLA model enhances robotic manipulation by integrating continual pre-training for spatial understanding, optimizing action prediction, and utilizing diverse datasets for improved 3D spatial alignment.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes. To accommodate this diversity, we introduce feature-dependent gates that adaptively aggregate visual embeddings from multiple VLA layers for spatial supervision. The teacher further exploits partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB observations, enabling effective use of heterogeneous geometric annotations. Probabilistic state dropout encourages reliance on visual cues and mitigates overfitting to demonstration trajectories. All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: EviSeek: An Evidence-Centric Agentic Framework for Embodied Active Information Seeking
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Jintao Li, Zhiyong Cao, Baihua Xiao, Yu Bai, Börje F. Karlsson
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: EviSeek is a framework that enhances embodied question answering by explicitly linking evidence acquisition objectives to actions, improving accuracy and efficiency in information seeking.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Active embodied question answering requires agents to acquire evidence through viewpoint changes and physical interaction. The central challenge is to avoid undirected interaction: taking plausible actions without specifying what evidence they should reveal for answering the question. Action plans and accumulated histories alone can leave the informational purpose of an interaction implicit. We introduce EviSeek, a training-free framework that makes question-derived evidence demands explicit acquisition objectives, linking observation-conditioned actions and selectively retained evidence to the information the agent seeks. On 3,436 ESI-Bench questions, EviSeek improves accuracy over the Single-model agent by 7.1 percentage points with Qwen3-VL-32B and 3.7 points with Gemini 3.1 Pro, while improving visual-support-weighted accuracy and reducing mean token usage. These findings support making the informational purpose of interaction explicit, with action selection and evidence retention organized around what the agent needs to learn to answer the question.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: MOST: Memory of Object States and Task Progress for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Diqi He, Jinbang Guo, Yijun Shen, Zhiwei Yu, Huan Yang
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: The MOST framework enhances long-horizon mobile manipulation by using a memory system that prioritizes task-relevant state changes and progress, outperforming previous models in various benchmarks.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Long-horizon embodied manipulation requires policies to act on information that is no longer visible. Modified objects may leave the field of view, while completed subtasks continue to constrain future actions. Existing approaches extend temporal context through recurrent state updates, test-time training, or storage and retrieval of past observations. As horizons grow, these mechanisms can still leave the policy to infer task state from long, redundant, and viewpoint-dependent visual experience. We argue that long-horizon agents benefit not merely from remembering more, but from remembering task-relevant state changes and progress. We propose Memory of Object States and Task Progress (MOST), a policy-internal memory framework that compresses multi-view observations into temporal tokens. Historical and predictive future tokens are explicitly supervised with object states and subtask progress, structuring memory around what has changed in the world and what has already been accomplished. The resulting memory directly conditions action generation within a single end-to-end policy, without an external planner or retrieval stage. We further introduce RoboCasa-Long, a benchmark of multi-minute, multi-stage mobile manipulation tasks. Across RoboCasa365, RoboCasa-Long, and real-world robot experiments, MOST consistently outperforms Xiaomi-Robotics-1 (XR-1), the previous state-of-the-art model. It raises average success from 65.9% to 72.1% on RoboCasa365, average maximum task progress from 20.83% to 42.22% on RoboCasa-Long, and real-world success from 6.66% to 43.33%. MOST also outperforms a matched visual-history memory variant, showing that effective long-horizon memory depends not only on how much experience is retained, but on whether it preserves decision-relevant progress and world-state changes.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: When the Past Shapes Action: Understanding Embodied Memory
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Siqi Li, Ziyi Bai, Xinrun Xu, Tinglei Huang, Börje F. Karlsson
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: This survey explores embodied memory in AI, detailing its requirements, architectural approaches, and challenges for enhancing decision-making in dynamic environments.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Recent advances in generative foundation models have expanded the capabilities of embodied AI, enabling increasingly general navigation, manipulation, and long-horizon task execution. However, effective interaction with dynamic environments requires more than only strong perception and reasoning: agents must act with partial knowledge and retain, retrieve, and update information from past observations, actions, and experiences. This survey examines embodied memory as a mechanism for preserving decision-relevant information beyond the current observation. We organize existing approaches along two complementary dimensions: six fundamental memory requirements, spanning world-state persistence, task progress, belief maintenance, and experiential learning; and eight architectural categories, including recurrent states, fast weights, visual and symbolic representations, spatial memory, and experience-based systems. We analyze their capabilities and limitations, and examine how existing benchmarks evaluate memory-dependent behavior, distinguishing genuine use of historical information from general task performance. Finally, we identify open challenges in selecting relevant experiences, maintaining consistent beliefs in changing environments, and consolidating knowledge across episodes. Our analysis provides a framework for understanding memory as an essential component of reliable, adaptive, and lifelong-horizon embodied intelligence.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: RoboSTD: Zero-Shot Single-to-Dual Transfer via Sagittal Mirroring for Bimanual Learning
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Hongyu Wu, Chong Liu, Shaoxuan Xie, Shaqi Luo, Hanyu Feng
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: RoboSTD enables zero-shot transfer from single-arm to bimanual robot manipulation using sagittal mirroring and LLM-generated coordination constraints, significantly enhancing performance without additional demonstrations.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Bimanual robot manipulation plays an important role in real-world robotic applications, but the high cost of collecting bimanual demonstrations limits the scalable development of bimanual policy learning. Meanwhile, existing single-arm manipulation data are difficult to directly transfer to bimanual systems due to the Single-to-Dual gap in action spaces, coordination requirements, and arm-side spatial preference. To address this issue, we propose RoboSTD, a zero-shot Single-to-Dual data construction method for bimanual robot learning. RoboSTD first applies sagittal-plane mirroring to observations, proprioception, and actions to construct executable contralateral pseudo-demonstrations. It then uses an LLM to generate structured spatio-temporal coordination constraints that guide the reconstruction of pseudo-bimanual supervision across workspace regions and task stages. We evaluate RoboSTD on the AgileX ALOHA platform in both RoboTwin simulation and real-world settings. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of RoboSTD for bimanual policy learning. Without requiring additional bimanual demonstrations, RoboSTD increases the average number of collected cups to 2.11x that of the single-arm baseline in the cup collection task. Project page: https://huahungy.github.io/RoboSTD/

具身智能研究中心.title: StreamEgo: Streaming Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Tianyi Xu, Boyang Lyu, Yunkai Tang, Kairan Ding, Jiahang Li
具身智能研究中心.summary: StreamEgo is a real-time framework for unbounded exocentric-to-egocentric video generation, enhancing immersive experiences and overcoming limitations of existing methods with innovative training techniques.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Exocentric-to-egocentric (Exo2Ego) video generation transforms third-person recordings into first-person viewpoints, unlocking immersive AR/VR experiences and scalable demonstration synthesis for embodied robotics. Extending it to a streaming setting is expected to further enable live applications. However, existing methods suffer from degraded manipulation regions, overfitting and confinement to fixed-length clips with prohibitive latency. To address these limitations, we present StreamEgo, a real-time framework for unbounded, generalizable Exo2Ego video generation. To resolve intricate manipulation dynamics while supporting the streaming pipeline, a streaming dual-branch prior provides pixel-aligned guidance for translating appearance and skeletal kinematics. We also introduce a region-aware loss curriculum to improve generalization and stabilize multi-objective diffusion training. Furthermore, we distill the model into a chunk-wise autoregressive model, augmented with a region-aware corruption mechanism and a first-chunk curriculum, enabling high-quality, generalizable real-time streaming Exo2Ego generation at 24.3 FPS on a single H100 GPU.

具身智能研究中心.title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Shihan Wu, You Liu, Chunyu He, Minghui Qin, Longhan Jiao
具身智能研究中心.summary: HumanCOIN is a comprehensive 12,500-hour dataset capturing human intent in egocentric manipulation through three observational tiers: gaze, muscle exertion, and cognitive decision-making.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: https://flagopen.github.io/HumanCOIN.

具身智能研究中心.title: AdaS-ViT: Test-Time Adaptive Routing for Spiking Vision Transformers with Ultra-High Energy Efficiency
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Zecheng Hao, Zihan Huang, Shenghao Xie, Jiyuan Zhang, Zhaofei Yu
具身智能研究中心.summary: AdaS-ViT introduces a test-time adaptive routing mechanism for spiking vision transformers, enhancing energy efficiency and performance through selective spike emission and fine-grained firing patterns.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise event-driven and energy-efficient vision, yet existing spiking vision transformers (S-ViTs) largely confine spiking tokens to fixed and uniform firing schemes along the temporal, spatial and channel dimensions, whereas suppressing the computational redundancy thus incurred calls for adaptive firing mechanisms that operate jointly across all three axes at test time. To this end, we propose the Adaptive Efficient Integrate-and-Fire (AdaE-IF) model, which consults the attention score of each spiking token and routes salient regions to fine-grained firing patterns while assigning energy-frugal coarse patterns to the remaining regions. Building on AdaE-IF, we further introduce Spiking Gated Self-Attention (S-GSA) and Spiking Local-Gated Unit (S-LGU), which enforce selective spike emission at token and channel granularity. We integrate the aforementioned mechanisms and modules into AdaS-ViT, a test-time adaptive-routing architecture trained with a progressive spatio-temporal curriculum that stabilizes the co-adaptation of firing precision and routing masks. Extensive experiments across benchmarks spanning diverse data scales and modalities demonstrate that AdaS-ViT consistently achieves highly competitive performance. Notably, on ImageNet-1k it consumes only 1.02 to 2.45 millijoules per image and attains an accuracy-per-energy ratio of 32$\times$ to 72$\times$, operating in an economical inference regime and thereby pushing the energy-efficiency boundary further.

具身智能研究中心.title: WISE: World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Chenhao Zhang, Hanyu Zhao, Zihan Que, Hang Cheng, Tengfei Pan
具身智能研究中心.summary: WISE introduces a framework for efficiently scheduling world-model imagination in post-training vision-language-action models, enhancing policy refinement and reducing computational costs while improving robustness.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Post-training VLA policies typically rely on supervised fine-tuning with costly expert demonstrations or reinforcement learning with expensive and potentially unstable real-world exploration. World models offer a promising alternative by evaluating candidate behaviors through imagined futures, yet effective post-training requires more than accurate prediction: imagination must be scheduled where it is useful, bounded within reliable horizons, and translated into trustworthy policy supervision. In robotic manipulation, the value of imagination varies substantially across execution stages, while extended rollouts can accumulate prediction errors and introduce unreliable learning signals. We introduce WISE (World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models), a unified framework that coordinates when and how world-model imagination is used during policy refinement. WISE selectively invokes imagination at interaction-relevant states, performs bounded multi-view rollouts, evaluates candidate futures using progress and completion signals, and uses their relative outcomes to refine actions generated from real interaction contexts. Extensive experiments with both $π_0$ and $π_{0.5}$ demonstrate consistent improvements across diverse manipulation tasks while reducing GPU computation time by approximately 80% compared with full imagination. Real-world evaluations further show substantial gains in robustness and generalization under diverse real-world distribution shifts.

具身智能研究中心.title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Haofeng Wang, Pengcheng Wen, Ruiqi Li, Yuhao Zhang, Tiange Zhang
具身智能研究中心.summary: PhysCapBench is a novel benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, evaluating annotation quality across diverse domains to enhance language supervision in physical AI applications.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning strategies, and guide training-data refinement. Motivated by our data construction for world-model pretraining, we introduce PhysCapBench, to our knowledge the first unified physical-caption benchmark spanning all three domains: third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It provides human-verified annotations for 1,500 video sequences and evaluates accuracy and coverage through seven physical dimensions. We examine downstream utility through video reconstruction and manipulation-policy fine-tuning. Physical captions reduce reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos relative to metadata captions. Training-instruction enrichment improves both PhysCapBench scores and policy success, including a 7.5-percentage-point gain for pi0.5 on a RoboTwin 2.0 subtask. PhysCapBench makes the physical content of language supervision inspectable and comparable, providing a cross-domain basis for its evaluation and improvement.

具身智能研究中心.title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Yichi Zhang, Bo Wang, Zhenghan Zhu, Yutong Han, Jiayin Zou
具身智能研究中心.summary: HEIR is a resource for studying human-robot interactions by integrating speech, gaze, and video data to enhance intent understanding and task execution in natural settings.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: For robots to assist, serve, and collaborate with humans, they must not only interpret human requests conveyed through language and multimodal intentional cues, but also execute long-horizon tasks that interleave navigation and manipulation. In this paper, we introduce HEIR, a resource for studying how to Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interaction. HEIR pairs human speech, measured gaze, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories, while each session preserves successive episodes, with each request fulfilled through multiple execution subtasks. The captured data, together with human-authored annotations, support the study of intent grounding, execution planning, and task completion within a unified interaction setting. To demonstrate the value of HEIR, we conduct extensive offline experiments to evaluate how models benefit from additional human-centric context across these tasks, together with real-robot experiments that assess execution task completion. HEIR thus provides a valuable resource for studying user-centric robot interaction in naturalistic household environments. Our demo and dataset are available online.

具身智能研究中心.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Agent Distillation across Models, Artifacts, and Harnesses
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Ziluowen Luo, Senzhang Wang, Chaozhuo Li, Jun Yin, Hao Yan
具身智能研究中心.summary: This paper presents a unified survey on Agent Distillation, emphasizing persistent knowledge transfer across models, artifacts, and harnesses to enhance agent capabilities and adaptability.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Knowledge distillation provides a teacher-student framework for transferring capabilities at reduced cost and has been widely studied for large language models (LLMs). As LLM-based agents move from response generation to sustained, closed-loop task solving, distillation expands beyond model parameters to knowledge retained in reusable resources and execution workflows. This shift from model-level to agent-level knowledge transfer supports efficient deployment, broader capability access, and continual self-evolution. However, existing surveys largely examine model distillation and agent system design separately, limiting comparison of transfer strategies across agent components. To bridge this gap, we formalize Agent Distillation as persistent knowledge transfer between teacher and student agents and present its first unified survey. Distinguishing experience used for transfer from knowledge retained for reuse, we develop a knowledge-substrate taxonomy based on where knowledge persists: models, artifacts, or harnesses. Building on this taxonomy, we analyze cross-substrate transfer paths and hybrid strategies. To assess the resulting capabilities, we review benchmarks and evaluation protocols for retention, causal attribution, and deployed utility without further teacher support. This survey provides a unified basis for studying agent knowledge transfer and developing efficient, adaptable, and self-evolving agents.

具身智能研究中心.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Fuhao Li, Wenxuan Song, Qizhou Huang, Ziyang Zhou, Jingbo Wang
具身智能研究中心.summary: The SLA model enhances robotic manipulation by integrating continual pre-training for spatial understanding, optimizing action prediction, and utilizing diverse datasets for improved 3D spatial alignment.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes. To accommodate this diversity, we introduce feature-dependent gates that adaptively aggregate visual embeddings from multiple VLA layers for spatial supervision. The teacher further exploits partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB observations, enabling effective use of heterogeneous geometric annotations. Probabilistic state dropout encourages reliance on visual cues and mitigates overfitting to demonstration trajectories. All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture.

具身智能研究中心.title: EviSeek: An Evidence-Centric Agentic Framework for Embodied Active Information Seeking
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Jintao Li, Zhiyong Cao, Baihua Xiao, Yu Bai, Börje F. Karlsson
具身智能研究中心.summary: EviSeek is a framework that enhances embodied question answering by explicitly linking evidence acquisition objectives to actions, improving accuracy and efficiency in information seeking.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Active embodied question answering requires agents to acquire evidence through viewpoint changes and physical interaction. The central challenge is to avoid undirected interaction: taking plausible actions without specifying what evidence they should reveal for answering the question. Action plans and accumulated histories alone can leave the informational purpose of an interaction implicit. We introduce EviSeek, a training-free framework that makes question-derived evidence demands explicit acquisition objectives, linking observation-conditioned actions and selectively retained evidence to the information the agent seeks. On 3,436 ESI-Bench questions, EviSeek improves accuracy over the Single-model agent by 7.1 percentage points with Qwen3-VL-32B and 3.7 points with Gemini 3.1 Pro, while improving visual-support-weighted accuracy and reducing mean token usage. These findings support making the informational purpose of interaction explicit, with action selection and evidence retention organized around what the agent needs to learn to answer the question.

具身智能研究中心.title: MOST: Memory of Object States and Task Progress for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Diqi He, Jinbang Guo, Yijun Shen, Zhiwei Yu, Huan Yang
具身智能研究中心.summary: The MOST framework enhances long-horizon mobile manipulation by using a memory system that prioritizes task-relevant state changes and progress, outperforming previous models in various benchmarks.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Long-horizon embodied manipulation requires policies to act on information that is no longer visible. Modified objects may leave the field of view, while completed subtasks continue to constrain future actions. Existing approaches extend temporal context through recurrent state updates, test-time training, or storage and retrieval of past observations. As horizons grow, these mechanisms can still leave the policy to infer task state from long, redundant, and viewpoint-dependent visual experience. We argue that long-horizon agents benefit not merely from remembering more, but from remembering task-relevant state changes and progress. We propose Memory of Object States and Task Progress (MOST), a policy-internal memory framework that compresses multi-view observations into temporal tokens. Historical and predictive future tokens are explicitly supervised with object states and subtask progress, structuring memory around what has changed in the world and what has already been accomplished. The resulting memory directly conditions action generation within a single end-to-end policy, without an external planner or retrieval stage. We further introduce RoboCasa-Long, a benchmark of multi-minute, multi-stage mobile manipulation tasks. Across RoboCasa365, RoboCasa-Long, and real-world robot experiments, MOST consistently outperforms Xiaomi-Robotics-1 (XR-1), the previous state-of-the-art model. It raises average success from 65.9% to 72.1% on RoboCasa365, average maximum task progress from 20.83% to 42.22% on RoboCasa-Long, and real-world success from 6.66% to 43.33%. MOST also outperforms a matched visual-history memory variant, showing that effective long-horizon memory depends not only on how much experience is retained, but on whether it preserves decision-relevant progress and world-state changes.

具身智能研究中心.title: When the Past Shapes Action: Understanding Embodied Memory
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Siqi Li, Ziyi Bai, Xinrun Xu, Tinglei Huang, Börje F. Karlsson
具身智能研究中心.summary: This survey explores embodied memory in AI, detailing its requirements, architectural approaches, and challenges for enhancing decision-making in dynamic environments.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Recent advances in generative foundation models have expanded the capabilities of embodied AI, enabling increasingly general navigation, manipulation, and long-horizon task execution. However, effective interaction with dynamic environments requires more than only strong perception and reasoning: agents must act with partial knowledge and retain, retrieve, and update information from past observations, actions, and experiences. This survey examines embodied memory as a mechanism for preserving decision-relevant information beyond the current observation. We organize existing approaches along two complementary dimensions: six fundamental memory requirements, spanning world-state persistence, task progress, belief maintenance, and experiential learning; and eight architectural categories, including recurrent states, fast weights, visual and symbolic representations, spatial memory, and experience-based systems. We analyze their capabilities and limitations, and examine how existing benchmarks evaluate memory-dependent behavior, distinguishing genuine use of historical information from general task performance. Finally, we identify open challenges in selecting relevant experiences, maintaining consistent beliefs in changing environments, and consolidating knowledge across episodes. Our analysis provides a framework for understanding memory as an essential component of reliable, adaptive, and lifelong-horizon embodied intelligence.

具身智能研究中心.title: RoboSTD: Zero-Shot Single-to-Dual Transfer via Sagittal Mirroring for Bimanual Learning
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Hongyu Wu, Chong Liu, Shaoxuan Xie, Shaqi Luo, Hanyu Feng
具身智能研究中心.summary: RoboSTD enables zero-shot transfer from single-arm to bimanual robot manipulation using sagittal mirroring and LLM-generated coordination constraints, significantly enhancing performance without additional demonstrations.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Bimanual robot manipulation plays an important role in real-world robotic applications, but the high cost of collecting bimanual demonstrations limits the scalable development of bimanual policy learning. Meanwhile, existing single-arm manipulation data are difficult to directly transfer to bimanual systems due to the Single-to-Dual gap in action spaces, coordination requirements, and arm-side spatial preference. Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: GTA: Generative Tower of Agents for Scalable Holonic Scene Generation
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Zeng Tao, Yunuo Chen, Xiang Feng, Yumeng He, Peihao Li
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: GTA introduces a scalable framework for world modeling by using holons and parallel agents to efficiently generate and refine dynamic scenes and characters.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Scalable world modeling requires coordinating scene-wide goals with fine-grained objects and dynamic characters under limited time and context budgets. We introduce GTA (Generative Tower of Agents), which represents every unit at every level of an adaptive scene hierarchy as a holon, both a self-contained construction task and a composable scene unit. Parallel agents recursively plan the hierarchy top-down, generate assets, and assemble and refine them bottom-up. Uniform interfaces carry scene-wide requirements down the hierarchy, guiding local construction so that each holon fits into the larger one. GTA accelerates scalable world modeling through high-throughput parallel execution while preserving well-structured layouts and fine-grained asset details. GTA then populates the assembled environments with dynamic human characters whose appearance and motion are guided by the scene, yielding realized 4D worlds. Project page: https://zt-zeng-tao.github.io/GTA/

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: One Frozen Simulator Is Not Enough: Simulator Collapse in Multi-Agent RL
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Simon Yu, Nicholas Tomlin, Marwa Abdulhai, Ximing Lu, Derek Chong
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: The paper identifies "simulator collapse" in multi-agent reinforcement learning, proposing Verbalized Sampling and Co-Training as solutions to enhance agent generalization and performance with diverse simulators.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for human-AI interaction usually trains the agent against a single large language model (LLM) that simulates the user. We show that agents trained this way can systematically fail to generalize, and we trace the failure to simulator collapse: the simulator LLM is mode-collapsed, and a policy trained against it learns narrow strategies that exploit the simulator's mode behavior; these strategies transfer poorly to unseen simulators and to real users. We formalize the collapse and propose two solutions. Verbalized Sampling, applied at inference time, samples each simulator reply from a verbalized response distribution. Co-Training, applied during training similar to self-play, co-evolves the simulator as the policy, so the policy cannot exploit the mode behavior. A population variant samples the simulator for each rollout from a pool of recent checkpoints. We validate both solutions on three benchmarks: Persuasion for Good, tau^2-bench, and CooperBench. Verbalized Sampling improves held-out success by up to 9% over single-simulator RL, and Co-Training pushes gains further to 14%; the human study shows similar gain on real users. Both solutions also preserve the policy diversity that collapses under single-simulator RL. Overall, our findings on simulator collapse point to diverse simulators as a requirement for RL agents that serve real users. We release SCOPE, an open-source framework for Population Co-Training in multi-agent RL.

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: Code4Scene: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Constructing and Editing 3D Scenes
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Xiaokang Ye, Siddhant Hitesh Mantri, Zimeng Chen, Edward Zhang, Zhaoxu Zheng
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: Code4Scene benchmarks coding agents' abilities in constructing and editing 3D scenes, revealing gaps in spatial reasoning and state control despite strong performance correlations.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Frontier coding agents can now write and execute code that authors 3D environments, but whether they reliably understand 3D structure and precisely control scene state remains unclear. The generated 3D scene is a persistent, executable artifact: a convincing render can hide incorrect spatial relations, intersecting objects, or unintended modifications. We introduce Code4Scene, a benchmark of 170 Unreal Engine cases built from human-assembled scenes that evaluates coding agents on two complementary settings under a shared execution interface. Construction tests scene-level spatial reasoning from open-ended language specifications, where many realizations are valid; editing tests precise control of scene state, where the agent must recover the target scene from reference images while preserving everything else. Rather than scoring code or rendered views, Code4Scene evaluates the generated engine-native scene for task fulfillment, artifact integrity, and static physical validity, with edits additionally compared against withheld ground truth. Across 14 coding-agent systems on the 83-case public set, construction and editing performance are strongly correlated but not interchangeable (Spearman $ρ= 0.67$): Claude Fable 5.1 leads construction, Gemini 3.8 Flash leads editing. Spatial Composition is the weakest construction category for every agent, while editing remains imprecise: the best Repair F1 is only 0.562, and 34.2% of edits that fully recover the target still introduce unintended changes elsewhere in the scene. These results expose a gap between plausible 3D generation and reliable spatial reasoning and state control. The project webpage is at https://simworld.org/code4scene.

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: HospitalBench: Diagnosing Where and Why Embodied Agents Fail on Long Hospital Task Chains
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Gaytri Jena, Kapil Wanaskar, Aman Chadha, Vasu Sharma, Vinija Jain
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: HospitalBench is a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating embodied agents on hospital tasks, revealing failure points in long-horizon task chains through causal analysis.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks fail in ways that end-task success cannot see. HospitalBench is a diagnostic benchmark of ten hospital chores in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, each two unscored warm-up steps followed by a causal chain of five scored sub-tasks in one continuous simulation: the state one step leaves (an object pose, a choice, a fact seen once) determines what the next step must do, unlike benchmarks that place sub-tasks side by side. Vision-language agents act through skill-level tools from camera images. A scripted robot that makes only the calls a model gets is the solvability check of a chore. From each trajectory the benchmark reads where a chain breaks, what the agent did after a failed call, and how far its own position estimate drifts from the true one. This version reports first results only: 15 of 60 planned runs (three models at high effort, one run each on chores T1 and T10 from both start states and T3 from one), with scripted-robot proofs on three of the ten chores. Of the 15 runs, 2 passed all five sub-tasks. Runs still going after sub-tasks 1 to 5 were 15, 8, 4, 2, 2. Of 189 failed calls, 168 were followed by a different call and 111 by a call that did not fail. These are first results and not a full benchmark. We will release the scenes, task chains, scripted robot, evaluation harness and trajectories.

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Jiarui Dong, Zhiheng Liang, Yanjun Li, Zeyu Zhang, Heejeong Nam
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: JEPA4R enhances JEPA world models by enabling 4D point planning from depth-camera point clouds, achieving superior performance in robotic manipulation tasks and zero-shot real-world application.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: When Should a Human Take Back Control? Optimal Delegation under Turbulent AI Risk
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Haoze Yan, Julien Roze, Ved Upadhyay, Unal Tatar, Thibaut Mastrolia
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: The paper presents a model for optimal human-AI control delegation under risk, utilizing incident history to enhance decision-making and improve operational outcomes.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: When should a human take control from an autonomous AI agent, how much checking is worthwhile, and when should autonomy resume? These decisions become harder when incidents cluster and recent errors signal elevated risk. Exploratory analyses of AgentLogs coding-agent traces and ODCV-Bench task runs show higher held-out log likelihood for Hawkes incident-history models than matched no-history baselines, with positive gains whose conditional $90\%$ intervals exclude zero. AgentLogs evaluates continuous-time incident timing and type; ODCV evaluates failure occurrence at discrete decisions. Motivated by this predictive evidence, we formulate a continuous-time delegation problem that jointly chooses productive action, verification effort, and switching rates between human-directed, AI-assisted operation and autonomous AI operation. The model assumes that verification weakens incident propagation and balances project benefits against operating, supervision, risk, and handoff costs. Our Hawkes-PPO method summarizes observed incidents with exponential memory filters and learns these decisions from rewards. In synthetic experiments, it achieves a higher evaluated objective than either fixed regime and PPO without history filters, and approaches an approximate full-information benchmark. Further experiments show how incident excitation and supervision costs shape delegation.

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: AITHER: Authority-Informed Evidence Routing for Mixed-Authority Vision-Language Reasoning
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Xinjin Li, Haoyue Zhang, Xinyi Gou, Yuruo Gong, Yuanjian He
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: AITHER introduces a novel framework for mixed-authority vision-language reasoning, achieving high accuracy by effectively routing evidence based on authority, improving claim correction while preserving task integrity.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Reliable vision-language reasoning requires a control decision that conventional grounding methods leave implicit: which input is entitled to determine the answer? Auxiliary text may be a defeasible claim about an image, a binding task instruction, or compatible context.
